【38】Although the causes of RM are diverse， its pathogenesis is thought to follow a common pathway . In normal skel-etal muscle， the sarcolemma， a thin membrane that enclos-es striated muscle fibers， has many pumps that regulate the cellular electrochemical gradients， maintaining low levels of intracellular sodium and calcium and a high level of intracel-lular potassium. These processes require adenosine triphos-phate (ATP) as an energy source； any process leading to ATP depletion may result in RM. ATP depletion triggers dysfunc-tion of pumps， such as the sodium-potassium ATPase pump in the sarcolemma and calcium ATPase pump in the sarcoplasm， increases cellular permeability to sodium ions， increasing intra-cellular calcium concentration， and eventually induces myocyte degradation. The presumed mechanism of hyponatremia-related

【39】RM involves sarcolemma disruption due to sodium-potassium ATPase pump dysfunction .

【40】The pathogenesis of IAD is not fully understood； however， IAD can be caused by traumatic injury ， lymphocytic hypophysi-tis ， pituitary autoimmunity (often associated with other organ-specific autoimmune disorders) ， medications ，or radiation therapy for a brain tumor . In addition， IAD may be associated with primary empty sella ， which is charac-terized by the intrasellar herniation of the subarachnoid space that is often associated with variable degrees of flattening of the pituitary gland in patients without previous pituitary pa-thologies . In the present case， the patient had never ex-perienced a brain tumor， radiation therapy， or traumatic injury， and did not exhibit clinically evident hypophysitis or auto-immunity. Her IAD was associated with primary empty sella.

【41】We report an unusual case of severe hyponatremia and RM in an elderly patient with IAD. This case highlights the impor-tance of considering the possibility of central Al in patients with hyponatremia and inappropriately high plasma AVP levels. In addition， physicians should be aware that RM associated with hyponatremia can be an unusual but important mani-festation of IAD.

【0】ABSTRACT Objective： To study the clinic-pathological and oncological outcome of all the patients presenting with a diagnosis of small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus at Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Center. Methodology： From 1997 to 2017， all patients diagnosed with small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus were included in the study. Demographic variables were collected. Clinico-pathological outcomes of the disease were recorded. All data were entered and analyzed in SPSS ver 21. Results： A total of 6 patients were included in the study. The median age was63.5 +/-8.09 years. There were l male and 5 female patients. The most common presentation was dysphagia in all 6patients. OGD was used to detect the location and diagnosis of the disease. CT scan is used for staging of the disease. All patients received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and one patient had surgical resection of the tumour. Almost all patients developed metastases or progression of the disease. Conclusion： Small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus is rare and needs to be managed aggressively. All patients are best treated with a formal systemic and local treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS Small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus， clinicopathological outcomes， a rare cancer of the oesophagus， extrapulmonary small cell carcinoma

【2】Introduction

【3】Small cell carcinoma of the lung is a known entity， but extra-pulmonary small cell entity has completely different biology， clinical behaviour， and response to either chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Extrapulmonary small cell carcinoma is reported in the trachea， larynx， salivary glands， pancreas， salivary glands， uterine body and esophagus. The most common subtypes of oesophagal carcinoma are adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma， but few hundred cases of small cell carcinoma have been reported in the literature.

【4】In 1952， Mckeown published 2 cases of small cell carcinoma of the esophagusJ. Primary small cell carcinoma is extremely accounting for 0.4 to 2.8% of all oesophagal malignancies.

【5】The pathogenesis remains unclear； however， argyrophilic cells or pluripotent barPsal epithelial cells are thought to be the pos- sible cells of origin. It is characterized by small cells with scanty cytoplasm， round nuclei and granule formation， immuno-histochemical stains for neuroendocrine tumour helps in the diagnosis.

【6】No standard treatment has been accepted because of the rarity of the disease. On retrospective studies have been pub-lished. There is no standard staging protocol. The American Joint Committee on Cancer(AJCC) of small cell carci-noma are followed most of the times.

【7】Treatment includes a multi-modality approach， including chemotherapy，radiotherapy and surgery. The role of surgery is controversial. There is debate among professional about radi-cal esophagectomy with extended lymph node dissection ver-sus systemic therapy alone like chemotherapy and radiother-apy.

【8】The rationale of this study is to understand the clinic-pathological factors， diagnostic measures and prognosis of the disease. Small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus is a rare neo-plasm due to which there is paucity in data from this part of the world. This study will enlighten the world and add the literature about small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus and its management.

【9】Methodology

【10】Six patients have been studied in a tertiary care hospital， Shaukat Khanum Hospital， from January 1995 to December 2017. It is a retrospective descriptive case series with convenient sampling. The ethical approval was sought from the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital &amp； Research Centre， Pakistan. Informed consent was taken be-fore the collection of data. All patients diagnosed with primary small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus at Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre are included. Patient with secondary malignancies is excluded. Data was col-lected through HIS (Electronic data) at Shaukat Khanum Memo-rial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre. Calculations were per-formed with Statistical Package for the Social Sciences(SPSS 20) for Windows version 20 statistical software. Data were described using median with minimum and maximum value for skew dis tributed quantitative variables. For categorical variables， the number of observations and percentages will be reported For survival analyses. Outcomes that will be assessed are age， man-agement， overall survival，disease-free survival，Recurrence and site of metastases.

【11】Description of cases

【12】Case 1

【13】A 60-year-old female presented with dysphagia and anorexia for three months with no comorbid and no family history of cancer. She had an addiction to chewing tobacco and smok-ing. She underwent oesophago-duodenoscopy(OGD)， which showed polypoid growth at the distal oesophagus. It was poorly differentiated small cell carcinoma， which was positive for chro-mogranin and synaptobrevin. Magnetic resonance imaging was performed， which showed distal oesophagal cancer with metastatic liver disease involving the liver. The patient was given palliative chemoradiotherapy. 5 cycles of cisplatin and etoposide were given along with 25 fractions of radiotherapy. There was a progression of the disease. SURVIVAL?

【14】Case 2

【15】60-year-old female patient presented with dysphagia for 3months with no co-morbdidities or addiction history， She had no family history of cancer. ODG was performed which showed plaque like tumor at 25 cm from incisors. CT scan confirmed the findings with no metastases. Neo adjuvant chemoradiotherarpy with 6 cycles of etoposide/cisplatin were given along with radio-therapy in 25 fractions. Surgery，i.e. transhiatal esophagectomy， was performed. Histopathology specimen showed poorly differ-entiated small cell carcinoma， which was positive for cytokeratin and chromogranin. The size of the tumour was 3 cm. Pathologi-cal T stage was 3， and N was 1c.13 out of 16lymph nodes were positive for carcinoma. After a year the patient developed brain and hepatic metastases. Palliative radiotherapy was given. The patient was followed up for one year， but she was lost to follow up.

【16】58-year-old female presented with a complaint of dysphagia. She was a hypertensive and positive family history of cancer. OGD was performed， which showed polypoidal mass from25 to 33 cm from incisors. Histopathology revealed small cell carcinoma， which was positive， TTF positive， CD 56 positive and chromogranin negative. Endoscopic ultrasound was performed， which showed a clinical T3N1 tumour. She was given four cycles of cisplatin/etoposide and 25 fractions of radiotherapy. No surgery was performed. She was lost to follow up after nine months.

【17】Case 4

【18】57 year old female presented with dysphagia for four months. No family history of cancer and no addiction. OGD showed an annular stenosing tumour at 32 cm from incisors (lower oe-sophagus). Histopathology showed CD56 positive， cytokeratin positive and TTF1 negative small cell carcinoma. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) staging was T4N1M1. Computed tomography(CT) scan showed stage 4 disease. Tumour was irresectable at present because of the encasement of the distal thoracic aorta and proximal abdominal aorta. Palliative chemotherapy (cis-platin/etoposide x6) and radiotherapy were given. CT scan performed， which showed progressive disease. She was fol-lowed up for a year， and then she was lost to follow up.

【19】Case 5

【20】A 68-year-old female presented with the complaint of dyspha-gia. She had no family history of cancer， no addiction history and no comorbidities. She was from Afghanistan. On OGD， mid oesophagal mass was seen， which was polypoidal 27 to 33cm from incisors. CT scan showed a T3N1 distal oesophagal tumour. EUS showed T3N1 disease. A positron emission tomog-raphy (PET) scan was performed， which showed T3N3 disease. Pathology co nfirmed small cell carcinoma with positivity for synaptobrevin. Neoadjuvant carboplatin/etoposide four cycles were given， and radiotherapy was given in 25 fractions along with carboplatin/etoposide two cycles. A recent CT scan was performed， which showed stable disease. The patient was alive，WI after two vears with no disease.

【21】Case 6

【22】A 78-year-old male presented with dysphagia for three months. No addiction or family history of cancer. OGD showed poly-poidal distal oesophagal growth 36 to 40 cm from incisors in-volving gastro-oesophagal junction. EUS staging was T3N1. CT scan showed T4aN1 disease. Cisplatin/etoposide six cycles were given along with consolidative radiotherapy in a neoadjuvant setting. No surgery was performed as the patients functional status was poor after chemoradiotherapy. The patient developed a metastatic lesion in the liver after six months of completion of chemoradiotherapy. The patient is alive at present.

【23】Discussion

【24】In this study， we reviewed and analyzed the clinicopathological and management of six patients with small cell carcinoma of the oesophagus retrospectively. Although small cell carcinoma primarily affects the lungs， it can affect other organs too. SMCE is a rare disease with only a few hundred cases reported to date.

【25】Americans have published the incidence of 0.5 to 2.4% while in Japan， the incidence was 9%.

【26】Our study showed that women between 55 to 70 are primarily affected， comparable to other studies. Some studies revealed male predominance with an affected range of age from 6th to the eighth decades.

【27】Progressive dysphagia was the most typical symptoms at present. Xu-jing Lu et al. I studied SMEC； in their study， dys-phagia and anorexia were the most standard symptoms ranging from 78% to 100%. Duration of symptoms between the first presentation of symptoms and diagnosis of disease was within six months， as Xu-Jing et al. 1 explained the same.

【28】One of our patients had an addiction to chewing and smok-ing tobacco， and one was hypertensive. In all of the patients， OGD helped in diagnosing the tumour and locating the tumour site. CT scan helped in staging the disease and identifying any metastases if present. EUS can be performed in adjunct with a CT scan to check for resectability of the disease and local staging. Most of the patient had a distal tumour which was a locally advanced disease at presentation. One of the patients had metas-tases at presentation. Synaptobrevin and cytokerating were the commonest immuno-markers identified in the histopathological specimen， as shown in the literature.

【29】Due to the rare occurrence of the disease， there is no guideline available for the management. Management remains controver-sial. In our study， all patients received chemo-radiotherapy and radiotherapy as SMEC is believed to be a systemic disease and having a poor prognosis. The regime of chemotherapy most of the time was six cycles of cisplatin and etoposide. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy can be used as standard treatment for manage-ment， and they may produce better survival outcomes. The longest survival of the patient in our study was 24 months after the treatment. The longest survival in patient with SMEC was96 months in literature published by Craig et al. In another study， Law et al. stated a patient survived 72 months after given both systemic and local treatment .

【30】The limitation of this study was only six patients were studied retrospectively. Most of the patients lost to follow up. Due to the lack of data， no associations were made between the prognostic factors and survival analyses.

【31】This study is the first of its kind from Pakistan. Oesophagal cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting the Northern areas of Pakistan. This research will help professionals in under-standing the disease and its management. However prospective research like randomized control trial or meta-analyses is needed in future to understand the disease. As a result that， better man-agement protocols can be designed to have better outcome and surviyal.

Many factors responsible for low birth weight can be classified as fetal or maternal. Evidence-based interventions could save many newborns. For this， the knowledge has to be transformed into practice. Method： This study was performed at a medical college and tertiary care hospital in western India’s Thane district of Maharashtra. Eligible female participants were those who have enrolled in the hospital over 5 months from February through June 2021. All statistical analyses were performed using Mystat statistical software version 12.0 or Statistical Package of Social Sciences version 20.0 for Windows (IBM Corp， Armonk，NY). The normality of the data distribution was determined using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Result： Maternal TSH and thyroxin are more than that of cord blood counterparts， while cord blood T3 levels were found to be more than maternal T3. Maternal TSH has a positive correlation with the birth weight of neonates. It shows a significant negative correlation between the birth weight of cord blood T3 (r=-0.563) and Thyroxin (r=-0.510)， respectively. The higher the maternal thyroxin and T3， the lower the birth weight. Conclusion： Present study shows the effect of thyroid status of mother and fetus both has an association with neonatal birth weight. 【2】the production of thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) in- which both mother and fetus contribute. Among these factors， thyroid hormones play an important role. Thyroid hormones are essential for fetal growth and development ， and several stud-ies have demonstrated the association between maternal thyroid dysfunction and pregnancy outcomes.  Maternal hyper- and hypothyroidism have been associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes， but studies have led to inconsis-tent results. Gestational age at delivery and birth weight is an important predictor of neonatal mortality and morbidity， and literature reports that some of the complications associated with maternal thyroid disease may be secondary to preterm birth .

【3】Maternal hypo， as well as hyperthyroidism， is associated with preterm birth. Maternal hyperthyroidism is associated with a risk of low birth weight and small gestational age incidences. In the case of maternal hypothyroidism， there are diverse re-sults as some mention incidences of small for gestational age(SGA) while some mention no correlation between maternal hy-pothyroidism and birth weight.  Maternal thyroid disease is associated with an increased risk of obstetrical and labour com-plications such as fetal losses， hypertensive disorders during pregnancy， and preterm birth. Literature reports that effective and timely treatment can curtail the untoward effects. 

【4】MATERIAL & METHODS

【5】Study population

【6】This study was performed at a medical college and tertiary care hospital in western India's Thane district of Maharashtra. Eli-gible female participants were those who have enrolled in the hospital over 5 months from February through June 2021. Writ-ten informed consent as per the Helsinki declaration has been obtained from subjects selected for the study. The sample size was calculated based on assuming a two-sided type I error &=5%， power  95% and correlation coefficient (p) 0.5， which provided the sample size required as 70. Every 10th term nor-mal weight baby delivered in authors' hospital was taken as control. Eighty neonates born in authors’ hospital， irrespective of the mode of delivery born at term，i.e.， 37-40 weak were in-cluded； 40 as cases and 40 as a control group. The maternal age group was 19-30 years， and weight was 52-68 kg. Those under treatment for hypo or hyperthyroidism were excluded. In addition， women who underwent in vitro fertilization had a twin pregnancy or fetal loss， used medication known to interfere with the thyroid， or had a history of thyroid disease， congeni-tal abnormality or maternal events like pre-eclampsia， chronic diseases， addictions like smoking/ tobacco chewing or any sig-nificant medical history were excluded. The Institutional Review Board and Institutional Ethics Committee approved this study protocol.

【7】Data collection

【8】During hospital visits， nurses， residents， and gynaecologists， with the use of the electronic patient file， prospectively collected all data. Maternal fasting blood samples were drawn from the median cubital vein. Cord blood sample (4mL) was collected in sterile serum separating tubes (BD vacutainer SST II advance) immediately after the birth of babies， drawn from a 15-20 cm length of umbilical cord incised while severing it at the time of birth of the baby. Thus， a mixed umbilical cord blood sample containing blood from both umbilical artery and vein was ob-tained. Samples obtained were centrifuged at 3，000RPM，and sera separated were analyzed immediately. According to the manufacturer's protocol， TSH， T4， and T3 concentrations were measured with the SNIBE Biolumi 8000. The intra-assay and in-terassay coefficients of variation were 1.6% to 3.6% for TSH， and1.9% to 4.0% for FT4. Birth weight was standardized for gesta-tional age at birth. Information on birth weight， gestational age， and fetal sex was prospectively collected in the medical records. Lipid profile and other parameters are done colourimet-rically using Erba XL-640 auto-analyzer. All the analytes are tested in maternal serum also.

【9】Statistical Analysis

【10】All analyses adjusted for potential confounders such as gesta-tional age at blood sampling， maternal age， BMI， parity， educa-tion level， fetal sex， hypertension， and diabetes based on biolog-ical plausibility， identification of a variable as a confounder in previous studies， change of the effect estimates of interest， or re-duction in the residual variability of the outcome. All statistical analyses were performed using Mystat statistical software ver-sion 12.0 or Statistical Package of Social Sciences version 20.0 for Windows (IBM Corp， Armonk， NY). The normality of the data distribution was determined using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.

【11】RESULTS

【12】As shown in Figure 1， there is a significant difference between the cord blood and maternal blood thyroid profile. Maternal TSH and thyroxin are more than cord blood counterparts， while cord blood T3 levels were found to be more than maternal T3. The lipid profile also reports  the significant difference between maternal and cord blood. Levels of all the lipid pro-file parameters are higher in the maternal serum than in cord blood. Maternal TSH positively correlates with the birth weight of neonates， as shown in Fig .2 (r=0.224). Trends toward lower maternal TSH levels and lower birth weight were observed but reached negligible statistical significance. Fig.3 shows maternal T3 (r=-0.451) and Fig.4 shows maternal thyroxin (r=-0.505) re-spectively， having significant negative correlation with neonatal birth weight. In Fig.5， the correlation of birth weight is shown with cord blood T3 and Thyroxin. It shows significant negative correlation of cord blood T3 (r=-0.563) and Thyroxin (r=-0.510) respectively， with the birth weight. The higher the maternal thyroxin and T3， the lower the birth weight. The same is appli-cable to cord blood thyroxin and T3. Higher thyroxin levels can be associated with low birth weight. Our study shows that as maternal TSH increases， neonatal birth weight increases， but as maternal T3 and thyroxin increase， birth weight shows a declinig trend. The same is applicable to cord blood T3 and thyroxin； as they increase， birth weight tends to decrease. Fig.6 shows the receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve for T4 and TSH. The area under the curve (AUC) gradually increases from 0.623to 0.896. This shows the contribution of T4 & TSH to neonatal birth weight. T3 has a very negligible contribution with an AUC of <0.5.

【13】DISCUSSION

【14】Some reports are showing maternal hypothyroidism in preg-nancy is associated with lower birth weight， whereas hypothy-roxinaemia is associated with higher birth weight. An inverse association of maternal TSH (even within the normal range) with birth weight was reported in the literature.  Our study showed the inverse association between maternal thyroxin and birth weight， but with increased maternal TSH， the birth weight tends to increase. Some studies have mentioned that high ma- ternal TSH is associated with a higher risk of prematurity and respiratory distress syndrome.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total cholesterol  | 234.71±72.51  | 76.87±38.58  | <0.05  |
| Triglycerides  | 191.04±65.90  | 40.91±16.73  | <0.05  |
| HDL  | 64.79±17.53  | 29.49±19.31  | <0.05  |
| LDL  | 116.84±39.86  | 27.11±7.66  | <0.05  |
| VLDL  | 38.24±13.16  | 8.39±3.34  | <0.05  |

【17】At birth， term infants experience a surge in TSH that peaks around 30 minutes post-delivery. In preterm infants of 24-27weeks， the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis development is more immature， and the TSH surge is smaller.  There are contradictory reports regarding the association between birth weight and cord blood TSH.  Our study observed no such correlation between birth weight and cord blood TSH.

【18】Various metabolic pathways and processes throughout the gestational period are controlled by thyroid hormones in the mother as well as the fetus. By facilitating placental implanta-tion， thyroid hormones control the growth of the fetus. Another way to regulate the growth is by regulating various metabolisms， oxygen and glucose consumption and various other factors， which are the part of skeletal growth， tissue differentiation and accretion. A meta-analysis reported the inverse association be-tween thyroxin and birth weight. Similar results are obtained in our study. Thyroid hormone crosses the placenta to reach the fetus. Maternal thyroxin has a direct effect on the developing fetus. It is hypothesized that the effects of thyroxin are mediated by increased catabolism of lipids and proteins in the fetus. This causes depletion of energy available. At the same time， vascular resistance in the placenta is also high. This adds to the effect of maternal thyroxin. Effect of thyroxin is amplified by an increased fetal nutritional demand and increased fetal growth rate associated with the progression of pregnancy. A recent trial showed that thyroxin supplementation is associated with the in creased risk of small for gestational age infants.  Our results displayed an inverse correlation between birth weight and T3. It is not clear that T3 crosses the placenta； hence， further studies are necessary to study the actual effect of T3 on neonatal birth weight.

【19】The present study shows that maternal thyroid and TSH have a profound effect on neonatal birth weight. Cord blood thyroxin and TSH also contribute to a certain extent. However， one of the study's limitations can be mentioned as there is no trimester pattern followed for the sample collection. That could provide a more detailed picture of the effects of thyroid status in various trimesters.

【20】CONCLUSION

【21】The present study shows the effect of thyroid status of mother and fetus both has association with neonatal birth weight. More detailed analysis with sample collection as per trimester is re-quired to know more about the impact of various confounding factors which have impact on birth weight. Maternal TSH rather than thyroxin is better predictor of the neonatal birth weight.

【0】Background：

【1】Osseous metaplasia is a heterotopic normal bone in soft tissues. It is occasionally found in mucosal polyps of the external auditory canal， tongue， gut， stomach，nasal cavity， and uterus. Choanal polyp with osseous meta-plasia originating from the latera wall of the nasopharynx has not been previously reported. In fact， osseous metaplasia in nasal polyps represents a very uncommon histological finding with only 12 cases described in the literature.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We reported here， the clinical， radiological， and therapeutic management of a nasopharynx choanal polyp in a patient with severe nasal obstruction and rhinolalia history. Endoscopic examination of nasal cavities revealed a polypoid-like mass in the left nasal fossa， extending to the choanal area and nasopharynx. Computed tomog-raphy scan and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a solitary and lob-ulated mass in the choanal area and nasopharynx. We performed the removal of the mass through careful hemostasis of left sphenopalatine artery using both transnasal and transoral paths， with no complications for the patient. Histopathological examination of the biopsy revealed a benign inflammatory polyp with osseous metaplasia. No recurrence was noted 24 months after surgery.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】The incidence of ossifying areas in nasal polyps is very low， with only 12 cases reported in the literature. Ossifying polyps originating from the lateral wall of nasopharynx has never been reported before. The use of a combined endoscopic and transoral surgical approach was shown to be reliable in terms of adequate exposure and visu-alization of the lesion， control of bleeding， and complete removal of the mass.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Bone Neoplasms · Metaplasia · Nasal Polyps · Nasopharyngeal Neoplasms Osseous metaplasia (OM) is a rare condition that has been report-ed to be present in only a few cases of mucosal polyps located in the external auditory canal， tongue， gut， stomach， nasal cav-ity and uterine cervix . Moreover， this alteration has not only been observed in patients with osteoma and ossifying fibroma， but， also in patients with inverted papilloma and esthesioneuro-blastoma . Furthermore， rare cases with osseous metapla-sia in the sinonasal tract have been described . In particu-lar， only 12 patients have been found with osseous metaplasia in nasal polyps originating from the ethmoid sinus， middle tur-binate， inferior turbinate， nasal septum， or middle meatus .

【7】To the best of our knowledge， choanal polyp with osseous metaplasia has never been previously reported in the lateral wall of the nasopharynx. Here， we describe， for the very first time， a clinical case of a choanal polyp with osseous metapla-sia arising from lateral wall of rhinopharynx that was success-fully managed with no recurrence of the disease after 2 years from the surgical procedure.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 51-years-old female with a history of severe nasal obstruc-tion associated to rhinolalia， was observed in May of 2016. Rhinofiberoptic endoscopy using a flexible instrument showed a mass resembling a polypoid formation in the left nasal cavity， which was also extended to the entire choanal area and naso-pharynx. No abnormalities of the mass surface were noted. Interestingly， even though the nasal sinuses seemed normal， computed tomography (CT) scans showed the presence of a solitary and lobulated mass with clustered radio-dense mate rial， suggesting a possible ossification in the area. In particular， from the CT images the mass seemed to be originating from the left inferior turbinate， reaching the posterior part of the left nasal cavity and extending to both the nasopharynx and the right posterior choana . Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed the presence of the mass in both the nasopharynx and choanal area suggesting that the possible origin of the lesion was the nasopharynx. Moreover， the imaging showed a calcific aspect within the mass and low contrast enhancement . Due to the size of the mass， only during the surgical procedure was it possible to identify the exact site of origin of the lesion within the nasopharynx.

【10】Surgical approach

【11】Surgery for the patient was performed under general anesthe-sia. A medicated tampon with xylocaine 1% and epinephrine1/100 000 was kept in place for 10 minutes. Then， in order to expose the mass， we performed an endoscopic resection of the left inferior turbinate. The left sphenopalatine foramen was visualized with cauterization of sphenopalatine artery. Subsequently， a transoral T-incision of the soft palate made access possible to the left lateral wall of the nasopharynx revealing the base of the lesion. Thereafter， the mass was com-pletely and successfully removed. The surgical incision was su-tured with Vicryl 4.0， and a nasal pack was positioned in both nasal cavities. Macroscopically， the mass was a hard polypoid specimen， 5x3x2 cm in size and white-grey in color and firm in consistence . The tissue section revealed it was diffusely calcific. Microscopically， the histological analysis re-vealed that the specimen was covered by respiratory epithe-lium， constituted by loose connective tissue with trabeculae of mature bone in the subepithelial chorion， and diffuse calcifi-cations were located in the loose stroma together with chron-ic inflammatory infiltrates and some plasma cells； eosinophils were absent. Immunohistochemical investigation (S100， p63， SOX10) were not positive. Moreover， respiratory glandular el-ements with some cystic dilatations were found .

【12】There were no postoperative complications and no recurrence of the disease at 24 months after surgery.

【13】Discussion

【14】Nasal polyps with osseous metaplasia are extremely rare . Two possible theories have been proposed to explain the mech-anism involved in the ossification of polyps： bone morphoge-TSI netic proteins (BMPs)， and post-traumatic or post-surgery . In particular， a potential role of BMP-4 in polyp ossification has been reported， even though it has been shown that TGFB-1 and BMP-7 synergic action induces bone formation . The osteo-blasts differentiation is divided into 2 stages. In the first stage， some undifferentiated mesenchymal cells may differentiate into osteogenic progenitors when stimulated by appropriate growth factors within sinonasal polyps . During the second stage， osteoblast progenitors become osteoblast cells ready to produce bone tissue . The second theory suggests that ossification within polyps could originate from bones left behind during pri-or surgery or trauma . The incidence of ossifying areas in nasal polyps is very low， with only 12 case have been reported. Ossifying polyps have been described to arise from the middle turbinate， inferior turbinate， maxillary sinus， ethmoid and superior turbinate， with the most common origin in the poste-rior portion of the nasal septum . Interestingly， ossifying polyps originating from the lateral wall of nasopharynx have not previously been reported. The accurate radiological examination of metaplastic ossifying polyps is useful and essential to identify not only calcifications， but also surrounding tissues patterns and erosions j.While polyps generally present with iso-density and a lobulated shape on CT imaging， osseous metaplasia appears to have multiple clustered densities with bony cortical and med-ullary cavities in the center of the polyp . Usually， a diffuse process of ossification with defined margins is a benign fibro-osseous type of lesions . On the other side， poorly de-fined margins have been reported to be present in sarcomas or metastatic undifferentiated carcinomas . On MRI images， normal polyps show hypo-intensity on T1WI and hyper-intensity on T2WI with marginal and septal enhancement on T1WI . The ossification process generally shows a moderate enhance-ment after administrating gadolinium . In opposite to normal polyps， the ones in which the ossification process has already started show thin hypo-intensity on both T1Wl and T2WI in the peripheral zone of ossification， corresponding to the bony corti-ces . Instead， ossifying polyps in the central zone exhibit mostly hyper-intensity on both T1Wl and T2WI images， as an adipose component of the medullary cavities . The bone tissue within a mass of nasal polyps needs a careful clinical diagnosis， since it can be associated with pathologies like rhinolith， myce-toma， inverted papilloma with calcifications， chondrosarcoma， osteosarcoma， and fibro-osseous lesions， which can mimic nasal polyps with osseous metaplasia on CT scans . Particularly， rhinolith and sinolith are calcareous concretion derived from a deposition of salts in the nose and paranasal sinuses， a condi-tion that may be associated to nasal polyps . On the other hand， sinonasal mycetoma typically appears on CT scans as a hy-per-attenuating lesion in most cases containing centrally locat-ed punctate， linear， or nodular calcifications . Mycetoma usu-ally shows marked diffuse hypo-intensity on T2-weighted images that do not enhance after injection of gadolinium； this condition is helpful in the diagnostic process in case of doubtful CT scans images . Furthermore， fungal rhino sinusitis might show ar-eas of ossification with an unclear and undefined trabecular pat-tern . Inverted papilloma， which generally originates from the lateral nasal wall， may have calcifications as well as a bone de-struction pattern which could be associated to polypoid chang-es . Differential diagnosis between chondrosarcoma and na-sal polyps with metaplastic ossification may be difficult because of the presence of multiple calcifications in the soft tissue mass on CT scans . Chondrosarcoma located in the nasal cavity is found in the cartilaginous nasal septum presenting a marginal bone erosion . CT scans of osteosarcoma present radioden-sities diffusely distributed within the mass with focal bone de-struction and a periosteal reaction such a"sunburst" aspect . Fibro-osseous lesions are located at the center of the mass . On CT scans， radiodensities associated with fibro-osseous lesions are well defined and distributed diffusely within the mass .In most cases， 2 main surgical approaches are advised： endoscopic and transoral . In particular， for larger and harder masses the transoral approach is preferred， with a low recurrence rate after years from surgery . Chondro-osseous respiratory epitheli-al adenomatoid hamartoma (COREAH) is an epithelial hamarto-ma with proliferation of glandular tissue， rare benign entity of sinonasal tract with 12 cases reported in literature. On CT scans， it appears as a polypoid mass with a central core of high-densi-ty not enhancing with contrast. On MRl images it has a heterog enous T2 hyperintensity and T1 hypo-intensity with cerebriform appearance after gadolinium contrast .

【16】Interestingly， in the described case， the mass seemed to be linked to the left inferior turbinate and therefore， we decid-ed to perform the endoscopic left inferior turbinate resection. Since the mass was large in size， we choose also transoral approach and we found that the lesion was linked to the left lateral wall of nasopharynx. The histological analysis revealed the unexpected presence of mature bone trabeculae in the sub-epithelial chorion and diffuse calcifications in the stroma.

【17】Conclusions

【18】Osseous metaplasia is an extremely rare finding in nasal polyp-osis. Radiological examination represents the only tool to indi-viduate an ossification within polyps in a preoperative staging. Different metaplastic lesions with osseous metaplasia are well known in the sinonasal tract. CT scans and MRIs are essential for a preoperative differential diagnosis in order to discriminate any characteristics of lesion malignancy. The use of a combined surgical approach，endoscopic and transoral， allow adequate exposure and visualization of the lesion， control of bleeding， and thus， a complete removal of the mass .After surgery， a histologic assessment performed on all surgical spec-imens helps give a definitive diagnosis.

【0】ABSTRACT Candida albicans is the most common human fungal pathogen causing diseases ranging from mucosal to systemic infections， mainly in an immunocompromised individual. Here， in the case of a female of 26 years of age， undergone renal transplantation and a week after transplantation recipient developed complications in urinary output， painful urination with fever. Bacterial urinary tract infection was suspected， and meropenem was given preliminary but did not show any recovery. Later， on blood culture， the patient was diagnosed with a bloodstream infection of C. albicans. After diagnosis with C. albicans， meropenem was replaced with antifungal drug voriconazole (200mg， BD)，and the patient was fully recovered from infection in a week.

【1】KEYWORDS Candida albicans， Renal transplant， Voriconazole

【2】Introduction

【3】More than 15 Candida species are found to be responsible for human infections. C. albicans are opportunistic pathogens and are the commensal human microflora that asymptomatically colonizes many areas of the human body. However， under the conditions of immune suppression or any disruption to the host environment， C. albicans can be a pathogen， causing various infections . Systemic candidiasis can be due to host-related or healthcare-related risk factors. The systemic infection can be life-threatening among immunocompromised patients due to AIDS，undergoing chemotherapy and radiotherapy treatment for cancers， organ transplants， etc.

【4】Candida infections in the United States are the fourth most common hospital-acquired infections and the second most com-mon cause of death due to such infections . Among the Can-dida species， C. albicans dominant causes of candidemia， fol- A 26 years old female had undergone renal allograft transplan-tation on 2019 July 15 at Sumeru Hospital Pvt. Ltd.， Lalitpur， Nepal. A week after post-transplantation， the recipient devel-oped fever， painful urination， weight loss， weakness， and ap-petite loss. Her body temperature at that period was 38.3℃ (101°F)； pulse rate： 63/min； blood pressure： 140/100 mm Hg and body weight： 41 kg.

【5】Initially， bacterial urinary tract infection was suspected， and antibiotic meropenem (500mg， BD) was given as provisional therapy. However， the fever and painful urination was persisted， and the patient's condition became worse. Urine， implanted DJ stent， and blood samples were sent for culture in a laboratory. The culture showed the growth of C. albicans in all tested sam-ples of blood， urine， and DJ stents. Following the C. albicans culture positivity， the patient was given an anti-fungal drug， voriconazole (200mg BD).

【6】After a week of voriconazole therapy， the patient’s condition was improved. Blood and urine samples were repeated for cul-ture on the 13th day and showed aseptic growth of the organism. The complete laboratory findings of the investigation at the time of infection and after her recovery are listed in Table 1.

【9】HCV-antibody Non-reactive Rapid Immunochromatographic

【10】Laboratory Investigation

【11】When the post-transplantation symptoms were seen， urine sam-ples and implanted DJ stents were sent for culture to the lab-oratory and were inoculated on CLED agar， Blood agar， and Mac-Conkey agar (HiMedia， India)， respectively， and incubated aerobically at 37℃ for 24 hours. After 24 hours of incubation， a small round， creamy white colony appears in blood agar and non-lactose forming small colonies on CLED agar. A blood sam-ple was also collected for the culture and was inoculated on DL-Bt64 automated blood culture detection system. After 48 hours， growth was indicated. Subculture on blood agar revealed similar morphology that observed as from urine and DJ stent culture， on Gram stain， gram-positive organism resembling yeast as shown in figure 2.

【12】Then the Germ tube test was done， which revealed the forma-tion of filamentous hyphae on microscopy resembling C. albicans as shown in figure 3. This was further confirmed by forming a greenish colony on candida chrome agar (Himedia， India)， as shown in figure 1.

【13】After identifying C. albicans as a cause of bloodstream infec-tion， an antifungal drug， voriconazole (200mg， twice a day)， was given. On the 7th day of voriconazole treatment， the patient's condition was improved， and on the 13th day， she completely re-covered without any signs of bloodstream infection. The results of laboratory investigations done on the initial and recovery of infection are listed in table 1.

【14】Discussion

【15】There are more than 150 Candida species recognized to date. However， only 15 of these species are regarded as infectious agents . In the United States， Candida species was consid-ered as the fourth most common cause of bloodstream infections(BSIs) with increasing prevalence in nosocomial infections . The pathogens mainly involved in 95% of infections are C. al- bicans， C. glabrata， C. parapsilosis， C. tropicalis， and C. krusei .

【16】C. albicans being the normal flora of the human body， can be pathogenic in a hospitalized patient， old age， and immunosup-pressive individual or patient having an implant Mostly they cause superficial infection affecting the mucosal membrane but can lead to life-threatening conditions by infecting the blood-stream and invading various internal organs . Infection with Candida species remains a frequent cause of morbidity after solid-organ transplantation， with invasive candidiasis occurring at a prevalence of 5% in kidney transplant recipients and 20% in liver transplant recipients . Similarly， in our subject， we found the C. albicans bloodstream infection in the transplant recipient who undergone recent renal transplantation.

【17】Despite the various antifungal agents available， there is still a limitation in treating systemic fungal infections. Polyenes， azoles， echinocandins， and flucytosine are the classes of antifun-gal agents that are effective against systemic fungal infections. For Candida infection， fluconazole is regarded as a drug of choice and most recommended . However， the resistance rate towards fluconazole is increasing ； therefore， for the treatment of fluconazole-resistant invasive Candida infection， the European Medicines Agency (EMEA)， since March 2002， has approved the use of voriconazole . Similarly， many other studies also reported a higher sensitivity rate of voriconazole towards C. albicans than fluconazole . Therefore， the patient was treated with voriconazole and was fully recovered after a week of treatment.

【18】In developing countries like Nepal， where limited sources for diagnosis and treatment of fungal infections， we could not perform anti-fungal susceptibility testing. Therefore， we used voriconazole as a safe option for the treatment of the patient. Which was found effective， and the patient recovered from can-dida infection.

【19】Conclusion

【20】Invasive candidiasis often leads to severe complications in pa-tients with a debilitated immune system，like among patients undergoing transplantation. Delayed initiation of therapy for invasive candidiasis results in considerably increased mortality. Our case report emphasizes the need for an early， comprehensive diagnosis of disseminated candidiasis and initiation of appro-priate antifungal treatment for clearance of the infection and also the voriconazole might be the safe treatment option for bloodstream candida infections in transplant patients.

【21】Data availability

【22】The corresponding author will provide data on request and approval.

【0】ABSTRACT Through its regulatory effects on pancreatic beta cells and immune cells， vitamin D demonstrates the ability to positively influence insulin sensitivity， enhance insulin secretion， decrease systematic inflammation and promote beta-cell longevity. These effects cumulatively link vitamin D to diabetes mellitus (DM) and therefore imply that this steroid hormone (vitamin D) may play a role in the prevention or even treatment of diabetes. Evidence from research has already established an inverse relationship between vitamin D and diabetes mellitus. Therefore， the aim of this review is to discuss any potential role that vitamin D may play in the prevention of type l and 2 diabetes mellitus.

【1】KEYWORDS Vitamin D， Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus， Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus， Diabetes Mellitus

【2】Introduction

【3】Diabetes mellitus (DM) is characterized by elevated blood glu-cose levels caused by insulin deficiency， insulin resistance or a combination of both. The long-term complications of DM are either micro-vascular or macro-vascular in nature and include nephropathies， retinopathies，neuropathies， in addition to cardio-vascular， peripheral vascular and neurovascular diseases. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) accounts for the majority of observed cases of the disease； however， type 1 diabetes (T1D) is also very common. T2D is characterized by insulin resistance and abnormal pancreatic beta-cell function. T1D is marked by an auto-immune process which destroys beta cells (insulin-producing cells) of the pancreas. This autoimmune destruction is triggered by environment factors in genetically predisposed individuals. Vitamin D is a steroid hormone that is synthe-sized by skin cells and is activated by hydroxylation reactions in the kidneys and liver. Chronic illnesses such as cardiovascular diseases， autoimmune diseases and cancers have all been associ-ated with reduced serum levels of vitamin D. In the past， links between vitamin D and diabetes have been established. Several decades ago， animals such as rabbits and rats had been used to demonstrate that low levels of vitamin D negatively affect pancreatic insulin production. Furthermore， vitamin

【4】D receptors (VDR) and vitamin D binding proteins (DBP) have been discovered in immune cells and pancreatic beta-cells； thus， further suggesting an association of vitamin D with insulin pro-duction and secretion.

【5】Despite these finding， some studies have concluded that vita-min D supplementation has no major effects in decreasing the risk for developing DM.

【6】A double-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial， con-ducted on postmenopausal women followed up for seven years， demonstrated that the supplementation of calcium combined with vitamin D3 yielded no reduction in the risk for developing DM. Another double blinded，randomized controlled trial， conducted for 12 weeks aimed at investigating the effects of vita-min D supplementation on insulin and glucose levels in normal subjects with vitamin D deficiency， concluded that vitamin D supplementation had no metabolic effects on glucose regulation. In addition， it demonstrated no positive effects of vitamin D sup-plementation on insulin production and sensitivity. Despite the findings from these studies that dispute potential positive effects of vitamin D in diabetes， this review aims at exploring any potential role that vitamin D may play in preventing the development of DM (T1D&T2D).

【7】Vitamin D Sources and Metabolism

【8】Vitamin D exists in two forms： ergocalciferol (D2) and chole calciferol (D3). Mushrooms that are exposed to sunlight make vitamin D2； however， in humans， vitamin D3 is made when the skin is exposed to ultraviolet- B (UVB) light from the sun. Humans are incapable of making Vitamin D2 .

【9】Upon exposure ofskin cellstoTJVB light，

【10】dehydrocholesterol is converted to vitamin D3.The biosynthesis of vitamin D in skin cells serves as the primary source of vitamin D in humans. Vitamin D3 is also obtained from foods such as fish； however， vitamin D2 is abundant in edible mushrooms. Vitamin D obtained from the skin or diet is transported to the liver where it undergoes hydroxylation to produce 25-hydroxyvitamin D(25-OHD) also known as calcidiol. This reaction is catalysed by CYP2R1 a significant vitamin D 25-hydroxylase enzyme .25-OHD is then transported to the kidneys where it undergoes a second hydroxylation reaction producing 1， 25-dihydroxy vitamin D (1，25(OH)2D) or calcitriol.CYP27B1 catalyses this second reaction， the only enzyme that has 25-OHD 1-a-hydroxylase activity and the resulting 1，25(OH)2D is considered to be the biologically active form of vitamin DJ. Once activated， vitamin D is transported to targeted tissues where it successfully binds to specific receptors exerting its effects.

【11】Type1 Diabetes and vitamin D

【12】T1D is considered an autoimmune disease. Therefore， the con-dition is characterized by destruction of pancreatic beta cells by autoantibodies and other immunological factors such as T lymphocytes， B lymphocytes and macrophages. Both genetic and environmental factors play a major role in the onset of the disease. Vitamin D acts as a regulator of the immune sys-tem and similarly to other autoimmune conditions， T1D is also considered to be associated with vitamin D deficiency.

【13】In the early stages of T1D， inflammatory infiltrates com-prising T-cells， B-cells， macrophages， and natural killer cells invade the pancreatic islet cells. Vitamin D has a protective effect through its ability to regulate cytokines such as interferon-gamma (INF-y) and interleukin-2 (IL-2)； thus， indirectly sup-pressing the activation of these immune cells. Further-more， with regards to TID other protective effects are achieved from vitamin D through its potential to regulate the prolifera-tion of lymphocytes and to protect pancreatic beta cells from death and destruction through the suppression of Fas expres-sion 25.

【14】Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and vitamin D

【15】T2D is marked by these three parameters： pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction， insulin resistance and systemic inflammation26，271.

【16】Pancreatic beta-cell function and Vitamin D

【17】Vitamin D directly or indirectly enhances the function of pan-creatic beta- cells. Beta-cells of the pancreas contain vitamin D receptors； therefore， vitamin D helps to modulate their func-tion . Pancreatic beta-cells contain an enzyme called 25-hydroxyvitamin D-1-alpha-hydroxylase， which allows vitamin D to be activated to exert a paracrine effect within the pancreas. Vitamin D also exhibits the ability to support beta-cell longevity through its regulations on cytokines’ production and effects.

【18】The process of insulin secretion is mediated by extracellu-lar calcium levels and the flow of calcium through beta-cells. Vitamin D indirectly modulates insulin secretion through its regulation of calcium influx into beta cells. J Calbindin is a cytosolic protein that is found in many tissues， including pancre-atic beta-cells. This protein， which is a calcium-binding protein， helps to regulate insulin secretion by controlling intracellular calcium levels. Vitamin D also regulates calbindin and therefore， indirectly regulates insulin secretion.

【19】Insulin sensitivity and Vitamin D

【20】In insulin-dependent tissues such as skeletal muscles and adipocytes， vitamin D promotes the expression of insulin recep-tors and therefore， directly supports insulin sensitivity. 【22】Systematic inflammation and vitamin D

【23】The development of T2D is proposed to be deeply influenced by inflammation which promotes insulin resistance. 【30】Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

【27】Animal studies have demonstrated that the administration of1，25(OH)2D3 (OH)2D3 (5 ug/kg/alternate day) to non-obese diabetic mice (NOD mice) at high doses has the potential to decrease the development of T1D in addition to decreasing the incidence of insulitis . This is achieved through the reg-ulatory effects that 1，25(OH)2D3 has on the number of effector T-cells and induction of Treg cells. The doses of 1，25(OH)2D3required to prevent diabetes in experimental subjects (NOD mice) result in side effects such as increased blood calcium levels and loss of bone calcium. These observed effects can be mini-mized through the utilization of structural analogues of 1， 25(OH)2D2. Similarly to 1，25(OH)2D3 these analogues has the potential to delay or inhibit the onset of insulitis in addition to delaying the development of T1D in NOD mice.

【28】An experimental study conducted on type 1 diabetic rats demonstrated that vitamin D supplementation could markedly decrease fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and slightly decrease haemoglobin A1c (HBA1c) levels. An 8-week long study demonstrated that activated vitamin D has the potential to im-prove T1D in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats (inflammation-driven model of diabetes). However，1，25(OH)2D3 had minimal effects on reversing overt diabetes . A birth cohort conducted in Finland， which enrolled over 10，000 children， demonstrated that dietary supplementation of vitamin D potentially reduces the risk for developing T1D. Furthermore， this study demon-strated that the sufficient intake of the steroid hormone during early infancy has the potential to reduce the number of observed cases of the disease . A population-based case-control study carried out in Norway， demonstrated a reduction in the inci-dence of T1D in children whose mothers took cod liver oil， a supplement rich in vitamin D， during pregnancy . Another case-control study conducted in Norway， which included 545cases of childhood-onset T1D and 1668 control subjects from the population， proposed that cod liver oil has the potential to decrease the risk for developing T1D when taken within the first year of life.

【29】A large case-control study， including 820 cases of T1D and2335 control subjects from seven different centres in Europe con-cluded that vitamin D supplementation during infancy has a protective effect against the development of TID. The results obtained from this study demonstrated that 1，25(OH)2D3 has the potential to regulate immune responses and therefore， delay or halt immune activities initiated by environmental exposures in patients susceptible to developing T1D. A meta-analysis was conducted to compare results from four case-control stud-ies and one cohort study. Results from the case-control studies demonstrated a reduction in the risk for developing T1D in in- fants who received vitamin D supplementation as compared to infants who were not supplemented. Results from the cohort study were also similar， thus signifying that the supplementa-tion of vitamin D during early childhood has a protective effect against the development of T1D 

【30】Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

【31】An experimental study on T2D in the spontaneously hyperten-sive rat (SHR) and Wister rat models demonstrated that chole-calciferol (12.5 Ag/kg\_1) exhibits the ability to reduce blood glucose levels. At the end of the study， 40% of SHR models showed a 60% reduction in blood glucose levels and the group of Wister rat models showed a 40% reduction in blood glucose concentrations. Another study carried out on vitamin D defi-cient rats demonstrated that glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from the pancreas was significantly impaired when vitamin D levels were low. However， with the supplementation of vitamin D， insulin secretion was restored.

【32】A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational stud-ies demonstrated an inverse relationship between serum vitamin D levels and blood glucose levels in diabetic and non-diabetic subjects. This analysis concluded that lower levels of vitamin D are associated with a potential increased risk for developing T2D. In addition， it was indicated through this study that blood glucose control can be potentially achieved through vitamin D supplementation in diabetic patients . Another systematic review investigated the relationship between vitamin D status and the development of T2D and also observed the effects of vitamin D on blood glucose concentrations. This review con-cluded that higher incidences of T2D occur in lower vitamin D status subjects. However， it failed to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on blood glycaemic control . A randomized placebo-controlled double-blinded clinical trial was conducted to investigate the effects of parentally administrated 25-OHD on glycaemic control and inflammation in type 2 diabetics suffering from ischemic heart diseases. This study， which included 95 patients， con-cluded that vitamin D has the potential to decrease blood glucose levels. However， the use of vitamin D demonstrated minimal effects on inflammation.

【33】Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease (MONICA)/Cooperative Health Research in the Re-gion of Augsburg (KORA) study demonstrated the relationship between serum 25-OHD concentrations and the development of T2D. It was concluded that higher incidences of T2D are observed with lower serum levels of 25-OHD，therefore demon-strating an inverse relationship between vitamin D status and the development of the disease . A prospective study， in-volving 1080 Korean non-diabetic subjects followed for three years， concluded that vitamin D metabolism might poten-tially influence the pathogenesis of T2D independent of known risk factors for the disease such as obesity， dyslipidemia， and hypertension.

【34】Future Outlook Conclusion

【35】To date， further research is being undertaken as medical per-sonnel strive to achieve deeper insight into the important role of vitamin D in the pathogenesis and prevention of DM. A large multicentre (n = 22 sites)， randomized， double-blinded， placebo-controlled， primary prevention clinical trial， called Base-line Characteristics of the Vitamin D and Type 2 Diabetes (D2d)， was recently undertaken to investigate and determine the un-derlying relationship between vitamin D and type 2 diabetes mellitus. It enrolled 2，423 subjects， and published results will establish whether or not the supplementation of vitamin Dhas the potential to lower the risk for developing DMJ.

【36】It is evident that through its ability to influence pancreatic beta-cell function and to regulate insulin secretion， production and sensitivity， vitamin D plays an important protective role in the prevention of DM. However， despite this fact， it is im-portant to be cognizant of the fact that DM is a multifactorial disease influenced by other factors such as the environment， genetics and lifestyle habits. Despite the wealth of knowledge that already supports a relationship between vitamin D and DM， additional high powered， larger multicentre studies with improved study designs are required to fully establish the role that vitamin D plays in the prevention， pathogenesis and treat-ment of this disease. In addition， further research is required to establish the dose of vitamin D required to produce protective effects in diabetic patients with minimal adverse reactions.
