【19】Herein， we have reported the first case of a dramatic response to T-DXd rechallenge in a patient with HER2-positive gastric cancer， with HER2 positivity being confirmed immediately be fore the rechallenge. This case suggested that re-biopsy imme-diately before the T-DXd rechallenge was important， and in the case of HER2 overexpression， T-DXd rechallenge was helpful.

【20】Some previous reports have indicated the loss of HER2 posi-tivity after initial trastuzumab-based chemotherapy； the T-ACT study， the most recent study in Japan， demonstrated that HER2positivity is maintained at only 31% after trastuzumab-based chemotherapy . This study also showed an associa-tion between trastuzumab-free intervals and the efficacy of trastuzumab beyond progression. The data suggest that HER2is re-expressed during trastuzumab-free chemotherapy. Three possible mechanisms underlie HER2 loss：  clonal selection， heterogeneity of HER2 expression， and  use of fixatives other than 10% neutral buffered formalin . Whether the loss of HER2 positivity occurred after T-DXd challenge remains unclear. In our case， although the expression of HER2 became weak after T-DXd challenge， the overexpression of HER2 was maintained.

【21】In the DESTINY-Gastric01 study， the overall response rate (ORR) for T-DXd in gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma with HER2 over-expression was significantly higher than that with chemother-apy (51.3% vs 14.3%， P<0.0001) . Explanatory analysis of the DESTINY-Gastric01 study showed that the ORR for T-DXd in gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma with low expression of HER2is 26.3% (for IHC 2+/ISH-negative) or 9.5% (for IHC 1+) . Another study demonstrated this efficacy， regardless of the time at which the HER2 status was tested (before trastuzum-ab vs after/during trastuzumab) . Furthermore， it includ-ed patients with 22 prior regimens， and a trastuzumab-free interval of several months was assumed. The HER2 status of almost all patients was considered positive， regardless of the time of biopsy in this study. As mentioned previously herein， the loss of HER2 occurred aftertrastuzumab treatment； there-fore， confirmation of HER2 overexpression would be impor-tant to maximize the efficacy of T-DXd.

【22】In gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma， biopsies are generally dif-ficult to perform for patients with recurrent cancer after resec-tion of the primary tumor. Anti-epidermal growth factor recep-tor (EGFR) antibodies are effective for patients RAS-wild-type colorectal cancer (CRC) but are ineffective for those with RAS-mutant CRC. Anti-EGFR therapy for RAS wild-type CRC induc-es resistance through acquired genomic alterations， especially through RAS mutations. The acquired RAS mutations can be detected by measuring circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)， and pa-tients without acquired RAS mutations might benefit from an-ti-EGFR antibody rechallenge. Acquired RAS mutations disap-pear with time after the withdrawal of anti-EGFR antibodies. By monitoring the RAS status using liquid biopsy，rechallenge with anti-EGFR antibodies can be considered for RAS wild-type tumors， assessed based on ctDNA. The CHRONOS trial showed the efficacy of ctDNA-driven rechallenge with anti-EGFR anti-bodies for CRC . In gastric and GEJ adenocarcinomas， re-biopsy is not a standard procedure. This suggests that moni-toring the HER2 status by biopsy from a primary tumor should be helpful for T-DXd rechallenge. Although liquid biopsy is eas-ier to perform， including in re-testing， the DESTINY-Gastric01study showed the efficacy of T-DXd regardless of the ERBB2plasma copy number in ctDNA . A predictive plasma mark-er that can be easily used to study gastric and GEJ adenocar-cinoma treated with T-DXd should be investigated.

【23】Recently， nivolumab and trifluridine/tipiracil have been ap-proved for the treatment of gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma. However， their response rate is only 4-11%， which is notably lower than that of T-DXd. The idea that the usefulness of T-DXd rechallenge can be determined by re-biopsy from the tumor and that the rechallenge would be meaningful if the tu-mor is HER2-positive could be of clinical importance.

【24】Conclusions

【25】We report the first case of response to T-DXd rechallenge in HER2-positive gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma. Rechallenge with T-DXd could be a treatment strategy worth considering for HER2-positive gastric cancer for cases in which the initial T-DXd treatment was effective. Confirmation of HER2 over-expression immediately before T-DXd rechallenge would be important， and re-biopsy could be a helpful and appropriate procedure for HER2-positive gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma before T-DXd rechallenge.

【0】Background：

【1】Intraoperative patellar tendon rupture is an uncommon and catastrophic complication. No detailed information exists on patellar tendon ruptures occurring intraoperatively during primary total knee prosthesis.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report 70-years-old patient with patellar tendon rupture during a total knee arthroplasty is presented. Also， simple， cheap and easy augmentation of the patellar tendon using a cerclage wire enabling an immediate mobilization is described.

【4】concluslons：

【5】The surgeon should avoid extreme forcing requiring for patellar eversion in stiff knees. However， patellar tendon rupture occurring intraoperatively despite all attempts to prevent it may be repaired readily， successfully and in a cheap way with a simple cerclage wire applied among primary repair without requiring any immobilization and all other techniques as well as without additional surgical experience or any complicated material.

【6】Key words： patellar tendon rupture · total knee arthroplasty· cerclage wlre

【7】Rupture of patellar tendon following total knee pros-thesis (TKP) is uncommon and usually occurs as a catastrophic complication. The incidence ofrupture of patellar tendon following TKP has been reported in the literature as 0.17% . No detailed informa-tion exists on patellar tendon ruptures occurring intraoperatively during TKP. This kind of complica-tions due to extensor mechanisms is mentioned to be associated rather with revision TKPs 

【8】Extensor mechanism in TKP is very important for postoperative rehabilitation of the patient. The pa-tients undergoing TKP should be allowed to move early in order to prevent occurrence of stiff knee and weakness of extensor mechanism after the operation. Unexpected rupture of patellar tendon and prima-ry repair without augmentation of this complication during TKP may lead to undesired complications such as occurrence of stiff knee and weakness of extensor mechanism as well as delay in rehabilitation. Thus， repair of patellar tendon rupture occurring during TKP should allow effective healing of the tendon as well as early movement of the knee with TKP by minimizing the risk ofre-rupture.

【9】Our aim in the current article is to report outcome of our patient who underwent patellar tendon augmenta-tion with cerclage wire in addition to primary repair being technically simple and cheap，requiring minimal additional operation time， not adversely influencing healing ofthe patellar tendon， allowing postoperative early rehabilitation and being performed for patellar tendon rupture occurring suddenly during operation. Literature was also reviewed in the current article.

【10】CASE REPORT

【11】A 70 years old patient presented to our hospital with pain on the left knee. On her physical examination， flexion contracture of 20 degrees was found on the left knee and there was varus deformity of about 15degrees. Range of motion was painful. Precipitation was felt on palpation. There was no varus or valgus instability. Medial space was seen to narrow on the knee radiogram. The patient was diagnosed as having advanced stage gonarthrosis and she was scheduled to TKP operation. She had no additional chronic conditions. The patient was admitted to clinic and informed on the operation and she gave informed consent for the operation.

【12】The patient was applied tourniquet and anterior midline incision was made after appropriate skin preparation had been made preoperatively in the operation room. Then， knee joint was entered through parapatellar approach. Difficulty was experienced in patellar eversion as the patient had a stiff knee. The patellar fat pad was removed to facilitate exploration. However， minimal patellar tendon damage occurring at this stage resulted in rupture through subpatellar region during eversion. The operation was continued from the point it interrupted following occurrence of rupture. Bone sections were made appropriately and the prosthesis (Biomet) intersecting the posterior oblique ligament was placed with cement.

【13】Following placement of the components， ruptured patellar tendon was primarily sutured according to Krackow technique with no： 5 ethibond suture. The patient underwent loop augmentation with cerclage wire through holes on the midpatellar and midtu-berositas sides in order to prevent occurrence of stiff knee and allow early movement postoperatively as well as for the possible risk of re-rupture due to early movement . No additional complication occurred intraoperatively.

【14】The patient was given full weight and began to move on the second postoperative day. Patient was dis-charged from the hospital on the 4th postoperative day. She was scheduled to monthly control visits. At the end of 6 months extension was full， flexion was 95degrees， the extensor mechanism was quite strong on the knee and the patient had apainless knee. At the end of 6 months， the wire was cut and removed by making mini-incisions under scopic guidance without entering the joint space . Following the removal of the wire， the patient was instructed to make isometric quadriceps exercise and then was discharged.

【15】DISCUSSION

【16】Patellar tendon rupture may develop spontaneously in the patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) as well as following injections of steroids. Cases have also been reported in the patients with metabolic diseases， repetitive micro-traumas， following realignment pro-cedures for distal patellar tendon and in those patients from whom bone-patellar， tendon-bone autografts for reconstruction of ACL .

【17】Although true incidence of patellar tendon ruptures following TKP operation due to rarity of this condi-tion， the incidence has been reported as 0.17%. No clear information， however， exists in the literature on the patellar tendon ruptures occurring intraopera-tively. This condition has usually been reported in the literature as in avulsion form in revision prosthesis surgery for the knee . Although several operative techniques and rehabilitation programs for patellar tendon rupture have been reported in the literature， there is not a“gold-standard”technique in the treat-ment of this condition.

【18】Operations defined in the literature for patellar tendon rupture occurring after TKP include ten-sion band wiring of the extensor mechanism ， bone-patellar tendon-bone allograft ， extensor mechanism allograft ， semi-tendinosus tendon auto graft ， the leeds-keio ligament lateral gastrocnemius muscle belly and achilles tendon and semitendinosus-gracilis with interference screw and staple fixation . These operations are especially for patellar tendon ruptures occurring postoperatively.

【19】Additionally， removing the flexors of the knee for reconstruction of intraoperative patellar tendon rupture reduces the flexor strength ； moreover， it is not easy to remove the tendons of semitendinosus or gracilis muscles in a knee in which the operation is being performed under tourniquet. Removal of these tendons may take a long time.

【20】Although successful results have been reported with reconstruction with allograft， it is difficult to obtain allograft in patellar tendon rupture developing sud-denly in the operation. Even though such allografts are obtained， its durability during the process of rehabilitation and healing of graft tissue take a long time. Furthermore； occurrence of gaps， graft rupture， separation of the graft from the suture side and oc-currence of fracture in the allograft have reported in the patients in whom allografts were used .

【21】Achilles tendon allograft has been advised rather as a salvage procedure in the patients who underwent multiple operations and it has problems in healing of allograft 

【22】All of these operations mentioned above are es-pecially for the patellar tendon rupture occurring postoperatively. Thus， they are operations requiring preparation. It may not be possible for every single surgeon to obtain allograft for intraoperative rupture in a patient undergoing operation for total primary knee operation.

【23】develop due to immobilization following TKP. And finally， early movement may protect the patellar length by eliminating stress that may develop on the patellar tendon during movement. Because it may cause development of premature tendon lengthening and patella alta .

【24】CONCLUSIONS

【25】The reason for that we augmented the primary re-pair with cerclage wire is that we desired to begin to move the patient immediately in the postoperative period and to minimize the risk of rerupture in the patellar tendon by giving most of the weight oc-curring during this movement onto the wire. Early movement following TKP is required mainly for three reasons. Firstly， early movement in the tendon that underwent repair may lead to more organized fibri-lar matrix formation by increasing collagen synthesis. Secondly， weakness of quadriceps muscle may In conclusion， intraoperative patellar tendon rupture is an uncommon complication. The surgeon should avoid extreme forcing requiring for patellar eversion in stiff knees. However， patellar tendon rupture oc-curring intraoperatively despite all attempts to pre-vent it may be repaired readily， successfully and in a cheap way with a simple cerclage wire applied among primary repair without requiring any immobilization and all other techniques as well as without additional surgical experience or any complicated material.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： The uterine cervix can be affected by conditions that are unusual. Diagnosis and management become challenging when the disease process and natural history are less well understood. Case series： We present three rare conditions affecting the cervix that caused significant morbidity in patients. Results： One patient had a huge necrosed cervical fibroid and underwent myomectomy followed by a hysterectomy. The second patient had a coexistent large Nabothian cyst with a large Gartner’s cyst. The third patient had metastatic cervical deposits of Phyllodes tumour. Conclusion： Detailed clinical examination， thorough imaging and management by experts can optimize outcomes.

【1】KEYWORDS Large cervical fibroid， Nabothian cyst with Gartner's cyst， Phylloides tumour， metastasis

【2】Introduction

【3】The uterine cervix is the narrowest part of the uterus. It is a small structure comprised of diverse cell types， like columnar epithe-lium lining the endocervix and squamous epithelium lining the ectocervix. Cervix is liable for several common diseases due to the location and cell types， like cervicitis， polyps， infections and cervical malignancy. However， many rare conditions of the cervix exist， which add to morbidity and mortality. The advantage of diagnosing cervical diseases is the relative ease of accessibility and the scope of direct visualization. Early clin-ical and histological diagnosis and appropriate treatment are， therefore， possible. However， when the clinical presentation is delayed， management becomes challenging due to various reasons. We present three rare cervical conditions that were clinically challenging with varying severity and outcomes.

【4】A 39year P3L3 presented to OPD with 3 months history of foul-smelling discharge and something coming out of the vagina with constipation for 1 week and dry cough for 2 days. She was migrant labour， thin built of seemingly poor nutrition. On examination， she was febrile (101°F) and tachycardic. The ab-domen was soft， no mass was felt. On local examination， a huge unhealthy mass of 40 x 30 cm with patchy necrosis areas was smeared with discharge.  It was a firm inconsistency. Per vaginal examination showed healthy labia and normal introi-tus. The broad stalk of the mass made per vaginal examination difficult. The cervix could not be well made out. Bilateral for-nices were free. Per rectal examination revealed an anal verge and canal closed by the mass by pressure effect. Rectum was loaded with stool. Ultrasonography showed a normal-sized uterus，normal tubes and ovaries， and a pulled down cervix and suggested that mass had originated from the matter of the cervix. CT suggested the same findings， and there was no evidence of distortion of ureters. She was posted for emergency excision. As there was uncertainty about the origin of the mass， exploratory laparotomy and total abdominal hysterectomy was done under continuous spinal-epidural anaesthesia. As Mackenrodt's lig-aments were divided， the vaginal mass shifted further down.

【5】First， the large necrosed part was divided at the narrowest part. Then， the uterus was pulled out through the vaginal vault with gentle downward traction. The mass was found to originate from the posterior cervical lip. No other abnormality was de-tected. Bilateral ureters were traced and were normal. Urine output was adequate and clear. The patient was discharged after10 days. Histopathology examination of all sections showed intersecting fascicles of monotonous spindles with indistinct borders， eosinophilic cytoplasm and nuclei with tapered ends and small nucleoli. There was no evidence of mitoses or atypia in any of the sections.

【6】Case 2

【7】A 23year old nullipara and her 25year old husband， married for10 months， came with complaints of coital difficulty. Neither of the partners had medical or surgical disorders.

【8】COn vaginal examination， a 5x6 cm pink cystic mass was seen occluding the cervix. The origin of the mass could not be made out. There was mild tenderness. Ultrasonography showed a cystic mass of 5.8x6.3cm of uncertain origin but abutted against the cervix's anterior aspect with septations and partially viscous content. Under spinal anaesthesia， the anterior cervical lip was held in the operation theatre. Two cysts were seen. The bladder was seen separate， and cystocele/fistula with bladder was ruled out by catheterisation. The first cyst， Gartner's cyst， accidentally ruptured and had clear viscous contents. The second cyst was a 3x4cm Nabothian cyst. Both cyst walls had flimsily adhered to each other.  Both cysts were excised from the base and sutured. Histopathology showed non-mucin secreting low columnar and cuboidal epithelial cells with neutrophilic inflam-matory infiltration characteristic of Gartner's cyst. The second cyst wall showed a single layer of columnar/Cuboidal epithe-lium without mitosis or atypia， suggestive of a Nabothian cyst.

【9】Case 3

【10】A 51year P3L3 woman was referred from medical oncology for a gynaecological opinion for suspicious lesions in the lower gen-ital tract on Computer Tomography. She had been admitted for chemo/radiotherapy for newly diagnosed metastatic lesions of bilateral Phylloides tumour in the breast that was operated 10years ago. The patient was frail had lost appetite and consider-able weight. On examination， the cervix looked pale and was nodular but mobile. Uterus was of normal size， anteverted and mobile. Parametrial induration was felt bilaterally. Per rectal examination showed an enlarged nodular posterior aspect of the cervix with parametrial hardening on both sides. The rectal mu-cosa was free. A biopsy was obtained. Histopathology showed malignant spindle cell neoplasm under ectocervical tissue.  CT showed multiple metastatic lesions in the lungs， liver and lower genital tract. The patient is on chemotherapy with Doxorubicin and Cisplatin at present

【11】Discussion

【12】Fibroids of the cervix comprise 2% of all fibroids. They can arise from any anatomical aspect of the cervix and can be inter-stitial， subserosal or submucosal. Fibroids growing too large sizes is uncommon. Large tumours can cause vaginal fullness， frequency of micturition， frequent urinary tract infections and constipation. Our patient had vaginal fullness and discomfort， and constipation for 10 days. Imaging must be detailed to look for the extent of disease to prevent neurovascular compromise at the surgery. Ureters are of particular concern. In a case re-port by B. Kavitha et al.， the authors describe the requirement of uretero ureteric anastomosis， bilateral ureteric stenting and bladder repair during the removal of large fibroid in their pa-tient. Surgery of a large cervical mass is dicey， and a planned myomectomy may sometimes get converted to an emergency hysterectomy. Expertise in pelvic anatomical distortion and experience are key factors in optimizing outcomes.

【13】Vaginal wall cysts are rare and arise from Mullerian rem-nants， epidermal remnants or Gartner’s duct.  They are usu-ally small but can grow into considerably large sizes on rare occasions， causing vaginal fullness， dyspareunia， discharge， uri-nary infection， and incontinence. Gartner's cyst (as was in our case number 2) arises from the anterolateral wall of the vagina. Surgical excision is the treatment of choice. Cyst marsupialisa-tion is another option. Nabothian cysts enlarge due to blocked os of the endocervical gland due to inflammation or squamous metaplasia . They rarely enlarge and do not usually require treatment. Simple excision and drainage with antibiotic therapy are likely to suffice in most patients. It is rare for a Gartner’s cyst to coexist with a Nabothian cyst， and our patient was one such case.

【14】Phyllodes tumour arises from fibroepithelial tissues and com-prises <1% of all breast neoplasms ， usually at 42 to 45 years. They present as breast masses of varying sizes. They exhibit biphasic growth patterns. They are usually benign， and surgical excision with a wide margin(>1cm) is the treatment of choice with a good prognosis. Malignancy is seen in about 20%. Metastasis is known to the brain， heart， pelvis ， thigh，and oral cavity. It carries a poor prognosis and survival of <2years. Chemotherapy with Doxorubicin and Cisplatin is practised， but the experience is limited to making recommendations. Radi-ation is a modality of palliation. Our patient was a rare case of metastatic disease whose primary was a Phylloides tumour that was excised a decade ago.

【15】Conclusion

【16】Cervix can be affected by unusual conditions. Many such condi-tions pose a clinical challenge due to distorted anatomy， limited space，and closely situated vital structures. However， not all con ditions are amenable to cure. Detailed workup and management by clinicians can help achieve the best outcomes.

【0】Background：

【1】Ischemic stroke can have a tremendously negative impact on the fitness and well-being of a child. Because endovascular interventions may be of benefit in the adult stroke population， many investigators have recently evaluated the safety and benefits of pharmacological and non-pharmacological options in the pediatric stroke population and compared pediatric patients to their adult counterparts. Some of these trials have had prom-ising results， showing the positive effects of endovascular treatment in children with arterial acute ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion (LVO). The 2015 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association guidelines suggest that mechanical thrombectomy with stent retrievers may be a consideration in some pa-tients who are younger than 18 years and have severe LVO， when treatment (groin puncture) is initiated with-in 6 h of symptom onset. However， the method remains under-studied in this age group.

【2】Case Report： A 7-year-old girl presented with migraine-like headache， right arm and facial weakness， and expressive apha-sia 9.5 h after symptom onset. Her PEDS-NIH stroke scale score was 4. Upon further investigations， she was found to have a left middle cerebral artery cryptogenic stroke with a distal left M1 clot， which was success-fully treated with mechanical thrombectomy. Huge improvement was noticed during her subsequent physical examination.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Endovascular therapy offers an exciting treatment option for the management of pediatric stroke. The extent of safety of mechanical thrombectomy among children who present with large-vessel occlusion over an ex-tended time window remains unknown and warrants further investigations.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Pediatrics ·Stroke · Thrombectomy

【6】Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in children is a rare medical condi-tion. Its diagnosis and treatment can be challenging because of the diverse range of risk factors leading to it and the lack of clear treatment guidelines for this age group. The presen-tation of ischemic stroke in pediatric patients can vary great-ly and differ according to the patient's age. For instance， chil-dren present with acute focal neurological deficits in up to94% of cases . However， they might also present with oth-er manifestations such as altered mental status (28% of cas-es)， headache (22%)， fever (35-40%)， or seizures (16%) . Mackay et al. confirmed that there are often multiple risk fac-tors of pediatric AIS， which appear to vary according to age and geography . However， the most important risk factors associated with childhood AlS seem to be non-atherosclerot-ic arteriopathies and cardiac disease， which was identified in almost one-third of patients . Other identified risk factors include previous varicella zoster infection， preceding trauma， recent infection， migraine， and anemia . As in adults， com-puted tomography (CT) in pediatric patients has low diagnostic accuracy for posterior circulation ischemic stroke (PCIS) diag-nosis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was often necessary to confirm the clinical suspicion of an acute cerebrovascular event， whereas CT could diagnose most anterior circulation ischemic stroke cases . Management of pediatric AlS is still lacking supportive clinical evidence， making the safety and ef-ficacy of acute pharmacological and non-pharmacological in-terventions of AlS a hot topic of research. The use of throm-bolytic therapy in the pediatric population is still controversial， and randomized controlled trials have been unsuccessful in investigating this treatment modality. However， some studies investigating thrombectomy in treating AlS among children revealed promising results， which are comparable to those of studies in the adult population.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 7-year-old left-handed girl presented with migraine-like headache， right arm weakness， right facial droop， and ex-pressive aphasia that began 9.5 h prior to presentation. Her PEDS-NIH stroke scale score was 4 (1 for smile asymmetry， 1for right upper extremity drift， 1 for right upper extremity sen-sory loss， and 1 for mild aphasia). An MRI of the head con-ducted 50 min after presentation revealed a diffusion-weight-ed imaging (DWI) hyperintensity in the left frontal operculum. Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) revealed severe ste-nosis of the left middle M1 segment and occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) inferior M2 branch . The ASPECTS-DWI score was 8. She immediately underwent me-chanical thrombectomy with a stent retriever . The pretreatment and posttreatment thrombolysis in cerebral in-farction scores were 0 and 2B， respectively， and door-to-groin puncture time was 90 min. The patient's 24-h and discharge PEDS-NIH stroke scale was 1， for mild aphasia only. The sub-sequent stroke workup was unremarkable and included an echocardiography with bubble study， lipid panel， hemoglobin Alc， lipoprotein A， hypercoagulable workup (cardiolipin an-tibody lgG and IgM， beta 2-glycoprotein 1 antibody lgG and IgM， lupus anticoagulant， protein S antigen， antithrombin ⅢII， factors 2 and 5 mutation analysis， and homocysteine)， serum inflammatory markers， infectious and metabolic studies (anti-nuclear antibody， myeloperoxidase antibody lgG， proteinase-3antibody lgG， SSB， SSA， C-reactive protein， sedimentation rate， HIV antigen and antibody， TSH， vitamin B12， peripheral blood smear， complete metabolic panel and complete blood count)， and CSF studies (protein level， cell count， glucose level， Gram stain， bacterial and fungal cultures， herpes simplex virus PCR， varicella zoster virus PCR， varicella zoster virus IgG， Lyme IgG antibody， angiotensin converting enzyme， oligoclonal bands， cytology， and flow cytometry). There was no hemorrhagic trans-formation apparent on MRI the day after the thrombectomy. The patient was discharged home on 81 mg of baby aspirin once daily. At the follow-up 3 months after discharge， she was back to her premorbid neurological baseline and the Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure score was 0. The patient underwent an MRI of the brain 6 months after discharge， which revealed stable sequelae of prior left MCA distribution infarct with mul-tifocal small old lacunar infarcts. There was no new or acute

【9】Discussion

【10】Most of the clinical care guidelines for pediatric stroke cas-es have been extrapolated from adult cases. In adults， time to restoration of blood flow in ischemic stroke is essential for better functional neurological outcomes . Therefore，admin-istration of recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator (r-tPA) to appropriate patients is currently the mainstay of acute medical aid in ischemic stroke patients within the adult popu-lation . However， thrombolytic therapy in pediatric patients is still controversial， and although efforts to study the safety of tPA in patients <18 years old in randomized controlled trials have been made， they have not identified the medical comor-bidities associated with pediatric stroke. The current medical views on the utilization of acute thrombolytic therapy depends on assessing the risk-benefit ratio of the treatment in each in-dividual case， balancing between no thrombolysis or consid-ering it if the only contraindication in the case is the patient's age . For stroke in adults， thrombectomy is indicated for AIS with LVO in acceptable clinical settings. Many random-ized controlled trials showed a high level of safety， improved functional outcomes， and extended time from symptom onset(in the DEFUSE 3 trial，6-16 h and in the DAWN trial， 6-24h) when thrombectomy was conducted in an appropriate clinical context and done in patients with LVO in the anterior circula-tion within 6 h of symptom onset .

【11】Many trials were conducted to study treatment options in pe-diatric stroke cases. Some showed the success of endovascu-lar treatment in children with arterial AlS due to LVO. In the retrospective Save ChildS trial， conducted from 2000 to 2018， researchers found that 87% of the enrolled children (<18 years of age) who underwent endovascular thrombectomy had suc-cessful recanalization . The median time from appearance of first clinical to recanalization therapy was 4 h； however， some cases were treated outside the 6-h window. This results of this trial suggested that the neurologic outcomes of chil-dren with AIS were largely positive， promising， and compara-ble with those noted in adult thrombectomy trials. Bigi et al. studied a cohort of 150 patients with AlS， who all presented with PEDS-NIH score of at least 4 and were aged <16 years. Sixteen patients received pharmacological management with thrombolytics and another 6 patients underwent mechanical thrombectomy. One patient was treated with thrombectomy only. All but 1 patient were diagnosed within a 12-h interval after symptom onset； however， 4 patients were treated more than 6 h after their symptoms appeared， which is similar to our patient. Treatment results at follow-up showed complete recanalization in 4 patients， partial recanalization in 6 patients， and no changes in 4 patients. The authors concluded that re-canalization treatment is possible and seems to be safe in se-verely affected pediatric patients with AlS and complications did not happen more frequently in patients who received re-canalization treatment .

【12】In a comprehensive review of the literature， Satti et al. de-scribed 29 case reports of recanalization in pediatric AIS cas-es . Time to recanalization treatment ranged from1.5 to 120 h. Excluding 3 patients with an unknown time to recanalization treatment and another 3 patients who were treat-ed beyond 24 h， the average time to recanalization treatment was 8.8 h. A total of 75.9% of the patients attained recanali-zation. Clinical outcomes were reported in 23 patients， with86.7% of patients achieving a good clinical outcome . The2015 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association guidelines on this topic declared that endovascular thrombec-tomy might be clinically of great value in children <18 years of age using adult parameters .

【13】Conclusions

【14】The safety of and clinical improvement from mechanical throm-bectomy in children with large-vessel occlusion over an ex-tended time period after symptom onset remains unknown. Although endovascular therapy offers an exciting and prom-ising method in the management of pediatric stroke cases， further research is needed to determine the clinical and tech-nical parameters for the successful use of this treatment in children with LVO.

【0】ABSTRACT Adherence to ethical principles is essential nowadays in neurology and neuroscience research. Although there are certain generally valid ethical principles for all medical domains， stated and regularly updated in works such as the Declaration of Helsinki or Beauchamp and Childress’s book "Principles of Biomedical Ethics"， the complexity of neurology leads to particular ethical issues that both the clinician and the researcher may face.

【1】While there are many ethical controversies， this article aims to explore four essential topics： ethical dilemmas in neurodegenerative diseases with a focus on amyotrophic lateral sclerosis， particularities in neuroscience research on a human subject， informed consent， and ethics in vascular neurology with emphasis on stroke. We searched Pubmed， Science Direct， and Google Scholar during March and April 2020. We retrieved the articles published during the last ten years， screened them， and selected the most relevant.

【2】We have shown that neurodegenerative pathologies pose a lot of potential ethical problems， beginning with the planning of a new clinical trial. Violations of ethical norms take place in both bedside medicine and clinical research， as nowadays neurologists are increasingly under the pressure of capitalist society. Informed consent is the third topic addressed， with a focus on particular aspects of decision-making capacity in neurological patients. At last， ethical issues in vascular neurology are presented， an intensively studied neurology subdomain with numerous improvements in recent years that still raises countless ethical issues.

【3】Introduction

【4】Observance of ethical principles is essential in the case of neu-rology and neuroscience research， as it is in all the other medical and surgical fields. Moreover， given the effervescence of re-search in recent years， there is a growing emphasis on the correct conduct of clinical trials and patient follow-up during and after participation in pharmacological studies .

【5】There are generally valid and applicable conventions for re-search on a human subject， which must also be respected in neurological research. These ethical principles were established in the 70s and 80s， being subsequently reviewed and supple-mented periodically to ensure patient safety， while being in line with the basic principle of medicine： primum non-nocere. The principles stated in the "Declaration of Helsinki"  and the ethical references promulgated by Beauchamp and Childress in their book "Principles of Biomedical Ethics" are cornerstones for current neurological practice .

【6】For a better understanding of the particular ethical issues that arise in neurology (both clinical practice and research)， the essential elements of bioethics will be briefly presented first.

【7】The central dogma of medical ethics refers to the following five essential principles： justice， benevolence， non-harm，main-taining the professional patient-doctor relationship and respect for autonomy. These principles will be applied in this order， the simultaneous respecting of them being mandatory . The questions asked to assess whether new studies maintain compli-ance with ethical principles remains the same for neurological clinical trials. For example， when determining if justice principle is not violated， the researcher must answer the following ques-tions before even starting the trial： what is the scientific element underlying the research， what is the question to be researched and is it worth asking， what type of clinical study is best suited to answer this question， what subjects do we include in the study and what are our inclusion criteria . However， even if the questions are similar in the case of neuroscience studies (a natural aspect given that ethical principles are universal for all biological sciences)， the answers that neurologists must give are not always easy.

【8】Materials and Methods

【9】This review aimed to highlight the particular ethical problems that can be encountered in neurology and neuroscience research， especially research on human subject. For this reason， literature was consulted in search of the most relevant questions on the topic at present. Because of space and time limitations， only four major subjects were taken into consideration： ethical dilem-mas in neurodegenerative diseases with a focus on amyotrophic lateral sclerosis， particularities in neuroscience research on a human subject， informed consent， and ethics in vascular neu-rology with emphasis on stroke (from hyperacute phase until rehabilitation).

【10】To identify relevant studies on these topics， a search was conducted using three electronic databases： PubMed， Science Direct and Google Scholar during March and April 2020. Key-words such as "ethical issues in neurology"，"neurodegenerative diseases"， "ethics in research on the human subject"， "inform consent"， "ethics in vascular neurology" were used， limiting our search to English language articles published during the last ten years. The most relevant articles per research topic were selected， data being analyzed， and the main conclusions extracted and compared to other related opinions from the literature.

【11】Discussion

【12】A first important aspect in neurological pathology is the pro-gressive nature of neurodegenerative diseases that inevitably lead to death， current research focusing on finding ways to slow down or even stop neuronal degeneration in order to prolong life. To demonstrate the ethical dilemmas， researchers may face when conducting studies on degenerative diseases，amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) will be taken as an example.

【13】ALS is a degenerative pathology of the central and peripheral motor neuron， with a rapidly progressive evolution of 2-5 years from the onset of the first symptoms (fasciculations， asthenia， muscle cramps and atrophies) inevitably resulting in death， so far without satisfactory， curative treatment J.

【14】Given the importance and severity of the pathology， more than 50 clinical trials have been conducted so far in which re-searchers have tested various drugs or more invasive proce-dures in order to prolong the life of patients who have ALS. It should be noted that among the numerous attempts， only Riluzole showed a modest benefit， prolonging survival by 3-6 months. Another example would be Edaravone， which has been approved and is used in Japan and the USA， but not in Europe， the results being inconclusive so far . Among the new therapies， stem cell therapy looks promising .

【15】Patients with ALS， having a reserved prognosis at the time of diagnosis， are vulnerable when it comes to participating in clinical trials. They will more readily accept a new treatment， despite possible essential side effects， as long as there is the hope of prolonging survival and raise the quality of life . That is why it is mandatory to maintain the doctor-patient relationship as professional as possible in which the doctor provides com-plete and correct information regarding the benefits and risks of a new therapy .

【16】This potential aspect of violation of ethical norms is not sin-gular， according to  there are five critical points where ethical behaviour can be easily breached . On the one hand， researchers and neurologists directly involved in clinical trials may have material or non-material benefits，forcing them to apply treatments known not to significantly improve the pa-tient's quality of life just for the sake of science. Moreover， there is always a bias when trying to assess positive results， exagger-ated optimism and a penchant for conducting clinical trials to confirm the healing abilities of a new drug， without considering other aspects such as side effects or other possible complications that may occur simultaneously with the new therapy. Some-times， studies only focus on prolonging the life span， without raising the issue of the patient quality of life during the final months/year of living. At the same time， given the difficult situation in the case of patients with ALS (few subjects， usually diagnosed in an advanced stage of the disease， with only one drug approved in Europe) the design of a control group or a placebo medication becomes a challenge that prevents studies from having a large number of participants and from meeting scientific and bioethical rigours . Another important point concerns the publishing process， fraudulent practices existing from the exposure of results (data fabrication) to selection and acceptance for publication (e.g. pirate journals)， an increasingly thorny issue in today's society where publishing innovative results has become almost a necessity for the researcher (job retention， career advancement) .

【17】On the other hand， it is necessary to mention the existence of incomplete information regarding the pathophysiology of neu-rodegenerative diseases， the absence of clear target molecules to explain the neuronal alterations present so that most pharmaco-1nci logical studies are simple attempts to match either new or taken from other therapies. Medical branches (eg immunosuppressive therapies used successfully in rheumatology)， without always correlating with the intrinsic mechanism of the disease .

【18】Another component with an impact on the ethics and profes-sionalism of the neurologist researcher is the commercial side of medicine， which is becoming increasingly important nowadays. As highlighted by ， the most acute ethical issues in neurology occur in the clinical context， in 。bedside medicine"： the difficult standards of public and private health care systems， conflict of interest， loss of healer role of the doctor and his transformation into an employee， the existence of quality indicators created on a purely theoretical basis without being able to be fulfilled in the concrete medical world， dilemmas on patient autonomy and new legal regularizations in this regard that can sometimes contradict World Health Organisation's ethi-cal principles . However， scientific research is not immune to this threat either. The current capitalistic society has favoured the transformation of the medical act into service， in the con-text in which hospitals and doctors become business models with employees who must give maximum efficiency while run-ning on lowest possible costs. In both clinical and fundamental research， the enormous pressure put on the discovery of inno-vative treatments that prolong life and restore the quality of life can push the researcher to violate ethical norms in the desire to produce spectacular results .

【19】Unlike other medical fields， research in neurology has a sig-nificant risk of violating ethical norms in the context of financial incentives . As  noted， two main causes favour the creation of conflicts of interest. First，the incidence and preva-lence of neurological diseases are high， these pathologies having high morbidity and mortality . From an economic point of view， on the one hand， it is in the interest of governments to find solutions for the rehabilitation and social reintegration and/or reemployment of the affected people， on the other hand， there is an extremely profitable market for pharmaceutics， in which criti-cal economic players are interested for more or less significant benefits .

【20】Another factor that pushes much research to the limit of com-pliance with ethical principles is precisely the nature of neurolog-ical diseases， in which the exact mechanism of production and a pathophysiological cascade of neurodegeneration and neuro-plasticity is not known. Thus， there is a risk of testing many sub-stances (some with effects in other medical pathologies) based on simple assumptions of pharmacological mechanisms that could work in neurological diseases . The risk/benefit ra-tio remains of maximum interest for medical ethics， and the researcher must first minimize the risks and then to think about the potential benefits of his work. Here appears another critical point where the principles of ethics and good practice can be violated， in the desire to accumulate new theoretical elements related to neurological diseases .

【21】An example of the difficulties encountered by researchers in neuroscience refers to the validation of new therapeutic tech-niques in Parkinson’s disease . Along with drug therapy that inevitably loses its effectiveness with the evolution of the disease， other more invasive methods (e.g.gene therapy) seem to offer solutions to slow the neurodegeneration of the substan-tia nigra and improve symptoms. The transfer of nucleic acids in gene therapy involves an invasive method， affecting the in-tegrity of the skull and the structures that protect the central nervous system . This raises various issues regarding the creation of the control group and how to administer the placebo substance： how to choose the control group? how to perform the neurosurgical intervention in the control group? (what is the risk/benefit ratio for a simple trepanation vs dura mater dis-continuation vs complete surgery)， is it necessary to introduce a placebo in the basal ganglia and substance is best to use?， is a direct transition from animal (mouse) to human model correct in the case of this large-scale surgery.

【22】Thus， the difficulty of conducting a clinical trial in these cir-cumstances is observed. Even if the benefits far outweigh the possible risks in the patient group， the same cannot be said in the control group， where the only intra- and peri-interventional risks can lead to the patient’s refusal to participate in the study， dyskinesias and non-motor symptoms. Being easier to bear than a potential postinterventional hemiparesis . Assuming， however， that all these obstacles have been successfully over-come， there is a danger of demonstrating the beneficial effects of placebo treatment， which requires a reassessment of the real benefits of the desired medication to be tested， but also of all other drug and interventional therapies already existing on the market. The design of research studies in neuroscience brings additional， complex ethical challenges， which are not currently clearly regulated by the methodology of medical ethics， medi-cal ethics must take new elements from other social sciences in order to ensure reliable and safe research for the patient .

【23】Another circumstance that may generate ethical issues en-countered in medicine and research nowadays is the informed consent of the patient or participant in the clinical trial .

【24】According to Emanuel et al.， three conditions must be ful-filled simultaneously for the research to take place in ethical conditions： the patient to be informed (verbally or written) as completely as possible about the reason， method， benefit， risks and alternatives of the research； the person's decision-making capacity to be intact； the decision to participate to be voluntary， without any constraints . These principles are also valid in the case of neuroscience research， the difficulties that arise mainly related to the decision-making capacity of the patient suffering from a neurological pathology .

【25】Nora， 2013 described decision-making capacity as having two main components， a legal and a medical one . From the legal point of view， adult patients have intact decision-making capacity as long as it has not been restricted following a court decision. The same is not true of minors， who， with a few ex-ceptions， cannot make medical decisions alone. The medical component， on the other hand， is a medical conclusion drawn by the neurologist， which varies depending on various factors：age， certain pathologies， medication .

【26】Given the impossibility of establishing definite boundaries related to decision-making capacity， many authors have been concerned with this topic， proof being the myriad of publications in recent years. Having diverse methodologies and conclusions， there are many aspects to be taken into consideration； this article only briefly resuming some of the most worthy elements when it comes to the neurological patient.

【27】Among neurological diseases， Alzheimer’s disease (AD) was the most studied pathology regarding informed consent issue， with fewer studies existing on the same topic for patients with Parkinson's disease (PD).

【28】In AD， the decision-making capacity is severely affected， since the early stages of the disease， the affected person hav-ing difficulties in understanding， appreciation and argumenta-tion. There was a direct relationship between impaired cognition(dementia) and decision-making ability， early training of other intellectual functions can also improve the ability to make deci-sions. On the other hand， if a low score is obtained following the empirical validation of decision-making capacity， it does not mean that the person is incapable of making decisions， new more valid methods being urgently needed .

【29】In the case of PD patients， the situation is different， as evi-denced by a study conducted by Karlawish et al. In that study， PD patients were divided into three subgroups (normal， border-line， and impaired) based on the scores obtained on the Mattis Dementia Rating Scale. Regarding the patients in the normal sub-group， 17% were found unable to give their informed consent， while in about 50% of PD patients in the borderline subgroup the lack of decision-making power was detected . It was shown that the main cause would be the patient’s misunderstanding of information， not only abolition of the memorization function， but also a difficulty in retrieving already known information and recall. These results confirm the results obtained by Martin et al. in another study on the ability to consent in patients with PD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI)， which have deficiencies especially in terms of appreciative abilities. However， it should not be forgotten that in PD， the cognitive component is affected during the late stages of the disease， the motor symptoms be-ing primarily problematic for the patient . In the absence of a person's competence to make an informed decision， legal representatives (surrogates) will be called upon (based on legal documents and laws in force at the national level， different from country to country) to make decisions on behalf of the patient. These documents allow competent patients to identify a surrogate for when they have lost competence； relatives will thus have the right to express their treatment preferences on behalf of the patient. Even so， all actions and decisions of the legal partner will respect the justice and best interest standard principles .

【30】The most common neurological disease in Romania， stroke， can pose ethical problems in all therapeutic phases， from the hyperacute stage to the rehabilitative and secondary prevention phase. As stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide， with a growing incidence， causing significant disabilities for sur-vivors， new methods of prevention and treatment have emerged in recent years J. All techniques and therapies，although cre-ated in order to reduce the time of ischemia and save as much brain tissue as possible ("time is brain" principle)， however raise many ethical issues .

【31】Acute management of ischemic stroke has known a real im-provement following the introduction of thrombolysis as stan-dard therapy. However， there are still emergency departments(ED) in small hospitals that do not benefit from 24/7 neurologic care. Thus， in case of the arrival of a patient who meets reperfu-sion therapy criteria， neurological advice could be obtained via telephone consultation. The situation， although with obvious short and long term benefits for the patient， raises the following ethical issues. First， is the neurologist required to provide thera-peutic advice over the phone? Strict criteria for the application of thrombolytic therapy and the high risk of bleeding (including intracranial haemorrhage) in some cases， should not be forgotten. Then， other factors must be considered in achieving the most beneficial treatment for the patient， from a rigorous exami-nation of the emergency physician， communication of all data of interest to the neurologist， the manner and validity of informed consent attesting to the patient's acceptance for thrombolysis and， in finally， the possibilities of fibrinolytic and subsequent supportive treatment (in case of cardiovascular decompensation) of the unit in question.

【32】Also in the hyperacute situation in the case of a stroke， there is the ethical issue of the informed consent of the patient (if he is conscious) or of the legal surrogate， when the patient is unable to make decisions， aspect already discussed above.

【33】After the first hours (hyperacute phase)， another critical pe-riod for the patient follows， lasting up to 30 days， in which the risk of death is highest . Especially in severe cases (massive hemorrhagic stroke， or ischemic stroke with ICP syndrome that requires decompression through craniectomy)， we notice an in-crease in the hospitalization time and a need for vital support(mechanical ventilation， nasogastric tube feeding). Numerous scales have been designed to assess mortality and quality of life after stroke， with the neurologist having to make predictions in such cases regarding the maintenance or removal of life sup port， as well as attempting more invasive life-saving treatments(neurosurgery cranial decompression). As in all clinical trials， there must be some moderation in this case， given the existence of bias errors that may occur . Extreme attitudes such as aggressive and early application of invasive measures that may subsequently have irreparable adverse effects should be avoided， but also limitation of supportive treatment in some cases where， based on unreliable assessment scales， there is a small chance of survival. The general opinion remains that the prognosis should not be made in the acute period of a stroke， despite questions from the patient or his family， the chronic rehabilitation period being the one that will determine the degree of recovery of lost runctions.

【34】Survival after a stroke involves a mandatory period of neu-rological rehabilitation when the patient， through sustained ex-ercises， regains to a greater or lesser extent the capabilities lost in the acute event (improvement of the motor deficit， aphasia). A common and topical issue， as noted by Wheeler et al.， is the assessment by the neurologist of the driving ability of vehicles. The act of driving a vehicle involves， in addition to having intact visual functions and coordination， many fine components related to attention， perception， execution and language that are affected by a stroke . Moreover， these minor deficiencies can escape the neurologist even after a detailed clinical examination. The position of the clinician is firm in these cases， and the patient no longer has the right to drive vehicles. However， given the need for driving nowadays， many patients do not immediately comply with this recommendation. There is the difficulty for the clinician， who， on the one hand， must maintain the confi-dentiality of the patient’s data， on the other hand， has the moral duty to convince the family and， in case of failure， to notify the authorities about the dangerous behaviour of the patient . This ethical issue is under scrutiny in the United States， where six states require the neurologist by federal laws to declare to authorities if patients are unable to drive. In contrast， in other states， neurologists are encouraged to inform authorities about the inappropriate driving behaviour of the patients they have under observation .

【35】Conclusion

【36】These are just some of the particular situations in neurology and neuroscience research when ethical issues arise， directly concern-ing the neurologist. Of course， with the new research in the field， with the emergence of modern treatments， ethical issues will become more and more frequent . It is therefore essential to develop bioethics and encourage discoveries in neuroscience to firmly respect the ethical principles available at the time of their publication.

【37】Limitations of this study

【38】Although this study reviews thoroughly four important bioethi-cal issues of current neurology and neuroscience research， other aspects such as brain death or ethics in pediatric neurology re-main to be discussed in a future article. Moreover， the author assumes that only articles in the English language from the last ten years have been researched， the omission of some data being possible， as the literature is too extensive to be reviewed in a single article.

【0】Background：

【1】Vascular anomalies of the carotid vessels can be attributed to false embryogenesis. A rare variant called a non-bifurcating carotid artery (NBCA) exists， where typical carotid bifurcation is not recognizable with its typical branches of the external carotid artery (ECA) and internal carotid artery (ICA). This paper describes a case of this anomaly and reviews the embryogenesis of the carotid arteries for explanation.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 66-year-old man received a routine health examination at our hospital. Initial carotid ultrasound indicated an absence of bifurcation in the right cervical carotid artery， and magnetic resonance imaging of the brain in-dicated an absence of the proximal cervical segment of the right ICA， with a remnant arterial stump at the ex-pected bifurcation level. No evidence of the carotid bulb was identified. The common carotid artery seemed to continue cranially in the trunk of the ECA， where it exhibited extracranial branches. After distributing these branches， the carotid artery coursed medially at the C2 level， where it ascended into the carotid canal to be-come the petrosal segment ofthe ICA. This carotid anomaly was labelled an NBCA. No aberrant intracranial ar-teries were derived from the NBCA in this case.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】In this case， the arterial stump was considered a remnant from agenesis of the right ICA. We assumed that the NBCA most likely developed because of false regression of the third embryogenic aortic arch with persistence of the second aortic arch.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Cardiovascular System · Carotid Arteries ·Embryology

【7】Carotid ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are2 commonly used noninvasive techniques for evaluating the carotid vessels. With the growing popularity of these tools in general health examinations， increasingly more anomalies of the common carotid artery (CCA) are being discovered. Among them， a rare anomaly exists in which the carotid bifurcation is indistinguishable from its typical branches of the external ca-rotid artery (ECA) and internal carotid artery (ICA). This anom-aly is referred to as a nonbifurcating carotid artery (NBCA) and was first proposed by Marimoto et al. in 1990 . In a retro-spective cohort study conducted in Japan， the estimated inci-dence of NBCAs was 0.21%， which was almost identical to the reported 0.2% incidence of persistent trigeminal arteries . In an NBCA， the carotid bulb is absent in the cervical segment； this is suggestive of proximal ICA agenesis. This paper describes a case of an NBCA and explains its possible embryogenesis.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 66-year-old man with hypertension and dyslipidemia under medical control underwent imaging studies during a health exam-ination at our hospital. A carotid ultrasound indicated an abrupt blockade of the right proximal ICA with a small residual arteri-al stump at the bifurcation. Neither atherosclerotic plaque nor turbulent flow was discovered in the vascular lumen . Therefore， the patient underwent brain MRI for the suspicious total occlusion of the right ICA. Magnetic resonance angiography(MRA) revealed that the right CCA was considerably enlarged at the C4 to C5 level to a size equivalent to that of the left carotid bulb， but did not taper 1-2 cm distally， as a healthy carotid bulb would. Moreover， no typical carotid bifurcation was present -only an arterial stump originating from the medial aspect of the right CCA . The right CCA continued in the trunk with 3major extracranial branches： the common trunk of the superior thyroid artery and facial artery， the occipital artery， and the com-mon trunk of the internal maxillary artery and posterior auricu-lar artery. After distribution from the extracranial branches，the right CCA coursed medially at the C2 level to enter the right ca-rotid canal， where it became the petrosal segment of the right ICA. The intracranial course of the right ICA was typical，and the left ECA， ICA， and vertebral artery (VA) were typical in appear-ance. The right VA was atrophic and the left VA was dominant in the posterior cerebral circulation. Diffusion-weighted imaging and brain perfusion imaging produced unremarkable findings.

【10】Discussion

【11】The embryogenesis of vascular systems in the head and neck is complicated. Early in the third gestational week， the cervical aortic primitives run in pairs as dorsal and ventral aortic roots. Six primitive aortic arches connect the dorsal and ventral aor-tic roots， and 6 intersegmental arteries run laterally from the dorsal aortic roots. The ventral aortic roots cranial to the third aortic arch become the ventral pharyngeal artery. The ven-tral second aortic arch eventually regresses. The dorsal sec-ond aortic arch becomes the hyoid artery and stapedial artery. The stapedial artery connects the ventral pharyngeal artery and separates from the hyoid artery at the 24-mm embryonic stage (approximately the seventh gestational week). The ECA develops from the combination of the ventral pharyngeal ar-tery and stapedial artery. The ICA derives from the third aortic arch and the dorsal aortic roots cranial to the third aortic arch.

【12】The CCA evolves from the fusion of the ventral pharyngeal ar-tery and ventral third aortic arch. The VA develops from the transverse anastomoses between the cervical intersegmental arteries . In our case， the embryogenesis of the left carot-id artery followed the typical development process .

【13】We hypothesized that the right NBCA coursed in the trunk of the proximal ECA and then turned medially at the C2 level to become the petrosal segment of the ICA. Our imaging findings supported this hypothesis. First， the carotid bulb was absent in the right NBCA， and thus it was unlikely that the right CCA coursed cranially in the trunk of the ICA， which usually forms a bulb in the proximal segment. Second， almost all extracra-nial branches， which are the branches of the ECA under typ-ical conditions， could be identified in the NBCA in our case. Third， the NBCA coursed with a great tortuosity at the C2 lev-el； this evidenced the anastomosis between the ECA and ICA.

【14】Therefore， we ascertained that the NBCA coursed cranially in the trunk of the ECA with an anastomosis with the ICA at the C2 level. Moreover， 3 extracranial branches derived from the stapedial artery were identifiable： the distal internal maxillary artery， the posterior auricular artery， and the occipital artery. Because the stapedial artery originated from the dorsal sec-ond aortic arch， we deduced that the second aortic arch per-sisted as a connection between the ventral and dorsal aortic roots. The dorsal third aortic arch regressed， thereby causing the ventral third aortic arch to become an arterial stump in the NBCA .

【15】Our case shared 2 common features identified in most pub-lished studies regarding agenesis of the proximal ICA. First， nearly all extracranial branches of the NBCA indicate identical courses to the healthy branches derived from the ventral pha-ryngeal artery and stapedial artery， which are the primitives of
