【13】He was subsequently re-admitted with ascites re-accumula-tion， worsening kidney function， and deranged LFTs . Repeat serology for hepatitis B/C virus and chronic liver dis-ease screening were negative. During this admission， he had recurrent episodes of lower-Gl bleeding associated with he-moglobin drop and hemodynamic instability. He had 3 further CT abdominal angiograms， all of which showed persisting con-trast enhancement around the graft pancreas but no evidence of local intraluminal hemorrhage. He had 2 further upper-GI endoscopies， with no evidence of active upper-gastrointestinal source of bleeding apart from moderate antral-predominant gas-tritis (although a biopsy was normal). LFTs subsequently nor-malized except for serum albumin (31 g/L) and the ascites re solved spontaneously. He also underwent 2 colonoscopies and both were unrevealing. He received a total of 13 units of PRBC，2 units of fresh frozen plasma， 2 pools of platelets， and 1 unit of cryoprecipitate. The patient then developed an acute coro-nary syndrome. As he continued to have lower-Gl bleeding， a further CTAP was performed， in which the areas of small-bowel varices related to the anastomosis between the transplant duo-denum and the recipient jejunum  were thought likely to be the source of recurrent hemorrhage. Endovascular obliteration of these varices was recommended. Retrospective review of previous imaging demonstrated subtle but present features of ectopic varices around the transplant duodenum， previously described as "hyperenhancement of the pancreas".

【14】Portal venography was performed via a percutaneous transhe-patic approach， which demonstrated retrograde flow within a dilated jejunal vein  communicating with the graft duodenal vein via multiple trans-anastomotic varices and drain-ing through the graft portal vein into the recipient left exter-nal iliac vein . These varices were selectively cathe-terized and were embolized with a total of 3 mL of 3% sodium tetradecyl sulphate (STD). A final portography confirmed com-plete occlusion of the varices with obliteration of the porto-systemic shunt and preserved antegrade flow in the superior mesenteric and main portal vein . Ascites increased after the procedure and 3.125 mg carvedilol was commenced. A trans-jugular liver biopsy and hepatic portal venous gradi-ent measurement were deferred due to clinical instability of the patient. The patient remained well， with no episodes of GI bleeding post-embolization； however， he then had a sec-ond acute coronary event leading to cardiac arrest with conse-quent irreversible hypoxic brain injury and he ultimately died.

【15】Discussion

【16】Arterial complications after pancreas transplantation can cause massive life-threatening GIB. Ectopic variceal bleed-ing due to porto-systemic trans-anastomotic varices between the transplant duodenum and recipient small bowel is a rare cause of GIB， with only 2 cases reported in the literature . Fontana et al.  described peri-transplant duodenal varices in a patient after kidney-pancreas transplant in the setting of por-tal hypertension， who was treated successfully with coil embo-lization followed by liver transplantation. Rostambegi et al.  reported a similar patient in whom variceal embolization was performed but who subsequently required surgical resection of the involved segment of bowel due to recurrent bleeding.

【17】The authors of the report  did not measure portal vein pres-sure but concluded that portal hypertension was not present despite the presence of the trans-anastomotic varices.

【18】Porto-systemic varices develop in portal hypertension (PHT) and are most commonly gastro-oesophageal. Ectopic varices are much less common but are known to develop across bowel anastomoses that allow porto-systemic communication； a typ-ical example is those that occur around a stoma where portal venous branches develop communications with abdominal wall veins. Such varices， which are neo-vessels rather than enlarge-ment of pre-existing porto-systemic communications as is the case with gastro-esophageal varices， are very friable and are par-ticularly prone to hemorrhage， which can be massive. The inci-dence of ectopic variceal bleed is 1% to 5% in cirrhosis， 27% to40% in extrahepatic portal hypertension， and up to 64% in co-existing portal venous occlusion and hepatobiliary surgery .

【19】The rarity of peri-transplant ectopic varices could have contrib-uted to the delay in radiological diagnosis given the variability of the location of the transplant-to-recipient bowel anastomo-sis， and typical appearances are not obvious on CT angiogra-phy. Ectopic varices can be very difficult to manage. Both en-doscopic and interventional radiological techniques may be helpful， although surgery may be necessary in some cases. Endoscopic access to ectopic varices depends on the location of the porto-systemic anastomosis， and in our patient's situa-tion would have been difficult to access (apart from an entero-scope or a capsule endoscope) for diagnosis. Emergency surgery in the form of transplant pancreatectomy is possible，although the morbidity rate is high. In the patient reported here， surgi-cal options were kept as a last resort， given his co-morbidities and the desire not to explant a functioning pancreas allograft.

【20】The underlying etiology of portal hypertension in this case was not established，although there were multiple putative risk fac-tors. Amoxycillin-clavulanic acid-induced liver injury is a pos-sible cause， as this agent is known to cause varying degrees of hepatic dysfunction， with cases of acute liver failure and chronic liver disease being described . Other etiologies that should be considered are idiopathic non-cirrhotic portal hyper-tension or chronic hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection. Hepatitis E infection is becoming more common and infection with type-3genotype can progress to chronic infection， leading to cirrho-sis and liver failure in solid-organ transplant recipients .

【21】Bleeding from ectopic varices around the pancreas transplant remain the most likely cause， as there were no typical varices in the oesophagus or rectum， and there was complete reso-lution of symptoms following radiological embolization ofthe varices. Unfortunately， due to the subsequent cardiac events that led to the death of the patient， establishing a pathologi-cal diagnosis was not possible.

【22】Conclusions

【23】This case report adds to the scarce literature on the manage-ment of ectopic variceal bleeding in pancreas transplant recip-ients， describing a novel minimally-interventional technique to obtain source control. Diagnosis can be very difficult， particu-larly as other signs of portal hypertension may be lacking， as was the case in the patient reported here. Management should be tailored to the patient's clinical state， the severity of hem-orrhage， and availability of appropriate expertise.

【0】Background：

【1】Patients with HIV infection tend to have poor intensive care unit (ICU) outcomes； however， survival in the mod-ern combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) era has markedly improved， but Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumo-nia (PJP) still remains a preeminent cause of respiratory failure in AIDS patients.

【2】Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an adapted cardiopulmonary bypass circuit for temporary life support for patients not responding to conventional treatment.

【3】Case Report： A 43-year-old male HIV "late presenter" was admitted to our hospital for fever and dyspnea. A chest CT scan revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities. Empiric antibiotic treatment and cART were started. The emergence of ARDS due to PJP dictated urgent veno-venous (VV) ECMO placement. One week later， radiologic findings and respiratory function had improved and the patient was started on a weaning trial from ECMO and removed 12days after placement.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a potentially reversible clinical syndrome with a high mortality rate. ECMO is a rescue therapy allowing lung recovery during acute processes and should be considered an adequate treatment option in HIV+ patients with respiratory failure. ECMO should be considered a useful and adequate treatment option in AIDS patients who have a high risk of dying from respiratory failure.

【6】MeSH Keywords：

【7】AIDS-Related Opportunistic Infections · Extracorporeal Circulation· Pneumocystis jirovecii·Respiratory Distress Syndrome， Adult Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is a seriously over-whelming complication of HIV infection， with mortality rates as high as 43% when mechanical ventilation is required and， together with bacterial pneumonia， it is the most recurrent and challenging cause of ARDS in AIDS patients .

【8】ARDS is a potentially reversible clinical syndrome with mortality rates as high as 30% to 40% . It is clinically defined as respi-ratory failure within 1 week of a known insult or new/worsening respiratory symptoms， along with bilateral opacities on chest radiograph or ultrasound， not fully explained by effusion， col-lapse， or nodules . Furthermore， respiratory failure has not been fully explained by cardiac function or volume overload .

【9】Management of ARDS is based around the diagnosis and treat-ment of infections， respiratory support (such as oxygen sup-plementation and positive pressure ventilation)， cautious fluid governance， and general supportive measures such as nutri-tional supplementation .

【10】Despite optimized standard therapies， some patients experi-ence further clinical deterioration. For these subjects， ECMO represents a rescue therapy providing time for lungs to recov-er from acute processes.

【11】Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an adapted cardiopulmonary bypass circuit in which the blood is oxygen-ated by circulating outside of the body in a membrane oxy-genator， for temporary life support for use in selected patients with potentially reversible respiratory and/or cardiac failure not responding to conventional medical management .

【12】There are 2 main methods： VV-ECMO， which operates cannu-lating a central vein for subsequent oxygenation and CO2 elim-ination； and venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO)， which involves a central artery cannulation and supplies hemodynamic and re-spiratory support . The veno-venous modality has been re-cently assessed as supportive therapy in severe acute respi-ratory failure .

【13】According to current guidelines ， extracorporeal life sup-port (ECLS) should be considered for use with patients in hy-poxic respiratory failure when the mortality risk is at least 50%， and it is indicated when the mortality risk is 80% or higher. Risks and benefits for each patient have to be considered in-dividually .

【14】Relative contraindications linked to a poor result in patients with respiratory failure， despite ECLS， are： mechanical ventila-tion at high levels for 7 days or more， major pharmacologic im-munosuppression， recent or expanding CNS hemorrhage， major CNS damage or terminal malignancy， and older age .

【15】Up until now， use of ECMO has been avoided in immunocom-promised patients because it can further suppress the immune system， and no clinical indications for HlV-infected or AIDS pa-tients have been established . Moreover， although there are currently no absolute contraindications to using ECMO in these patients ， just a few cases of ARDS treated by VV-ECMO have been reported， with variable outcomes， and very few AlDS patients with respiratory failure during PJP are report-ed to survive after ECMO in developed countries .

【16】Here， we report the successful V-ECMO treatment of an AIDS patient with ARDS complicating a PJP. We hope that this re-port， together with the associated literature， will improve the knowledge and management of these conditions.

【17】Case Report

【18】A 43-year-old man was admitted at our hospital because of7 days of high fever (T max 38.5C). His recent medical his-tory reported recurring cough not responding to empiric treat-ments， which deteriorated with dyspnea. He had an unremark-able clinical history. He had never undergone major surgery or medical invasive procedures. As he had no comorbidities， he did not take any drugs. His medical family history was also unremarkable.

【19】At admission， the patient was febrile (peaking up 39℃)， blood pressure was 95/40 mmHg， heart rate was 124 bpm， and ox-ygen saturation was 94% on room air. Blood testing showed leukopenia with lymphocytopenia，and a chest X-ray and high-resolution thorax CT scan evidenced bilateral ground-glass opac-ities. AIDS was diagnosed. His CD4 cell count was 10 cell/p! and HIV-RNA was 469 654 copies/ml.

【20】Bronchoscopy was not performed； a sputum smear examina-tion was negative for PJP， acid-fast bacilli (AFB) and other bac-teria， but it was positive for Candida spp.

【21】Empiric treatment was started with sulfamethoxazole/trime-thoprim， caspofungin， azithromycin， rifampicin， and steroids， and antiretroviral treatment with tenofovir/emtricitabine and raltegravir.

【22】Six days later， after an initial improvement， therapy failed to im-prove respiratory patterns， and an unexpected ARDS was ob-served. The patient was then intubated and transferred to the ICU.

【23】On day 4 in the ICU， after conventional treatment with op-timal mechanical ventilation， a worsened chest X-ray result， hypoxia (pa02 68 with 100% Fi02)， and hyper-capnia (paCO2 68) were sufficiently severe to require urgent VV-ECMO placement before transferring him to the regional ECMO referral Center.

【24】The patient was started on V-ECMO support (miniaturized tip-tip-tip heparin-coated circuit； Cardiohelp System； Maquet， Rastatt， Germany). Vessel cannulation Fr return (jugular) and24 Fr drainage (femoral)\] was performed after the administra-tion of a heparin bolus. Blood flow was kept at 4 L/min (about65-70% of cardiac output) and sweep gas at 4-5 L/min with100% FiO2. Anticoagulant therapy with unfractionated hepa-rin was also administered. The RESPSCORE was 2.

【25】A second bronchoscopy was performed and PJP was identified， whereas molecular biology (BIOFIRE@ FILMARRAY RP Panel) excluded other pathogens. Comprehensive screening ruled out other opportunistic infections， whereas PCR on blood showed positive Cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA (1000 copies/mL) and a fundus examination revealed CMV retinitis.

【26】Therapy was de-escalated，relying on sulfamethoxazole/trim-ethoprim，steroids， and caspofungin combination， while cART was confirmed； anti-CMV therapy started with Ganciclovir. After 3 days， his temperature decreased until defervescence， and the hemodynamic picture improved enough to allow nor-adrenaline weaning.

【27】One week later， radiologic findings  and respiratory function improved and the patient was started on a wean-ing trial from ECMO， and was removed on day 16 of ICU stay.

【28】On day 18 of ICU stay， the second day after ECMO removal， the patient， still sedated and checked for complications as per protocol， presented abrupt anisocoria. A brain CT scan re-vealed a hemorrhage involving temporo-parietal-occipital pa-renchyma with mass effect . Neurosurgical evacua-tion was promptly performed， without complications.

【29】On day 34 of ICU stay， the team proceeded with extubation. The patient maintained good respiratory patterns with a mist mask， and no motor or sensory deficits remained. He was switched to secondary prophylaxis with oral sulfamethoxa-zole/trimethoprim and valganciclovir. On day 37 of ICU stay， he was transferred to the general ward and then admitted to a rehabilitation program. Finally， he was admitted to the HⅣ out-patient unit when his CD4 cell count was 469 lymphocyte/pl and HIV-RNA 508 copies/ml. At 8 months after the onset of PJP， when his CD4 cell count was 519 cell/pl and HIV-RNA was103 copies/ml， oral valganciclovir was stopped. The patient was able to resume working and he had a complete recovery.

【30】Discussion

【31】We successfully used ECMO in an AIDS patient with ARDS sec-ondary to PJP associated with an undiagnosed HIV infection. Our patient presented with an extremely high HIV viral load and a very low CD4 count， likely correlating with the extended period of untreated infection， and making him a “late presenter”. In addition， the diagnosis of PJP defined him as an AIDS patient.

【32】While some authors contraindicated ECMO treatment in pa-tients with AIDS ， other authors reported a non-inferior mor-tality compared to the general population in patients with well-controlled HlV infection and a satisfactory immune status .

【33】An increasing number of AIDS patients with respiratory failure due to PJP pneumonia are reported to be treated with ECMO therapy  and， as with the case described here， most reported cases of PJP treated with ECMO were man-aged using the V modality， only 1 receiving with VA-ECMO. Moreover， regardless of CD4+ cell count and HIV-RNA load， the majority of patients survived after ECMO treatment， as did the case reported here.

【35】In addition， although our patient was older than the others listed in Table 1， he had no comorbidities and he was promptly started on ECMO treatment. These facts， along with the ap-propriate treatment of PJP and HlV infection， led to the suc-cessful result.

【36】Thus， as in other reports， our case suggests that ECMO is an option to consider and is a practical rescue modality for the treatment of AIDS patients with ARDS due to PjP， if promptly initiated during their hypoxemic respiratory failure and asso-ciated with appropriate support therapies.

【37】In this scenario， it is also crucial to rule out other respiratory infections， whether opportunistic or not， such as tuberculo-sis， non-tubercular mycobacterial infections， Legionellosis， Mycoplasma pneumonia， and viral pneumonia. After the PJP diagnosis， we were able to exclude other pathogens using mo-lecular biology in bronchoscopy samples.

【38】Finally， because of our patient’s very low CD4+ cell count(10 cell/pl) and the development of PJ pneumonia， we could not exclude that an immune reconstitution inflammatory syn-drome (IRIS) played a role to the ARDS presentation， along with CMV retinitis， although this is only a clinical speculation.

【39】Conclusions

【40】Our findings confirm that ECMO support may be justified in immu-nocompromised patients with PJP-associated ARDS with a high risk of dying from respiratory failure. This is one of the few case reports of AlDS patients surviving after decannulation from ECMO and successfully discharged from the hospital. It should be useful to speculate on the baseline characteristics of patients to identi-fy predictive criteria of positive outcome. Moreover， this case re-port is unique not only for the discussion of clinical management， but also because the patient was managed in 5 different clini-cal units， achieving prompt management of his clinical situation.

【0】Background：

【1】Anti-PL-12 syndrome is a rare form of myositis. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the commonest of the motor neuron disorders. However， the 2 conditions have not been reported to occur together in a single indi-vidual. This case report describes a patient who was diagnosed with anti-PL-12 anti-synthetase syndrome and then subsequently was diagnosed with ALS.

【2】Case Report： A 55-year-old male patient had anti-PL-12 syndrome and ALS occurring together. The patient initially present-ed with musculoskeletal complaints and was diagnosed with anti-PL-12 syndrome. He later went on to develop shortness of breath. Neurophysiological testing subsequently confirmed ALS as the patient experienced wors-ening muscle weakness over a 2-year period. A muscle biopsy performed showed neurogenic and myopathic process. The patient eventually lost the ability to ambulate without mobility assistance and suffered cardiac arrest due to complications from ALS， specifically diaphragmatic dysfunction.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】This case report represents the first documented case of a patient having both anit-PL-12 syndrome and ALS together. It has been suggested that having an autoimmune disease (AID) may increase the subsequent risk of developing ALS. Previous studies did not conduct evaluation to ascertain serological markers for AS antibod-ies. Lab tests were rechecked and revalidated multiple times in separate facilities for confirmation of results in case of initial lab error. This may suggest a common etiology for both anti-PL-12 syndrome and ALS.

【5】Keywords： Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis ·Antisynthetase Syndrome ·Case Reports

【6】Rockville， MD USA

【7】There is increasing evidence to suggest autoimmune diseas-es can precede amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) ， which is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative condition. Limited data suggest that ALS and other autoimmune diseases， like polymyositis (PM)， can co-exist . However， there are no reported cases of anti-synthetase syndrome (AS) and ALS OC-curring together.

【8】Here， we describe a patient who was diagnosed with anti-PL-12 anti-synthetase syndrome and then subsequently was diagnosed with ALS. To the best of our knowledge these 2conditions have never been reported to occur together in a single individual.

【9】Case Report

【10】A 55-year-old left-handed man developed multiple joint pains in 2015. Blood test  revealed elevated anti-citrulli-nated peptide (anti-CCP) and anti-Sjogren’s syndrome A an-tibodies (anti-SSA). However， he did not have any joint sy-novitis. In 2017， he developed recurrent muscle cramps and dyspnea on exertion. Creatine kinase and aldolase were ele-vated， with normal C-reactive protein. Anti-PL-12 was positive. Pulmonary function testing showed severe restrictive defect with moderate reduction in diffusing capacity. CT scan of the chest showed elevated right hemidiaphragm， but was other-wise negative. EMG showed acute-on-chronic denervation of several distal and proximal muscles. The skeletal muscle his-topathology showed mixed， neurogenic， and myopathic fea-tures as well as a mild degree of myonecrosis and regener-ation along with complement C5b-9 deposition. He received Prednisone， Azathioprine， and intravenous immune globu-lin (IVIG)， but his condition did not improve. He had an aller-gic reaction to mycophenolate mofetil， manifested by a rash.

【14】By the end of 2017， the muscle weakness worsened， and he was using a walker to ambulate. Muscle atrophy was noted in both shoulders and dorsal webs of the hands. Multiple EMGs and a muscle biopsy were performed . Because of shortness of breath without evidence of interstitial lung dis-ease and elevated enzymes， a diaphragmatic EMG was per-formed at a tertiary hospital. It showed abnormal spontaneous activity and neurogenic units in most of the tested muscles of all extremities， trapezius， and right diaphragm， confirming ALS.

【15】By late 2018， he had to use a mobility scooter to get around. In 2020， he went into cardiac arrest due to acute respiratory failure due to diaphragmatic dysfunction from ALS.

【16】Discussion

【17】To the best of our knowledge this is the first reported case of Anti-PL-12 anti-synthetase antibody occurring together with ALS. Although it is unclear， some studies suggest that having an autoimmune disease (AID) may increase the subsequent risk of developing ALS. This may suggest a shared etiology 

【18】A retrospective study using the all-England hospital record-linkage dataset from 1999 to 2011 considered AID preceding ALS. They calculated the rate ratio from the incidence of ALS in each AID cohort and compared it with the incidence of ALS in a cohort of individuals with no prior history of AID. There was a significantly increased incidence of ALS in those who had a previous diagnosis of AID including PM .

【19】A study from Taiwan suggests a similar association with AID and ALS. Taiwan’s Registry of Catastrophic Illness Database of 1778 PM patients found 6 patients subsequently developed ALS . Although there is some debate about whether the ini-tial diagnosis of PM was really the onset of ALS ， the PM patients met the Bohan and Peter criteria， including EMG and muscle biopsy requirements . The study concluded that patients with PM had a higher risk of developing ALS . A similar association was noted in 2021 with AlD and ALS in a Swedish population-based study .

【20】Myositis is a rare systemic condition. The adjusted annual in-cidence is 5.8-7.9 per 100 000 person-years and the preva-lence is 14-17.4 per 100 000 person-years . About 25% of patients with PM or dermatomyositis have AS antibodies . Of the known antibodies， anti-PL-12 accounts for less than5%. It is possible that other studies had AS antibodies in their PM cohorts and further evaluations to ascertain sero-logical markers were not conducted. There were initially con-cerns that the anti-PL-12 antibody result was an error. It was rechecked in the same lab， then it was reconfirmed twice at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation's Arthritis and Clinical Immunology Research Program.

【21】In daily clinical practice， it is rare that both anti-PL-12 syndrome and ALS would occur concurrently in one individual. Knowing the presence of both would help plan treatment and provide prognostic value. The mainstay of therapies for anti-PL-12syndrome are corticosteroids and other immunosuppressive agents. The prognosis worsens with the presence of intersti-tial lung disease (ILD)， which is typically present in more than90% of anti-PL-12 syndrome patients . Although our pa-tient had dyspnea， ILD was not present. While only 14% of pa-tients with AS and ILD die at 5 years ， mortality is known to be very high with ALS， and life expectancy of 3-5 year is typi-cal . It is important to look for concurrent ALS in patients with AS myositis who appear to be progressing more rapidly. ALS is no longer considered a singular entity but rather a con-tinuum consisting of ALS and other phenotypes， including my-opathies. These distinct phenotypes are not attributable sole-ly to motor neuron dysfunction and now are thought to be linked to certain genes： VCP， MATR3， CHCHD10，HNRNPA2B and SQTSM1 . While having the CHCHD10 gene appears to predispose a person to myopathic conditions (like inclusion body myositis)， the presence of the other genetic traits will lead to ALS. The presence of additional genes， like C9orf72，can further lead to frontotemporal dementia and other dementing conditions . Other concomitant muscle conditions， like ac-quired neuromyotonia (Isaac’s syndrome)， have been reported to occur together . It is postulated that all ALS subtypes (in particular， patients with inclusion body myositis) may have a common pathological feature of accumulation of transactive response DNA binding protein (TDP-43) . Our patient did not test positive for TDP-43 .

【22】While in myositis the presence of antibodies to the protein synthesizing machinery is well established， similarly targeted antibodies are now described in patients with ALS. The myo-sitis specific antibodies are directed towards the tRNA synthe-tases and have prognostic value. Anti-PL-12 antibodies are di-rected specifically against alany. tRNA synthetase. In a small group of patients with ALS， a mutant Cu，Zn-superoxide dis-mutase (SOD1) leads to misfolding of mitochondrial proteins， leading to cell toxicity . Lysyl-tRNA synthetase appears to be a target propagating mutant SOD1 toxicity . The pres-ence of higher levels of endogenous autoantibodies against the mutant SOD1 are associated with longer survival in ALS patients. Like the anti-PL-12 autoantibodies， the presence of autoantibodies against mutant SOD1 also has prognostic val-ue in ALS patients .

【23】Conclusions

【24】This is the first documented case of anti-PL-12 antibody and ALS occurring in the same patient. In our patient， we feel that both conditions existed together， although the anti-PL-12 an-tibody was identified first. Associations of these diseases oc-curring together may possibly suggest a common etiology and pathogenesis.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) has varied presentations and outcomes. TNM Stage， pathological features and performance status are the established factors prognosticating the disease. Recently， the role of thrombo-cytosis has been evaluated as a simple， cost-effective and accurate prognostic marker in RCC patients. Objective： To study the effect of thrombocytosis in renal cell carcinoma on the prognosis of the disease. Materials And Methods： A retrospective observational follow-up study of 142 patients with RCC from January 2007 to December 2017 was conducted at the Institute of Nephrourology， Bengaluru (Karnataka). Platelet count of more than 400000/mm3 was considered thrombocytosis. The clinical parameters， tumour stage， grade， progression and survival of the disease were compared concerning platelet count. The mean follow-up was 28 months (24-60 months). In addition， patients' time to disease progression and overall survival were studied concerning thrombocytosis. Data were analysed using SPSS V26.0 using Chi-square test， binary logistic and linear regression model and Kaplan Meir curve. Results： Mean age was 54.59 years. The mean platelet count was 2， 45，292 /mm3 and the mean tumour size was 7.67cm. Thrombocytosis correlates with total leucocyte count (p-value <0.001)， tumour necrosis (p-value 0.04)， lymph node invasion(p-value 0.01)， metastasis(p-value 0.027)， TNM stage(p-value <0.001) and overall survival(p-value <0.001). These patients also had poor histology and more lymphovascular invasion. On regression analysis， only TNM stage correlates significantly (p value 0.01) with time to progression. Platelet count >400000/mm3 was associated with poorer survival outcomes with a 5-year mortality rate of 38%. Conclusion： Thrombocytosis in RCC is associated with advanced disease， poor histology and rapid disease progression. It is a simple and easy tool for prognosticating RCC and predicting survival outcomes.

【1】KEYWORDS TNM stage， Renal Malignancy， follow-up， Platelet Count， Survival

【2】Introduction

【3】Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) accounts for nearly 85% of all pri-mary renal malignancies and about 3% of all adult malignant neoplasms. RCC can have varied presentations， including small tumour size， localised disease， metastatic disease， an ex-tensive disease with very high survival and even a distant metastatic RCC that spontaneously regresses later. This has led to difficulty in predicting the prognosis of the disease. Vari-ous prognostic factors like stage， grade and performance status have been used. Moreover， integrated staging and prognostic systems and nomograms improve predictive accuracy. But the need for a simple tool for predicting post-radical nephrectomy outcomes has led to the advent of the role of thrombocytosis in RCC patients. Raised platelet count has been an established marker of aggressive behaviour and poorer prognosis in patients with carcinoma stomach and gynaecological malignancies.JA study was conducted to determine the role of thrombocytosis in relation to clinical /pathological features and tumour stage in RCC patients and predict its role in the overall survival of the patients.

【4】A retrospective observational study was conducted in the De-partment of urology at the Institute of Nephrourology from January 2007 to December 2017. A total of 142 patients satisfied the inclusion criteria. All cases of RCC that underwent radical nephrectomy， histo-pathologically proven， and on strict regular follow-up were included in the study. Patients with multiple or bilateral tumours or unavailable platelet count were excluded from the study. Institutional ethical committee approval was taken.(INU/RRC/20/2018). The medical records of a total of179 patients of RCC who underwent nephrectomy with no adju-vant therapy were assessed during the study period. 36 patients were excluded as either record doesn'’t have platelet counts or patients lost to follow-up. Out of 143 remaining patients， one had bilateral tumours and was excluded. So， finally 142 cases were included in the study. 

【5】Table/Fig 1 Methodology of Data Collection.

【6】Patient's clinical features， biochemical parameters， CT Ab-domen findings， Tumour Stage and demographic character-istics were all retrieved from hospital records and tabulated. Histopathological findings and follow-up of the patients were done via details of OPD visits for disease progression. Throm-bocytosis was defined as a platelet count of >400，000/mm3. Disease progression was defined as the appearance of local re-currence or distant metastasis on follow-up.

【7】Patient recordings were tabulated and classified into two arms： Those with and without thrombocytosis. These groups were then compared concerning gross and microscopic tumour characteristics， TNM stage， and disease progression.

【8】Statistical analysis： Standard statistical tests of significance were applied. The Chi-square test was used to compare categor-ical variables. A binary logistic and linear regression model was used to predict outcomes. Cause-specific Survival plots were interpreted using the Kaplan Meir curve. A P value of <0.05was considered statistically significant. Statistical analysis was performed using the SPSS version.

【9】Results

【10】Out of the total cases， the mean age was 54.59 years. Gender distribution showed male preponderance. The mean platelet count was 2，45，292 /mm3 and the mean tumour size was 7.67cm. Histopathologically， most cases were of Clear cell carcinoma，and Fuhrman Grade 2 was most commonly encountered. 4.3% pa-tients presented with metastasis at diagnosis， and maximum pa-tients presented with Stage 1 RCC. The follow-up period ranged from 24-60 months， with a mean follow-up of 28 months. 

【11】All variables were compared in both groups.  On applying the Pearson correlation test  for thrombocytosis with various tumour factors， total leu-cocyte count， necrosis， lymph node invasion， metastasis， TNM stage， and overall survival shows significant correlation with thrombocytosis. In contrast， renal vein invasion and haemor-rhage are not related to thrombocytosis. Only Total leucocyte count and TNM stage were significant in multivariate analysis.

【12】Kaplan Meier Survival curve predicts better 5-year survival for patients with platelet counts<400000. 

【13】Table/Fig 6 Kaplan Meier 5 year Survival Analysis of both groups.

【14】Discussion

【15】Thrombocytosis or raised platelet counts can either be primary， as seen in myeloproliferative disorders or secondary， as in ma-lignancies，anaemia， depleted iron stores， inflammation and in the absence of a spleen. Thrombocytosis has been established by many authors in urological malignancies and RCC. It is a predictor of advanced stage， poor cancer-specific survival and death. In general， thrombocytosis represents high-stage cancer.

【16】Tumour-induced angiogenesis is the main driving force for cancer progression. Platelets adhere to tumoral endothelium and secrete an increased amount of VEGF (Vascular endothe-lial growth factor)， which promotes megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and subsequent platelet production. Cytokines like TPO(Thrombopoietin) and IL-6 also stimulate megakaryocytes. Platelets also provide adherence， penetration and sequestration of malignant cells through the endothelial wall and inhibit the immune system from clearing tumour cells from circulation. Recently， the diagnosis of RCC has increased exponentially due to incidental detection of small， low-grade tumours and the effect of environmental factors.Moreover， the biological be-haviour of the disease is also unpredictable， as 4-7% of T1a tumours can harbour metastasis at presentation. Advanced and metastatic tumours have poor survival outcomes and poorer quality of life. Hence， numerous prognostic factors have been reported in RCC， including tumour stage， tumour grade， perfor-mance status etc. To upgrade prognostication， Integrated staging systems like IMDC， SSIGN， and Kattan'sNomogram have also been introduced. But none of these models is 100% accurate.

【28】The first evidence of the role of thrombocytosis in RCC was demonstrated by Symbas et al. in the year 2000， who concluded that patients with metastatic RCC on adjuvant therapy with per-sistently normal platelet counts have 64% longer life expectancy than those with thrombocytosis. 【29】Based on correlation analysis， thrombocytosis significantly correlated with total leucocyte count， necrosis， lymph node in-vasion， metastasis， TNM stage， and overall survival. While on multivariate analysis only raised neutrophil count and TNM stage had a significant correlation with thrombocytosis with a p-value 0.02 and 0.04， respectively.

Overall， 5-year mortality was 12%.7.2% mortality rate for the normal platelet group， while it was 38% for the thrombocy-tosis group. This could be attributed to a greater number of lower-stage cases in the normal platelet group. OKeefe et al. obtained similar results， who reported a 42% death rate in the thrombocytosis group. They reported 5.75 times death rate in thrombocytosis， which was 5.4 times in our study. In a study by Patel et al.， a categorization approach of platelet changes showed that all patients with increased platelet count by 20%from the baseline had a recurrence of renal cell carcinoma. In a study by Symbas et al.， the mean survival for these pa-tients was 92 months， compared with 151 months for those with normal platelet countNegrier et al. demonstrated it as a sig-nificant predictor for survival on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis， as biological signs of inflammation were also an independent variable.\]Thrombocytosis has indepen-dent predictor status (HR： 1.49； p =0.01) in predicting overall survival in MRCC patients treated with VEGF-targeted agents as per Heng et al.

【31】Neither Total leucocyte count nor thrombocytosis was found significant. Only the TNM stage was a statistically significant predictor of time to progression. Present results are comparable to the results of Vivek et al. They also concluded that the TNM stage is the most significant factor.

【32】Vivek et al. in their study， noted that thrombocytosis patients are more likely to have a sarcomatoid variant，lymphovascular invasion and capsular invasion. Table 6 depicts the demography and comparison of the present study with a study by Inoe et al.， Vivek et al. and Erdemir et al.

【33】Hence， thrombocytosis can select a subset of patients most likely to benefit from aggressive therapeutic intervention. Platelet count >400，000/mm3 implicates a worse survival with other clinical or biochemical factors. It predicts a cascade of events correlated with advanced tumour stage and poor prog-nOsls.

【34】Limitations

【35】The present study has many limitations like its retrospective nature， a smaller subset of thrombocytosis patients， lack of com-parison with other standard predictive models and lack of long-term follow-up. But the current study is one of thelargest studies representing the study population in the Indian subcontinent. A prospective a randomised study with a larger sample size may consolidate the present study's findings and emphasise a broader spread of platelet levels in depicting the outcomes of renal cell carcinoma patients.

【36】Conclusion

【37】Thrombocytosis is an easy and inexpensive tool to prognosticate renal cell carcinoma. It is associated with poor histology，rapid disease progression and advanced presentation of tumours. It is a useful guide for predicting the need for adjuvant therapy when used in conjugation with established clinical and pathological parameters.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Trauma guidelines state that a thoracotomy should be performed if tube thoracostomy output reaches 1500mL promptly or 200mL every hour for 2-4 hours. However adhering to this rule religiously will lead to poor outcomes in some patient groups， particularly in those with blunt injuries. These patients likely have bleeding perpetuated by an acquired traumatic coagulopathy which is not surgically amendable. This is a case report describing a patient who sustained blunt injuries which although had 1500mL of initial blood loss after tube thoracostomy insertion， by adhering to the principles of damage control resuscitation， his chest bleeding stopped，and a thoracotomy was avoided. Case report： A 68-year-old male fell from a ladder and sustained catastrophic head and chest injuries. He had a history of cardiac disease and was taking clopidogrel. A chest drain was placed， and 1500mLs was promptly evacuated. Although this level of bleeding would usually necessitate a thoracotomy， there was concern that this bleeding was actually due to a profound coagulopathic state. His initial measures of coagulation function on ROTEM confirmed this coagulopathy， and he was aggressively treated blood products and tranexamic acid with damage control principles. Once his coagulation function had returned， his chest bleeding ceased. Unfortunately， the patient was unable to recover from his head injuries and died in hospital on day ten post-injury. Conclusion： The idea that a trauma thoracotomy should be performed if thoracic bleeding reaches pre-defined thresholds is too simplistic and does not take into account the complex physiology that occurs in those with a significant injury. Without care， a trauma thoracotomy in the wrong patient will add to the patient's injury burden， worsening their outcome. The primary focus needs to be on appropriate resuscitation， including the assessment of coagulation function before surgical intervention is considered.

【1】Introduction

【2】The management of the trauma patient exsanguinating from a chest injury is a difficult scenario， hampered by the stress of the resuscitation environment and the time-critical need for haemorrhage control. To assist in the decision making in these scenarios， the trauma literature describes the immediate output from a tube thoracostomy of ≥1500mL or ongoing blood loss of≥200mL hourly for 2-4 hours being indications for thoracotomy. However， the evidence surrounding this trauma dogma is not solid， with further concerns this may relate to inappropriate thoracotomies for the blunt injured patient. Those with blunt injuries are more likely to sustain an acquired coagulopathy as a result of their injuries worsening their bleeding and attempts to surgically control this bleeding will not be successful until this coagulopathy has been corrected. Initial attempts need to be focussed on damage control resuscitation with early adminis-tration of blood products and tranexamic acid. This case report describes a patient who had catastrophic chest bleeding per-petuated by his coagulopathy， but once this was corrected， the bleeding ceased， and a thoracotomy was not required.

【3】Case report

【4】A 68-year-old male fell four metres from a ladder， landing on his head and right chest. The pre-hospital assessment noted that he was combative， with vital signs of BP 86/77； HR 87； RR 24； saturating 81% on room air and a GCS of 9.

【5】·Airway： Oropharyngeal airway in place. Loose teeth with blood in his airway.

【6】·Breathing： Saturating 100% with 12L of oxygen. Reduced right-sided breath sounds with a clinical flail.

【7】·Disability： GCS6 (E1；V1；M4). Pupils equal and reactive.

【8】His medical history included coronary artery disease， and he was on clopidogrel and a statin.

【9】E-FAST showed no intra-abdominal bleeding but suggested a right haemopneumothorax， confirmed on chest X-ray . His initial haemoglobin on the venous gas was 135g/L.

【10】While being intubated， a 32Fr right-sided intercostal catheter was inserted， leading to an immediate evacuation of 500mL blood. Massive transfusion protocol was initiated， and he was transferred to computed tomography (CT).

【11】CT chest revealed a small contrast blush near the chest wall， although interventional radiology was not confident in emobolis-ing it . The CT brain showed an extensive closed head injury .

【12】Over the next 15min while in CT， a total of 1500mL had ac-cumulated within the chest drain and further blood products were administered along with tranexamic acid. Whilst determin-ing a surgical plan， the patient’s pupils became progressively unequal， and 250mL of 3% saline was given. His haemoglobin was repeated and returned at 92g/L. A decision was made for a decompressive craniectomy and potentially thoracotomy if the chest drain bleeding did not settle.

【13】On arrival at the operating theatre， his INR returned at1.4， and Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM) showed pro-found coagulopathy， particularly evident in the FIBTEM assay.

【14】Craniectomy was commenced， which resulted in significant venous bleeding. Whilst a plan for thoracotomy to control bleed-ing from chest wall was being considered， ongoing transfusion with cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma resulted in near-complete cessation of bleeding into the chest drain system， as well as controlling the bleeding from the craniectomy. The pa-tient's haemodynamics stabilised concurrently. A thoracotomy was not performed.

【15】Following ongoing monitoring and assessment in the operat-ing theatre， the patient was taken to the ICU. His total transfu-sion at this point was：

【16】·18 units PRBC

【17】· 8 units FFP

【18】· 4 unit platelets

【19】·335 units cryoprecipitate

【20】·250mL hypertonic saline

【21】·500ml of 5%Albumin

【22】11L normal saline

【23】· 2g tranexamic acid

【24】The drainage from the intercostal catheter remained mini-mal， and a repeat CXR revealed no significant haemothorax. The repeat ROTEM done on arrival to ICU showed his coagula-tion function had returned . Repeat CT brain showed the evolution of parenchymal contusions and intraventricular haemorrhages with watershed infarcts . After extensive discussions with family， a decision was made to with hold active treatment and provide comfort measures only. He was extubated on day 9 and passed away on day 10.

【25】Discussion

【26】The nature of blunt force trauma means several anatomicallo-cations can have severe life-threatening injuries which need to be addressed and managed promptly. Our patient here had sus-tained what ultimately was a fatal traumatic head injury but also had a catastrophic haemorrhage from his chest. Both injuries were time-critical and needed concurrent management. This was not an injury pattern that should be managed alone， but rather with a well-rehearsed multi-speciality trauma team.

【27】It was quickly determined that the patient's unstable haemo-dynamics and respiratory function were due to a significant chest wall injury and a chest drain was immediately inserted. On insertion， 1500mL was blood was promptly evacuated. This figure would usually indicate that the patient needs to undergo a thoracotomy to control the chest bleeding surgically. This trauma guideline based on historical observations on penetrat-ing trauma，  with more recent research looking at blunt chest injury showing that chest drain outputs should not be used in isolation when determining whether or not a thoraco-tomy should be performedJ.

【28】Blunt victims will experience a large amount of soft tissue injury， and this can trigger an aggressive inflammatory cascade. The inflammation would normally serve as a biological function to promote healing for these injured patients. However， if the'wrong'cytokines and inflammatory mediators are activated， the patient's coagulation function can be inadvertently down-regulated. This has been termed acute trauma coagulopathy and has been shown to occur right at the onset of injury before appreciable bleeding would have begun. Complicating the matter， those who have significant haemorrhage have this coagu-lopathy further perpetuated， leading to a vicious cycle for more bleeding. The molecular mechanisms and triggers surround-ing acute trauma coagulopathy are still completely unclear but is thought to relate to the interplay between hyperfibrinolysis， protein C activation and endothelial dysfunction. This area remains an important frontier in the management of traumatic injury.

【29】Considering the level of tissue injury and blood loss that our patient had experienced， it was suspected he has devel-oped a level of this acute trauma coagulopathy， compounded further by his regular clopidogrel. This was subsequently confirmed through Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM)， which showed very poor fibrinogen activity on the FIBTEM assay. Had a thoracotomy been performed at this time with-out correction of his coagulation function， he most certainly would have exsanguinated leading to unsurvivable haemor-rhage. Through damage control resuscitation with early and directed use of blood products (particularly the fibrinogen) and tranexamic acid， his coagulation function returned along with controlling the bleeding from his chest drain， avoiding a thora-cotomy altogether. The suggestion that early use of fibrinogenin the re3Cs1u1scitation of those with severe traumatic haemorrhage has been previously identified and has formed the basis for the CYROSTAT-2 trial， which is still currently being undertaken.

【30】Conclusion

【31】Unfortunately， our patient died due to the severe extent of his traumatic head injury. However， he survived for ten days post-injury allowing the intensive care physicians and neurosurgeons to assess if the patient’s injuries were recoverable. Importantly this also provided family members with the ability to spend time with him in intensive care to say their final goodbyes. This in itself can be invaluable to help close relatives heal with the grief after the death of a family member. Had an inappropriate thora-cotomy been performed and the patient exsanguinated， leading to sudden death， these opportunities would have lost. This case describes how pre-defined thresholds for chest drain outputs may not be appropriate for the blunt chest trauma victim.

【0】ABSTRACT Vulvar elephantiasis is a very rare condition often caused by filariasis infection. Other causes like general inflammatory disease， cancer treatment， traumatic causes or other infections can also explain the occurrence of this condition. In some cases， it is due to unknown causes. In this study， we present the clinical case of a Moroccan youth female patient with no significant history who presented vulvar elephantiasis associated with scabies with no evidence of filariasis infection， general inflammatory disease， malignancy， or other infection. This clinical case is unusual because of the large volume of lymphedema， its atypical localisation， its association with generalised scabies， and the absence of a well-defined aetiology， which may explain its occurrence.

【1】KEYWORDS Elephantiasis， vulvar scabies，lymphedema.

【2】Introduction

【3】Elephantiasis describes a massive enlargement of a limb or the external genitalia because of chronic lymphedema . The ele-phantiasis of the vulva is a rare condition often caused by fi-lariasis in developing nations . In this study， we present the clinical case of a 27-year-old patient with no significant medical history， who presented elephantiasis of the vulva evolved one year ago， associated with scabies. The patient did not show any evidence of filariasis infection or any other known cause which can explain the occurrence of this condition.

【4】Case report：

【5】A female patient of 27-years-old， with no previous medical his-tory was admitted to our department for vulvar elephantiasis of one-year evolution associated with generalised itchy skin le-sions. The general clinical examination found： BMI=26， normal body temperature， generalised， smooth and slightly elevated erythematous papules， and scratch lesions. The vulvar exam-ination found a voluminous pendulous swelling mass in the left labia majora with minimal skin inflammation， and moder-ate lymphedema in the right labia majora. The clinical examination also found bilateral inguinal adenopathy， and lower limb varices. However， the clinical and radiological examinations did not reveal the presence of an abdominal or gynaecological mass. The biological testing showed an increas-ing number of circulating eosinophilic granulocytes. C-reactive protein (CRP) was also elevated (84 mg/L)， and the routine bio-chemistry， glucose， serological testing for sexually transmitted infection (hepatitis B， HIV， syphilis) didn't show any particular-ity. We also performed a Midnight peripheral blood smear for filarial worms， but the result was negative. The patient received an antiscabies treatment for her skin lesions， and she underwent into a complete excision of her vulvar masses， which carried out a mass of 2 kg from the left labia majora and a mass of 500 g from the right labia majora . Simple cutaneous su- tures were realised to close the residual substance loss . The pieces were sent to the anatomopathological study which re-turned for vulvar lymphedema， without any sign of malignancy. The surgical follow-up was simple， but the patient presented again after two months with a new recurrence of lymphedema in the left labia majora ， without any associated general skin lesions.

【6】Discussion：

【7】Lymphedema can be defined as swelling of soft tissues which are the result of the accumulation of protein-rich interstitial fluids caused by a low output failure of lymph .

【8】The Impairment of lymphatic drainage can be due to con-genital abnormal vessel development (primary lymphedema) or damaged lymphatic vessels from infection， trauma， surgery， ra- diation， persistent inflammation， obstruction due to metastases or parasite infestation (secondary lymphedema)J.

【9】Lymphedema is frequently encountered in the limbs， less commonly in the face and the genital organs . In its earli-est stages， lymphedema is soft and pitting； however， with per-sistence， lymphedema has a brawny， non-pitting appearance likened to peau d'orange because of accentuation of skin folds and follicular ostia. Most of the swelling occurs in the subcu-taneous tissue， but the skin exhibits the most changes， which， when severe， is termed elephantiasis . Elephantiasis described a gross enlargement of the part of the body that has been in-volved. Review of the world's literature reveals that chronic vulvar elephantiasis is a very rare condition .

【10】The majority of cases of vulvar elephantiasis found in the lit-erature are due to filariasis  . Other causes include bacterial sexually transmitted infections (STI’s)， especially lymphogranu-lomavenereum (LGV) and donovanosis； tuberculosis， haemato-logical malignancies， and dermatological diseases and in some cases from unknown cause .

【11】Lu et al.  presented a clinical series of 24 cases of localised lymphedema； he made a comparison between those patients and the patients with diffuse lymphedema. Lu found that the most frequent localisation in these patients is anogenital， and overall， women were more frequently affected by lymphedema， particularly in the anogenital region and trunk， than men.

【12】The patients in Lu et al. series did not have any form of cancer treatment， they were significantly more likely to have history of trauma to the site (vaginal delivery)， and less likely to have a coexisting， chronic inflammatory process (rosacea and Crohn's disease)， No etiology or associated disease was found in about one-third of all cases. Lu and al. Also， show in his study that85% of patients were obese or overweight which can promote lymphedema by obstruction of the lymphatic canals by fat cells.

【13】Antonio et al.  presented two clinical cases of unilabial vulvar lymphedema similar to the Lu and Al series， but unlike the Lu et al. series， they did not find any factors that may explain the onset of Lymphedema except obesity in one patient.

【14】In our study the patient did not have any previous medical history or an apparent cause that can explain the vulvar ele-phantiasis， the research of filariasis was negative and also no sign of sexually transmitted infection， neither a sign of malig-nancy or inflammatory disease. Histological examination of the excised mass showed Acanthosis papillomatous epidermis sur-mounted by hyperkeratosis and orthokeratosis without cytonu-clear atypia； in the dermis， we found many dilated lymphatic vessels of variable size. Important interstitial oedema without any sign of malignancy. The only abnormality she presented beside the vulvar elephantiasis was the skin lesions which were resolved after antiscabies treatment and， the slightly elevated level of circulating granulocyte and the CRP which may correlate with the previous scabies infestation.

【15】Our patient presented a recurrence of lymphedema after ex-cision. In Lu and al series the majority of lymphedematous tumours were cured with excision， and those that recurred or progressed were associated with factors known to aggravate lymphedema： obesity， cellulitis， signs of persistent inflamma-tion. In our patient， we believe that persistent of inflammation can explain recurrence. However we planned to realise more investigation to explain the recurrence， but the patient refuse to go under supplementary examination.

【16】Conclusion

【17】This clinical case is unusual because of the large volume of lymphedema， its atypical localisation， its association with gen-eralised scabies， and the absence of a well-defined aetiology， which may explain its occurrence.

【0】ABSTRACT Although rare， the aberrant right subclavian artery (arteria lusoria) is the most frequent anatomical variant of the aortic arch and can be responsible for dysphagia. Its association with oesophagal cancer， which is another cause of dysphagia， is exceptional. We report the case of a 41-year-old female patient in whom this association was present. The preoperative identification of these associated anomalies by CT scan allowed to perform a transhiatal esophagectomy while avoiding potential surgical complications.

【1】KEYWORDS arteria lusoria， aberrant right subclavian artery， dysphagia lusoria， esophageal cancer， transhiatal esophagectomy

【2】Introduction

【3】Aberrant right subclavian artery or arteria lusoria is a rare con-genital anomaly in which the subclavian artery arises directly from the aortic arch and follows an aberrant course behind the esophagus. This retroesophageal pathway can cause symp-toms， the most frequent of which is dysphagia， called dysphagia lusoria. The concomitant presence of arteria lusoria and oe-116sophagal cancer is exceptional and can be life-threatening dueto the high risk of complications during oesophagal surgery. We report the case of a patient with oesophagal cancer and arte-ria lusoria in whom a transhiatal esophagectomy was performed while avoiding the surgical pitfall of this association.

【4】Case report

【5】We report the case of a 41-year-old female patient， without any particular medical or surgical history， non-alcoholic and non-smoker. She presented with dysphagia progressively evolving for three years， first to solids then to liquids， associated with moderate chest pain. The patient also reported an unappreciated weight loss without alteration of her general condition.

【6】A chest CT scan with contrast was performed， showing ir-regular， circumferential， stenosing parietal thickening of the middle third of the thoracic oesophagus over a height of 5.8cm . This CT scan also identified an aberrant right subclavian artery arising from the aortic arch and pass-ing behind the oesophagus， corresponding to an arteria lusoria. There were no other thoracic abnormali-ties， including thoracic adenopathy or pulmonary lesions. An oesophagal fibroscopy performed with biopsy confirmed the neoplastic nature of this thickening with histology of squamous cell carcinoma.

【7】The rest of the workup did not show any secondary localiza tion， and the tumour was classified as pT2pN0pM0. One month after the neoadjuvant radiochemotherapy sessions， a transhi-atal esophagectomy with gastroplasty was performed without intraoperative bleeding complications while scrupulously avoid-ing the known aberrant subclavian artery. After two months of follow-up， there was no event.

【8】Although rare， the aberrant right subclavian artery (arteria lu-soria) is the most frequent anatomical variant of the aortic arch， representing 0.2 to 1.7% of aortic arch anomalies and 1% of supra-aortic trunk variants . It is most often asymptomatic but can be responsible for dyspnea， chest pain， and dysphagia， called dysphagia lusoria. This dysphagia is related to a compression of the oesophagus by the aberrant subclavian artery which passes behind it. This compression and， therefore the dysphagia can be more severe when there is also an aneurysm on the arteria lusoria. The concomitant presence of an aberrant subclavian artery and oesophagal cancer is an exceptional situation and naturally increases the intensity of dysphagia.

【9】Moreover， if the diagnosis of arteria lusoria is already known， any symptomatology of dysphagia may be attributed to it and potentially lead to a delayed diagnosis of additional oesophagal cancer. In our patient， dysphagia had been present for three years， but it was likely the oesophagal tumour that accentuated this dysphagia and led him to consult. However， the real con-cern with this association is the surgical challenge that it induces during an esophagectomy with a high risk of haemorrhage or esophago-arterial fistula. This risk is reduced by preoperative imaging， which allows the surgeon to take the necessary pre-cautions. There are many imaging techniques that can be used to make this diagnosis， ranging from barium swallow to MRI. Still， thoracic CT remains the examination of choice， accessible and sufficient spatial resolution to specify the anatomical rela-tionships necessary for the surgeon to accurately anticipate the surgical procedureA\]. This anticipation of the surgical proce-dure is essential to avoid intraoperative complications， which can be disastrous. In our patient， the surgical challenge posed by this association was thus met.

【0】Background：

【1】Only 0.5% of all ovarian tumors are Leydig cell tumors and they are generally benign and unilateral. These an-drogen-secreting tumors lead to virilizing symptoms， most often in postmenopausal women. Because Leydig cell tumors are typically small， diagnosing them accurately can be challenging.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who was referred to our Endocrinology Clinic because of a 5-year history of hirsutism (Ferriman-Gallwey score of 11) with no discernible cause. The patient had high levels of serum testosterone and a normal level of dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate. Imaging， including transvaginal ul-trasound and pelvic magnetic resonance， revealed a 16-mm uterine nodule， which was suspected to be a sub-mucous leiomyoma， but no adrenal or ovarian lesions. Despite the lack of findings on imaging and because of the high suspicion for an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor， bilateral laparoscopic oophorectomy was per-formed. Histological examination of the specimen revealed a non-hilar Leydig cell tumor that measured 8 mm in its largest axis. After the surgery， the patient had significant clinical improvement and her laboratory test re-sults normalized. Her sister had the same symptoms and laboratory findings at a similar age， which raised the suspicion of a possible familial genetic syndrome. No genetic testing was performed， however， because the pa- tient's sister declined further diagnostic investigation.

【4】Conclusions： Leydig cell tumors are rare， and even when they are small， they can cause symptoms related to androgen ex-cess. As a result， diagnosing them often is challenging.

【5】Keywords： Hyperandrogenism· Leydig Cell Tumor · Postmenopause

【6】The appearance of a few terminal hairs on the face and a de crease in body and scalp hair in women during menopause are considered part of the natural process following cessation of menses . The appearance of virilizing features in a meno-pausal patient， such as male alopecia， clitoromegaly， a deep voice， acne， increased libido， and hirsutism， however， should lead to an investigation. These symptoms can be due to adrenal tumors， including androgen-secreting carcinomas， and ovarian tumors. Leydig cell tumors are rare ovarian neoplasms classi-fied as sex cord-stromal tumors and they can cause hyperan-drogenism. Only 0.5% of all ovarian tumors are Leydig cell tu-mors and most are benign and unilateral . Diagnosing them can be challenging because they may be symptomatic despite their small size and they often are not detected on imaging.

【7】Case Report

【8】We report the case of a 77-year-old woman with a history of autoimmune hepatitis， type 2 diabetes， dyslipidemia， and Hashimoto thyroiditis. She was taking azathioprine (50 mg bid) and was not receiving any treatment associated with hir-sutism， including glucocorticoids. She had a history of 4 un-complicated pregnancies and experienced menopause at age42 years. She had not taken hormone replacement therapy.

【9】Over the past 4 years， the patient had experienced generalized hirsutism， which was most prominent on her face (Ferriman-Gallwey score of 11)， and caused her significant psychological distress. Laboratory testing revealed the following levels： total testosterone 290 ng/dL (normal range， <41)， free testosterone5.60 ng/mL (normal range， 0.10-4.70)， delta-4 androstenedi-one 2.9 ng/mL (normal range， 0.4-3.7)， 17-hydroxyprogester-one 1.80 ng/mL， dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S)72 ug/dL (normal range， 26-460)， thyroid stimulating hormone2.84 mUI/L (normal range， 0.27-4.20)， and free T4 16.0 pmol/L(normal range， 12.0-22.0). On transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS)， after adjustment for age， the patient's ovaries were enlarged but the echostructure was normal and there were no other findings. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed only a 16-mm uterine nodule， which appeared to be a sub-mucous leiomyoma，and no adrenal lesions.

【10】After adrenal causes of virilization were eliminated， a laparoscop-ic bilateral oophorectomy and hysterectomy were performed. Histopathology revealed an 8-mm ovarian tumor with foci of lu-teinized cells and Reinke crystals， which was positive for inhibin and calretinin and negative for estrogen and progesterone recep-tors， findings that supported the diagnosis of a non-hilar Leydig cell tumor . After the surgery， the patient’s testoster-one and free testosterone levels returned to normal .

【11】It is important to note that the patient's sister had the same symptoms of marked hirsutism， at age 79 years. Her serums lev-els were as follows： total testosterone 258 ng/dL (normal range，<41)， free testosterone 3.30 ng/mL (normal range， 0.10-4.70)， serum hormone binding globulin 61.0 nmol/L (normal range，18.0-144.0)， DHEA-S 84 ug/dL (normal range， 26-460)， and del-ta-4 androstenedione 3.1 ng/mL (normal range， 0.3-3.7). The patient's sister underwent pelvic MRI， which showed normal-sized ovaries and no large lesions. A bilateral oophorectomy was recommended， but she declined the treatment.

【12】Discussion

【13】Accurately diagnosing virilizing ovarian tumors is often chal-lenging because they may be too small to detect on imaging. Identifying small functioning can require use of multiple types of imaging and an integrated approach. TVUS is often used as a good first-line exam and pelvic MRI adds to clear character-ization of the ovarian anatomy. However， even both types of imaging together can be insufficient if a tumor is very small.

【14】In the patient in our case， a normal serum DHEA-S level ex-cluded adrenal causes of hyperandrogenism， leaving an ovari-an androgen-secreting tumor as the most likely diagnosis. For this reason， an oophorectomy was recommended. After the surgery， the patient's symptoms improved and her serum tes-tosterone levels normalized. The histopathological examina-tion supported the diagnosis of a non-hilar Leydig cell tumor， which is considered a steroid cell tumor. Such tumors are de-fined as ovarian neoplasms， composed of steroid hormone-se-creting cells， and divided into 3 subtypes： stromal luteomas arising from ovarian stroma， Leydig cell tumors arising from Leydig cells in the hilum， and steroid cell tumors not other-wise specified when the lineage of the tumor is unknown . This latter subtype is the most common， accounting for 80%of steroid cell tumors . Usually， Leydig cell tumors arise from the ovarian hilum. Non-hilar Leydig cell tumors， as in our patient， occur in ovarian cortical stroma and can be difficult to distinguish from other stromal tumors .

【15】Pure Leydig cell tumors of the non-hilar type closely resem-ble the stromal luteoma， a distinctive form of lipid cell tumor described by Scully . It is distinguished from a stromal lu-teoma by the presence of characteristic crystalloids of Reinke within the tumor cells . These tumors secrete androgens， which are responsible for virilizing symptoms， and they are usually unilateral and benign. However， there is a risk of ma-lignant transformation. About 20% of patients develop me-tastasis， usually limited to the peritoneal cavity； metastasis to distant sites is rare . Because the patient’s sister had the same symptoms and laboratory findings at a similar age， we suspected a familial genetic syndrome. However， no histologic diagnosis was confirmed for her because she declined surgery and genetic testing was not performed. In her case， therapy with spironolactone was provided.
