【19】The phenotypic and molecular switch in BCR-ABLpositive BC in CML has been previously reported ， but the mech-anism of this phenomenon remains obscure. The recent data stress the role of BCR-ABL kinase in lineage choice and infidelity in pathology. The cell signaling pathway in-duced by p210BCRABL is able to suppress or activate some tran- scription of repressor factors involved in the regulation of the erythro/megakaryocytic commitment. p210BCRABL can reprogram megakaryocytic progenitor cells into erythroid cells. This lineage switching is associated with the downreg ulation of the Friend leukemia integration 1 (Fli-1) tran-scription factor. A profound effect on the phenotype of CML-transformed cells is associated with modulation of the translation-regulating proteins level by the BCR-ABL tran-script. For example， the block in differentiation associated with downregulation of C/EBPa protein levels and the in-creased survival associated with MDM2-dependent inhibi-tion of the p53 proapoptotic effects are essential features of highly malignant cell clones in the CML blast crisis .It t CI1S1S is well documented that modulation of p210BCR-ABL activity may control lineage programming. Particularly relevant is the single report of spontaneous lineage switching from a mast cell to an erythroid or myeloid phenotype in certain established lines of BCR-ABL-transformed murine cells . Chalandon et al. reported that the expression of high lev-eV-els of the p210BCRABL oncoprotein in primitive human cord blood cells can activate an erythroid differentiation pro-gram in apparently granulopoietic-restricted cells through a BCR-ABL kinase-dependent mechanism. This occurs even in apparently committed granulopoietic progenitors . Jamieson et al. supported the data that in CML cases gran- ulocyte-macrophage progenitors are candidate leukemic stem cells in blast crisis . Our patient’s disease outcome may confirm this data.

【20】In the reported case the conversion to p190BCRABL with p210ECRABL transcript disappearance was documented in post-transplant period. In p190 positive CML， the myelo-proliferative process includes the monecytic and the gran-ulocytic lineage. In a review of the literature p190 positive CML may be grouped into 2 categories： approximately half of the patients exhibited prominent monocytosis and in-termediate hematological phenotype between CML and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia， and the remaining pa-tients showed no monocytosis . Lichty et al. reported that p190BCRABL mRNA is associated with high white cell and blast counts . The p190 BCR-ABL protein is known to be transforming more strongly than the p210 protein . Therefore， a detection ofthe p190 transcript after the trans-plant could not only be a marker of total tumor burden， but also a more aggressive feature of the CML clone and infers impending cytogenetic and clinical relapse . This may confirm the clonal evolution of the disease. The expression of p190 transcript may indicate early re-expansion of the Ph positive stem cell compartment.

【21】Theoretically， the phenomenon of the F311L mutation present both in p190 and p210 transcripts may be ex-plained by their common origin. The mutation in p210was detectable for at least 9 months before p190 transcript was discovered. It cannot be excluded that p190 positive Philadelphia chromosome derived from the already exist-ing p210 Pht by deletion of 36-92 kb fragment (BCR ex-ons 2-14 and a part of intron 1). Along with other chro-mosomal abnormalities， microdeletions in CML are not uncommon， and their occurrence has been broadly re-ported . On the other hand， native p190 was also de-tected . Probably the second subpopulation of cells carrying native p190 Ph had a different origin， such as de novo (9；22) translocation.

【22】Another possible explanation of the changes observed is al-ternative splicing. The presence of p190 transcript is some-times observed in CML， especially in more advanced diseas-es such as acceleration or blast crisis phases . However， usually in p210 positive patients p190 transcript appears in very small quantities. In our case， however， both F311L posi-tive and negative p190 transcripts were detected at the same time， while the analysis of p210 transcript from the same sample showed only the presence of mutated BCR-ABL.

【23】It is impossible to confirm that both transcripts  originated from one cell. Along with the fact that ear-lier two transcripts of p210 was detected (b2-a2 and b3-a2) this may lead to the conclusion that the genomic stability of this patient was extraordinarily impaired.

【24】It also cannot be excluded that in the presented case p210BCRABL and p190BCRAEL were present in different sub-clones ofleukemic cells. The oligoclonality of CML was also exampled in the case of patient with four distinct imatinib-resistant subclones in the Talpaz study . Unfortunately there are currently no molecular techniques which would allow verification of this speculations， especially on the ar-chival material.

【25】CONCLUSIONS

【26】Our data confirms the genomic instability of the CML BC phase which may lead to a phenotypic variability. The open question is how the treatment can modulate natural disease activity. It is especially important due to recent evidence sug-gesting that leukemia stem cells cannot be eradicated even when allogenic SCT or tyrosine kinase inhibitors treatment is administered

【0】Background：

【1】Regional nerve blocks ideally provide safe and effective post-operative pain control， decrease opiate require-ments， and enhance recovery from intense pain following major thoracic， abdominal， and musculoskeletal sur-geries. The erector spinae plane block， a recently described novel treatment for chronic neuropathic pain and acute pain after thoracic surgery， can be performed with in plane infiltration and placement of a continuous infusion catheter deep to the erector spinae muscle at the tip of the transverse process， resulting in diffusion of local anesthetic between vertebrae and the paravertebral space with sensory blockade of spinal nerves as well as sympathetic branches.

【2】Case Report： We describe the novel use of the erector spinae block for primary pain control and uncomplicated catheter re-moval in the setting of anticoagulation following a major hepatectomy for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The use of the erector spinae block in this context provided effective post-operative analgesia.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Additional evidence from clinical trials will be helpful to evaluate the role of this relatively new block for peri-operative analgesia.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Acute Pain· Cholangiocarcinoma ·Nerve Block

【6】Cholangiocarcinoma represents the second most common liver malignancy . Elevated serum biomarkers， serial liver ultra-sound， computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging， and needle biopsy are useful in the diagnosis and staging of intrahepatic malignancy . Surgery is offered to non-cirrhotic patients with good performance status who present at an ear-ly stage with curable disease . Hepatectomy is desirable in the setting of a localized nodule with adequate remnant liv-er volume， while liver transplantation within Milan criteria is reserved for multifocal disease and/or in the presence of cir-rhosis not amenable to anatomic resection .

【7】Anesthetic considerations for liver resection include pre-oper-ative patient selection with risk stratification， intra-operative management of acute bleeding， and post-operative monitor-ing . Cirrhotic patients with intrahepatic carcinoma require assessment of pre-operative hepatic function and prognosti-cation for peri-operative complications using the model for end-stage-liver-disease or the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score (A， B， or C) . Intraoperatively， maintaining a central venous pres-sure <5 mmHg through fluid minimization， volatile anesthetic agents， vasodilators such as nitroglycerin， or acute normovole-mic hemodilution is recommended to decrease venous bleed-ing during transection of liver parenchyma .

【8】Epidural analgesia confers benefits related to decreased pain scores and side effects compared to systemic intravenous analgesics following open abdominal surgery . However epidural analgesia has been found non-superior to regional techniques，such the paravertebral block， in achieving patient satisfaction . Complications of epidural analgesia include a varying incidence of post-dural puncture headache， local anes thetic systemic toxicity， spinal hematoma and abscess， hypo-tension， nausea and vomiting， and urinary retention . Epidural catheter removal can be delayed following liver re-section due to post-operative coagulopathy .

【9】The erector spinae regional block is emerging as an intriguing alternative to conventional neuraxial analgesia for a variety of thoracic， intraabdominal， and joint surgeries due in part to a decreased risk for spinal hematoma，infection， and adverse hemodynamic effects . To date， descriptions of the ben-eficial effects of the erector spinae block on patients include reduced opioid consumption and decreased pain and temper-ature sensation， with no reports of adverse bleeding， hypo-tension， or urinary retention . Experience suggests that the erector spinae block is less technically challenging to perform than other thoracic nerve blocks， such as the paravertebral block， and not absolutely contraindicated in patients who are on therapeutic anticoagulation .

【10】Case Report

【11】Written informed consent for this report was obtained from a75-year-old male patient (weight 103.5 kg； height 182.9 cm； BMI 30.9 kg/m2) with coronary artery disease， obstructive sleep apnea， abdominal aortic aneurysm， atrial fibrillation， mitral regurgitation， psoriatic arthritis， gastroesophageal reflux dis-ease， chronic kidney disease， type Il diabetes， hypertension， and hyperlipidemia who presented for an open right extend-ed hepatectomy and cholecystectomy for resection of cholan-giocarcinoma .

【12】On the day of the surgery， the patient’s vitals were temper-ature 36.6℃， blood pressure 130/72 mmHg， respiratory rate18 breathes per minute， pulse oximetry 98% on room air， and pain 0/10. Airway examination revealed limited neck exten-sion， small oral opening (Mallampati Class IV)， and 3 finger breadth thyromental disease. He was able to sustain activity greater than 4 metabolic equivalents and deemed American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status IV by the anesthesiologist . An electrocardiogram revealed rate controlled atrial fibrillation， premature ventricular complexes， and evidence of a prior septal infarct.

【13】After informed consent was obtained， the patient was marked by the operating provider， a timeout was conducted， and the patient was positioned for bilateral erector spine block in a sitting position with standard monitors and oxygen adminis-tered through a nasal cannula. The skin was prepped in a sterile fashion using chlorhexidine cleansing solution. After relevant anatomy was identified by palpation， the T7 spinous process was marked. Using the curvilinear ultrasound (Sonosite Edge) probe in a transverse orientation on the left side， the trans-verse process was identified. A 17-gauge 9 cm Tuohy needle(Arrow) was inserted in plane in a cranial-to-caudal direction underneath the erector spinae muscle at the transverse pro-cess of the vertebrae. The plane was hydrodissected with 5 mL saline until the transverse process was met.

【16】After negative aspiration of heme， 1 mL of local anesthetic was injected without signs of local anesthetic toxicity. A to-tal of 20 mL of ropivacaine 0.5% was injected with intermit-tent negative heme aspiration in 5 mL aliquots. Once a pock-et of local anesthetic was created， a flexible 19-gauge 60 cm catheter (Arrow) was threaded through the Tuohy needle be-low the level of the erector spinae muscle. This catheter was left at 12 cm. Visual confirmation of the catheter in the mus-cle plane was confirmed with further administration of nor-mal saline. Then the ultrasound was directed to the right side. After relevant anatomy and landmarks were identified utilizing ultrasound guidance on the right side， the procedure was re-peated. The catheter on the right side was left at 15 cm. Vital signs were stable， and the patient tolerated the procedure well.

【17】On post-operative day 1， the patient was successfully weaned off pressors and extubated in the surgical intensive care unit. He reported 0/10 pain with a continuous infusion of10 cc/hour of 0.2% ropivicaine without programmed boluses through each erector spinae catheter . On post-oper-ative day 2， the patient was out of bed and continued to re-port 0/10 pain without any requirement for additional intra-venous or oral analgesics . The patient was resumed on therapeutic anticoagulation with unfractionated intrave-nous heparin. On post-operative day 4， after holding the lo-cal anesthetic infusions for several hours to confirm adequate pain control， both catheters were removed without complica-tion despite an elevated prothrombin time/international nor-malized ratio (PT/INR) of 2.4.

【18】During the 4-day catheter-based infusion， the patient received a single dose of intravenous fentanyl for a total morphine mg equivalent dose of 4.99 mg for breakthrough pain. On each sub-sequent day， the patient was able to achieve improving incentive spirometry scores of 9.7 cc/kg， 14.5 cc/kg， and 16.9 cc/kg. He was transferred out of the intensive care unit on post-operative day 7 for monitoring of coagulopathy and discharged home on post-operative day 18 after liver function began to normalize.

【19】Discussion

【20】In 2016， the erector spinae block was first described as a new regional block for the treatment of neuropathic thoracic pain . Subsequently， the block has been adapted for acute and chronic pain control with ease and low complica-tions for a variety of surgeries and conditions including spine surgery， breast surgery， limb amputation， video assisted tho-racoscopic surgery， rib fractures， post-herpetic neuralgia， com-plex regional pain syndrome， cardiac surgery， laparoscopic and open abdominal surgery， and hip surgery . The site of action includes a large area involving the intercostal nerve， the dorsal ramus of the spinal nerve， paravertebral region， and the epidural space， providing analgesia for somatic and vis-ceral nociceptive sensation with an average numerical rating scale for pain less than or equal to 3/10 in most reports .

【21】The erector spinae block is performed using ultrasound guid-ance to visualize the relevant anatomy in awake， sedated， or fully anesthetized adult or pediatric patients who are po-sitioned in sitting， lateral， or prone position . A linear high frequency probe in the thoracic region or curvilinear low frequency probe in the lumbar region is placed in a transverse fashion to initially locate the appropriate spinous process . The transverse process is then identified by moving the ultra-sound probe laterally and changing the probe orientation by90°. At T5， the needle is inserted in the plane through the skin， subcutaneous tissue， trapezius， rhomboid major， and erector spinae， followed by hydrodissection with saline， and a single shot injection of bupivacaine or ropivicaine and catheter place-ment if needed for continuous infusion .

【22】The erector spinae block is potentially a safer alternative in the presence of contraindications to an epidural or paraver-tebral technique， including systemic anticoagulation， coagula-tion disorders， use of antiplatelet medications， and following heparinization . Advantages include simplicity and low risk of complications given that the block is not immediate-ly adjacent to the spinal cord， lung pleura， or vascular struc-tures . Optimal volume， concentration， and type of lo-cal anesthetic to reach the target dermatomes and enter the paravertebral space， while avoiding systemic toxicity are un-der active investigation .

【23】Patients undergoing extensive liver surgery experience dra-matic somatic and visceral pain due to extended subcostal in-cision， rib retraction， as well as diaphragmatic and peritoneal irritation . Despite the absence of a pre-operative contra-indication for epidural placement， patients undergoing hepat-ic surgery are prone to the development of post-operative co-agulopathy which could potentially pose a bleeding risk and delay removal of an epidural catheter . Risk factors for the development of post-operative elevations in internation-al normalized ratios following hepatic resection include small remnant liver volumes，decreased body mass index， and long duration of procedure . In such clinical scenarios， the erec-tor spinae block may serve as a safe new and effective meth-od to achieve control of pain related to hepatic surgery .

【24】We report on the successful outcome of a regional nerve block as a replacement for gold standard epidural analgesia in achiev-ing effective pain control following hepatic surgery. Additional randomized clinical trials are needed to further elucidate the role for non-traditional pain management in patients with con-traindications to neuraxial anesthesia.

【0】Background：

【1】Aortic stent-graft placement is intended to be a procedure with minimal perioperative risk in com-parison to the open procedure. However， the 1.5% mortality rate and the possibility of procedure-related complications should be taken into account.

【2】Case Report：

【3】This paper presents multiple procedure-related complications including acute limb ischemia and bowel necrosis in a patient with preexisting nephrostomy operated on with EVAR (endovascular aortic repair). Issues regarding proper anatomical planning and imaging are discussed， and ways to avoid such complications are highlighted.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Multiple complications during EVAR may significantly reduce the early benefit of the procedure. Correct preoperative assessment of CT scans can avoid making an inappropriate decision regard-ing use of EVAR. In cases of concomitant urological pathology， any surgical intervention should be decided upon in cooperation with the vascular surgeon and urologist.

【6】key words：

【7】abdominal aortic aneurysm complications · aortic stentgrafts · nephrostomy·bowel necrosis · acute limb ischemia Aortic stent-graft placement is intended to have minimal perioperative risk for the patient in comparison to the open procedure； however， the 1.5% mortality rate and the pos-sibility of procedure-related complications should be tak-en into account. The aim of this paper is to present multi-ple procedure-related complications in a patient operated on with endovascular procedure for AAA (abdominal aor-tic aneurysm).

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】The patient was a 58-year-old white male admitted to the hospital for scheduled surgery of AAA. Diagnosis of AAA was made in 2004 with abdominal ultrasound showing a53mm abdominal aortic aneurysm with a thick concentric zone of thrombus. The patient was scheduled for the CT and eventual surgery， but he did not consult the vascular surgeon again until urological treatment 1 month before the admission. The patient was hospitalized in the urology department for blockage of the right ureter with coexist-ing hydronephrosis. The problem was caused by a 1.5 cm stone blocking the right ureter. The patient was disqualified by the treating urologist from ESWL (extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy) due to diagnosis of AAA in ultrasound with a maximum diameter of 6 cm. Percutaneous nephrostomy was performed and the patient was discharged from the hos-pital with prescription of the consultation of the vascular surgeon. The patient was referred to the vascular surgeon2 weeks later and was qualified for schedule admission af-ter performing spiral angio CT， which revealed an aortic an-eurysm of 63 mm maximum transverse diameter. The neck of the aneurysm measured 20-21 mm below the renal ar-tery. The patient’s iliacs diameters were l1 mm (right)and12 mm (left). Iliac and femoral arteries were found athero-sclerotically changed， but patent. No exact description of the eventual stenosis was given.

【10】The patient was admitted to the department. Cardiological risk factors were assessed and the patient was qualified as an ASA II patient (moderate risk). Anatomical an alysis of the angio CT revealed that the patient was appropriate for open procedure or for en dovascular repair； however， atheroscle-rotic changes in the femoral and iliac arteries were noticed. In clinical examination， popliteal pulse was present only on the right side. Urological consultation confirmed per-sistent blockage of the right ureter and the patient insisted on AAA surgery prior to any radical urological intervention.

【11】In attempting to minimize the possibility of infection dur-ing the open aortic procedure (the nephrostomy site was close to the potential operating field)， the decision was made to perform stent-graft placement despite atheroscle-rotic changes in the iliac and femoral arteries.

【12】The procedure was done under spinal anesthesia. Both com-mon femoral arteries were surgically exposed. The calibrat-ed 5F type pigtail catheter was introduced into the aorta above the renal artery through the left common femoral ar-tery over a 0.035 hydrophilic guidewire (Roadrunner： Cook Ireland Ltd.， Limerick， Ireland). Then， the prosthesis was introduced over a stiff Lunderquist 0.035 guide through the right femoral artery into the abdominal aorta， and positioned below the renal arteries. The brachial artery was then selec-tively catheterized and the guide was introduced into the graft. The iliac part of the stent-graft was introduced into the aorta through an Amplatz 0.035 guide. The right stent-graft arm was then extended up to the iliac artery. A dig-ital subtraction angiography (DSA) was performed to ex-amine the location and tightness of the stent-graft. DSA revealed thrombosis of the right iliac artery， possibly due to the dissection. A Fogarthy catheter thrombectomy was done and， due to hemodynamic stenosis， 2 stents were in-troduced into the external iliac artery. Due to signs of dis-section of the left femoral artery， open endarterectomy was performed. After primary wound closure， signs of acute left lower limb ischemia were detected. Immediate IV DSA was performed， revealing the dissection of the left profunda fem-oral artery and occlusion of the left superficial femoral ar-tery. The patient was operated on immediately with endar-terectomy of the branches with prosthetic patch of the left profunda femora artery and prosthetic PTFE femoro-pop-liteal (distal) by-pass. The patient required fluid and blood replacement. Progressive edema of the left lower limb and signs of developing compartment syndrome required fasci-otomy 4 hours after the by-pass surgery following the VAC dressing in the place of the open fasciotomy. Despite the treatment， the paresis of the left peroneal nerve persisted until the discharge day. The postoperative period was com-plicated by diarrhea on the third postoperative day. With no reaction to the treatment， and due to electrolyte imbal-ance with an unspecific increase in lactic acid， bowel isch-emia was suspected. Due to normal results of rectal exam-ination and rectoscopy， the angio CT was performed for evaluation of internal iliac arteries and blood supply of the sigmoid colon. The CT scan confirmed aneurysms eliminat-ed from circulation with normal blood flow in the endovas-cular prosthesis and iliac arteries. Celiac trunk， mesenter-ic superior and left renal artery were contrasting. CT scan confirmed distension bowel loop with level of fluids in the sigmoid colon interpreted by the radiologist as a possible ischemia. Both internal iliac arteries were found to be oc-cluded. The patient was operated on and focal necrosis of the sigmoid colon was found . Sigmoid resection within healthy tissue was performed with primary end-to-end anastomosis. The postoperative period was uncompli-cated. The patent was released with correct healing of the wounds and normal bowel movement and stools； however， persistent peroneal nerve paresis of the left lower extrem-ity was noticed. No signs of perigraft infection were found in control ultrasound.

【13】DISCUSSION

【14】Aortic stentgraft placement is a procedure with significantly lower 30-day mortality. Endovascular procedure is indicated in all cases of patients with high or moderate cardiovascu-lar risk . Concomitant morbidity or scheduled or past surgeries may also be indications for EVAR . In the pre-sented case the patient was disqualified from primary uro-logical kidney-saving procedures such as ESWL due to the possibility of sudden aneurysm rupture .EVAR has re-cently become the preferred treatment in such cases . However， this patient additionally was treated with nephros-tomy， which significantly increases the infection risk during the open procedure. The patient was diagnosed in 2004 but despite surgeons'advice declined diagnostics and surgery.

【15】Concomitant urological pathology on the day of admission complicated the decision regarding choice of intervention. The anatomy of the aneurysm permitted both open and en-dovascular procedures. To reduce perioperative infection risk， the endovascular procedure was chosen； however， the first angio CT underestimated the degree of atherosclerotic changes in the iliac and femoral arteries. The importance of correct preoperative anatomical assessment is stressed by the majority of reports on EVAR cases . Acute limb ischemia caused by arterial dissection is a known compli-cation of EVAR， but in this case both extremities required revascularization in hybrid open and endovascular meth-ods. Multiple vascular interventions may deteriorate the sta-tus of a patient， necessitating blood transfusion and caus-ing compartment syndrome. Even early fasciotomy could not prevent the complications of compartment syndrome， such as peroneal nerve paresis. Another complication that occurred during the treatment was sigmoid necrosis. The possibility of sigmoid necrosis after EVAR is widely discussed in the literature . In this patient， we found occlu-sion of both internal iliac arteries. Occlusion of the IMA was procedure-related. Many authors neglect this compli-cation and prefer to obliterate internal iliac arteries in the routine way during primary EVAR procedure . The presented case and experience from the other cases suggest the importance of preserving the internal iliac artery when-C ever possible . Primary assessment of the IMA (infe-rior mesenteric artery) and internal iliac arteries should be helpful in the choice between open or endovascular proce-dures. Retrospective analysis of CT scans taken before the surgery revealed that in such a development of atheroscle-rotic changes in the iliac arteries and femoral arteries， the open procedure may be safer for the patient in terms of risk of limb ischemia (common iliac arteries patent with-out significant atherosclerotic changes). Implantation of a straight tube graft could prevent the iliac and femoral dis-section and preserve both internal iliac arteries covered and occluded during EVAR

【16】Common vascular and urological interventions should also be taken in to consideration ， especially if the patient is undergoes an open operation for AAA. Unfortunately， ac-cording to the literature， this is not a common procedure due to the elevated risk of graft infection .

【17】CONCLUSIONS

【18】Multiple complications during EVAR may significantly re-duce the early benefit of the procedure. Correct preoper-ative assessment of CT scans can avoid inappropriate deci-sions regarding EVAR. In case of concomitant urological pathology， any surgical intervention (even emergency) should be made in cooperation with the vascular surgeon and urologist. The patient may benefit from simultaneous intervention.

【0】ABSTRACT Kocuria rosea is an Actinobacteria belonging to the family Micrococcaceae. Despite being rare， infections to Kocuria species have been reported more often in the last decade， usually in immunocompromised hosts. Here we report a case of a 62-year-old immunocompetent male， with a ventricular septal defect who was diagnosed with infective endocarditis due to Kocuria rosea identified in four blood cultures. The patient completed five weeks of empiric antibiotic combination therapy with complete resolution of the infection. Although infection by Kocuria species is rare， due to better identification methods， it is becoming a more frequent diagnosis. Further studies are needed to investigate the susceptibility and resistance of these pathogens in order to develop specific guidelines for antibiotic treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS Kocuria rosea， Infective endocarditis， Ventricular septal defect

【2】Introduction

【3】Kocuria rosea， is an Actinobacteria belonging to the family Mi-crococcaceae . Despite being rare， infections to Kocuria spp. have been reported more often in the last decade， usually in immunocompromised patients. Only five cases of infec-tive endocarditis (IE) by K. rosea have been cited in the English literature. Here， we report a case of IE due to Kocuria rosea， in a immunocompetent patient with a predisposing condition， ventricular septal defect (VSD).

【4】Case report

【5】A 62-year-old male， with the previous diagnosis of VSD and dilated myocardiopathy， presented with a 2-month history of vespertine fever， asthenia and anorexia. The patient denied other symptoms or epidemiological background. On physical exam-ination， pallor， fever (TT 38.1℃) and a holosystolic murmur best heard along the left sternal board. On admission， labora-tory studies showed leukopenia with 2100 WBC/ml， anaemia with an haemoglobin of 9.3g/dL， thrombocytopenia of 20000platelets/ml， an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 70mm and a CRP of 6.8mg/dL. With a clinical suspicion of infective endocarditis， the patient underwent a transthoracic echocardio-gram， which revealed the possibility of vegetation on the VSD. Empiric combination antibiotic therapy with intravenous (IV) ceftriaxone 2gm od and vancomycin 1.5gm bid was started. In order to make a definitive diagnosis， the patient was subjected to a transoesophageal echocardiogram， which confirmed a vege-tation of 3.2cm2 on the right side of de VSD. During this period， four blood cultures were obtained， first pair on day zero，before antibiotic therapy and second pair on day two after antibiotic therapy. All four samples showed Gram-positive cocci in pairs and tetrads. Replication on blood agar yielded small convex， pale-pink， non-haemolytic colonies that were Gram-positive in pairs and tetrads， catalase-positive， coagulase-negative and DNase-negative. Subsequent additional tests， such as bacitracin susceptibility and resistance to furazolidone， helped to discrimi-nate Micrococci from coagulase-negative Staphylococci(CoNS). Species identification as K. rosea was made using a Vitek 2 sys-tem (BioMerieux@， France). Antibiotic susceptibility test (AST) was performed， using CoNS breakpoints， showing sensibility to Benzylpenicillin， Ampicillin， Cefotaxime， Ceftriaxone， Clin-damycin， Vancomycin1.

【6】On day 22 of empiric antibiotic treatment， due to sustained fever， and persistence， though with smaller dimensions (1cm2)， of the vegetation image on the control transoesophageal echocar-diogram， IV gentamicin 240mg od was associated.

【7】The patient completed 36 days of ceftriaxone and vancomycin and 14 days of gentamicin with complete resolution of the clin-ical symptoms and imagological findings. Was discharged re-ferred to cardiac surgery consultation to evaluate the need to surgical closure of the VSD.

【8】Discussion

【9】Infective endocarditis (IE) is defined as an infection of the endo-cardium. Is a relatively rare disorder with an estimated incidence of 3-10 cases per 100 000 per year. Despite improvements in its management， it remains associated with high mortality and severe complications， as reflected by hospital mortality of about22%.

【10】This case is relevant， since we report a known and deadly infection caused by an atypical and rare agent， Kocuria rosea， with only five cases described. In this case， the VSD as an im-portant risk factor for IE associated with poor dental hygiene， probably lead to developing the infection. Kocuria rosea， is a Gram-positive， coagulase-negative， strictly aerobic， coccoid bacteria belonging to the class Actinobacteria， order Actinomyc-etales， family Micrococcaceae. There are about nineteen species of Kocuria identified， though only five are known to be oppor-tunistic pathogens. These bacteria may be found in drinking water sources， seed and fermented food. They form part of the normal flora in human beings and frequently colonize the skin， mucosa and oropharynx. Kocuria species can form a biofilm which explains the reported cases of infection associated with long-term catheters . Other predisposing factors include immunosuppression and congenital deformities. This case， along with other recent case reports， have shown that Kocu-ria spp. can cause disease not only in immunosuppressed， but also in immunocompetent patients， questioning the previous assumption that these were only opportunistic agents.

【11】The prevalence of infection due to Kocuria spp. can be un-derestimated considering their close similarity to CoNS. The basic criteria for discrimination between Micrococci and Staphy-lococci is based on Kocuria species sensitivity to bacitracin and lysozyme and resistance to nitrofurantoin/furazolidone. More recently the enhanced biochemical Vitek-2 system (BioMerieux@， France)， is being used rising de odds of correct species identifi-cation to 90-95%. This same system was used in our patient’s blood cultures.

【12】Since there are no accepted guidelines for antibiotic treat-ment nor， specific MIC or break points for Kocuria spp.patients are being treated according to sensitivity and resistance results based on Staphylococcus interpretive values. Our patient fully responded to triple antibiotic treatment with ceftriaxone， vancomycin and gentamicin.

【13】Conclusion

【14】Although infections due to Kocuria spp. are rare， it is becoming an increasingly frequent diagnosis， mostly due to availability of better identification methods， so clinicians must not underesti-mate these pathogens. Further studies are needed to investigate the susceptibility and resistance of Kocuria species in order to develop specific guidelines for antibiotic treatment.

【0】Background：

【1】Gallbladder torsion is a rare entity of acute abdomen that can be fatal if not diagnosed and treated promptly It presents in a multitude of ways but the most common is a presentation similar to acute cholecystitis. Diagnosis can be made clinically by abdominal ultrasound with Doppler flow， and treatment is detorsion with cholecystectomy.

【2】Case Report： A 57-year-old female presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain， bilious vomiting， and loose stools. An initial diagnosis of gastroenteritis was made， however， the patient did not respond to symp-tomatic treatment and continued having pain， nausea and vomiting. Abdominal ultrasound revealed signs of acute cholecystitis and the patient underwent an open cholecystectomy where the gallbladder was found to be black， gangrenous， and voluminous due to torsion. Detorsion and cholecystectomy were performed with-out any complications.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Gallbladder torsion is a rare entity of acute abdomen that can be fatal if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Gallbladder torsion should be a part of the differential diagnosis of any patient presenting with an acute ab-domen and unusual symptoms of acute cholecystitis.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Cholecystectomy·Cholecystitis· Gallbladder Diseases

【6】Gallbladder torsion with resulting volvulus is a rare entity of acute abdomen. It was first described in 1898 by Wendel in a25-year-old pregnant woman . Since then， over 500 cases of gallbladder torsion have been reported with an incidence of approximately 1 in 356 000 hospital admissions . The most common presentation of gallbladder volvulus is that of acute cholecystitis， and a preoperative diagnosis of gallbladder vol-vulus is rarely made . Unlike acute cholecystitis， gallbladder volvulus carries the risk of perforation ， thus early diagno-sis and prompt treatment of gallbladder volvulus is impera-tive， as it decreases mortality and morbidity from a perfo-rated gallbladder and ensuing peritonitis . In this report we present a case of galbladder volvulus that initially pre-sented as gastroenteritis then with the findings of acute cho-lecystitis on imaging.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 57-year-old female presented to the emergency department with severe upper abdominal pain， 2 episodes of bilious vomit-ing， and one episode of loose stools. The patient’s only medi-cal history is hypertension that is adequately controlled. On presentation she was hemodynamically stable and afebrile.

【9】On physical examination the patient had a soft non-distended abdomen with normal bowel sounds； epigastric pain on deep palpation was noted as well as right upper quadrant tender-ness， however Murphy's sign was negative. The patient's labo-ratory studies including leukocyte count， hepatic enzymes， and pancreatic enzymes were all within normal range.

【10】An initial diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis was made based upon the patient's presentation with vomiting and loose stools， as such the patient was given symptomatic treatment. The patient had no relief from the pain and was given pethi-dine 75 mg subcutaneously， also without improvement in pain. Due to these unusual findings， the patient was admitted to the hospital for further workup. During this time the patient was still experiencing nausea and vomiting resistant to medi-cations (metoclopramide and ondansetron).

【11】An abdominal ultrasound was performed which showed find-ings of acute cholecystitis with microlithiasis without signs of dilation of intra or extra-hepatic bile ducts. A diagnosis of acute cholecystitis was made， and the patient was planned for cholecystectomy less than 24 hours of admission. An open ap-proach was agreed upon due to the unusual presentation of re-sistant pain， recurrent vomiting， and a new finding on physical examination of a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant.

【12】Operative findings included a black， gangrenous， and volumi-nous gallbladder with a large mesentery displacing the gall-bladder from the liver bed . A clockwise torsion around the gallbladder axis was noted， detorsion was done manually， and the cholecystectomy proceeded without any complications. The patient was discharged home on the third day following surgery.

【13】Discussion

【14】Gallbladder volvulus is a rare condition that might carry signifi-cant mortality risk if not identified and treated early on in its course. The frequency of this disease increases with age， with some reports stating an average age between 60 and 80 years old . Gallbladder volvulus has a predilection among adult females with a female： male ratio of 4： 1， however， the reverse is true in the pediatric population with a female： male ratio of1： 3 . The literature reports a mortality rate up to 6%  if promptly treated and 100% if left untreated 

【15】It is hypothesized that certain congenital gallbladder anoma-lies might predispose to torsion. Of particular importance is the free-floating gallbladders classified by Gross  into 2types： type A where a long and wide mesentery supports both the gallbladder and the cystic duct， and type B， where an in-complete mesentery supports only the cystic duct. Four other anatomic variants of the gallbladder have been described that might increase the risk of gallbladder volvulus . The first variant is a congenital anomaly where the pars cystica fails to migrate normally from the hepatic diverticulum during week4 to week 7 of embryological development which causes a complete absence of the gallbladder mesentery. The result is a free-floating gallbladder suspended by the cystic duct and artery alone. The second abnormality is a result of normal ag-ing where the gallbladder mesentery elongates and becomes mobile； this combined with atrophy of the liver increases the risk of gallbladder torsion. The third anomaly is described as a detached fundus of the gallbladder from the liver bed， increasing its mobility and the risk of torsion. The fourth vari-ant is also the rarest and is a normal gallbladder fixed to a mobile hepatic lobe. Volvulus might be complete (180°tor-sion or less) or incomplete (more than 180°) ， and it might be clockwise or anticlockwise . Our patient had a large and elongated gallbladder mesentery which is the result of nor-mal aging and might have contributed to the clockwise tor-sion of the gallbladder.

【16】Clinical presentation of gallbladder volvulus is non-specific and variable， it ranges from acute abdomen to chest pain， but most commonly present similarly to acute cholecystitis with right upper quadrant pain . Presentation can be cor-related with the type of torsion， recurrent episodes of incom-plete torsion might lead to recurrent pain ， as such a careful history must be obtained from the patient. Clinical symptoms include abdominal pain， nausea and vomiting， and a palpable mass in the right quadrant . A triple triad has been described to clinically differentiate between acute cholecys-titis and gallbladder volvulus ； the first is patient char-acteristics where there is increased risk of torsion among the elderly， thin， or patients with spine deformities. The second triad is based on clinical symptoms of sudden onset pain， right upper quadrant pain， and emesis all of which favor gallblad-der torsion. The third triad is of clinical signs seen on physical examination； a non-toxic appearing patient with pulse tem-perature discrepancy and a palpable mass in the right up-per quadrant make the diagnosis of gallbladder torsion more likely. The case presented here is unusual， as the patient had signs and symptoms suggestive of gastroenteritis which is an extremely unusual presentation for gallbladder volvulus that has not been described in the literature.

【17】Preoperative diagnosis of gallbladder volvulus has increased from 10%  to 26% ， most likely due to advancements in imaging modalities. Ultrasound is the preferred modality， as a first line of imaging ， to diagnose both acute chole-cystitis and gallbladder volvulus， however distinguishing be-tween these 2 entities might not always be possible， as both might show wall thickening and surrounding edema with gall-stones ， as was the case with our patient. Another differ-ential diagnosis that can be made based on ultrasound find-ings is acalculous cholecystitis since gallbladder torsion might present with no gallstones . Certain signs on ultrasound have been solely described in gallbladder torsion which might assist in diagnosis ， these include a free-floating gallblad-der detached from the liver bed or a floating gallbladder with discontinuity of the lumen. Another finding described in gall-bladder volvulus is the presence of a continuous hypoechoic zone between 2 echogenic areas which signifies venous and lymphatic stasis . Doppler ultrasound can confirm the diag-nosis by the absence of blood flow in the cystic artery ， however this method is not routinely used probably due to the low index of suspicion for gallbladder torsion.

【18】To be more precise ultrasonography and computed tomography(CT) are the primary imaging approaches used for diagnosis. But the difference a CT scan can reveal a "floating gallbladder”with gallbladder wall thickening. A magnetic resonance imag-ing (MRI) can help with the imaging of a twisted cystic duct， and T2 weighted images are beneficial for evaluating necro-sis of the gallbladder wall. Early diagnosis of gallbladder tor-sion can help to prevent life-threatening complications such as gallbladder gangrene， perforations causing bilious perito-nitis， and other infections. For preventing this sequela， ultra-sonography and CT are the primary imaging approaches.Early use of appropriate imaging prevents complications， reduces mortality and morbidity rates， and decreases hospitalization costs .

【19】Treatment of gallbladder volvulus is emergency cholecystec-tomy， as delay in treatment might increase the risk of perfo-ration， peritonitis， and death . A laparoscopic approach has been described and is the preferred method for detorsion and cholecystectomy . We opted for an open approach as the diagnosis was unclear and the patient had an unusual presentation of what was presumed to be acute cholecystitis based on ultrasound. Percutaneous drainage of the gallblad-der might sometime be wrongly performed due to the initial diagnosis of acute cholecystitis in an elderly patient with con-traindications to laparoscopy . Drainage should not be per-formed for gallbladder volvulus as it will only address the pa-tient's symptoms， and the torsion will continue to exist further increasing the risk of perforation and peritonitis .

【20】Conclusions

【21】Gallbladder volvulus is an uncommon occurrence that is mainy seen among elderly women and is frequently undiagnosed pre-operatively due to unspecific presentations that might mimic acute cholecystitis. Improvements in imaging modalities have assisted physicians in making the diagnosis of gallbladder vol-vulus； ultrasound is the modality of choice as a first line of imaging ， and Doppler might be used if there is a high in-dex of suspicion for gallbladder volvulus. Once the diagnosis of gallbladder volvulus is made， prompt treatment with lap-aroscopic cholecystectomy must be performed. Early detec-tion and prompt treatment are imperative as delay in diag-nosis might be fatal.

【0】Background：

【1】Bronchial foreign body aspiration is rare problem in adults. However， it is not an uncommon prob-lem， particularly in children， the elderly and patients with neurological impairment. Aspiration of foreign bodies into the airways can remain undetected for months to years.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We described here a case of 78-years-old nonsmoker male， who was hospitalized in our Department because of radiological and clinical suspicion of pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient underwent bronchoscopy and computed tomography. On flexible bronchoscopy， a tumor with necrosis oc-cluded right upper lobe bronchus was identified. A CT scan of the thorax showed cavitations and fibrous changes in the right upper lobe as well as lymphadenopathy with right upper bronchus compression. However， the pulmonary tuberculosis as well as lung cancer were not confirmed in bacteriological and histopathological examination. A second fibreaptic bronchoscopy was done to evaluate the aetiology of lung abnormality. This showed the foreign body and allowed the success-ful removal of chicken bone. The patients recovered with no residual respiratory symptoms over one year.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】The foreign body may be present in the bronchi despite complete unawareness of the patient about aspiration and should be considered in the diagnosis of clinical symptoms and radiological lesions of unclear aetiology. In some cases despite the radiological features of tuberculosis， more intensive examinations should be administrated which could confirm diagnosis. In such cases bronchosco-pies， sometimes repeated， are necessary.

【6】key words： foreign body aspiration· lung tumour· tuberculosis

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Foreign body in the bronchi is rare in adults， more often it is found in children， the elderly and patients with neu-rological disorders \[l. According to literature， the time between the foreign body aspiration and the diagno-sis may be very long， even 40 years . Many patients are not aware of aspiration and the presenting symptoms are dyspnoea， fever， cough or radiological findings . The diagnosis and treatment are based on bronchoscopy . Bronchoscopy was first used to remove the foreign body by Gustaw Killian one hundred years ago .

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】A 78-year-old patient was admitted for diagnostic procedures due to chest X-ray changes-infiltration with disintegration in the upper right lung. The patient had the about l-month history of subfibrile body temperature， malaise， cough with the mucopurulent sputum expectorated.

【11】The history concerned past diseases：

【12】1980 - myocardial infarction； 1990 - cerebral stroke， sus-pected Parkinson's disease；1995-tuberculosis，bacteriologically not confirmed， treat-ed routinely for 6 months-radiological improvement， 2001- exudative non-specific right pleurisy； 2003- right-side pneumonia.

【13】For 3 years the patient was treated by GP due to chronic ob-structive pulmonary disease， periodic symptoms of ulcer dis-ease， benign prostate hypertrophy， nephrolithiasis.

【0】Background：

【1】Antisynthetase syndrome (ASS) is a rare systemic autoimmune disease. The clinical features of ASS include in-terstitial lung disease (ILD)， myositis， arthritis， Raynaud's phenomenon， mechanic’s hands， and unexplained fever. There is a paucity of reported cases and management guidelines in pregnancy. This report describes the case of a 25-year-old Saudi woman with a 2-year history of ASS with ILD who commenced azathioprine treat-ment in the third trimester and had a successful birth at term.

【2】Case Report： A 25-year-old Saudi primigravida woman with a 2-year history of ASS with ILD presented at 26 weeks of ges-tation after being lost to prepregnancy follow-up and discontinuing her medications. Azathioprine treatment was commenced， and despite poor prepregnancy follow-up， her pregnancy remained uneventful until 39 weeks， when fetal ultrasonography showed oligohydramnios. Therefore， labor induction was initiated， and she deliv-ered vaginally with no postpartum complications or flare-ups.

【3】Conclusions： The multisystem autoimmune disease ASS is a rare condition， and there are no clinical guidelines for its man-agement in pregnant women. This case report highlights some aspects of ASS management and the impor-tance of a multidisciplinary approach.

【4】Keywords： Anti-Jo-1 Autoantibody·Antisynthetase Syndrome · Pregnancy· Myositis·

【5】Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia

【6】Antisynthetase syndrome (ASS) is a rare systemic autoim-mune disease with an estimated prevalence of 1 to 9 per100 000 . ASS is characterized by autoantibodies against aminoacy. transfer ribonucleic acid synthetases (tRNAs). The most identified tRNA autoantibody is anti-histidyl (o-1)， a myositis-specific antibody ； others include anti-threo-ny! (anti-PL7) and anti-alany! (anti-PL12) . Publications report that ASS symptoms and morbidity vary depending on the identified antibodies . For instance，anti-Sjogren's syn-drome-related antigen A (anti-Ro/SSA)， a myositis-associated antibody ， has been associated with ASS and a predisposi-tion to severe ILD and lung fibrosis .

【7】ASS diagnosis is challenging due to symptom heterogene-ity and similarity to those of other connective tissue diseases and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies . Clinical fea-tures include ILD， myositis， arthritis， Raynaud's phenomenon， mechanic's hands， and unexplained fever . Pulmonary hypertension is also associated with ASS . Two di-agnostic criteria have been proposed by Solomon el al and Connors et al  . No unified treatment protocol exists for ASS ， and the systems involved and symptom severity are considered when planning the management . The typical first-line treatment is corticosteroids； however， when corticosteroids are used as monotherapy， lung disease frequently recurs with tapering . Other agents used as adjunct and maintenance treatments include azathioprine， mycophenolate mofetil， tacrolimus， cyclosporine， cyclophospha-mide， and rituximab . When the symptoms improve and the disease stabilizes， corticosteroids are often gradual-ly discontinued . For treatment in pregnancy， there are no management guidelines， and the literature is scarce . This report describes the case of a 25-year-old Saudi woman with a 2-year history of ASS with ILD who commenced aza-thioprine treatment in the third trimester and had a succeSS-ful birth at term despite poor follow-up.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 25-year-old Saudi primigravida woman at 26 weeks of ges-tation presented to the pulmonology clinic for a follow-up. She had a past medical history of ASS with ILD and no surgical his-tory. She had no allergies and no history of blood transfusion， smoking， or alcohol or substance use. Her medications includ-ed oral ferrous sulfate-folic acid 150-0.5 mg and oral calcium carbonate 600 mg daily.

【13】She was diagnosed with ASS at the age of 23. At that time， she presented to the pulmonology clinic with 2 months of short-ness of breath， nonproductive cough， arthritis， and mechan-ic's hands. She had no past medical history or exposure to oc-cupational or environmental agents. Investigations showed positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) and anti-Ro/SSA. Salivary gland/lip biopsy samples for autoimmune sialadenitis/Sjogren's syndrome， anti-smooth muscle antibody (ASMA)， myeloper-oxidase anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic (MPO)， and ribonucleo-protein (RNP) antibodies were negative. Pulmonary function test (PFT) results showed a restrictive lung pattern . Echocardiography was normal. High-resolution computed to-mography (HRCT) showed peripheral lower lobe predominant interlobular septal thickening with ground-glass attenuation and traction bronchiectasis with no evidence of honeycomb-ing， consistent with combined nonspecific interstitial pneumo-nia (NSIP)-organizing pneumonia (OP) . A transbron-chial biopsy sample from the left lower lobe showed chronic inflammatory cell infiltration and early Masson’s body forma-tion consistent with secondary cryptogenic OP. ILD (NSIP-OP) was diagnosed based on symptoms， PFT， HRCT， and transbron-chial biopsy. ASS was diagnosed according to Solomon's and Connor's criteria  . Her daily treatment includ-ed oral prednisolone 25 mg， oral trimethoprim/sulfamethoxa-zole 400 mg/80 mg， and oral mycophenolate mofetil 2 g，and she did not require supplemental oxygen. At the 3-month fol-low-up， her symptoms had improved， but her PFT results had not . Accordingly， rituximab was added (1 g intrave-nous infusion every 2 weeks for 1 month， then 1 dose every 6months). Three months later， PFT results improved ， but HRCT showed no significant change from the previous study. At the 18-month follow-up， PFT results showed fur-ther improvement ， although HRCT revealed no sig-nificant change . As she was planning pregnancy， she was advised to discontinue mycophenolate mofetil， ta-per prednisolone to 5 mg， commence azathioprine， and re-turn after 1 month.

【14】Unfortunately， she was lost to follow-up. Then， at 26 weeks of gestation， she presented to the pulmonology clinic and had stopped taking all the medications 2 months before concep-tion. She had mild shortness of breath but no other respiratory symptoms，myositis， or arthritis. Oral azathioprine 50 mg daily was initiated with the goal of increasing the dose to 100 mg. When she returned for a follow-up after 1 week， her complete blood count (CBC) revealed a normal white blood cell (WBC) count and low hemoglobin (7.5 g/dL). She received 6 doses of200 mg of intravenous iron sucrose， and she was referred to the obstetric maternal-fetal medicine clinic.

【15】At her obstetric booking visit at 29 weeks of gestation， she reported an improvement in her shortness of breath. Fetal ul-trasonography showed normal anatomy and heart rate， and weight was estimated to be within the normal range. Her WBC count was normal， her hemoglobin level increased to 9.6 g/dL， and her oral glucose challenge test result was normal. Fetal echocardiogram was ordered due to the presence of anti-Ro/SSA， but， unfortunately， she missed that appointment. After1 week， a multidisciplinary meeting with her pulmonologist took place to establish a management plan. The impression was that her disease was stable， it would not affect the timing and mode of delivery， and the shortness of breath was likely due to low hemoglobin. Azathioprine was increased to 100 mg. Although she was not followed up regularly， she was compli-ant with azathioprine. There was no concern for severe pulmo-nary impairment， and a repeat PFT was not performed， as she was asymptomatic and did not require supplemental oxygen.

【16】Her pregnancy was uneventful until she presented to the Emergency Department at 39 weeks of gestation due to de-creased fetal movement for 2 days. She had no labor pain or vaginal leakage. Her vital signs were within the normal range， and fetal heart tracing by cardiotocography was cate-gory 1. Fetal ultrasonography showed oligohydramnios (am-niotic fluid index 3.1)， and the estimated fetal weight was within the normal range. Due to oligohydramnios， labor was induced by dinoprostone 10 mg vaginal insert， and labor pro-gressed smoothly. She received epidural anesthesia and had a vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery due to poor maternal ef-fort. She delivered a girl with an Apgar score of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes， respectively， and the cord pH was 7.26. The patient and her baby were discharged home on day 2 post-partum in good condition.

【17】At 2-month follow-up， she was asymptomatic and compliant with azathioprine. She was advised to continue follow-up with her pulmonologist and present for preconception counseling before planning subsequent pregnancies.

【18】Discussion

【19】Although our patient stopped her preconception treatment without consultation， conceived only 2 months after myco-phenolate mofetil withdrawal， and was not adherent to her follow-up， she had good outcomes without maternal or fetal morbidities other than oligohydramnios. This case highlights some aspects of optimal ASS management in pregnancy that our patient missed.

【20】The effect of ASS on pregnancy and management has been ex-trapolated from other connective tissue and autoimmune dis-orders . The possible morbidities include preeclampsia，fe-tal growth restriction， prematurity， congenital heart block， and neonatal lupus in the presence of anti-SSA/Ro or anti-Sjogren’s syndrome-related antigen B (anti-SSB/La) . The disease course may partly depend on the prepregnancy status， as ev-idenced by previous publications . Similar to our pa-tient， a patient with stable disease preconception who was on azathioprine and prednisone had an uncomplicated pregnan-cy and term delivery . Another successful outcome was re-ported for a patient with severe ILD and fibrosis who was on long-term rituximab infusion for 5 years and conceived 2 years after clinical condition improvement and treatment discontin-uation . Adverse outcomes were described in patients with severe disease. One patient had severe myositis and was new-ly diagnosed in her second trimester， but her pregnancy end-ed with a miscarriage . Another patient with pulmonary hypertension and substantial parenchymal restrictive disease prior to conception had worsening PFT results and required supplemental oxygen during pregnancy. She had an iatrogenic preterm delivery at 35 weeks of gestation due to oligohydram-nios attributed to chronic maternal hypoxemia .Although our patient developed oligohydramnios， it was unlikely due to chronic maternal hypoxemia， as her disease was quiescent.

【21】Management in pregnancy starts with a preconception visit to plan conception when the disease is in remission， discon-tinue teratogenic medications， and perform baseline PFT and echocardiography . Antepartum， low-dose aspirin is initiated at between 12 and 28 weeks of gestation (optimally before 16 weeks) as recommended by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists-Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guidelines for pregnant women with autoimmune disorders to decrease the risk of preeclampsia . Moreover， serial fetal growth assessment should be considered， and fetal echocardiography should be done to assess congenital heart block in patients with anti-Ro/SSA or anti-SSB/La . For treatment in pregnancy， corticosteroids， azathioprine， and cy-closporine are safely used in pregnant women with systemic lupus erythematosus ； cyclophosphamide is contrain-dicated due to the increased risk of miscarriage and congen-ital anomalies ； and because data on rituximab are limited， rituximab discontinuation before conception is ad-vised . Tacrolimus and cyclosporine are safe options for pregnant women after organ transplantation； however， mycophenolate mofetil is contraindicated， as it is associated with a high risk of miscarriage and congenital anomalies and must be discontinued 3-6 months before pregnancy . As the course of ASS is unknown， a multidisciplinary approach is advised， particularly if severe manifestations such as pul-monary hypertension or severe ILD develop to alter the treat-ment and timing of delivery.

【22】Conclusions

【23】The multisystem autoimmune disease ASS is a rare condi-tion， and there are no clinical guidelines for its management in pregnant women. This case highlights some aspects of ASS management in pregnancy and the importance of a multidis-ciplinary approach.

【0】ABSTRACT Non-traumatic spontaneous subcapsular renal hematoma， also known as Winderlich syndrome， is a rare entity that is associated with a few renal pathologies， mainly tumours or cysts， anticoagulant drugs administration or unknown reasons. We present a case of an elderly patient that presented with spontaneous subcapsular renal hematoma and complete deterioration of his kidney due to severe pyonephrosis that was managed conservatively.

【1】KEYWORDS Pyonephrosis，Subcapsular hematoma， Spontaneous renal hematoma， Wiinderlich syndrome

【2】Case report

【3】A 94-year-old male with a medical history of chronic kidney failure (CKD-stage ⅣV)， atrophic left kidney， hypertension， coro-nary heart disease and a recent diagnosis of colorectal cancer was hospitalized due to febrile urinary tract infection (UTI). The patient had been submitted to non-contrast CT scan one month ago that showed a mild left renal hydronephrosis， and an at-rophic kidney was recognized as well as a left sigmoid mass which was palliatively treated with external radiation therapy alone due to rectal hemorrhage. Initially， the patient was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics， one blood transfusion and close monitoring. Concomitantly， a routine ultrasound check for UTI revealed a huge left urinary dilatation indicating pyonephrosis. A subsequent CT scan， however， demonstrated a complete de-terioration of the left kidney with severe hydronephrosis and a large subcapsular hematoma . Additionally， the obstruction was not extended towards the ureter， and there was no perirenal leakage. The patient had a normal cognitive func-tion and did not report any injury incident， and he also was completely asymptomatic. The anticoagulation therapy had al- ready been stopped one month ago during the pelvic radiation therapy. The patient was unwilling and unfit to undergo the sug-gested surgery. Thus， more conservative treatment was decided which included a nephrostomy tube placement under careful ultrasonographic guidance. The subcapsular hematoma was aspirated too， using a second puncture. 900ml of hemorrhagic-purulent fluid was aspirated in total. The fluid culture revealed a fungal infection and the patient was treated accordingly. The urine production from the left nephrostomy was less than 150ml per day due to the history of renal deficiency. The patient was finally discharged three days later with no signs of infection. A second CT scan two weeks later  showed the normal position of the nephrostomy tube with the absence of any pyelocalyceal dilatation and a recurrence in the subcapsular hematoma which remained stable under close follow-up up to 6months with no need for further treatment.

【4】Discussion

【5】In our case， the rare entity of spontaneous renal hematoma， also known as Winderlich syndrome ， is possibly associated with the sudden severe obstructive pyonephrosis at the atrophic kid-ney. No other renal pathology was present， such as， tumours， angiomyolipomas or cysts that could explain this presentation as literature describes . Furthermore， the prior radiation beam field was out of site， and there were no signs of external injury or history of trauma. Lastly， the patient was not under anti-coagulation therapy that could be related to the spontaneous hematoma . Surgical treatment may be necessary， yet con-servative treatment is feasible， especially in elderly and frail patients.

【0】Background： Priapism is rarely reported as a potential complication after the cardiac ablation procedure. We report the case of a teenager admitted for atrial flutter ablation who developed priapism following the procedure.

【1】Case Report：

【2】A 16-year-old male with episodic atrial flutter came to our hospital for an electrophysiological study and cath-eter ablation. During the procedure， he was given l propofol for anesthesia and lV heparin for anticoagula-tion. After the procedure， nursing noted that he had an erection， which persisted for 5 h， with complaints of discomfort. There was no known history of sickle cell disease or trauma to the perineum， nor did he endorse any prior prolonged erections. On physical examination， he had a circumcised phallus with rigid and non-ten-der corpora cavernosa. He was given 5 mg terbutaline PO， without improvement. Three hours later， a second dose of terbutaline was given. In addition， a penis corporal venous blood gas was taken， and the result was consistent with an ischemic priapism. He had detumescence 1-2 min later. The total duration of his priapism was 8 h. There was no swelling， pain， or any sequelae after detumescence.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Although priapism rarely occurs as a complication following catheter ablation procedures due to propofol use， prolonged priapism can result in corporal fibrosis and cause future erectile dysfunction. Recognition and treat-ment of priapism in the postoperative period may be delayed due to a patient's hesitance to express concerns. To prevent future erectile dysfunction， signs of priapism should be included in routine postoperative evalua-tion in male patients.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Catheter Ablation ·Heparin· Priapism·Propofol

【6】Cardiac catheter ablation is an established procedure for treatment of cardiac arrhythmias in both adults and children. The procedure complications reported in the literature usually include vascular and/or conduction system injuries. Priapism， although reported as a possible complication of catheter ab-lation due to propofol use ， is usually not mentioned as a potential complication of the procedure to the male patients or to their parents. We report such a case in a teenager ad-mitted for atrial flutter catheter ablation， in whom priapism was treated successfully.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 16-year-old male had several episodes of palpitations at age15. He had an episode of palpitations while he was running in school at age 16. He went to an emergency department， with an ECG showing a narrow QRS tachycardia of 163 bpm. The heart rate slowed from 163 to 148 bpm be-fore adenosine was given， which revealed underlying atrial flutter waves at 300 bpm . He was admitted to the hospital and had several episodes of nonsustained atrial flut-ter shown on the telemetry recordings.

【9】He was discharged home without medication and was sched-uled for an electrophysiological study and catheter ablation.

【10】In the baseline electrophysiological study， there were no dual atrioventricular nodal pathways， no accessory pathway， no ventricular-atrial conduction， and no inducible supraventricu-lar tachycardia or atrial flutter. With isoproterenol challenge， there was still no tachycardia induced. By using an irrigated tip radiofrequency ablation catheter， cavotricuspid isthmus lin-ear ablation resulted in bi-directional conduction block through the ablation line. The procedure lasted for 2 h， during which he was given I propofol for anesthesia (total dose of bolus plus infusion： 3215 mg) and IV heparin for anticoagulation(total dose： 90 units/kg).

【11】Shortly after arrival to the intermediate care unit after the pro-cedure， a nurse noted that the patient had an erection. Five hours later， his mother reported that his erection persisted and he started having some discomfort. There was no known his-tory of sickle cell disease or trauma to the perineum， nor did he endorse any prior prolonged erections. He denied any pre-vious history of using alcohol or illicit drugs.

【12】On physical examination， he had a circumcised phallus with rigid and non-tender corpora cavernosa， glans soft， testes de-scended and without masses bilaterally. 【13】At 8-month follow-up， there was no reported arrhythmia or sexual dysfunction.

【15】Priapism is defined as a penile erection that persists beyond4 h and is unrelated to sexual interest or stimulation . It can be classified into ischemic (low-flow)， arterial (high-flow)， or stuttering (recurrent or intermittent) . Ischemic priapism is the most common form， accounting for >95% of all priapism episodes . This condition can occur in males of all ages， including neonates. While cavernous blood gas values in men with nonischemic priapism are similar to the blood gas values of arterial blood， it typically has a p02 of <30 mmHg， pCo2of >60 mmHg， and pH <7.25 in patients with ischemic pria-pism . This is similar to the cavernous blood gas analysis of our case， and confirmed the diagnosis of ischemic priapism The most common causes of priapism in children are sickle cell disease (65%)， leukemia (10%)， trauma (10%)， idiopathic(10%)， and pharmacologically induced (5%) . Although it is rare， there are 3 reports of propofol inducing priapism in the literature ， 2 of them confirmed by rechallenge . Similar to the case reported by Vesta et al. of a 17-year-old with supraventricular tachycardia catheter ablation who de-veloped priapism ， our patient， without any known hema-tological disease and who received l propofol as anesthesia， might have had propofol-induced priapism. The mechanism of propofol-induced priapism remains poorly understood， but could be due to sympathetic vasoconstrictor action or parasym-pathetic vasodilatory action， or nitric oxide-mediated smooth-muscle relaxation.

【16】There are rare reports of heparin causing priapism .Our patient received I heparin for anticoagulation during the pro-cedure. The mechanism could be veno-occlusion secondary to platelet aggregation triggered by antiplatelet antibodies， a clin-ical sequela of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia ， but the fact that our patient had no previous exposure to hepa-rin， and because the priapism occurred within 3 h after expo-sure， argues against this hypothesis. Unfortunately， no platelet count was obtained in our case during his priapism episode.

【17】The mechanism of ischemic priapism is that a persistent cor-poral smooth-muscle relaxation compresses the subtunical veins and prevents sinusoidal outflow. When the intracorpo-real pressure is increased above the mean arterial pressure of the cavernosal arteries， no inflow of blood can occur. Because prolonged priapism can result in corporal fibrosis and cause future erectile dysfunction ， it is a true emergency and should be handled with the same urgency as an ischemic heart attack medical emergency.
