【20】were administered preoperatively. Given that NSAIDs can in-crease the likelihood of bleeding complications of DOACs ， they were also considered as a trigger for DAH. Furthermore， hemorrhagic events due to concurrent administration of dab-igatran and cephalosporins have been reported . Although there are no reports about hemorrhagic events due to concur-rent administration of apixaban and cephalosporins， DAH was triggered by the drug interaction between antibiotics and apix-aban in the present case. The calculated imputability score was13， because there was no cause of DAH other than the effects of apixaban， and DAH was a reported adverse event that im-proved with discontinuation . Although the evaluation did not reveal any infection， we cannot exclude the possibili-ty that bacterial pneumonia might have contributed to DAH.

【21】The onset of DOAC-associated DAH is not limited to the early stages of medication initiation. With the increase in the num-ber of DOAC prescriptions ，similar cases are expected more frequently in clinical practice. Although DOACs are generally as-sociated with lower rates of fatal bleeding than those associated with warfarin in elderly people ， it should be recognized that DAH can occur with various triggers in patients taking DOACs.

【22】Conclusions

【23】The onset of DOAC-associated DAH is not limited to the early stages of medication initiation. Various triggers， such as mul-tiple surgeries， infections， and drug interactions， can induce DAH in patients receiving DOACs.

【0】ABSTRACT Aberrant expression of fibroblast growth factor and its receptors plays an essential role in carcinogenesis. Here we report that local application of etamsylate， an inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor signalling pathways， led to a clinical improvement in a patient with squamous lung cell carcinoma.

【1】KEYWORDS Squamous lung cell carcinoma， Etamsylate， Fibroblast growth factor.

【2】Introduction

【3】Deregulation of the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) and FGF receptor (FGFR) network frequently occurs in tumours due to gene amplification， activating mutations and oncogenic fu-sions. Thus， the development of FGF/FGFR pathways targeting therapies is the focus of several preclinical and clinical studies. FGF/FGFR pathways have been proposed to be involved in the pathophysiology of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung . Here we present a patient with squamous lung cell carcinoma treated with inhaled etamsylate， a well-characterized inhibitor of FGF/FGFR network .

【4】Case presentation

【5】A 45 years-old woman was brought to Pneumology department at the Universitary Hospital Ramón y Cajal with substantial dyspnea. Transthoracic electrocardiogram and transesophageal echography revealed a large pericardial effusion and collapse of the right and left atria in end-diastole， which is consistent with cardiac tamponade.Haemoglobin saturation was 94% in2，5 liters of O2. Chest x-ray showed left pulmonary lobe atelec-tasis and mediastinal effusion . Bronchoscopy revealed a tumour partially occluding the left main bronchus. A biopsy was taken， which led to a diagnosis of squamous lung cell car-cinoma. The patient was then stabilized with inhaled oxygen， corticoid therapy and bronchodilators. Never a retraction of the tumour was observed within three days of the stabilization treat-ment protocol. After three days of protocol stabilization therapy treatment with etamsylate was started. Etamsylate (Dycinone. Sanofi-Aventis. Paris. France) was administrated through a va-porized solution (500mg)， mixed with aspirated air， using an electronic device to disperse medication in aerosol form (eFlow rapid， PARI GmbH 82319 Sternberg. Germany). After four days of etamsylate treatment， roenterographies showed a drastic re-duction of both mediastinal effusion and atelectasis  and the degree of dyspnea no longer required oxygen therapy. Despite amelioration， unfortunately， the patient died the next day due to cardiac complications unrelated to the treatment.

【6】Discussion

【7】with lung adenocarcinoma . On the basis of these data， it has been proposed that FGF represents a promising therapeu-tic target for lung tumours . As a milestone in developing rational and safe therapies against FGF activities in neoplasms， we have spent great efforts in the development of synthetic FGF inhibitors . We have shown that 2，5-dihydroxyphenyl sulfonate salts (etamsylate and dobesilate) interact with both FGF and its receptors， displacing heparin from its binding site， modifying the tridimensional structure of the protein and its receptor recognizing site and， consequently， dissociating the receptor-growth factor signalling complex . These proper-ties may account for the efficacy of the treatment. Therefore etamsylate therapy could be an option in treating squamous lung cell carcinomas.

【8】Conclusion

【9】Etamsylate is an old medicament showing markedly anti-inflammatory and anti-angiogenic activities that can interrupt inflammatory and angiogenic network during origin and pro-gression of oncogenesis， through blockade of FGF signalling pathways， providing a treatment alternative for squamous lung cell carcinoma.

【0】Background：

【1】Etretinate， an aromatique retinoid， has been used to treat severe or treatment-resistant psoria-sis， and has been found to cause transient， mild abnormalities of liver function tests in about one third of patients. Significant liver disease may occur in a few patients， ranging from acute hepatitis to chronic， aggressive hepatitis and cirrhosis.

【2】Case report：

【3】A case of chronic hepatitis associated with steatosis and fibrosis in a 39-year-old male patient treated with etretinate for severe palmoplantar psoriasis is reported. Results of periodical liver function tests were still normal 4 and 8 weeks after initiation of etretinate therapy， but became abnormal 12 weeks later， when asthenia was referred and liver enzyme levels were found to be elevated. The liver enzyme levels gradually decrease after therapy with retinoid was stopped， but these biochemical abnormalities were still evident 5 years later. The liver biopsy showed small inflammatory cell infiltrates， in addition to initial， slight fibrosis， steatosis， and ductular proliferation， and ultrastructural study of biopsy specimens demonstrated diffuse abnormalities， consistent with a drug-related， chronic liver damage.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Etretinate therapy may lead to a wide spectrum of hepatotoxic reactions， ranging from non-specific reactive hepatitis to cirrhosis， and requires a close monitoring of liver function during the first 6 months.

【6】Key words： etretinate · aromatic retinoid · psoriasis · chronic hepatitis · steatosis · fibrosis Etretinate， an aromatique synthetic derivative of vitamin A， has been found to be particularly effective in the therapy of severe or disabling， treatment-resistant， pustular psoriasis and other disorders of keratinization (such as ichthyosis and diskeratosis). At the doses usually administered， the most common side effects are represented by cheilitis， xerosis， exfoliation of palms and soles， alopecia， pruritus， teratogenicity， hypertriglyceridemia and abnormality of liver function tests， including transient， mild increases of transaminase， alkaline phosphatase， and bilirubin， which generally returned to normal shortly after discontinuation of the retinoid therapy . Nevertheless， in a few patients etretinate treatment may lead to significant elevation of liver enzyme levels， that persists for several months， and histologically confirmed chronic liver damage . In1978， the first 2 cases of chronic aggressive hepatitis were described by Fredriksson as a possible com-plication of palmoplantar psoriasis treated with aromatic retinoid， and more than 20 cases of etretinate-induced histologically confirmed hepato-toxicity have been reported to date by the literature. Histological examination of hepatic specimens in these cases has shown a wide spectrum of liver damage， including acute hepatitis， chronic active hepatitis， steatosis， cholestasis， fibrosis and cirrhosis.

【7】A case of chronic liver disease associated with steatosis and mild fibrosis is reported in a 39-year-old male patient after a 3-month etretinate therapy administered for severe palmoplantar psoriasis.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】A 39-year-old male patient with a 12-year history of severe palmoplantar psoriasis began therapy with oral etretinate (1 mg/Kg/day)， because previous treatment with oral tetracycline， psoralen photochemotherapy， topical steroids and low-voltage X-rays was unsuc-cessful. Routine liver function studies before the first dose of etretinate were normal and the patient did not receive any other systemic medication during admin-istration of aromatic retinoid. Results of periodical liver function tests were still normal 4 and 8 weeks after initiation of etretinate therapy， but became abnormal 12 weeks later， when asthenia was referred and liver enzyme levels were found to be elevated(serum glutamic-oxalacetic transaminase or SGOT，129 IO； serum glutamic-pyruvate transaminase or SGPT，225 IO； y-glutamine transferase or y-GT，527IU). Even though pustular eruptions have been shown a good clinical response and the patient remained healthy， without generalized symptoms of hypersensi-tivity (such as fever， skin rash， itching or eosinophilia)， etretinate therapy was discontinued 3 months after the start. History of other hepatotoxic medications(for exemple methotrexate)， alcohol or drug abuse， and transfusions was carefully excluded； serologies for hepatitis A， B and C viruses， cytomegalovirus， Epstein-Barr virus， Toxoplasma gondii and autoanti-bodies proved negative； glycaemic， lipidemic， copper and iron outlines were normal， such as serum α，-antit-rypsin level. Liver ultrasonographic study demon-strated slight hepatomegaly associated with moderate steatosis， confirmed by abdomen contrast-enhanced CT scan， without focal lesions.

【10】The liver enzyme levels gradually decrease after therapy with retinoid was stopped： 4 weeks later， transaminase were almost normal (SGOT， 39 IU； SGPT， 67 IU)， while y-GT was still elevated (403 IU)， and palmoplantar psoriasis returned to its pre-treatment state. Blood chemistry tests periodically carried out during the following months showed per sistently normal SGOT， associated with intermit-tently， slightly increased SGPT (highest value， 91 IU)， and continously， moderately elevated y-GT (ranging from 126 to 228 IU)， while other liver function tests were always regular， as summarized in Table 1.

【13】These biochemical abnormalities were still evident 5years later (SGPT， 47 IU； Y-GT， 221 IU)， when new abdominal ultrasonography revealed an increased， diffuse hepatic steatosis. The liver biopsy showed small inflammatory cell infiltrates (including lym-phocytes， plasmacells and histiocytes) inside a few portal spaces， in addition to initial， slight fibrosis， steatosis， and ductular proliferation. Ultrastructural study of biopsy specimens performed by electronic microscope demonstrated diffuse micro-. macrosteatosis， besides focal dilatation of bilious canalicoli， glycogen storage， considerable collagen amount inside the Disse’s space， and hypertrophy of Kupffer and Ito cells， consistent with a drug-related， chronic liver damage.

【14】DISCUSSION

【15】Hepatotoxic reactions are well known as established side effects of hypervitaminosis A following a long-term high-dose retinol therapy， attributed to the storage of massive amounts of vitamin in Kupffer cells， with increased number of Ito cells or lipocytes(retinol-storing cells). This progressive， large accumu-lation of retinol leads to dose-related liver toxicity， including hepatic fibrosis， obstruction of portal blood flow， portal hypertension， deterioration of hepatic function， ascites and liver insufficiency . Syn-thetic derivatives of retinoic acid or retinoids(etretinate and isotretinoin) are structurally similar to vitamin A， but different for an aromatic ring and an ester end group， and for this reason they are not chronically stored in the liver and have not been found associated to date with dose-dependent hepatotoxic reactions . However， a wide spectrum of liver damage has been described as possible consequence of etretinate therapy， which indicates that this aromatic retinoid probably operates by a different mechanism .

【16】Abnormal liver function tests are observed in approx-imately 30% of patients treated with etretinate： these abnormalities usually include mild， transient increases of transaminase， alkaline phosphatase， y-glutamine transferase and bilirubin， and recede within 4 to 8weeks after therapy interruption . On the other hand， increased liver enzyme levels can be consid-erable or persist for several months， and histologically confirmed acute or chronic hepatitis were reported in a few cases .

【17】After the first 2 patients with chronic aggressive hepatitis described by Fredriksson in 1978 ， in 1979 transaminase and total bilirubin values in a series of 235 patients with psoriasis treated with etretinate， even though obesity， alcohol abuse， and preexisting liver diseases were not examined in these persons. In1980， Thune et al. observed a case of centrolobular toxic necrosis of the liver during therapy with aromatic retinoid for erythrodermia ichthyosiformis non- bullosa. Nevertheless， in 1981 Glazer et al. per formed liver biopsies in a series of 20 patients at pretreatment and at 6 months after discontinuation of etretinate therapy， and concluded that synthetic retinoid did not cause a consistent toxic effect on the liver as a result of a 6-month treatment.

【18】Liver diseases related to the etretinate therapy may be divided into 4 distinct categories， on the basis of histo-logical examination： nonspecific reactive hepatitis， acute hepatitis， chronic hepatitis and severe fibrosis or cirrhosis . As far as we know， only 25 cases of histo-logically confirmed hepatotoxic reactions were reported to date by the literature in association with etretinate treatment： 10 cases were classified as non-specific reactive hepatitis ，6 as acute hepatitis ，6 as chronic hepatitis ， and 3 as severe fibrosis or cirrhosis .

【19】The reproducible association between etretinate therapy and hepatotoxicity certainly identifies the aromatic retinoid as the causative agent of hepatic damage， but abnormal accumulation of the synthetic compound in the liver does not seem associated with hepatitis， for the lack of correlation between dosage， onset of liver disease， clinico-pathological severity of hepatitis， and usually rapid improvement after the therapy discontinuation . Moreover， the remark that the functionally similar compound isotretinoin does not produce apparent hepatotoxicity， in addition to concurrent fever and eosinophilia observed in some patients with etretinate-related hepatitis， indicates that this retinoid probably causes liver diseases by a drug specific， idiosyncrasy or hypersensitivity reaction. Described patients with etretinate-induced hepatitis usually were middle-aged or elderly females， often associated with HLA-A type， which may be responsible for a greater immunological vulnerability， as supposed by Green et al.  about a case of hepatitis related to etretinate therapy and hepatitis B vaccine. In the reported studies， administered dosage of etretinate ranged between 0.3 and 1.5 mg/Kg/day， and the onset of hepatitis generally occurred within 3to 6 months after the start of treatment； the severity of clinical and biochemical findings was very variable， such as the time to recovery . A few patients developed chronic active hepatitis， with persistently abnormal liver function tests， leading to severe fibrosis and cirrhosis several years after discontin-uation of retinoid therapy .

【20】In our reported case， chronic hepatitis occurred after a 3-month therapy with etretinate， and it was charac-terized by intermittent， slight increase of SGPT and continous， moderate elevation of y-GT during the fol-lowing years. Liver biopsy carried out 5 years after retinoid treatment showed chronic persistent hepatitis with diffuse steatosis and initial， slight fibrosis， con-firmed by the ultrastructural microscopical exami-nation， and consistent with a drug-related， chronic liver damage. 【0】Background：

【1】Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is the most prevalent primary immunodeficiency in adults. Patients frequently present with recurrent sino-pulmonary infection. Here we discuss an unusual presentation of CVID to our surgical department.

【2】Case Report：

【3】This report discusses the unusual presentation of inguinal pain and swelling leading to the diagno-sis of this condition. A 61 year old male presented to the Surgical department on several occasions with swellings in his groins， one of which was an abscess requiring drainage. Histological examina-tion of a lymph node that was surgically excised on initial presentation was consistent with reactive hyperplasia. An ultrasound scan of his groins was carried out when he presented some time after this， and revealed what appeared to be reactive lymph nodes. Blood tests then confirmed the di-agnosis of common variable immunodeficiency.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】CVID is rare， but immunodeficiency disorders should be considered in all cases of recurrent lymph-adenopathy when the diagnosis is not im mediately obvious.

【6】key words： surgery·CVID · immunodeficiency·lymphadenopathy· immunoglobulin

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is the com-monest primary immunodeficiency disease， which is char-acterised by frequent bacterial infections and hypogam-maglobulinaemia. The prevalence of CVID is estimated at1：25，000 in the Western world . Males and females are affected equally with a peak onset between twenty and for-ty years. There is an average of 4-6 years between onset of symptoms and diagnosis. The commonest manifestation of CVID is recurrent bronchitisWe report a case of a patient whose first presentation of CVID was an inguinal swelling， which on secondary to reactive lymphadenopathy.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】A 61-year old Greek male presented to the Surgical Department with a firm， tender and erythematous right inguinal swelling. He was not taking any regular medica-tions and had a history of chronic bronchitis for the past twenty years. The patient underwent a groin exploration under general anaesthetic， which revealed an enlarged in-fected lymph node that was excised and sent for histology. The histology report indicated reactive follicular hyperpla-sia. Ten weeks later， he presented again with a right ingui-nal abscess  which was drained and treated with antibiotics. He then represented two weeks after this with a left inguinal swelling. An ultrasound scan of the groin iden-tified several reactive nodes. Tuberculosis and sarcoidosis were excluded following a chest x-ray， mantoux test and se-rum angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) measurements(51 iU/L). HIV， toxoplasmosis， cytomegalovirus， hepa-titis B and syphilis were all considered and excluded fol-lowing negative serology results. Serum immunoglobulin levels were found to be low； IgG <2.7g/L (6-16 g/L) and IgA <0.40g/L (0.8-4 g/L) but with normal IgM 1.57g/L(0.5-2 g/L). Serum protein electrophoresis found <lg/L of paraprotein in the gamma region . The patient was diagnosed with common variable immunodeficien cy.

【11】DISCUSSION

【12】A "lump in the groin” is a very common surgical presentation， with many possible causes； where the swelling is found to be an inguinal lymph node， there are a myriad of diseases that may be responsible. CVID is a rare cause - infections and malig-nancies are perhaps more important differentials to consider， and the history and examination should be tailored as such. Painful nodes are usually secondary to inflammation from infection， and can be secondary to a number of microbes in-cluding Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Painless， firm nodes should raise the clinician's suspicion of malighnancy . Testicular， penile， vulva， urethral， melanoma and lymphoma can all pres-ent with inguinal lymphadenopathy . CVID should be considered as a diagnosis of exclusion ， and investigations for it should not be initiated until infection and malignancy have been ruled out. Other important causes of hypo-immu-noglobulinaemia include nephrotic syndrome， chronic lym-phocytic leukaemia and myeloma. These need to be excluded before pursuing the diagnosis of CVID ， as do other sec-ondary causes of antibody deficiency  e.g. drug induced.

【13】The underlying pathophysiology of CVID is poorly under-stood， but is believed to be due to disruption of the B cell differentiation process， leading to decreased immunoglob-ulin secretion . It is a group of conditions character-ised by this feature， rather than an individual disease .

【14】Patients with CVID typically present with respiratory tract infections usually caused by Streptococeus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae . Chronic respiratory infections can cause bronchiectasis， emphysema， and fibrosis. It is likely the patient's history of chronic bronchitis in this re-port is related to his previously undiagnosed immunodefi-ciency. Clinicians should include CVID amongst their dif-ferentials where recurrent respiratory tract infections with lymphadenopathy is present (bearing in mind that haema-tological malignancies can present like this， and thus need to be investigated).

【15】Gastrointestinal symptoms are the second commonest man-ifestation， namely malabsorption， and chronic diarrhoea as a result of secondary infection . Typical causative organ- isms are Giardia lamblia and Campylobacter jejuni. Bone and joint inflammation may be caused by infection with myco-plasmas or chronic rheumatoid inflammation.

【16】Approximately 20% of individuals with CVID have autoim-mune manifestations： in particular autoimmune haemolyt-ic anaemia and autoimmune thrombocytopenia. There is also an increased incidence of cancer， especially lympho-mas and gastric cancer . Non-malignant lymphoprolif-eration also accurs in these patients causing splenomegaly， lymphadenopathy and follicular nodular lymphatic hyper-plasia of the gastrointestin al tract， but it is unusual for pa-tients to present in this way.

【17】Diagnosis of CVID is achieved through testing serum im-munoglobulin levels with reduced IgG， IgA and/or IgM in the absence of any other clear cause for immunodeficien-cy . Full blood count and film and protein electropho-resis can exclude haematological malignancies； biopsy of lymph nodes can rule out solid organ cancer.

【18】Management of CVID currently consists of immunoglobu-lin replacement ，and active treatment of the asso-ciated manifestations described above. Prophylactic antibi- otics covering both Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae may help prevent associated recurrent sinopul-monary infection and control small bowel bacterial over-growth. Infections need to be treated early with higher dos-es and longer courses of antibiotics.

【19】The prognosis is affected by the presence of structural lung damage， malignancy and autoimmune disease. The twenty year survival rate is approximately 65%.

【20】CONCLUSIONS

【21】Inguinal swellings are common presentations to surgical de-partments. This case demonstrates a possible presentation of CVID to surgical departments and should be considered in patients with persistent or infected lymphadenopathy.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Fetal vascular malperfusion refers to placental lesions indicating reduced or absent perfusion of the villous parenchyma by the fetus. Fetal vascular malperfusion remains an underrecognized condition associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. It may also predispose infants to thromboembolic events. Few cases of inferior vena cava and renal vein thrombosis in an asymptomatic newborn are described. Case presentation： We report the case of an asymptomatic female neonate delivered at 32 weeks of gestation to a mother with type 1 diabetes and preeclampsia. Prenatal renal vein and inferior vena cava thrombosis were diagnosed at 30 weeks. Thrombophilia work-up was negative. Diagnosis was guided by the placental pathological examination that showed thrombosis of several fetal vessels of the chorionic plate， high-grade poor perfusion lesions and distal villous hypoplasia， suggestive of Fetal vascular malperfusion. Treatment with low-molecular-weight heparin was effective in the complete resolution of the thrombus and preservation of renal function. Conclusion： This case emphasizes the importance of placental pathological examination in the presence of fetal abnormalities. Fetal vascular malperfusion may cause unrecognized neonatal thrombosis， which may result in growth impairment or organic dysfunction. Therefore， pregnant women with known risk factors for Fetal vascular malperfusion should be monitored more closely， both antenatally and postnatally， to detect possible placental and fetal target organ involvement at an early stage.

【1】KEYWORDS fetal vascular malperfusion， thrombosis， neonate， preterm， treatment， outcome

【2】Introduction

【3】Fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM)， previously known as fetal thrombotic vasculopathy， refers to a group of placental lesions in-dicating reduced or absent perfusion of the villous parenchyma by the fetus. Although the underlying aetiology of FVM remains unclear， pre-existing maternal diabetes is a known risk factor . FVM can lead to severely adverse perinatal outcomes， including fetal growth restriction (FGR)， thromboembolic events and in-trauterine demise . Neonatal renal vein thrombosis (RVT) is a rare event  that went undiagnosed for many decades and can occur insidiously during pregnancy . We report the case of a neonate with a prenatal diagnosis of RVT and inferior vena cava(IVC) involvement related to FVM， confirmed by a pathological exam of the placenta.

【4】Case report

【5】Our patient is a caucasian female born to non-consanguineous parents. The mother was 36 years old， had type 1 diabetes with retinopathy and preconception glycated haemoglobin (A1c) was8.7%. There was no known family history of thrombophilia. The pregnancy was uneventful until 30 weeks， when the prenatal ul-trasound showed FGR， altered uteroplacental blood flow， oligo-hydramnios， and normal-sized left kidney with heterogeneous parenchyma and multiple hyperechogenic images， suggesting parenchymal oedema  and a thrombus in the IVC and left renal vein . No antithrombotic therapy was started during pregnancy. A diagnosis of pre-eclampsia was also made. Following a multidisciplinary meeting， the infant was born at 32 weeks by elective caesarean section. APGAR score was 10/10 at 1 and 5 minutes， respectively. Somatometry at birth： weight 1190g (-1.33SD)， body length 37.5cm (-1.42SD)，and head circumference 26.5cm (-1.58SD). She was asymptomatic at birth. Physical examination revealed a well-developed female in-fant with a regular heartbeat， palpable pulses on all extremities， and moderate intercostal retractions. She required non-invasive ventilation for 7 days； and remained hemodynamically stable. Initial imaging included chest X-rays， echocardiograms， and cerebral， abdominal， and renal ultrasounds. Abdominal and renal ultrasound with Doppler velocimetry confirmed the left RVT and extension to the lumen of the IVC (20mmx8mm). Cere-bral ultrasound revealed grade II periventricular haemorrhage. Laboratory investigation revealed hemoglobin concentration of18.9g/dL \[reference range (RR)， hematocrit 53.3% (RR 45-75)， thrombocytopenia (37/uL； RR 150-450)， blood urea nitrogen25 mg/dL (RR 3-12) and creatinine 1.03mg/dL (RR0，32-1，01). In the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit， two platelet concentrates were administered with normalization of the platelet value. Her blood pressure was always within normal range. She had spontaneous and adequate diuresis， no macroscopic or microscopic hema-turia was detected. Anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) (1mg/Kg， twice daily) was started on the 6th day. Serological and polymerase chain reaction-based diagnostic procedures excluded infection with entero-， hepatitis-， parvo-， cytomegalic-， varicella-zoster- and herpes simplex viruses， HⅣV， rubella， and toxoplasmosis. A thrombophilia work-up was neg-ative in both the neonate and the mother. It included a search for Factor V Leiden， prothrombin G20210A or MTHFR gene alterations； protein S， protein C or antithrombin III deficiencies； homocysteine， lupus anticoagulant， and anticardiolipin anti-body. She was discharged home at 33 days old， with normal renal function. The placental pathological examination showed thrombosis of several fetal vessels of the chorionic plate， high-grade poor perfusion lesions and distal villous hypoplasia.

【6】During follow-up， a nuclear medicine renal flow study with dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA) was performed at 2 months old and was normal. At 6 months old，LMWH was stopped. Serial renal ultrasounds showed progressive reduction of the throm-bus. The last Doppler ultrasound， performed at 10 months old， revealed complete resolution of the thrombus， a normal venous flow bilaterally， and no difference in kidney size or echogenic-ity. To date， she has adequate growth and normal psychomotor development.

【7】Discussion

【8】Neonates have a higher incidence of thrombosis compared to older children. It has been suggested that their susceptibility is due to decreased levels of anticoagulants and lower levels of thrombotic components J. RVT represents the most com-mon non-catheter-related cause of venous thromboembolism during the neonatal period . However， its mechanism of onset and progression within this population remains unclear. Reported risk factors include perinatal asphyxia， maternal diabetes， infections， genetic thrombophilic states， maternal his-tory of thrombosis，pregnancy-induced hypertension， premature birth， polycythemia， dehydration， and shock . Our case had several known risk factors for RVT， including maternal dia-betes and preeclampsia. Although FVM was not reported in the literature as a classic risk factor ， cases reported by Brown et al. in 2019 and Giacchetti et al. in 2017 highlight the importance of FVM as a risk factor for fetal/neonatal RVT. Considering all the results， it was presumed that， in our case， FVM was also a contributing factor to fetal thrombosis. Given the prenatal diagnosis of the thrombus and its progressive increase during pregnancy with no available therapy， there was a considerable risk of fetal harm， namely renal failure. Placental insufficiency， also present in our case， canbe associated with a higher risk of fe-tal morbidity and mortality， especially in high-risk pregnancies. In addition， there was also a maternal risk， as preeclampsia can be a life-threatening condition. All these factors were considered and contributed to the difficult decision deliver before the term.

【9】Investigation of prothrombotic factors is not mandatory. However， given the severity of the condition， it was con-ducted. Typical postnatal signs and symptoms of RVT in-clude nephromegaly， macroscopic or microscopic hematuria， and thrombocytopenia . As described above， our patient only had thrombocytopenia. Doppler ultrasound remains the gold-standard exam to confirm renal vein obstruction and to detect its extension to the contralateral kidney， IVC and adrenal glands . Therefore， the pathological examination of the pla-centa， enabling a postnatal diagnosis， was fundamental in our case. Moreover， recognizing FVM as a potential complication of maternal diabetes and sending the placenta for pathological examination is extremely valuable as it provides care providers with important information to rule out the significant neonatal complications associated with this entity . A definitive diag-nosis is also important for managing future pregnancies due to possible recurrence risk in mothers with known risk factors .

【10】Various therapeutic options can be used， such as supportive care alone and anticoagulation therapy with unfractionated hep-arin or LMWH. In addition， fibrinolytic treatment or surgical intervention may be considered in bilateral RVT， especially if there is concomitant renal failure. Successful treatment would restore renal vascular permeability and preserves renal function in the long term while causing minimal side effects to the pa-tient . Considering the unilateral RVT， treatment with LMWH with an anti-Xa therapeutic level was effective in the complete resolution of the thrombus and preservation of renal function.

【11】Conclusion

【12】In conclusion， FVM is a recently emphasized entity but remains under-recognized clinically. A pathological examination of the placenta should always be done， especially in patients who present with unexplained thrombocytopenia or thromboembolic events of unknown origin7. This case highlights the possible association between FVM and fetal/neonatal thrombosis. Preg-nant women with known risk factors for FVM should be mon-itored more closely， both antenatally and postnatally， to detect possible placental and fetal target organ involvement at an early stage. There is a lack of consensus in management guidelines， and the balance between the benefits and possible side effects of therapies remains challenging. Additional research is required to enable prenatal diagnosis， better management， and prevention of FVM.

【0】Background：

【1】Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura is a rare， usually benign， and slow-growing neoplasm. Complete surgical resection for giant tumor of the pleura is challenging because of poor exposure and a large blood supply. We report the case of a giant hypervascular fibrous tumor that filled nearly the entire left hemithorax and anteri-or mediastinum， and its preoperative management.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 59-year-old woman presented to us with exertional dyspnea and chest pain. A chest radiograph showed the right hemithorax completely opaque and a mediastinal shift to the left hemithorax. A tomography scan of the thorax showed a giant mass that almost completely filled the right hemithorax and compressed the mediasti-num to the left. Because of excessive bleeding during dissection， the operation was terminated after a biopsy specimen was obtained. The biopsy was diagnosed as a benign fibrous tumour. A thoracic computed tomogra-phy angiogram showed that the mass was supplied by multiple intercostal arteries as well as an aberrant ar-tery that branches off the celiac trunk in the subdiaphragmatic region. Due to the many arteries that needed to be embolized， the final decision was to control the bleeding following resection by inducing total circulatory arrest with the help of cardiopulmonary bypass. The bleeding could not be controlled under cardiopulmonary bypass and the patient's death was confirmed.

【4】Conclusions： We report this case to emphasize the necessity of preoperative embolization； the use of cardiopulmonary by-pass and total circulatory arrest is not a valid alternative method to control the bleeding.

【5】Key words： benign· intrathoracic·fibrous· giant tumor · benign tumors · solitary fibrous · tumors ·therapy Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura is a rare intrathoracic neo plasm； about 80% originate in the visceral pleura and 20% in the parietal pleura. Many are pedunculated on pleural-based pedicles that contain in a large number feeding arteries and draining veins. They present as an asymptomatic mass， are usually large， and are benign in about 80% of patients . The initial evaluation and surgical treatment are main top-ics in management. The tumor is fatal in 12% of cases due to its extensive intrathoracic growth . Complete en bloc sur-gical resection is a commonly used treatment of this tumor.

【6】Case Report

【7】A 59-year-old woman presented to our clinic complaining of exercise dyspnea， chest pain， and inability to lie on her left side. On posterior-anterior chest X-ray， the right hemithorax was completely opaque and there was a mediastinal shift towards the left side. On the thoracic computed tomogra-phy (CT) image， there was a giant heterogeneous mass that almost completely filled the right hemithorax and pushed the heart to the left and the diaphragm downwards . Routine chemistry and hematology lab test results were nor-mal. Arterial blood gas analysis results were Pa02 65 mmHg and PaCO2 42 mmHg. Lung function test results were forced expiratory volume in 1 second 37% and forced vital capacity36%. The decision was to surgically manage the patient， thus median sternotomy was performed. Due to excessive bleed-ing， the surgery was terminated after a biopsy specimen was obtained. The pathology exam revealed a benign fibrous tu-mor. The thoracic CT angiogram showed that the mass was supplied by multiple intercostal arteries， as well as an aberrant artery that branches off the celiac trunk in the subdiaphrag-matic region . The initial plan was to interrupt the arterial supply by embolization to control the bleeding during the operation. Due to of the many arteries that needed to be embolized， the final decision was to control bleeding follow-ing resection by inducing total circulatory arrest with the help of cardiopulmonary bypass.

【8】Following femoral artery and vein catheterization in the su-pine position， the thorax and mediastinum were exposed using a Clamshell incision. Cardiopulmonary bypass was ini-tiated and the cooling process was started. At 32℃， a cross-clamp was placed on the ascending aorta and cardiac arrest was induced by antegrade cold-blood cardioplegia. The pa-tient was cooled to 17C. The hypervascular tumor that invad-ed the mediastinum was completely removed under low-flow total circulatory arrest. There was blood leakage from the en-tire thoracic and diaphragmatic surface but no vascular sup-ply was identified. Bleeding was controlled using electrocau-tery. After the patient was warmed and separated from the total circulatory arrest， the entire thoracic and diaphragmat-ic surfaces started to bleed profusely. The bleeding could not be controlled under cardiopulmonary bypass. Patient death was confirmed. The resected specimen was 25x18x15 cm and 2.870 g .

【9】Discussion

【10】Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura may have grown to giant size by the time of diagnosis. About 80% of these tumors orig-inate in the visceral pleura and 20% arise from parietal pleu-ra. Tumors more than 8 cm are more likely to have a parietal pleural origin and have a vascular pedicle . Identifying the vascularity of the giant intrathoracic mass using a CT an-giogram can be useful in the surgical management. For intra-thoracic hypervascular tumors， interrupting the vascularity us-ing embolization may decrease the amount of intraoperative bleeding and improve the safety of the procedure in suitable cases .Total circulatory arrest is routinely used in open-heart surgeries today. This technique has also been used to decrease the risk of massive bleeding in the treatment of pa-tients who have an intracranial aneurysm， resection of a ma-jor hepatic artery， or other tumors .Our decision to per-form the resection under circulatory arrest was made on the basis of 2 facts： risk of uncontrollable bleeding， and the many arteries that needed to be embolized.

【11】Conclusions

【12】Highly vascular tumors should be resected after interrupting the vascularity using embolization. The use of cardiopulmo-nary bypass and total circulatory arrest is not a valid alterna-tive method to control bleeding in cases such as ours.

【0】Background：

【1】Cardiac inflammatory pseudotumors are rarely observed. Their etiology might include immunologic abnormali-ties， fibrogenetic disorders， specific reactions to infections or abnormalities related to trauma， necrosis， or neo-plasm. Life-threatening ventricular tachycardia and cases of sudden death related to cardiac tumors have been reported. The present report describes and discusses diagnostic and therapeutic solutions for the treatment of nonsarcoid multiorgan pseudotumors with cardiac involvement.

【2】Case Report： A 38-year-old woman presented to the clinic with symptomatic ventricu lar tachycardia. As coronary artery dis-ease， cardiomyopathy， and channelopathy were ruled out， and electrocardiograms were not typical of idiopathic arrhythmia， the patient underwent detailed diagnostics which included targeted endomyocardial biopsy，which revealed a cardiac inflammatory pseudotumor. Laborious testing (and eventually， antibiotic therapy) led to ex juvantibus diagnosis of multiorgan disseminated brucellosis with cardiac involvement. Treatment with ceftriax-one， doxycycline， and rifampicin resulted in a complete resolution of all lesions after 3 months， and sustained recovery was observed during a 5-year follow-up. As the risk of ventricular tachycardia could not be reliably predicted， the patient had a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implanted.

【3】Conclusions： A vast diagnostic armamentarium of modern medicine allowed us to diagnose an unsuspected and rare cardi-ac inflammatory pseudotumor. In the case of travelers， the possibility of regionally specific illnesses， especial-ly infections， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may be useful in patients with idiopathic ventricular tachycardias' to detect non-apparent myocardi-al lesions which may result from the underlying cause of the arrhythmia.

【4】Keywords： Brucellosis ·Case Reports · Tachycardia， Ventricular

【5】The initial assessment of an episode of sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) typically includes 12-lead ECG， transthorac-ic echocardiography， and functional testing and/or imaging for coronary artery abnormalities . If structural or electrical heart disease is not excluded， a patient is deemed to have id-iopathic VT， and further treatment， either pharmacological or invasive， must be planned， with consideration for the patient's preference . However， in rare cases， a thorough diagnostic process may lead to unsuspected findings. Infections should also be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhyth-mias. Isolated cases of arrhythmia-triggering cardiac pseudotu-mors have been reported. Their etiology might include immu-nologic abnormalities， fibrogenetic disorders， specific reactions to infections， or abnormalities related to trauma， necrosis， or neoplasm. In the case of travelers， the possibility of contract-ing regionally specific illnesses， especially infections (includ-ing zoonoses)， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias.

【6】A 38-year-old woman， with no previous medical history， pre-sented in our hospital with palpitations which had lasted a few hours and were associated with 2 episodes of presyncope. Ventricular tachycardia of approximately 180 bpm  was diagnosed and sinus rhythm was restored with direct-cur-rent cardioversion 200J (Schiller DEFIGARD 5000).

【7】Ventricular tachycardia recurred after several days and required another cardioversion. Initial evaluation included basic labora-tory blood tests， the results of which were found to be normal， and transthoracic echocardiography that disclosed no abnor-mality. ECG revealed sinus bradycardia， lack of R-wave progres-sion V1-4， and non-specific repolarization abnormalities with QTc falling within the normal range (QTc=380 ms) . The patient presented adequate exercise tolerance， heart rate， and blood pressure reactions， with no ECG changes during the treadmill test. Coronary angiography disclosed no abnormal-ities. The patient denied having any history of ventricular ar-rythmia events， sudden cardiac deaths， or premature deaths in her relatives. As typical pathologies related to VT (coronary artery disease， cardiomyopathies，and channelopathies) were excluded， idiopathic VT was considered as a primary working diagnosis. However， an electrophysiologist opined that our pa-tient's ECGs did not match a typical picture of idiopathic VT and scar-related arrhythmia was suspected . Therefore， the patient was referred for cMRl， which revealed tumorous contrast enhancement in the middle portion of interventricular septum (1x2.7 cm) and in the subendocardial region， in the basal segment of the right ventricle .

【8】As the nature of the cardiac tumor could not be precisely es-tablished based on cMRl， a whole-body positron emission to-mography scan (18F-FDG-PET/CT) was performed. The scan revealed several foci of increased metabolism in multiple or-gans with maximal standardized uptake value (SUVmax) vary-ing from 5.3 to 14.5 .

【9】Additionally， MRI of the brain disclosed a 12x13x10 mm lesion in the central part of the pons . The patient present-ed no symptoms typical of localized or disseminated infection or myocarditis. The markers for systemic inflammation and myocardial injury were within normal ranges. Disseminated sarcoidosis was considered as the most probable initial di-agnosis. Transbronchial biopsy of pulmonary foci， however， appeared to be inconclusive as no abnormal cells were found on histopathology. For the abdominal foci， it was too risky to undergo biopsy， so targeted biopsy of the septal focus in the heart was performed. For this purpose， we used multiple-im-aging guidance， which included intraoperative fluoroscopy， transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)， and 3D electrophys-iological mapping with the CARTO System (Biosense Webster Inc.， Irvine， CA， USA) .

【10】The echocardiographer led the bioptome to the middle of the septum and electroanatomical mapping showed areas of sub-tle reduction of voltage which were considered to be connect-ed with the tumor. The subsequent histopathology disclosed an inflammatory pseudotumor (IP) with no signs of sarcoid-osis .

【11】Therefore， bearing in mind that the patient had visited 4 dif-ferent continents during the previous 6 months， stepwise di-agnostics  of possible causes of multiorgan IP were undertaken. The following tests gave positive results： 

【12】IgG antibodies against Toxoplasma gondii， Aspergillus， and

【13】Pneumocystis carinii；  IgM antibodies against Brucella sp； antinuclear antibodies (1： 320). As the blood count， serum protein electrophoresis，and C-reactive protein were all found to be normal， our consultant specialist in internal medicine found no indication for a bone marrow biopsy.

【14】Multiorgan brucellosis or an autoimmunological disorder did not seem likely， but they were not impossible either. However， having considered a possibility of infection with Brucella mi-croorganisms， we meticulously reassessed the patient's his-tory of possible risky habits. It was disclosed that during her travels to central and southern Asia， as well as to the Middle East and southeastern Europe， she did consume non-pasteur-ized and non-processed milk， home-made cheese， and oth-er local meals. Additionally， during the 3-month period pre-ceding hospitalization， she had experienced several episodes of fever and joint pains which were interpreted as seasonal common infections. Therefore， after consultation with a mul-tidisciplinary specialist team， we decided to start antimicro-bial treatment against Brucella sp. with ceftriaxone 2 g in-travenously， oral doxycycline 100 mg， twice daily， and oral rifampicin， 900 mg daily. Considering the potential for failure， steroid therapy was to be initiated if the antimicrobial treat-ment failed to resolve her symptoms. At 4 weeks of antibi-otic therapy， 18F-FDG-PET/CT revealed a significant regres-sion of the hypermetabolic foci ， and cerebral MRI disclosed a lower saturation of the lesion in the pons， inter-preted as a post-inflammatory scar. As we could not reliably estimate the risk of VT recurrence， the patient had a subcu-taneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) insert-ed . 【15】hypermetabolic foci. Approximately 2 and 4 years after the ces-sation of antibiotic therapy， the patient underwent addition-al general evaluations， which confirmed the regression of the disease. During S-ICD check-ups performed every 6 months， no arrhythmic events were detected .

【16】Discussion

【17】We describe here the case of a patient in whom multiorgan brucellosis with cardiac involvement in the form of intraven-tricular tumor provoking symptomatic VT was considered the most probable diagnosis.

【18】The possibility that the lesion was a neoplastic tumor was the keynote of our decisions； therefore， a whole-body PET/CT was for this reason that we decided to initiate antimicrobial treat-ment first. As this resulted in full resolution of the inflamma-tory lesions， the final diagnosis of the underlying cause of the IP was Brucella infection.

【30】To the best of our knowledge， only one case of an inflammatory tumor in the interventricular septum of the heart has been pub-lished， and its underlying cause was not disclosed . Cardiac involvement during Brucella infection may have different clin-ical manifestations： it can be limited to inflammation of the endocardium (usually on an aortic valve)， myocardium， or peri-cardium， but pancarditis has also been reported. On the other hand， infection with the Brucella microorganism can result in tumor-like lesions in different organs (eg， the liver or brain). It is thought that these lesions begin to develop in the acute phase as purulent-like foci that in time transform into pseu-dotumoral structures that develop into caseous necrotic tu-mors known as brucellomas . Such unusual inflammato-ry structures are formed as a result of the suppressive effect Brucella microorganisms produce on the host immune system. Brucellosis presenting as cardiac IP has not been reported so far； thus， we found it baffling to accept such a clinical suspi-cion. Nevertheless， after stepwise and laborious work-up en-gaging several specialists of distinct medical disciplines， we deemed such a diagnosis as probable， which resulted in anti-biotic treatment initiation. Possible alternatives for therapy of inflammatory pseudotumors include nonsteroidal anti-inflam-matory drugs or steroids and chemotherapeutic drugs， both of which are usually applied as adjuvant therapy to surgical resec-tion . Of note， although some authors recommend surgi-cal resection as the optimal therapy for inflammatory pseudotu-mors ， in our case，this option was considered as the last-line treatment due to multiorgan lesions in unfavorable locations.

【31】Life-threatening VTs and cardiac tumor-related sudden death cas-es have been reported . The future risk of VT recurrence could not be reliably estimated in our patient due to the extremely rare etiology and uncertain dynamics of her inflammatory cardiac le-sions. As no stratification method (ie， invasive electrophysiologi-cal study) has been demonstrated in such a clinical scenario， we decided to implant a cardioverter-defibrillator. As the patient did not require permanent pacing and， bearing in mind that over the course of a 3-month in-hospital observation she had no VT re-currence， a subcutaneous device was chosen instead of a trans-venous system. Disadvantages of S-ICD systems include the in-ability to provide antitachycardia pacing in case of monomorphic VT； however， by not implanting the defibrillation lead into the right ventricle， we avoided its possible harmful interaction with the injured myocardium . Other possible options could be a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator but taking into account obser-vations of recurrences of brucellosis， we decided that permanent protection with the implantable device might be a better option.

【32】A vast diagnostic armamentarium of modern medicine allowed us to diagnose an unsuspected and rare cardiac inflammato-ry pseudotumor. In the case of travelers， the possibility of re gionally specific illnesses， especially infections， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may be useful in patients with‘idiopathic ventricular tachycardias' to detect non-appar-ent myocardial lesions， which may prove to be an underly-ing cause of the arrhythmia. Even though diagnosis exjuvan-tibus exists in medical practices， it is considered an inelegant route to the identification of the underlying cause of a dis-ease. Nevertheless，even in modern medicine， there are clini-cal situations when such an approach must be considered . Our therapeutic success allowed us to establish a diagnosis of disseminated brucellosis with cardiac involvement with a high degree of certainty.

【0】Background：

【1】Cardiac inflammatory pseudotumors are rarely observed. Their etiology might include immunologic abnormali-ties， fibrogenetic disorders， specific reactions to infections or abnormalities related to trauma， necrosis， or neo-plasm. Life-threatening ventricular tachycardia and cases of sudden death related to cardiac tumors have been reported. The present report describes and discusses diagnostic and therapeutic solutions for the treatment of nonsarcoid multiorgan pseudotumors with cardiac involvement.

【2】Case Report： A 38-year-old woman presented to the clinic with symptomatic ventricu lar tachycardia. As coronary artery dis-ease， cardiomyopathy， and channelopathy were ruled out， and electrocardiograms were not typical of idiopathic arrhythmia， the patient underwent detailed diagnostics which included targeted endomyocardial biopsy，which revealed a cardiac inflammatory pseudotumor. Laborious testing (and eventually， antibiotic therapy) led to ex juvantibus diagnosis of multiorgan disseminated brucellosis with cardiac involvement. Treatment with ceftriax-one， doxycycline， and rifampicin resulted in a complete resolution of all lesions after 3 months， and sustained recovery was observed during a 5-year follow-up. As the risk of ventricular tachycardia could not be reliably predicted， the patient had a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implanted.

【3】Conclusions： A vast diagnostic armamentarium of modern medicine allowed us to diagnose an unsuspected and rare cardi-ac inflammatory pseudotumor. In the case of travelers， the possibility of regionally specific illnesses， especial-ly infections， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may be useful in patients with idiopathic ventricular tachycardias' to detect non-apparent myocardi-al lesions which may result from the underlying cause of the arrhythmia.

【4】Keywords： Brucellosis ·Case Reports · Tachycardia， Ventricular

【5】The initial assessment of an episode of sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) typically includes 12-lead ECG， transthorac-ic echocardiography， and functional testing and/or imaging for coronary artery abnormalities . If structural or electrical heart disease is not excluded， a patient is deemed to have id-iopathic VT， and further treatment， either pharmacological or invasive， must be planned， with consideration for the patient's preference . However， in rare cases， a thorough diagnostic process may lead to unsuspected findings. Infections should also be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhyth-mias. Isolated cases of arrhythmia-triggering cardiac pseudotu-mors have been reported. Their etiology might include immu-nologic abnormalities， fibrogenetic disorders， specific reactions to infections， or abnormalities related to trauma， necrosis， or neoplasm. In the case of travelers， the possibility of contract-ing regionally specific illnesses， especially infections (includ-ing zoonoses)， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias.

【6】A 38-year-old woman， with no previous medical history， pre-sented in our hospital with palpitations which had lasted a few hours and were associated with 2 episodes of presyncope. Ventricular tachycardia of approximately 180 bpm  was diagnosed and sinus rhythm was restored with direct-cur-rent cardioversion 200J (Schiller DEFIGARD 5000).

【7】Ventricular tachycardia recurred after several days and required another cardioversion. Initial evaluation included basic labora-tory blood tests， the results of which were found to be normal， and transthoracic echocardiography that disclosed no abnor-mality. ECG revealed sinus bradycardia， lack of R-wave progres-sion V1-4， and non-specific repolarization abnormalities with QTc falling within the normal range (QTc=380 ms) . The patient presented adequate exercise tolerance， heart rate， and blood pressure reactions， with no ECG changes during the treadmill test. Coronary angiography disclosed no abnormal-ities. The patient denied having any history of ventricular ar-rythmia events， sudden cardiac deaths， or premature deaths in her relatives. As typical pathologies related to VT (coronary artery disease， cardiomyopathies，and channelopathies) were excluded， idiopathic VT was considered as a primary working diagnosis. However， an electrophysiologist opined that our pa-tient's ECGs did not match a typical picture of idiopathic VT and scar-related arrhythmia was suspected . Therefore， the patient was referred for cMRl， which revealed tumorous contrast enhancement in the middle portion of interventricular septum (1x2.7 cm) and in the subendocardial region， in the basal segment of the right ventricle .

【8】As the nature of the cardiac tumor could not be precisely es-tablished based on cMRl， a whole-body positron emission to-mography scan (18F-FDG-PET/CT) was performed. The scan revealed several foci of increased metabolism in multiple or-gans with maximal standardized uptake value (SUVmax) vary-ing from 5.3 to 14.5 .

【9】Additionally， MRI of the brain disclosed a 12x13x10 mm lesion in the central part of the pons . The patient present-ed no symptoms typical of localized or disseminated infection or myocarditis. The markers for systemic inflammation and myocardial injury were within normal ranges. Disseminated sarcoidosis was considered as the most probable initial di-agnosis. Transbronchial biopsy of pulmonary foci， however， appeared to be inconclusive as no abnormal cells were found on histopathology. For the abdominal foci， it was too risky to undergo biopsy， so targeted biopsy of the septal focus in the heart was performed. For this purpose， we used multiple-im-aging guidance， which included intraoperative fluoroscopy， transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)， and 3D electrophys-iological mapping with the CARTO System (Biosense Webster Inc.， Irvine， CA， USA) .

【10】The echocardiographer led the bioptome to the middle of the septum and electroanatomical mapping showed areas of sub-tle reduction of voltage which were considered to be connect-ed with the tumor. The subsequent histopathology disclosed an inflammatory pseudotumor (IP) with no signs of sarcoid-osis .

【11】Therefore， bearing in mind that the patient had visited 4 dif-ferent continents during the previous 6 months， stepwise di-agnostics  of possible causes of multiorgan IP were undertaken. The following tests gave positive results： 

【12】IgG antibodies against Toxoplasma gondii， Aspergillus， and

【13】Pneumocystis carinii；  IgM antibodies against Brucella sp； antinuclear antibodies (1： 320). As the blood count， serum protein electrophoresis，and C-reactive protein were all found to be normal， our consultant specialist in internal medicine found no indication for a bone marrow biopsy.

【14】Multiorgan brucellosis or an autoimmunological disorder did not seem likely， but they were not impossible either. However， having considered a possibility of infection with Brucella mi-croorganisms， we meticulously reassessed the patient's his-tory of possible risky habits. It was disclosed that during her travels to central and southern Asia， as well as to the Middle East and southeastern Europe， she did consume non-pasteur-ized and non-processed milk， home-made cheese， and oth-er local meals. Additionally， during the 3-month period pre-ceding hospitalization， she had experienced several episodes of fever and joint pains which were interpreted as seasonal common infections. Therefore， after consultation with a mul-tidisciplinary specialist team， we decided to start antimicro-bial treatment against Brucella sp. with ceftriaxone 2 g in-travenously， oral doxycycline 100 mg， twice daily， and oral rifampicin， 900 mg daily. Considering the potential for failure， steroid therapy was to be initiated if the antimicrobial treat-ment failed to resolve her symptoms. At 4 weeks of antibi-otic therapy， 18F-FDG-PET/CT revealed a significant regres-sion of the hypermetabolic foci ， and cerebral MRI disclosed a lower saturation of the lesion in the pons， inter-preted as a post-inflammatory scar. As we could not reliably estimate the risk of VT recurrence， the patient had a subcu-taneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) insert-ed . 【16】Discussion

【17】We describe here the case of a patient in whom multiorgan brucellosis with cardiac involvement in the form of intraven-tricular tumor provoking symptomatic VT was considered the most probable diagnosis.

【18】The possibility that the lesion was a neoplastic tumor was the keynote of our decisions； therefore， a whole-body PET/CT was for this reason that we decided to initiate antimicrobial treat-ment first. As this resulted in full resolution of the inflamma-tory lesions， the final diagnosis of the underlying cause of the IP was Brucella infection.

【30】To the best of our knowledge， only one case of an inflammatory tumor in the interventricular septum of the heart has been pub-lished， and its underlying cause was not disclosed . Cardiac involvement during Brucella infection may have different clin-ical manifestations： it can be limited to inflammation of the endocardium (usually on an aortic valve)， myocardium， or peri-cardium， but pancarditis has also been reported. On the other hand， infection with the Brucella microorganism can result in tumor-like lesions in different organs (eg， the liver or brain). It is thought that these lesions begin to develop in the acute phase as purulent-like foci that in time transform into pseu-dotumoral structures that develop into caseous necrotic tu-mors known as brucellomas . Such unusual inflammato-ry structures are formed as a result of the suppressive effect Brucella microorganisms produce on the host immune system. Brucellosis presenting as cardiac IP has not been reported so far； thus， we found it baffling to accept such a clinical suspi-cion. Nevertheless， after stepwise and laborious work-up en-gaging several specialists of distinct medical disciplines， we deemed such a diagnosis as probable， which resulted in anti-biotic treatment initiation. Possible alternatives for therapy of inflammatory pseudotumors include nonsteroidal anti-inflam-matory drugs or steroids and chemotherapeutic drugs， both of which are usually applied as adjuvant therapy to surgical resec-tion . Of note， although some authors recommend surgi-cal resection as the optimal therapy for inflammatory pseudotu-mors ， in our case，this option was considered as the last-line treatment due to multiorgan lesions in unfavorable locations.

【31】Life-threatening VTs and cardiac tumor-related sudden death cas-es have been reported . The future risk of VT recurrence could not be reliably estimated in our patient due to the extremely rare etiology and uncertain dynamics of her inflammatory cardiac le-sions. As no stratification method (ie， invasive electrophysiologi-cal study) has been demonstrated in such a clinical scenario， we decided to implant a cardioverter-defibrillator. As the patient did not require permanent pacing and， bearing in mind that over the course of a 3-month in-hospital observation she had no VT re-currence， a subcutaneous device was chosen instead of a trans-venous system. Disadvantages of S-ICD systems include the in-ability to provide antitachycardia pacing in case of monomorphic VT； however， by not implanting the defibrillation lead into the right ventricle， we avoided its possible harmful interaction with the injured myocardium . Other possible options could be a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator but taking into account obser-vations of recurrences of brucellosis， we decided that permanent protection with the implantable device might be a better option.

【32】A vast diagnostic armamentarium of modern medicine allowed us to diagnose an unsuspected and rare cardiac inflammato-ry pseudotumor. In the case of travelers， the possibility of re gionally specific illnesses， especially infections， must be taken into consideration as possible causes of arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may be useful in patients with‘idiopathic ventricular tachycardias' to detect non-appar-ent myocardial lesions， which may prove to be an underly-ing cause of the arrhythmia. Even though diagnosis exjuvan-tibus exists in medical practices， it is considered an inelegant route to the identification of the underlying cause of a dis-ease. Nevertheless，even in modern medicine， there are clini-cal situations when such an approach must be considered . Our therapeutic success allowed us to establish a diagnosis of disseminated brucellosis with cardiac involvement with a high degree of certainty.
