【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Insulinomas are a rare group of neuroendocrine tumours. Ninety percent are benign and most are solitary. They can have varied presentations and long-standing history of symptoms. Most patients are affected in the fourth to sixth decades of life. Insulinomas can have an association with multiple endocrine neoplasia(MEN) type 1. However， typically they are sporadic. Most are solitary and benign. Their most common presentation is symptomatic hypoglycemia. After investigations， surgery is the treatment of choice and can offer cure. Laparoscopic surgery can provide all the benefits of minimally invasive surgery and at least equal oncological outcomes in high volume centers. 3D laparoscopy can further improve outcomes with better depth perception and control during the surgery. Case Presentation： This case report is about an 80-year-old female who presented to us with long-standing symptoms of hypoglycemia. She was symptomatic for at least seven years before she was being diagnosed. Her symptoms gradually became severe in three months before she presented to us. After confirmation of the diagnosis with biochemical and radiological investigations， she was treated with 3-D laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. Histopathology was consistent with insulinoma， and she had resolution of symptoms. Conclusion：Insulinomas are rare neuroendocrine tumours. There shall be a high index of suspicion for these disorders. Management is multidisciplinary. Surgery is the treatment of choice. Proper management leads to rapid cure and resolution of the symptoms.

【1】KEYWORDS insulinoma， neuroendocrine， laparoscopy， 3-D laparoscopy Endoscopic ultrasound， multiple endocrine neoplasias

【2】Introduction

【3】Insulinomas are a rare group of neoplasms that arise from insulin-producing beta type islet cells . The annual incidence is around four cases per million individuals per year . Indi-viduals are mostly affected in the fourth to sixth decade of life with gender predilection for females . Up to 90% of these tumours are benign. They constitute the most common group of functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (pNETS). Ten percent of the insulinomas are multiple， around 10% are ma-lignant ， and 10% are having an association with syndromes such as Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 1 (. Due to the indolent nature of the tumour and non-specific symptoms， the presentation is often delayed， and the patient attends various specialties before being finally diagnosed. There is a classic triad of low blood sugari.e. <55 mg/dl， hypoglycemic symptoms and improvement in the symptoms after the provision of glucose. This is referred to as Whipple's triad. Insulinoma can be sus-pected if there are symptoms of Whipple’s triad in the presence of Insulin levels > 3pU/mL and C-peptide levels >0.6 ng/mL. 72-hour fasting test is the gold standard for the diagnosis of insulinoma 71.

【4】After biochemical confirmation， the next goal is the localiza-tion of the tumour and exclusion of metastasis. Localization of insulinoma can be difficult. Starting from Ultrasound， CT scan and MRI are useful for the localization of the tumour. Endo-scopic ultrasound (EUS) is of paramount importance in local-ization of the tumour as well as to depict the relationship of the lesion with the pancreatic duct， nearby vasculature and the ability to further perform endoscopic ultrasound guided fine needle aspiration (EUS-FNA). EUS has detection rates of 86.6-92.3%. Other invasive procedures such as Angiography and arterial stimulation venous sampling (ASVS) can help to diagnose the location of the tumour by utilizing the endocrine function of the tumour， in cases where the initial studies fail to localize the lesion.

【5】Surgical excision is the treatment of choice. However， the choice of procedure depends on many factors such as the loca-tion of the tumour in the gland， proximity to the duct system and whether the lesion is single or multiple. For lesions that are either malignant， relatively large-sized， close to the ductal system and located in the head， pancreaticoduodenectomy is warranted. Smaller lesions in this region and away from the duc-tal system can be treated with enucleation. For lesions of body and tail similarly either distal pancreatectomy and enucleation can be carried out depending on above mentioned factors .

【6】The present case report is about our experience of manage-ment of an 80 year old patient of insulinoma who had long-standing symptoms that gradually worsened.

【7】Case presentation

【8】We report a case of an 80-year-old woman who presented to us with history of dizziness， sweating and altered sensorium for seven years. The symptoms gradually worsened over a period of previous three months. She also reported a few episodes of fall and getting unconscious. The condition of the patient used to improve after meals. Her blood sugar levels were found low during these episodes. The episodes were more frequent and profound by the time the patient sought medical attention at our center. Her medical history was significant for osteoarthritis and well-controlled hypertension. She had no previous surgical history. She was a mother to six.

【9】Upon presentation to the hospital she underwent routine hematological and biochemical investigations. She was drowsy and irritable. Her random blood sugar levels came out to be 39mg/dl. She was hospitalized and treated with glucose infusion. Her insulin and C-Peptide levels were obtained that came out to be 12 pU/mL and 9.21ng/ml. During the course of her admis-sion and investigations at the hospital， she became unconscious. Her blood glucose levels were again obtained. This time critical alert was received for blood sugar levels of 28 mg/dl. Thus， she was treated with continuous dextrose infusion. Her planned72-hour fasting test was cancelled due to her frail condition and ongoing severe symptoms of hypoglycemia. Clinically and on the basis of biochemical investigations the diagnosis of insuli-noma was almost certain. Thus， it was decided to proceed to localization investigations.

【10】She had a CT scan of Chest， Abdomen and Pelvis with con-trast that demonstrated a 20x 18 mm arterially enhanced lesion in the tail of the pancreas. It was a solitary lesion with well defined margins. CT scan findings favored a primary pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour without any distant metastasis. Endo-scopic ultrasound was performed. The lesion was assessed， it was found to be in close proximity of the pancreatic duct. More- over， the EUS complimented the findings of the CT scan. EUS-FNA was obtained and results favored a well differentiated neuroendocrine (NET) tumor.

【11】As she had ongoing symptoms and her symptoms were only managed by continuous dextrose infusions， she was planned for resection on emergency list. She was planned for 3-Dlaparo-scopic distal pancreatectomy on next available list. Meanwhile her assessments and work-up was performed urgently.

【12】The operating team consisted of operating surgeon， an assis-tant surgeon and a camera assistant. We used modified Lloyd Davis position. Four 5mm working ports and one 11mm camera port were utilized. We use LigasureTM (Mary land) dissector as energy device. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed no metastasis. After exposure the tumour was found in the tail of pancreas closely abutting the splenic hilum. The pancreas was transected with Echelon stapler after the splenic artery and vein were sepa-rately clipped using Hem-o-loks. Pancreatic remnant was over-sewen with prolene. Jackson Pratt (JP) drain was placed in the splenic bed. Operative time was 150 minutes. Intra-operative blood loss was 30 ml. The patient stayed in intensive care unit for one day and was stepped down to the floor the next day. Drain was removed on day three and she was discharged the same day in stable condition. She had smooth recovery other than a urinary tract infection that was medically managed.

【13】Histopathology came out as well-differentiated neuroen-docrine tumour World Health Organization (WHO) Grade I. Mitosis was reported less than2/2mm-.Ki-67 was 2% with pos-itive synaptophysin. Grossly it was 2.1 cm in greatest dimension and margins were free of tumor. There was islet cell hyperplasia seen that was consistent with nesidioblastosis， a phenomenon seen in insulinomas of pancreas. Her case was discussed in the hospital Multidisciplinary Tumour (MDT) board and no further oncological treatment was advised.

【14】Post-operatively， patient had normalization of the blood glu-cose levels. Later the blood glucose levels went in the diabetic range. Currently， the patient is eight months post-surgery and is free from symptoms. Her HbA1C currently is 7.1

【15】Discussion

【16】Insulinoma is a rare tumour and has an indolent course with the clinical signs and symptoms that can mimic other common medi- cal disorders. Most of the symptoms are related to hypoglycemia. Most common being confusion， changes in the behavior， visual disturbances， dizziness， seizures and loss of consciousness， anxi-ety， sweating， palpitations and tremors . These symptoms can also be present in a variety of other medical and psychiatric disorders. Thus it is common for these patients to present late and present to various specialties and get treated based on symp-toms before they land to either endocrinologists and surgeons. Commonly， there is a delay for more than 15 months before the disease is diagnosed . In our case， the patient had symp-toms for seven years before she was being diagnosed. The age group in which disease is common is fourth to a sixth decade ； however， our patient presented in the eighth decade of her life.

【17】Insulinoma can occur in conjunction with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN)-type-1 which includes parathyroid hyperpla-sia， anterior pituitary adenomas and pancreatic or duodenal neuroendocrine tumours. It is an autosomal dominant disorder. Insulinomas that occur in conjunction with this disorder are often multicentric and develop earlier in life as compared to the sporadic cases .

【18】The diagnosis and localization of the tumour is the trickiest part. One has to have a high index of suspicion for these lesions. The classic Whipple's triad， along with C- peptide and insulin levels play an imperative role in the diagnosis of the lesion . In our case， the patient had all the typical symptoms of Whipple’s triad and had raised C-peptide and insulin levels as well. The 72hour fasting test is considered gold standard for the diagnosis. However， our patient was old， frail and fairly symptomatic with repeated bouts of hypoglycemia with very low blood sugar levels； thus， it was not possible to carry out a 72-hour fasting test.

【19】After diagnosis， the next imperative step is localization of the tumour. Contrast-enhanced CT scan is thought to be the first-line investigation. Helical contrast-enhanced CT scan has a sensitivity of around 94% . EUS has become the modality of choice in the localization of these tumours. It can pinpoint the exact location， its relation to the pancreatic duct and biliary tree along with surrounding vasculature. Its sensitivity is around94-96%. However， the main issue with EUS is user dependabil-ity J. ASVS can be a useful modality in cases where the localization is still a problem . However， it is an invasive pro-cedure like EUS. It requires equipment and trained personnel to do it， hence not routinely done and available. At our institution， we routinely perform CT scan， MR and EUS for these tumours and other neuroendocrine tumours of the pancreas. Similarly， in this case -CT scan and EUS were used for the localization of the Surgery is the mainstay of the management of insulinoma， if adequately performed， the patient can be cured . The choice of procedure depends on the location of the tumour， whether its solitary or multiple， the relationship of biliary and pancreatic ducts and the presence of suspicious lymph nodes. Tumour enucleation is the procedure of choice if the tumour is solitary superficial and free of nearby ducts . Most of the lesions have a distinct appearance that can be recognized at the surgery； and there is a well-defined plane that can be used for enucleation. For cases that are in close proximity to the ductal system， major vasculature and there is suspicion of malignancy resection of the pancreas is a better option to avoid pancreatic fistulae and vascular complications. Surgical resection options include pancreaticoduodenectomy， distal pancreatectomy with or without splenectomy and central pancreatectomy. In our case， as the lesion appeared to be in close proximity to the pancreatic duct and was closely abutting the splenic hilum thus we opted for distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy.

【20】The laparoscopic approach is increasingly used and favoured approach for the management of pancreatic lesions in high vol-ume centers. It decreases the morbidity. Oncological outcomes are however similar. The use of laparoscopic ultrasound can fur-ther aid in the localization of the tumour Moreover， the 3-D approach gives better depth perception and further makes la-paroscopic surgery easy and productive . Our case was done by 3-D laparoscopic approach. At our institute， we routinely use3-D High Definition laparoscopy for hepatopancreatic-biliary(HPB) surgery as well as upper and lower Gastrointestinal surg-eries.

【21】Histologically these lesions are neuroendocrine in nature. They have a strong expression of chromogranin and synapto-physin. Ki-67 index and number of mitosis per high field are used to differentiate between grades of tumour. caseOur case was low grade neuroendocrine tumor on the basis of these cri-teria. The diagnosis of malignancy can be difficult to make and only becomes apparent once there are established metastasis.

【22】Conclusion

【23】Insulinomas are rare tumours. Most are benign. Physicians shall have a high index of suspicion based on the symptoms. Management is multidisciplinary and involves endocrinologists， physicians from various specialties， surgeons and pathologist. Insulinomas can be difficult to localize， and there are different investigations with varied accuracy； thus， judicious use shall be made， however， it is imperative to localize the lesion prior to surgery. Surgery， preferably laparoscopy， is the treatment of choice and offers a cure.

Most common being confusion， changes in the behavior， visual disturbances， dizziness， seizures and loss of consciousness， anxi-ety， sweating， palpitations and tremors . These symptoms can also be present in a variety of other medical and psychiatric disorders. Thus it is common for these patients to present late and present to various specialties and get treated based on symp-toms before they land to either endocrinologists and surgeons. Commonly， there is a delay for more than 15 months before the disease is diagnosed . In our case， the patient had symp-toms for seven years before she was being diagnosed. The age group in which disease is common is fourth to a sixth decade ； however， our patient presented in the eighth decade of her life.

【17】Insulinoma can occur in conjunction with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN)-type-1 which includes parathyroid hyperpla-sia， anterior pituitary adenomas and pancreatic or duodenal neuroendocrine tumours. It is an autosomal dominant disorder. Insulinomas that occur in conjunction with this disorder are often multicentric and develop earlier in life as compared to the sporadic cases .

【18】The diagnosis and localization of the tumour is the trickiest part. One has to have a high index of suspicion for these lesions. The classic Whipple's triad， along with C- peptide and insulin levels play an imperative role in the diagnosis of the lesion . In our case， the patient had all the typical symptoms of Whipple’s triad and had raised C-peptide and insulin levels as well. The 72hour fasting test is considered gold standard for the diagnosis. However， our patient was old， frail and fairly symptomatic with repeated bouts of hypoglycemia with very low blood sugar levels； thus， it was not possible to carry out a 72-hour fasting test.

【19】After diagnosis， the next imperative step is localization of the tumour. Contrast-enhanced CT scan is thought to be the first-line investigation. Helical contrast-enhanced CT scan has a sensitivity of around 94% . EUS has become the modality of choice in the localization of these tumours. It can pinpoint the exact location， its relation to the pancreatic duct and biliary tree along with surrounding vasculature. Its sensitivity is around94-96%. However， the main issue with EUS is user dependabil-ity J. ASVS can be a useful modality in cases where the localization is still a problem . However， it is an invasive pro-cedure like EUS. It requires equipment and trained personnel to do it， hence not routinely done and available. At our institution， we routinely perform CT scan， MR and EUS for these tumours and other neuroendocrine tumours of the pancreas. Similarly， in this case -CT scan and EUS were used for the localization of the Surgery is the mainstay of the management of insulinoma， if adequately performed， the patient can be cured . The choice of procedure depends on the location of the tumour， whether its solitary or multiple， the relationship of biliary and pancreatic ducts and the presence of suspicious lymph nodes. Tumour enucleation is the procedure of choice if the tumour is solitary superficial and free of nearby ducts . Most of the lesions have a distinct appearance that can be recognized at the surgery； and there is a well-defined plane that can be used for enucleation. For cases that are in close proximity to the ductal system， major vasculature and there is suspicion of malignancy resection of the pancreas is a better option to avoid pancreatic fistulae and vascular complications. Surgical resection options include pancreaticoduodenectomy， distal pancreatectomy with or without splenectomy and central pancreatectomy. In our case， as the lesion appeared to be in close proximity to the pancreatic duct and was closely abutting the splenic hilum thus we opted for distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy.

【20】The laparoscopic approach is increasingly used and favoured approach for the management of pancreatic lesions in high vol-ume centers. It decreases the morbidity. Oncological outcomes are however similar. The use of laparoscopic ultrasound can fur-ther aid in the localization of the tumour Moreover， the 3-D approach gives better depth perception and further makes la-paroscopic surgery easy and productive . Our case was done by 3-D laparoscopic approach. At our institute， we routinely use3-D High Definition laparoscopy for hepatopancreatic-biliary(HPB) surgery as well as upper and lower Gastrointestinal surg-eries.

【21】Histologically these lesions are neuroendocrine in nature. They have a strong expression of chromogranin and synapto-physin. Ki-67 index and number of mitosis per high field are used to differentiate between grades of tumour. caseOur case was low grade neuroendocrine tumor on the basis of these cri-teria. The diagnosis of malignancy can be difficult to make and only becomes apparent once there are established metastasis.

【22】Conclusion

【23】Insulinomas are rare tumours. Most are benign. Physicians shall have a high index of suspicion based on the symptoms. Management is multidisciplinary and involves endocrinologists， physicians from various specialties， surgeons and pathologist. Insulinomas can be difficult to localize， and there are different investigations with varied accuracy； thus， judicious use shall be made， however， it is imperative to localize the lesion prior to surgery. Surgery， preferably laparoscopy， is the treatment of choice and offers a cure.

【0】ABSTRACT The quantity of cancer survivors in developed countries has tripled since 1970 and is growing by 2% each year. The 5-year survival rate of cancer patients is about 66%， and in 2004 there were 10 million cancer survivors in the United States. Due to improvements in early detection and treatment， the quantity of patients with multiple cancers is rapidly growing. The rapid improvement of cancer treatment (chemotherapy or radiotherapy) will increase the side effects， such as the emergence of other types of malignancies. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasm (t-MN) consists of therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia (t-AML) and therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (t-MDS). This type of malignancy is raised after treatment with chemotherapy， radiotherapy， immunosuppressive agents， or after documented exposure to environmental carcinogens. We report the case of 49 years old woman with cervical cancer. She was treated by chemotherapy (paclitaxel， carboplatin) and radiotherapy. After about 4 years of initial chemotherapy， she was diagnosed with t-MN(t-AML). Based on the event's timeline in our patient， we strongly suspected carboplatin， paclitaxel， and radiotherapy as the culprit in the pathogenesis of this myeloid neoplasm. After incomplete induction chemotherapy， she passed away following pulmonary leukostasis and septic shock suspicion.

【1】KEYWORDS therapy-related myeloid neoplasm， chemotherapy， radiotherapy

【2】Introduction

【3】The prevalence of cancer survivors in developing countries has increased since 1970 and has grown by 2% each year. The 5-year survival rate of cancer was 66%， and approximately 10 million cancer survivors were exposed to a carcinogenic environment in2004. One of the serious conditions often experienced by cancer survivors is the development of other types of cancer. Improve-ment of early detection and advances in chemotherapy and ra-diotherapy modalities make the quantity of multiple cancers pa tients increase rapidly (1/6 of primary cancers). Therapy-related myeloid neoplasm (t-MN)， consisting of therapy-related acute myeloid leukaemia (t-AML) and therapy-related myelodysplas-tic syndrome (t-MDS)， is a malignancy as a result of chemother-apy， radiotherapy， immunosuppressive agents， or exposure to the carcinogenic environment. There are overlapping clinical， morphological， and genetic features between t-AML and t-MDS； WHO Classification of Hematopoietic Neoplasms considers t-AML and t-MDS a unique clinicopathological syndrome unit of t-MN

【4】Recent studies reported that t-MN has a poor prognosis with a median survival of only 8 months and a survival rate of fewer than 10 years. t-MN is often involved with the loss of chromo-somes 5 and/or 7. Patients with t-MN are generally excluded from clinical trials； therefore， prospective data on t-MN therapy are limited. However， bone marrow transplantation is the only curative therapy for t-MN patients， although its survival was low. Therefore， increasing cancer survivors and poor progno- sis of t-MN become urgent for clinicians to identify the t-MN earlier， resulting in earlier therapy and improved survival.

【5】In this case report， we will discuss a 49-year-old woman with cervical carcinoma who has a history of chemotherapy regimens of paclitaxel and carboplatin， as well as 33 times of radiotherapy. Four years after the first exposure to chemotherapy， patients presented with a clinical presentation of bicytopenia， and a bone marrow puncture (BMP) examination showed AML. This case report is expected to increase the knowledge and awareness of clinicians regarding the possibility of secondary malignancies as a result of chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

【6】Case report

【7】On 16 November 2019， a female patient， 49 years old， Balinese， came with complaints of weakness in the last 7 days before admission to the hospital and had worsened since a day be-fore coming to the hospital. Weakness is felt all over the body， accompanied by blurred vision and ringing ears. The patient also complained of defecation mixed with blood since a day before admission to the hospital. The stool was blood red mixed with faeces. Complaints of bloody stools did not coincide with bleeding from the genital.

【8】The patient had been diagnosed with cervical carcinoma since2015 at Sanglah Hospital. The patient underwent a chemother-apy regimen of paclitaxel carboplatin 6 series in 2015， then un-derwent radiotherapy 33 times since 2016. Afterwards， the pa-tient was declared to have completed therapy by an Obstetrics-gynecology doctor and had repeated pap smear tests. The pa-tient stated no complaints during 2017 until mid-2019， On phys-ical examination， the general condition was moderately ill and fully alert. Blood pressure was 110/70 mmHg， pulse rate was90 beats per minute， respiratory rate was 18 breaths per minute， and axillary temperature was 36.3 C. On examination of the head， the conjunctiva was anaemic， and there were no enlarged lymph nodes in the neck to axillary and inguinal areas. The tho-racic examination was normal. On abdominal examination was also normal， with no palpable enlargement of the liver or spleen. Extremities felt warm. The supporting examination revealed leukocyte levels of 18.15 x 103/uL (4.10-11.0x103/uL)，lympho-cytes 14.51 x103/pL (1.00-4.00x103/pL)， monocytes 0.12 x103/uL (0.10-1.2x103/uL)，eosinophils 0.00x103/pL (0.00-0.5x103/uL)，basophils 0.17 x103/ L (0.00-0.1x103/pL)，neutrophils3.34x103/uL(2.50-7.50x103/pL)，hemoglobin 8.38 g/dL(13.5-17，5 g/dL)， MCV 90.48 fL (80-100 fL)， MCH 30.52 pg (26-34 pg)， MCHC 33.73 g/dl(31-36g/dL)， platelets 13.3x103/uL (150-440x103/uL)， Serum Glutamic Oxaloacetic Transaminase (SGOT)96.2 U/L (11-33 U/L)， Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase(SGPT) 44.4 U/L(11-50 U/L)， Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)5mg/dL (8-23 mg/dL)， serum creatinine 0.68 mg/dL (0.7-1.2mg/dL)， sodium 135 mmol/L(136-145 mmol/L) and potassium4.33 mmol/L (3.5-5.1 mmol/L). Hemostasis physiology examina-tion result was PPT 16.3 seconds (10.8-14.4 seconds)， APTT 22.8seconds (24-36 seconds)， and INR 1.17 seconds (0.9-1.1 seconds). Peripheral blood smear examination showed normochromic anisopoikilocytosis erythrocytes (spherocytes， ovalocytes)， poly-chromasia cells (+)， normoblasts ；leukocyte count increased， differential count lymphocytosis， immature cells resembling lym-phoblasts was found， atypical positive lymphocytes， negative toxic granules； negative vacuolization； platelet count decreased， negative giant platelets， negative clumping； bicytopenia with leukocytosis， suspected acute leukemia dd/ALL/AML. Figure 1shows the results of peripheral blood smear result. Imaging ex- aminations were performed， consisting of a chest X-ray and CT scan of the abdomen with contrast. The first chest X-ray with the anteroposterior (AP) position was taken on November 16，2019， showed no abnormalities on the heart and lungs . An abdominal CT scan with contrast was performed regarding the patient's complaints of blood in the stool. On examination， there were multiple nodules in both lungs suspected of metastatic nodules， compression of the L1 corpus， abdominal aortosclero-sis， and lumbar spondylosis， no visible metastatic nodules in the liver and paraaortic， uterine atrophy， differential diagnosis of post-chemotherapy， and no visible uterine mass .

【9】examination on November 26， 2019. The bone marrow aspira-tion showed hypercellular cellularity； the activity of erythroid system decreased； myeloid system activity increased， about 30%of myeloblasts had positive maturation； activity of megakary-ocyte system decreased； no non-hematopoietic cell infiltration into the bone marrow was found； in conclusion that the bone marrow picture characterized an AML M2 . Mean-while， morphological picture based on bone biopsy examination of the iliac crest revealed marrow hypercellular with increased number of blast cells， almost non-existent maturation could be appropriate for Acute Myeloid Leukemia .

【10】Based on those BMP results， the patient was diagnosed with AML M2. The patient was currently optimizing his general con-dition by administering packed red cell (PRC) transfusions up to Hb level reach 10 g/dL and thrombocyte concentrate up to platelet level reach 20，000 or the bleeding stops. Based on her age and good performance status (Eastern Cooperative Oncol-ogy Group/ECOG 1)， she was planning to receive induction chemotherapy of daunorubicin for 3 days and cytarabine for7 days， but the patient was still discussing. The patient was also referred back to the Obstetrics and Gynecology Department to manage cervical carcinoma. The Obstetrics and Gynecology Department diagnosed the patient with residual cervical carci-noma stage III B， and a repeat pap smear was performed. The results of a repeat pap smear  concluded no intraepithelial lesions or malignancy， and there were reactive cellular changes related to post-radiation inflammation. The pap smear results are similar to her last pap smear on 15 May 2017with no evidence of malignant cells， and there were reactive cellular changes related to radiation. According to the results of repeated pap smears， gynaecologists did not plan specific treatment， only supportive therapy.

【11】and cytarabine regimen on 2 January 2020. On the fourth day， chemotherapy had to be stopped because the patient got febrile neutropenia. Patient complained fever with axillary temperature of 38.7oC and a complete blood examination revealed leukocytes0.82x103/pL(4.10-11.0x103/uL)，lymphocytes 0.46x103/pL(1.00-4.00x103/pL)，eosinophil 0.00x103/uL (0.00-0.5x103/uL)， basophils 0.01x103/pL (0.00-0，1x103/uL)， neutrophils 0.34 x103/uL(2.50-7.50x103/uL)， monocytes 0.00x103/uL (0.10-1.20x 103/uL)，hemoglobin 10.61 g/dL (13.5-17.5g/dL)， MCV 77.02fL (80-100 fL)， MCH 26.03 pg (26-34 pg)， MCHC 33.80 g /dl(31-36g/dL)， platelet 17.77x 103/uL(150-440x103/uL). To rule out the source of infection， the urinalysis revealed normal results(leukocyte sediment 3/High Power Field (HPF)， erythrocyte sed-iment 1/HPF， and chest X-ray examination on 6 January 2020was also normal . The patient received treatment for febrile neutropenia in administering granulocyte-colony stim-ulating factor (G-CSF)300 meg once a day subcutaneously， cef-tazidime 2 gram three times a day intravenously， and transfusion of thrombocyte concentrate. After the patient's condition im-proved， she was discharged and planned to undergo another induction chemotherapy of daunorubicin and cytarabine.

【12】In the end， induction chemotherapy could not be carried out because the patient was re-hospitalized on 1 March 2020 and diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) class ⅣV according to Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) concomitant with Bell's palsy. After receiving empiric antibiotic therapy and treat-ment of Bell's palsy from the neurologist， the patient was dis-charged， and reinduction chemotherapy was postponed. On 26March 2020， the patient was re-hospitalized again with diagnosis of CAP PSI class IV concomitant by septic shock and suspicion of pulmonary leukostasis. Laboratory examination revealed leuko-cytes 328 x103/pL (4.10-11.0x 103/uL)， lymphocytes 13.1 x103/pL(1.00-4.00x103/uL)， eosinophils 0.24 x 103/pL (0.00-0.5x103/uL)， basophils 121.00x103/uL(0.00-0.1x103/uL)，neu-trophils 14.10x103/uL (2.50-7.50x103/uL)， monocytes 180.00x103/pL(0.10-1.20x103/uL)，hemoglobin 9.15 g/dL (13.5-17.5gr/dL)， MCV 87.84 fL (80-100 fL)， MCH 26.10 pg (26-34 pg)， MCHC 29.80 g/dl(31-36g/dL)， platelets 20.84x103/pL (150-440x103/uL)， SGOT52.4U/L (11-33U/L)， SGPT 60.70U/L(11-50 U/L)， BUN 11.1 mg/dL (8-23 mg/dL)，serum creatinine 0.70mg/dL (0.7-1.2 mg/dL)， sodium 133 mmol/L (136-145mmol/L) and potassium 2.24 mmol/L (3.5-5.1 mmol/L)， albumin 3.10g/dL (3.40-4.80 g/dL)， LDH 2002 u/1 (240-480 u/L)， and uric acid 5.9 mg/dL (2.00-5.70 mg/dL)， pH 7.55 (7.35-7.45)，pCO236.3 mmHg (35-45mmHg)， pO2 50.10 mmHg (80-100mmHg)， HCO3-31 mmol/L (22-26 mmol/L)， and SO2 90% (95-100%).A chest X-ray examination on 26 March 2020 characterized pneu-monia and there were no abnormalities on heart . At the time， patient got hydrated， empiric antibiotic therapy for pneumonia (cefoperazone and levofloxacin)， cytoreduction with hydroxyurea (1000 mg dose twice a day)， potassium correction and thrombocyte concentrate transfusion. In the end， patient died of septic shock and pulmonary leukostasis. Figure 6 shows the disease history of patient from the diagnosis of cervical car-cinoma to AML.

【13】Discussion

【14】T-MN malignancy， which consists of t-AML and t-MDS， is one of the malignancies as a result of chemotherapy，radiotherapy， immunosuppressive agents， or exposure to a carcinogenic en-vironment. Epidemiologically， the study by Morton et al.， revealed the highest standardized incidence ratio t-MN was in patients who received chemotherapy at a young age. The stan-dardized incidence ratio increased again in patients older than 65vears old. The standardized incidence ratio was also increased in the higher stage of malignancy， associated with more frequent and longer exposure to leukemogenic agents (chemotherapy and other agents). In most cases， the t-MN is associated with breast cancer and lymphoproliferative therapy. A population-based study by Morton et al. consisting of 426，068 adults re-ceiving chemotherapy identified 801 cases of t-MN showed an increased risk of t-MN by 4.7 times compared to the general population. Group receiving chemotherapy for oesophagal， anal， cervical，endometrial， and prostate malignancies are a new high-risk group for t-MN other than breast and lymphoprolifer-ative cancers . The risk of developing t-MN is also much higher in patients receiving combination chemotherapy and radiotherapy than chemotherapy alone， which is related to the radiotherapy effect in increasing t-MN risk.

【15】Based on this epidemiological study， the growth of t-MN， in this case， might be related to the combination of chemotherapy and radiotherapy in the patient. Chemotherapy in cervical car-cinoma is recognized as a high-risk factor of developing t-MN， although it is less frequently compared to breast and lympho-proliferative mali1gg1nancies. In addition， the type of chemother-apy agent administered also plays a role in developing t-MN. Based on previous studies， chemotherapy agents that often trig-ger the emergence of t-MN are alkylating agents (carboplatin， cisplatin， cyclophosphamide， nitrosourea， and melphalan) and DNA-topoisomerase I inhibitors (etoposide， daunorubicin， and doxorubicin). A case-control study by Travis et al.， reported that carboplatin and cisplatin would increase the risk of t-MN， especially t-AML type. The study by Travis et al. included pa-tients with ovarian cancer and did not include the paclitaxel regimen. In addition to chemotherapy， administration of G-CSF in patients undergoing chemotherapy or severe congenital neu-tropenia is also a risk factor for the development of t-MN . Chemotherapy agents suspected to cause t-MN， in this case， are carboplatin and paclitaxel. As an alkylating agent contain-ing platinum， Carboplatin can interact with DNA through vari-ous mechanisms， such as monoadduct formation， inter-strand cross-links， and intra-strand cross-links， including DNA base alkylation. Some of these mechanisms may result in cell death， termination of DNA replication， and loss of chromosomes，lead-ing to mutations and the development of leukaemia. Meanwhile， the role of paclitaxel as a causal agent of t-MN is still contro-versial. The literature stated that paclitaxel was not a leuke-mogenic agent in animals or humans. Meanwhile， several case reports showed the role of paclitaxel in the development of t-MN in ovarian and breast cancer， non-small cell lung can-cer (NSCLC)， neuroendocrine， and seminoma. In these studies， the mean total dose of paclitaxel administered was 1342.5 mg； the standard dose for gynecologic malignancies (175mg/m2). The malignancy-induced potential of paclitaxel is probably not dose-related but rather related to the idiosyncratic response to the drug. The underlying mechanism of t-MN development by paclitaxel is still unclear， but it may be mediated through DNA damage. Paclitaxel as a microtubule-stabilizing drug may cause cytokinesis failure . Subsequent cytokinesis failure can result in DNA damage. In this case， radiotherapy is also suspected of playing a role in causing the emergence of t-MN. Radiation exposure can damage DNA through the same mechanism as alkylating agents. Photon energy radiation can directly damage the DNA strand. Studies of radiotherapy in the pelvic region (in invasive tumours of the vulva， cervix， uterus， anus， and rectosigmoid) showed that the risk of post-treatment leukaemia increased by 72% (Hazard ratio \[HR\]=1.72； 95% CI，1.37-2.15). The risk of leukemia peaks at 5-10 years after radio-therapy.

【16】Each chemotherapy agent， as well as radiotherapy， has a different latency period. The latency period is between first exposure to an agent (chemotherapy， radiation) until t-MN de-velops. Carboplatin has an average latency period of 4 years(the minimumlatency period is 1.3 years)； some studies revealed up to 10 years. According to several case reports， the la- tency period of paclitaxel varies， but the mean latency period of paclitaxel was 8.75 months. However， in one case reported by Ishikawa et al.， the latency period was up to 3 years 10months. Meanwhile， the latency period of radiotherapy is al-most similar to alkylating agent， which is 4 years. In our case， the patient’s latency period was about 4 years， which sig nifies the most likely causal agent for developing t-MN in this patient： carboplatin and radiotherapy. However， the latency period varied in some cases， so the role of paclitaxel cannot be ruled out.

【17】The diagnosis between de novo AML and t-MN (t-AML type) is not different. This patient came with a clinical presentation of weak bloody stools， and a complete blood count revealed leuko-cytosis， anaemia， thrombocytopenia. The diagnosis of AML was confirmed by morphological examination of bone marrow aspi-ration and was also supported by examination of the iliac crest bone biopsy. In this case， the patient met the diagnostic criteria for AML with >20% myeloblasts (30% in this case). This di-agnosis was also supported by a bone biopsy which revealed marrow hypercellularity with an increased number of blast cells， appropriate for AML .

【18】Karyotypic abnormalities are often found in t-MN. Clonal chromosomal abnormalities can be detected in 80-95% of t-MN(both t-AML and t-MDS). t-MN often involves deletions of chro-mosomes 5q and 7q (these chromosomes likely contain the myeloid tumour-suppressor gene)， with the breakpoint of the deletion referred to as the critical region . Researchers have identified a critical region on chromosome 5，5q31.1，con-taining an early growth response (EGR-1). Meanwhile， the break-points for the deletion of chromosome 7q varied， 7q22 in the proximal and q31 to q36 in the distal. Abnormalities on chromo-some 7q are common in myeloid malignancies.

【19】In this case， no cytogenetic examination was performed， which can differentiate t-MN (type t-AML) from de novo AML based on several studies. However， Nardi et al.， reported differences in karyotype abnormalities between t-MN due to radiation (external-beam radiation therapy) and t-MN due to chemotherapy/combined-modality therapy (CMT). In cytoge-netic findings， 83% of t-MN due to chemotherapy/CMT showed a karyotype abnormality， whereas only 50% cases of t-MN were due to radiation and de novo AML (p<0.001). The most com-mon abnormality in chemotherapy/CMT-induced t-MN was the deletion of the long arm or entire chromosome 5 or 7， which was less common in radiation-induced t-MN (p<0.001). This study emphasizes that the genetic abnormality of AML de novo was almost similar to radiation-induced t-MN. Attempts to differentiate t-MN (t-AML type) from AML de novo was also carried out by Wang et al. They found the most common chro-mosomal abnormalities of t-AML compared with de novo AML were copy-losses of chromosome 5 (4.8 vs. 1.6%， p=0.02) and chromosome 13 (2.7 vs. 0.6%，p=0.02). Abnormality of chro-mosomes 3， 10， 14， 15， 16， and 22 were only found in de novo AML

【20】Although promising， it should be noted that about 14% of cases of t-MN have a normal karyotype. Therefore， the diag-nosis of t-MN based on chronological events is very important. The diagnosis of t-MN in this particular case was established based on the chronology of t-MN emergence (latency period) since the patient was exposed to carboplatin， paclitaxel， and ra-diotherapy. This chronological analysis was also applied to other case reports regarding t-MN， such as case reports by Bhatnagar et al.， Lalya et al.， and Vijayaraghavan et al.

【21】Risk factors of t-MN

【22】Alkylating agent therapy：May cause MDS (preleukemic phase)， need 4-10 years until AML developed5g or 7g deletion， the prognosis is poor DNA-topoisomerase II inhibitor therapy (epipodophyllotoxins and anthracyclines)：May develop to t-Acute Myeloid leukaemia (t-AML) without preleukemic phase， the short median of latency period (33 months). Translocation 11q23 (MLL) or 21g22Morphologic phenotype， usually M4M5 (based on FAB classification) Ionizing radiation therapy：Similar to alkylating-related AML

【23】G-CSF

【24】Treatment of t-MN (in this case， t-AML) consists of chemotherapy and bone marrow transplantation. In chemotherapy， we should decide whether to apply intensive or non-intensive (palliative) induction chemotherapy based on age， comorbidities， bone marrow reserve， and performance status. In general， age below 70 years and good performance are indica-tions for intensive induction chemotherapy. In this case， the patient met the criteria for intensive induction chemotherapy49 years of age， with an ECOG score of 1. Meanwhile， bone marrow transplantation was not planned because of the limited facilities.

【25】The choice of the chemotherapy regimen of this case is quite difficult because there are still few studies on the efficacy of standard chemotherapy for the t-AML type. Induction chemotherapy regimens of daunorubicin and cytarabine have become the standard regimen for AML patients. A German-Austrian AL study group assessed the clinical outcome of 200t-AML patients treated between 1993 and 2008， which survival of t-AML patients was compared with 2653 AML de novo pa-tients. Although the response rate to induction chemotherapy was similar， the overall survival (OS) of t-AML patients was worse than de novo AML patients. The poor efficacy of the standard regimen has led several studies to seek alternative regimens for t-AML cases. One of the regimens which were reported to have better efficacy than the standard regimen was liposomal cytarabine-daunorubicin 351 (CPX-351)， a formula-tion of daunorubicin and cytarabine with a molar ratio of 5：1(in a liposomal carrier). Patients given CPX-351 had better OS at 24 months (hazard ratio=0.46， p=0.01). Meanwhile， in this case， the patient received induction chemotherapy regimens of daunorubicin and cytarabine but had to be stopped on the 4th day because of febrile neutropenia. Efficacy and response of in-duction chemotherapy， in this case， cannot be evaluated because it may only be done after the patient has completed all steps of induction chemotherapy.

【26】This patient died from pulmonary leukostasis and infection(sepsis) four months after diagnosis. This is consistent with pre-vious studies that reported t-MN patients would have a poor prognosis despite proper diagnosis and treatment. Specif-ically， the median survival of t-MN is only 8 months， and the survival rate is less than 10 years. However， the invention of alternative chemotherapeutic agents which have greater efficacy than standard chemotherapy is an opportunity for clinicians to improve the survival of t-MN patients.

【27】Summary

【28】We reported a female patient， 49 years， Balinese， with cervical carcinoma and t-MN. The diagnosis of t-MN was confirmed by tracing the history of therapy (the latency period of leuke-mogenic agents)， examination of peripheral blood smears， bone marrow aspiration， and examination of the iliac crest bone biopsy. The suspected causative agents of t-MN in this patient are carboplatin， paclitaxel， and radiotherapy. Treatment of t-MN， specifically in t-AML type， consists of chemotherapy and bone marrow transplantation. However， the OS of t-MN patients treated with standard chemotherapy worse than de novo AML patients. After receiving induction chemotherapy regimens of daunorubicin and cytarabine， which had to be stopped on day4 due to febrile neutropenia， the patient died within 3 months after chemotherapy. This is inseparable from epidemiological studies， which showed that t-MN has a poor prognosis withlow median survival.

【0】ABSTRACT Limitation in joint mobility was recognized as the most common and earliest long-term complication of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The study assessed the range of motion in selected joints of patients with type 2diabetes mellitus and compared it with aged-matched healthy individuals Fifty subjects volunteered to participate in the study this comprised of 25 patients with type 2 diabetic mellitus and 25age and sex matched healthy individuals.

【1】The range of motion of the joints of the shoulder， wrist thumb， index and the middle fingers of diabetics and normal subjects were measured with a full circle universal goniometer using a standard protocol. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Alpha level was set at 0.05

【2】The result showed that there was a significant difference between the range of motion of the measured joints； shoulder(t=-23， p=0.000)， metacarpophalangeal joints of the index finger in flexion (t=7.056， p=0.000) and extension (t=-13.548， p=0.000) in diabetics when compared with non-diabetic subjects (p<0.005).

【3】In conclusion， limited joint mobility occurs in subjects with type 2 diabetics as one of the complications of the disease.

【4】KEYWORDS range of motion， shoulder joints， elbow joint upper limb joints， type 2 diabetes mellitus

【5】Introduction

【6】Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is a significant health problem with a report by the World Health Organization that about 422 million people have diabetes mellitus in the world. The prevalence of diabetes mellitus is increasing rapidly； by 2025 it’s suggested that the number of people with diabetes mellitus will be dou- bled. According to International Diabetes Foundation it was estimated that about 415 million adults have diabetes， it's expected to rise to 642 million by 2040. Seventy-five percent of adults with diabetes are found in low and middle-income countries， and about 5 million people died of diabetes in 2015 . The prevalence of diabetes in Africa is 1% in rural areas， and it ranges from 5%-7% in urban sub-Saharan African . Past stud-ies in Nigeria have shown the prevalence of the condition among the citizens in which the prevalence was at 0.8% to 2.8%. However， the current prevalence of DM in Nigeria is not known but maybe around 8% to 10%.

【7】Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease that occurs when the pancreas fails to produce insulin or when the body cannot uti-lize the insulin produced. The world health organization classified diabetes mellitus into two principal forms， type 1 dia-betes also known as insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus(IDDM) and typed 2 diabetes known as non-insulin dependent diabetes (NIDDM) . In type 1 diabetes， the pancreas fails to produce insulin， and in type 2 diabetes is as a result of ineffective use of the insulin produced by the pancreas1. Fisman et al. reported that the prolong hyperglycemia was due to increased protein glycation among diabetes patients and the resultant generation of free radicals which leads to glycation of extracellular matrix and increased tissue stiffness.

【8】Diabetes mellitus is one of the leading cause of neuropathy， and the most prevalent clinical form of diabetic neuropathy is distal symmetrical polyneuropathy affecting about 90 percent of the patients I. Limitation in joint mobility was recog-nized as the most common and earliest long-term complication of type 1 DM and also in type 2 DM. Musculoskeletal dis-orders， Achilles tendon pathology， trigger finger， Dupuytren limited joint mobility syndrome， carpal tunnel syndrome， frozen shoulder and plantar fasciitis have been found to occur more often in subjects with diabetes compared to non-diabetics . Reduced joint mobility is frequent but not widely recognized musculoskeletal complication of diabetes . Ikem et al doc-umented some of the characteristics of diabetic foot disease， another study on the association between the hand abnormal-ity and the duration of diabetes but not age or sex was carried out by Gamstedtit are appropriate to evaluate the effects of dia-betes on a range of motion of hand and shoulder joints. Hence， this study therefore， assessed the quantitative effects of type 2 diabetes mellitus in these joints especially among blacks.

【9】Materials and Methods

【10】Subjects

【11】Subjects for this study were individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus attending the diabetes clinics of the Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospital Complex (OAUTHC)，Ile-Ife，Osun State and healthy individuals of the same age and sex.

【12】Inclusion Criteria

【13】The study involved both male and female individuals with type2 diabetes mellitus attending the diabetes clinics of Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospital Complex (OAUTHC)， lle-Ife， Osun State for at least one year and healthy individuals of the same age and sex.

【14】Exclusion Criteria

【15】1\. Patients with limited joint mobility due to trauma

【16】2\. Patients with stroke

【17】3\. Patients with joint disease like osteoarthritis

【37】The ethical approval was obtained from the Health Research and Ethics Committee， Institute of Public Health， Obafemi Awolowo University， Ile-Ife， Osun State， for the study. The purpose and procedures of the research were explained to each subject， and their informed consent was obtained as well. Participants were also screened for history of trauma of the joint， joints disease(osteoarthritis) and joint pain. The joints’ range of motion was measured and recorded in degrees.

【38】The range of motion of the following joint was measured

【39】Shoulder joint

【40】The subject was in supine position， with the knee flexed to flatten the lumbar spine. The shoulder is positioned in 0 degrees of abduction， adduction， and rotation. The forearm is positioned in 0 degrees of supination and pronation so that the palm faces the body. The fulcrum of the goniometer was placed close to the acromial process； the two arms were aligned along the lateral midline of the humerus and extend over the lateral epicondyle of the humerus. The subject was instructed to flex the shoulder，and the angle was measured with the movable arm. For shoulder extension the subject was in prone position， with the goniometer at the same position as flexion， the subject was instructed to move the hand backwards， the angle measured

【41】Wrist joint

【42】The patient was in sitting position， the forearm resting on a table for both wrist flexion and extension. The fulcrum of the goniometer was placed at the level of the triquetrum. The sta-tionary arm was aligned along the ulna in line with the olecranon process and the ulnar styloid process. The movable arm was aligned along the fifth metacarpal. For wrist flexion， the subject was instructed to move the hand down and the angle measured. Wrist extension was measured with the goniometer at the same position， the subject was instructed to move the hand upward， and the angle measured .

【59】This study was carried out to assess the range of motion in se-lected joints of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and age and sex match control. This indicates the homogeneity of the two groups and that any variation observed in the measure ment were as a result of the disease not based on anthropometric differences.

【0】ABSTRACT Medicinal plants have been used by the Moroccan population from ancient times. They have an important role in traditional healing practices. Patients use CAM for different purposes and due to several factors， such as low economic and financial income and/or cultural and religious beliefs. However， proof of efficacy and safety of the vast majority of traditional and herbal medicine have not been fully established through an evidence-based approach. During the current Covid 19 pandemic， the long-term implementation of national emergency and lockdown measures resulted in difficulties accessing healthcare services. Therefore， cancer patients at Hematology and Oncology Hospital of Marrakech showed an increased interest in using traditional herbal medicine. The present study attempts to determine the prevalence and the aim of using each method of CAM by cancer patients during the Covid-19 pandemic in Marrakech.

【1】KEYWORDS Covid-19， cancer， complementary and alternative medicine， herbal medicine

【2】Introduction

【3】At the end of December 2019， The world known the COVID-19pandemic， also known as the coronavirus pandemic， caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) .

【4】The disease was first identified in Wuhan， China. It became a

【5】Public Health Emergency of International Concern in January 2020 and was subsequently recognized as a pandemic in March 2020.

【6】On March the 2nd， 2020， the Moroccan Ministry of Health announced the first coronavirus case. Until October the 6th 2020， Morocco has confirmed more than 133.272 cases of the infection. including 2330 deaths and 111036 recoveries .

【7】This pandemic had a major impact on cancer patients . Liang et al. have reported that cancer patients might have a higher risk of COVID-19 infection. They have also shown that this particular population presents a higher risk of severe events such as admission to the intensive care unit， requiring invasive ventilation and death， especially if they have received chemotherapy or undergone surgery in the past month .

【8】In Morocco， patients use CAM for preventive and/or cura-tive purposes due to low economic and financial income and/or cultural and religious beliefs. According to the literature， the methods often used are medicinal plants and spiritual practices. During the ongoing pandemic， the Moroccan population used traditional herbal medicines to prevent this disease. Medic inal plants have been used by the Moroccan population from ancient times. They have an important role in traditional heal-ing practices. Today herbal medicine is practiced in all parts of Morocco. It is still the primary healthcare system for a large fraction of the population， especially in rural communities . However， the long-term implementation of national emergency and lockdown measures resulted in difficulties accessing health-care services. Therefore， cancer patients at Hematology and Oncology Hospital of Marrakech showed an increased interest in using traditional herbal medicine.

【9】However， proof of efficacy and safety of the vast majority of traditional and herbal medicine have not been fully established through an evidence-based approach， inducing a dilemma for physicians regarding the use of Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) among their patients. Therefore， the present study attempts to determine the prevalence and the aim of using each method of CAM by cancer patients during the Covid-19pandemic in Marrakech.

【10】Materials and methods

【11】Study Design and setting

【12】The present study is a cross-sectional study； data were collected using an anonymous questionnaire filled by cancer patients who visited the Marrakesh haematology-oncology Hospital (HOH) during the first six months of the Covid-19 pandemic in Mo-IOCCO.

【13】Participants and sampling Method

【14】The sample size was calculated by the Yamane simplified for-mula， using a 95% confidence level. A minimum sample of 285was calculated. Therefore， 300 participants were included in this study. They were randomly selected through the"Random Sample Generator" from the cancer centre database.

【15】Study questionnaire

【16】We used an anonymous questionnaire to collect information from the participants between March and June 2020. Partici-pants were interviewed by phone using dialectal Arabic as a language (response rate： 100%). We asked them about their socio-demographic characteristics， cultural variables， type of cancer， ongoing treatment， and CAM methods.

【17】The participants could choose the relevant used CAM method either from the list， or they could specify any unlisted methods and score as“others".

【18】Some sections of the questionnaire aimed to appreciate how our participants perceived the use of CAM and whether they sought advice from their health care providers regarding CAM use.

【19】Statistical Analysis

【20】We used descriptive statistics to calculate frequencies and per-centages for each variable. The statistical analysis was per-formed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 24.0.

【21】Results

【22】Demographic and social characteristiccss ooff oouurr patients5

【23】The current study included a total of 300 participants. The preva-lence of CAM use was 70% (210 participants)； 52% had used at least one CAM method over a lifetime， 13% had used CAM after their cancer diagnosis， and only 7.3% had begun to use CAM during the COVID-19 pandemic. Half of the patients who used CAM were above the age of 50 years. 76% of them were married， and 70% of them were females， illiterates in 64.29% of cases and from a low socioeconomic level in 88.5%

【24】CAM methods used by our participants

【25】Our results showed that natural honey was the frequent bio-logical modality used， followed by medicinal plants， especially Clove and Eucalyptus. Although，interestingly， spiritual modal-ities are widely used in our sample (57%)， they included the practice of prayer， the reading of the 《Qur’an》， and fasting.

【26】Reasons for use and perceived effectiveness

【27】In our study， CAM users believed CAM use could improve the immune system against viral infection， increase the efficacy of prescribed treatment and improve the general health condition. However， a quarter of them believed that CAM should be taken with conventional cancer treatment， and 12% think it should be used alone.

【28】Reasons of non-use

【29】61% of the participants reported that they do not believe in the effectiveness of CAM， and 39% worried about the adverse effects of CAM use and the possible interactions with cancer treatment.

【30】Sources of information received by CAM users

【31】Different sources of information were observed. dominated by the entourage (55.71%) and social media (28%). On the other hand， none of our patients has sought information from their health care providers.

【32】Discussion

【33】Morocco has one of the oldest and richest traditions of herbal medicine， and local people possess valuable knowledge of medicinal plants. The researchers counted more than 600 plants used in herbal medicine in this North African country .

【34】Complementary and alternative medicine has become more frequently used in the routine practice of cancer patients world-wide . The prevalence of use of CAM in our study was70%， which is in accordance with what was reported in previ-ous studies exploring CAM use in Morocco . Although the international data showed variable results， in a meta-analysis by Ernst E and al the prevalence of CAM use across the literature ranged from 7% to 85% J. We also found a little increase in CAM use in cancer patients during the pandemic (5%). This increased use may be explained by gender， age， and socioeco-nomic level factors. Previous studies found that the use of CAM is associated with female gender， younger age and tertiary ed-ucation level. In our research， over 50% of CAM users were females over 50 and from a low socioeconomic range. In the African and Arabic series， the profile of CAM users is identical to ours .

【35】In our study， 90% of users reported at least one benefit from CAM. Natural products (NPs)， such as plants and honey， are in-valuable sources of new chemical entities with innovative chem-ical profiles and key biological properties . Their importance is shown by the fact that about 40 to 80% of drugs approved by the FDA during the period 1981-2014 were directly or indirectly derived from NPs， with antimicrobials and anticancer drugs having the highest percentages. Medicinal plants were used by 70% of our patients； the majority of these plants are usually used to treat respiratory diseases causing symptoms and signs similar to coronavirus disease， according to several studies . Anserine and Marrubium， for example， are two traditional Moroccan treatments for fever and flu， the significant symptoms similar to those of coronavirus disease . Our patients also used them to prevent and treat fever and cough. Honey has a known potential to soothe the throat and provide relief for symptomatic cough . This product was used by 50% of our patients in this pandemic period showing increased levels of consumption compared to what was reported in a previous study in Marrakesh .

【36】Many researchers claim antiviral properties in CAM， but the choice of its use in COVID-19 is still in the experimental stage
