【20】The filarial dance sign refers to the twirling motion of microfilariae noted in dilated lymphatic channels. It is a characteristic sign and indicator of Scrotal filariasis.

【21】Discussion

【22】Scrotal Anatomy on ultrasound

【23】Both testes lie within the scrotum， divided into the right and left hemiscrotum by a median raphe. The normal male testes are oval-shaped and measuree5x3x2cm with a homogenous echotexture. The epididymis is an elongated structure situated at the posterior border of the testicle and is divided into the head， tail and body. The epididymis lies in the superior pole of the testes and is isoechoic or slightly hyperechoic to the adjacent testes parenchyma. The epididymis body and tail are sit-uated behind and along the inferior pole of the testes and are isoechoic to the testes. The testes and epididymis are covered by a fibrous capsule， the tunica albuginea， which is seen as a thin echogenic band that outlines the testes. We encountered a common pitfall at the junction of the head and body region of the epididymis， where prominent focal hypoechogenicity was seen. This is the normal entry of the body of epididymis into the head and should not be over-diagnosed. The spermatic cord appears as a highly echogenic band within the inguinal canal. The mediastinum of testes appears as an echogenic band .

【24】Scrotal pathologies on ultrasound

【25】Epididymitis and epididymo-orchitis is the most common cause of acute scrotal pain in adolescent boys and young male adults， with a prevalence of 40 per 10000 due to acute bacterial infection， which is also seen in our study. When this infection spreads to the testes， it is called epididymo-orchitis， occurring in about20-40% of cases. Ultrasound findings of epididymitis include an enlarged and hypervascular epididymis with inhomogeneous echotexture， predominantly hypoechoic. Colour Doppler USG has a sensitivity of almost 100% in the diagnosis of acute inflammation. Ancillary findings include hydrocele or pyocele， scrotal wall thickening， fistula formation and calcifications Timely diagnosis becomes important because of impending com-plications like an epididymal abscess， pyocele or hematopyocele. Our findings were concordant with Rizvi et al. 

【26】Orchitis appears as diffuse testicular involvement and is asso-ciated with epididymis. We found that testicles appear enlarged and heterogeneous with the markedly increased flow on colour Doppler. Epididymo-orchitis demonstrates diffuse hetero-geneous echotexture with increased vascularity within . Rizvi et al.  reported similar imaging findings and propor- tions. Funiculitis can present with radiating dull aching pain and ultrasound spermatic cord thickening and heterogeneity with increased vascularity on colour Doppler and probe tenderness .

【27】Torsion is mostly seen in adolescent males but can occur at any age. The bell clapper deformity is found bilaterally most often. The most sensitive and specific sign of torsion is the whirlpool sign， seen as spiral twisting or rotation of the spermatic cord. Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency. A definite diagnosis of complete testicular torsion is made when colour Doppler fails to detect blood flow in the affected testes compared to the unaffected . Surgical intervention is prime important， and there is 100% successful if operated within6 hours of symptoms onset. Success rates drop to 0%-20% if symptoms have been present for 12-24 hours. Torsion constitutes17% of scrotal emergencies with an incidence of 1：4000 . Real-time imaging is important in torsion syndrome or intermittent testicular torsion， which presents as intermittent sharp pain caused by impeded vasculature. Multiple repeated episodes over a period of time lead to chronic testicular atrophy . Therefore， colour Doppler evaluation depicting diastolic flow(centripetal flow from Testicular artery branches) is of utmost importance. The most consistent indicator of impaired testicular microcirculation is increased Doppler indices of Resistive index(R.I) and Pulsatility Index (P.I) of capsular branches of testicular arteries .

【28】Pain， swelling and fever combined comprised 44% of our cases， and the testicular abscess was found in most of such patients. Testicular abscesses are mostly complication of epididymo- orchitis or torsion. Rare causes include infected or gangrenous tumors or primary pyogenic infections. Ultra-sound shows heterogeneous hypoechogenicity， with no or mild peripheral vascularity. Testicular architecture is altered with hyperechoic striations separating hypoechoic spaces . Similar imaging can be confined to the epididymis in cases of an epididymal abscess .

【29】The spectrum of inflammatory pathologies is compiled in Chart 3 and Table 3. The most common associated finding in these cases was cellulitis of the scrotal wall， which is a cause of inflammatory scrotal wall oedema. It is mostly seen in immuno-compromised， diabetes， obesity or presence of other intrascrotal pathology. USG shows an increased scrotal wall thickness with hypoechogenicity and increased blood flow on colour Doppler.

【30】COther commonly encountered testicular pathologies include Vasilis. The acute inflammation of the vas deferens results from the retrograde spread of infection from the prostate， prostatic urethra or seminal vesicle. The most common organisms are Haemophilus influenza and Escherichia coli . Ultrasound demonstrates a heterogeneously hypoechoic mass within the inguinal canal， extending towards the scrotal segment and asso-ciated with increased vascularity. Parasitic filariasis infection can involve the scrotum presenting as linear hypoechoic channels secondary to dilated lymphatics. In addition， internal echogenic structures can be seen， showing movement， representing micro-filariae  .

【31】Trauma can manifest as fluid collections (haematocele， hy-drocele or hematoma)， testicular disruption or vascular injury. A discontinuity in the parenchyma of testes is considered a testicu-lar fracture. It is defined by a hypoechoic， linear stripe within the testes. Fracture line has been visualised in 17% of cases . We encountered 4 cases of trauma， and their USG showed het- erogeneous echotexture of testes and irregular contour with the compromised vascular flow， especially diastolic testicular flow Undescended testis primarily presents as an empty scrotal sac. Appropriate localization becomes important because of the substantially increased risk of developing germ cell tumours. We found 7 such cases(7%) and predominantly in pediatric and younger populations 

【32】In our study， 5 cases of the epididymal cyst were encountered， appearing as well defined and anechoic. It contains clear serous fluid content， sometimes showing echoes due to chronicity .

【33】Testicular cysts； simple cysts in the testicular parenchyma，are solitary， anechoic and well-circumscribed and found incidentally Spermatocele mostly arises from the epididymal head and is caused by cystic dilatation of the tubules of the efferent ductules. It shows scattered moving echoes and is mostly due to reflux from obstruction in the vas deference  .

【34】Hydrocele is the collection of fluid between the layers of visceral and parietal lavers of the tunica vaginalis and is the most common cause of painless scrotal swelling. It may or may not communicate with the peritoneal cavity . Congenital hydroceles are due to patent processes vaginalis， whereas ac-quired hydroceles are either idiopathic due to overproduction or impaired absorption secondary to infection， trauma or tor-sion. Hydrocele is encysted if it does not communicate with peritoneum above or tunica vaginalis below. On USG， it is seen as a well-defined fluid collection， not taking vascularity and causing posterior acoustic enhancement .

【35】Varicocele was found in 7 cases in our study (9% of the cases). Infertility was the primary presenting complaint in 2.6% of our cases. As detected by ultrasound， varicocele is the most fre-quent cause of male factor infertility. Others include testicular microlithiasis， epididymal cysts and testicular cysts . A direct correlation of testicular volume (as measured by ultra-sound) with the testicular function was reported by Schurich et al Microlithiasis is usually found incidentally and seen in about5% of males between 17 and 35. Five or more calcified foci per transducer field in single testes are considered abnormal.

【36】Sacrotolith is mobile calcifications in the scrotum and mea-sures less than 10 mm with posterior shadowing on USG. Over-all， these calcifications have no clinical importance.

【37】Other potentially rarer pathologies include Adenomatoid tumour， a benign tumour that mostly arises from the epididy-mal tail . Ultrasonography shows a well-circumscribed hypoechoic， rounded mass with a homogeneous echotexture. Non-germ cell tumour tumours do not show specific ultrasono-graphic characteristics but appear as well defined hypoechoic lesions. Germ cell tumours are most common among all tes-ticular tumours.TThey are divided into seminoma and non-seminomatous gem cell tumours. Seminomas are the most com-mon testicular maglinancy (35-50%) . They appear as hy-poechoic solid lesions with internal blood flow， ranging in size to replace the entire testis . The non-seminomatous tumour appears as heterogeneous and cystic masses with irregular mar-gins. Echogenic foci within the lesion may be associated. The tumour may show increased vascularity mimicking acute tes-ticular inflammation in some cases. However， the underlying testicular parenchyma shows an inhomogeneous appearance rather than a regular echotexture. Ultrasonography follow-up evaluations are recommended to differentiate true inflammatory from tumours mimicking inflammation .

【38】Conclusions

【39】Ultrasonography is the first-line diagnostic modality in evaluat-ing acute or chronic scrotal disease. USG is adjuvant to physical examination to arrive at the correct clinical diagnosis. It is a safe and reliable investigation for demonstrating scrotal anatomy， localization of testicular masses and evaluation of vascularity in real-time. This is of special importance in cases of torsion-detorsion sequelae. High-frequency ultrasound is non-invasive， lacks ionizing radiation， and is simple with reproducible re-sults. It is highly accurate in differentiating between testicular ischemia and torsion from acute inflammatory diseases and solid cases from cystic scrotal masses.

【0】Background：

【1】Melanoma is a common disease that may present in non-cutaneous sites and recur many years after initial diagnosis. These characteristics can make diagnosis and long-term management a challenge for physicians.

【2】Case Report：

【3】This case involves a patient who experienced a recurrence of melanoma in the form of a large pelvic mass 35 years after an initial diagnosis and treatment of cutaneous disease. The presentation of melanoma as a pelvic lesion is highly unusual， and the disease free interval experienced by this patient was the longest we found noted in the medical literature.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Physicians should be aware that melanoma may recur many years after initial diagnosis， and involve numerous non-cutaneous sites. Unfortunately， there are no good recommendations for long-term screening.

【6】Key words： Malignant melanoma · Pelvic mass ·Ultra-late recurrence

【7】Melanoma is a common malignancy that has experi-enced an increasing incidence over the last century. This case report details a highly unusual presentation of this disease. A 55 year old male with abdominal pain was found to have a large pelvic mass， biopsy of which was positive for malignant melanoma. The patient had a history of cutaneous melanoma that was surgically removed 35 years prior. There had been no evidence of recurrence since that time and no cutaneous involvement was found during this pre-sentation. While melanoma is a disease that is known to involve non-cutaneous sites (either as primary or metastatic disease) and may recur many years after initial diagnosis， our patient's time interval and site of recurrence are both rare findings.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】A 55 year old Caucasian male presented to the emer-gency room with a complaint of generalized lower abdominal pain. The pain was moderate， crampy，and had been steadily increasing over the last two months. There was no melena or hematochezia， though he did describe slightly decreased frequency and caliber of stools. He denied nausea， vomiting， dysuria， fevers， chills or nightsweats.Review of systems was remark-able for an unintentional 20 pound weight loss over the preceding two months. The patient had not seen a physician for many years and was on no medica-tions. His only significant past medical history was cutaneous melanoma removed from his abdomen 35years prior. He was divorced and reported no recent sexual activity.

【10】On exam， the patient was afebrile with a blood pres-sure of 130/70 mm/hg and a pulse of 88 beats per minute. He was a well-developed man who appeared in mild distress secondary to abdominal pain. The remainder of his exam was unremarkable except for moderate tenderness to palpation throughout the lower abdomen and pelvis. Laboratory analysis revealed the following： WBC 18，800 cells per cubic millimeter， Hgb 12.9 g/dL (MCV 80)， and platelets495，000 cells per cubic millimeter. Chemistries and urinalysis were unremarkable A computed tomography scan of the abdomen/pel-vis revealed a 10cm x 10cm enhancing mass in the mid-pelvic region with an area of central necrosis. The mass appeared to encase multiple loops of small bowel as well as both ureters. The bladder was displaced anteriorly and compressed. The origin of the mass was unclear. The lower lung zones displayed two pulmonary nodules approxi-mately 1 cm in diameter suspicious for metastatic disease. A trans-rectal biopsy was performed and the pathology was consistent with malignant mela-noria.

【11】DISCUSSION

【12】Cutaneous melanoma is a common disease that has displayed an increasing incidence over the last century. It is currently the 5th most common cancer among men and 7th among women. In the United States in 2004， there were an estimated 55，000 people diagnosed with melanoma， and 7，900 deaths were at-tributed to the disease . Risk factors for melanoma include light complexion， the presence of multiple pigmented lesions， and intermittent sun exposure and severe sunburns (especially in childhood) . A prior history of cutaneous melanoma increases the risk of future primary melanoma tenfold .

【13】It has been estimated that anywhere from 1.0-6.7%melanomas recur after ≥ 10 years， a phenomenon known as late recurrence . Tsao，et al.，identified a group of 20 patients who had recurrence of mela-noma ≥ 15 years after initial diagnosis and labeled this ultra-late recurrence . In this group， almost all of the recurrences were in the form of either distant or regional metastasis (55% and 40%， respectively). The 35 year disease-free interval (DFI) seen in our patient was the longest we could find in a review of such reports . Of interest， it appeared that in patients with the longest DFI’s there was a high incidence of ocular primary lesions.

【14】Melanoma may involve other organs in addition to the skin. The American Joint Commission on Cancer(AJCC) has published the following classification for melanoma depending on the site of metastatic dis-ease： Mla (non-visceral； ie.， skin， lymph nodes)， Mib(pulmonary)， or Mlc (all other sites or an elevated

【15】LDH) . In terms of visceral organ involvement， the lungs are the most common site for metastatic disease， followed by the central nervous system . Gastrointestinal (GI) metastasis are uncommon in melanoma patients (2-4%)， though melanoma itself is one of the more common primary tumors that will spread to the GI tract .

【16】The overall prognosis for metastatic melanoma is poor， with a 5-year survival rate of less than 5%and a median survival of 6-10 months . Standard chemotherapy regimens have been of little use in treating this disease. While interleukin-2 based im-munotherapy appears to show benefit in a minor percentage of patients， to date there are no random-ized， prospective trials that have documented any significant overall survival advantage from any spe-cific drug regimen . There have been reports of survival benefits in selected patients with metastatic disease who undergo surgical resection， though these data come mainly from case reports and small series Our patient did elect to undergo chemotherapy.

【17】Unfortunately， his condition continued to decline with progression of disease and the development of brain metastasis. At last follow-up he was under the care of Hospice.

【18】CONCLUSIONS

【19】Malignant melanoma may recur many years after initial presentation. Physicians should therefore be cautious about using the traditional 5-year disease free interval as evidence of“cure”. Unfortunately， the overall low incidence of late recurrence. combined with the high likelihood that it will be in the form of metastatic disease， makes it difficult to offer guide-lines for effective surveillance. The primary non-cu-taneous sites of involvement are lymph nodes， lung and brain. Involvement in other organs may occur， though it is rare. The presence of metastatic disease indicates a dismal prognosis. Selected patients may obtain a survival benefit from surgical intervention， otherwise they should be referred to ongoing clinical trials or palliative care.

【0】Background：

【1】There are very few reports in the literature worldwide on how to deliver continuous renal replacement thera-py (CRRT) to patients with multi-organ trauma and severe hemophilia A. The aim of this case report is to de-scribe successful multidisciplinary intensive treatment of a patient with multi-organ trauma suffering from se-vere hemophilia A with the use of continuous veno-venous hemodialysis with regional citrate anticoagulation(Ci-Ca CVVHD).

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report a case of a 47-year-old man with severe hemophilia A， who had multi-organ trauma as a result of a serious traffic accident and was admitted to the Trauma Centre of Emergency and Disaster Medicine in Krakow， Poland in critical condition. Due to elevated laboratory markers of kidney damage (creatinine 204 mmol/l， glo-merular filtration rate (GFR) 32 ml/min/1.73 m²)， very high myoglobin level (>1000 p/l) associated with rhab-domyolysis， oliguria (diuresis <0.5 ml/kg/h)， and overhydration as a consequence of massive transfusion of blood products and fluids， on day 2 after the injury Ci-Ca CVHD was initiated as a part of intensive， multi-disciplinary treatment. This approach proved to be successful in our patient as he was discharged from the Intensive Care Unit on day 45 after the injury in good general condition， with stable circulatory and respirato-ry system， without any apparent neurological deficits， and with good renal function (creatinine 50 mmol/l， GFR>60 ml/min/1.73m².

【4】Conclusions： Our case report shows that intensive， multidisciplinary treatment with implementation of Ci-Ca CWHD may be an effective and safe method of care for patients with multi-organ trauma and hemophilia A.

【5】Keywords： Barotrauma · Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy· Critical Care

【6】Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a very useful method of dialysis， because of its unique characteristics com-pared with intermittent hemodialysis， which include excellent ability to precisely control fluid status and steady acid-base and electrolyte correction. CRRT provides slow and relative ly gentle treatment， and it is indicated especially in hemody-namically unstable patients .

【7】In the available medical literature， there are only a few reports referring to implementation of CRRT in patients with multi-or-gan trauma and hemophilia A . CRRT in patients with hemo-philia A is challenging for many reasons. The major problems include high risk of complications， both during establishing vascular access and during the therapy. Placement of central vascular catheters in patients with hemophilia is associated with high risk of bleeding. It is also challenging to prevent cir-cle clotting during CRRT on the one hand， and avoid bleeding of the patient on the other hand. Another critically important issue is how to properly supplement factor VIII in such pa-tients taking into consideration possible losses into dialysate.

【8】This case report presents successful multidisciplinary， inten-sive treatment of a patient with multi-organ trauma suffering from severe hemophilia A with implementation of continuous veno-venous hemodialysis with regional citrate anticoagula-tion (Ci-Ca CVVHD).

【9】A 47-year-old man with severe hemophilia A had multi-organ trauma as a result of a serious traffic accident. The patient was brought to the Trauma Centre of Emergency and Disaster Medicine in Krakow with symptoms of a hemorrhagic shock(hemoglobin level in the first measurement was 2.6 g/dL) and exacerbating symptoms of bilateral pneumothorax. After ad-mission to the Emergency Department (ED)， vital functions of the patient were secured (endotracheal intubation， mechani-cal ventilation， infusion of fluids and catecholamines)，bilater-al pneumothorax drainage was inserted， and emergency trans-fusions of packed red blood cells (PRBC) type 0 negative， fresh frozen plasma (FFP) type AB， fibrinogen and factor VIII were performed. Immediately after that， the patient received a CT scan， which showed severe chest trauma with multiple， bilat-eral rib fractures， contusion of both lungs， bilateral pneumo-and hemothorax and pneumomediastinum， fractures of the pel-vis， an open fracture of the right thigh， and closed fractures of the right arm， right lower leg and metatarsal bones .

【10】Due to the need to surgically stabilize the open fracture of the right thigh and to control the bleeding， the patient was im-mediately transported to the operating theater. Once the frac-ture was externally fixated， the patient was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU)， where further treatment aimed at stabilization of vital functions and correction of the hemostat-ic disturbances was continued. Initially， the patient required ventilation with high oxygen concentrations (fi020.7-0.8)，in-fusion of high doses of norepinephrine， and transfusion of fur-ther units of factor VIII， PRBC， FFP， platelet concentrates (PC)， and fibrinogen.

【11】Findings of the CT performed on admission to the ICU included：a massive contusion of both lungs， normal echocardiographic image of the left heart with the ejection fraction (EF) of 55%， while the image of the right heart showed dilatation and over-load with mildly elevated pulmonary artery pressure， moder-ate tricuspid insufficiency， and a 30-mm-wide inferior vena cava. Due to elevated laboratory markers of kidney damage(creatinine 204 mmol/l， glomerular filtration rate (GFR) 32 ml/min/1.73 m²)， very high myoglobin level (>1000 p/l) associat-ed with rhabdomyolysis， oliguria (diuresis <0.5 ml/kg/h)，over-hydration as a consequence of massive transfusion of blood products and fluids， further need for transfusion of PRBC， FFP， PC， fibrinogen， and factor VIII to ensure hemostasis， and need for enteral and parenteral nutrition in the subsequent days，on day 2 after the injury， renal replacement therapy was initiat-ed in the form of continuous veno-venous hemodialysis with regional citrate anticoagulation (Ci-Ca CVVHD). The initial set-tings of CVVHD parameters were： blood flow 120 ml/h， dialy sate flow 2000 ml/h， and ultrafiltration 150 ml/h.

【12】On day 3， the patient's exacerbating symptoms of hemody-namic instability prompted us to increase the norepinephrine dosage. Echocardiography findings included acute tricuspid valve dysfunction with fourth-degree regurgitation and a de-tached fragment of the papillary muscle， further increase in the size of the right ventricle and the right atrium， presence of regurgitation in the pulmonary trunk， and progressive en-largement of the inferior vena cava. The patient was consult-ed by cardiac surgeons， who decided that a surgical interven-tion using cardiopulmonary by-pass was unadvisable at the moment due to the serious condition of the patient .

【13】On subsequent days the treatment was continued. Due to the need for prolonged ventilation， after the preparation of the pa-tient and obtaining optimal coagulation parameters， percuta-neous tracheotomy using the Griggs method was performed. Additionally， starting on day 9， a progressive increase in bili-rubin and liver enzyme levels was observed. Subsequent im-aging studies (ultrasound and CT) of the abdomen showed an enlarged liver， most probably due to pathological chang-es secondary to heart failure. Over the next several days， the patient's condition stabilized， which made it possible to re-duce the oxygen concentrations and the dose of norepineph-rine. Drains were also removed from the pleural cavities. Additionally， the previously elevated liver parameters and in-flammatory markers gradually declined. Due to the normal-ization of kidney parameters (creatinine 50 mmol/l)， satisfac-tory diuresis， and stabilization of echocardiographic findings， CWVHD was discontinued after 14 days. The improvement in the patient's general condition made it possible to surgically stabilize the fractures. The patient was consulted again by a team of cardiac surgeons and qualified for tricuspid valve re-construction surgery， optimally after stabilization of respira-tory and hematological status.

【14】In subsequent days， the dosage of sedatives was gradually re-duced， and on day 33 after the injury， the patient was weaned from the mechanical ventilation. He was conscious， improving neurologically， and after the tracheostomy tube was replaced with the phonation one， also able to speak. At that time， he underwent intense rehabilitation. As the patient was able to tolerate a more varied diet orally， parenteral nutrition was dis-continued. In laboratory tests， a normalization of liver and kid-ney parameters as well as a steady decrease in inflammatory markers were observed. On day 45 of hospitalization， the pa-tient was discharged from the ICU. He was in a good general condition， conscious， without neurological deficits， with stable cardiopulmonary and respiratory functions， and with normal kidney parameters and diuresis. He was scheduled for tricus-pid valve reconstruction surgery in 3 months'time.

【15】Discussion

【16】Hemophilia A is an inherited， genetic， chromosome X-linked disease which causes factor VIII deficit. Clinically， the disease presents as a bleeding diathesis， and the severity of the symp-toms depends on the percentage of factor VIII deficiency. Severe hemophilia A is recognized when the factor VIII serum concen-tration is below 1% of normal value. The state-of-the-art treat-ment for hemophilia A is a replacement therapy with recom-binant factor VIII， with a replacement dose depending on the severity of the disease and the current clinical situation .

【17】Analyzing the course of events， it should be emphasized that in our patient the crucial element of the successful treatment was an early identification of hemophilia A by the Medical Rescue Team at the site of the accident and immediate ad-ministration of factor VIII by the Team (the patient had 2000units (U) of factor VIII in his car). Moreover， a local blood bank was promptly informed by the Medical Rescue Team， which al-lowed prior securing of the intended dose of factor VIII and its quick administration right after hospital admission.

【18】Due to the severity and extent of trauma， our patient required interdisciplinary treatment with involvement of many special-ists in different fields. Right after admission to the ED， advance life support was started， including tracheal intubation， mechan-ical ventilation， pleural drainage， catecholamine infusion and transfusion of PRBC， FFP， PC， fibrinogen， factor VIII， and crys-talloids， which were continued later in the ICU. In the subse-quent days the patient underwent many invasive procedures， including percutaneous tracheostomy. On the first hospital day， he had external stabilization of femoral fracture， which was followed， after stabilization of his condition， by final or-thopedic surgeries. All these procedures， due to coexistent he-mophilia A and coagulopathy secondary to massive bleeding， involved a high risk of bleeding and required careful prepara-tion and transfusion of factor VIIl. According to available re-ports in the medical literature  and our hematologist's rec-ommendations， we were aiming at factor VIll levels of around80-100%. The factor VIII requirement was calculated based on the information that administration of 1 U of factor VIII per kilogram of body weight results in a factor VIIl increase of ap-proximately 2%. Because the half-life of factor Vill is 12 h， we administered it twice a day and monitored its levels daily .

【19】In our opinion， an important role in the success of the therapy was played by early initiation of renal replacement therapy in the form of Ci-Ca CVVHD. The decision to start Ci-Ca CVVHD was made because of acute renal failure secondary to shock and rhabdomyolysis and the significant volume burden placed on the patient’s cardiovascular system， including both blood products and infusion fluids (crystalloids， colloids) resulting from the need to replace the blood loss and to ensure optimal tissue perfusion. Continuing Ci-Ca CWHD also helped during the most difficult period of treatment of lung contusion and right ventricular failure， until lung and heart function improved with a concomitant decline in pulmonary vascular resistance. It should be emphasized that the decision to use Ci-Ca CVVHD in the case of our patient was a difficult one， because of the lack of our own experience in this group of patients and the scarcity of reports in the medical literature worldwide on how to deliver continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) to pa-tients with severe hemophilia A . The decision was made af-ter an in-depth analysis of benefits and risks associated with potential complications. CRRT in patients with hemophilia A is challenging for many reasons. The major problems include high risk of complications， both during establishing vascular access and during the therapy. Placement of central vascular catheters in patients with hemophilia is associated with high risk of bleeding. It is also challenging to prevent circle clotting during CRRT on the one hand， and avoid bleeding of the pa-tient on the other hand. Another critically important issue is how to properly supplement factor VIII in such patients， tak-ing into consideration possible losses into dialysate. We decid-ed to use regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA)， because RCA compared with heparin anticoagulation is associated with sig-nificantly lower risk of bleeding， less blood transfusions， and extended life of the extracorporeal circuit . It was espe-cially important in our patient， because the risk of bleeding was very high due to his severe hemophilia A.

【20】It is critically important in patients with hemophilia A to prop-erly supplement the deficient factor VIII. As recommended by the patient's hematologist， factor Viil levels were monitored daily and the replacement doses were titrated to achieve 80-100% of serum activity in the acute phase of the disease. We had not found information in the literature on whether and to what extent factor VIll is removed during CRRT. Also， the man-ufacturer of the filter we used was unable to provide us with such information. Therefore， we measured serum concentra-tion of factor VIII daily and guided the supplementation by these results. We considered it to be the only reasonable and effective way to supply the patient with the adequate dose. We observed that in order to maintain the desired serum level of factor VIII during Ci-Ca CVVHD， it was necessary to increase its dosage by an average of 15 U/kg during circuit replacement.

【21】Our approach proved to be successful in our patient， as he was discharged from the ICU on day 45 after the injury in good gen-eral condition， with stable circulatory and respiratory system， without any apparent neurological deficits， and with good re-nal function (creatinine 50 mmol/l， GFR >60 ml/min/1.73 m²).

【22】This treatment outcome was a source of great satisfaction for the whole team involved in caring for the patient， since the se-verity of the original injury， the patient's condition on admis-sion， including extremely low hemoglobin level (Hb 2.6 g/dL) combined with a severe lung injury， raised serious concerns about consequences of organ hypoxia. Fortunately， multidis-ciplinary intensive treatment protected the patient from such an untoward course of the disease. Three months later， the patient had a minimally invasive tricuspid valve reconstruc-tion via a right minithoracotomy with extracorporeal circula-tion. The procedure was uncomplicated. Currently， the patient is in a good condition and is returning to his activities from before the accident.

【23】This report describes a successful treatment with Ci-Ca CVVHD as a part of multidisciplinary， intensive treatment of patient with polytrauma and severe hemophilia A. Our case report shows that such an approach may be an effective and safe method of treatment in this group of patients. However， fur-ther studies are needed to confirm our findings and to opti-mize this method of treatment in patients with hemophilia.

【0】ABSTRACT Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affecting one in every 59 newborns with a significant surge in the preva-lence rates over the last few decades has a complex underlying pathophysiological mechanism which is not fully understood. We hypothesize that such association might be associated with paracetamol-induced alterations in cytokine levels， oxidative stress and dysregulation of neurotransmission， especially dopaminergic pathways. Additionally， disrup-tion of prostaglandin synthesis following paracetamol administration has a considerable impact over neurodevelopment. We performed a literature review by searching our topic of interest on three databases， including PubMed， Embase and the Cochrane library by utilizing keywords. Recent large scale nationwide birth cohort studies implicate link between paracetamol use during pregnancy， most commonly utilized antipyretic and analgesic medication at that period， and risk of autism in infants. Alterations at cytokine and prostaglandin levels， elevated oxidative stress and impairment of neurotransmission may have a role in ASD pathogenesis， though， it has not been demonstrated in human studies. There is clear need for future comprehensive molecular and clinical studies to investigate the association between paracetamol use in pregnancy and ASD risk. This study is significant by investigating the role of paracetamol use in upward projection in ASD prevalence and providing a hypothetical underlying mechanism for the association between paracetamol use and ASD risk.

【1】KEYWORDS Autism spectrum disorder， paracetamol， prostaglandin， cytokine， oxidative stress， a neurotransmitter

【2】Introduction

【3】Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by defects at social interactions and restricted behaviours or interests while effec-tive treatment options are yet to be identified Lord， Brugha . Although ASD affects one in every 59 newborns according to the latest epidemiological studies， the dramatic surge in prevalence has been recorded in the 1990s and 2000s. In comparison， the es-timated prevalence of one in 2.000 newborns in 1960s and one in1.000 newborns in 1980s have been implicated . Multiple risk factors including maternal age， few genetic syndromes， assisted reproductive technologies， folic acid deficiency， exposure to cer-tain toxins and medications such as valproic acid have been identified. Nevertheless， none is presumed to correspond to such surge in prevalence . Therefore， environmental factors appear as primary candidates that may explain the surge in ASD prevalence over time and attain considerable attention. Never-theless， comprehension of the exact pathophysiology of ASD is crucial for the identification of all risk factors， development of effective treatment options， as well as possible preventive measures.

【4】Maternal infections are the third most common cause of ma-ternal mortality worldwide. Thus， antibiotics and antipyretic drugs are crucial during pregnancy to overcome adverse con- sequences of infections such as abortus， teratogenicity， preterm labour， sepsis， intrauterine growth retardation and maternal mortality . However， most medications are contraindicated during pregnancy， mainly due to teratogenic concerns. Recent studies indicated a possible association between the use of parac-etamol， the most commonly used antipyretic medication in preg nancy and early infancy period， and ASD risk in infants . In this study， we aim to investigate the risk associated with paracetamol use during pregnancy and risk of ASD in infant and provide a hypothetical pathophysiological mechanism involving inflammatory processes， cytokines and oxidative stress.

【5】ASD and Immune System

【6】Immune system dysregulation as a possible pathophysiological mechanism in ASD was first proposed in 1977 by a study con-ducted with 25 participants (12 ASD patients and 13 controls) demonstrating lower lymphocyte response to a stimulation test， phytohemagglutinin stimulation， in patients with ASD . Dur-ing the outbreak of Rubella  in the USA approximately20-30.000 children with various congenital disabilities were born among which ASD had been reported at a rate of 905 cases per 10.000 children， considerable higher that prevalence rate of the general population at that time . Besides， later studies demonstrate that congenital infection of cytomegalovirus， in-fluenza， measles and mumps are potential risk factors for ASD. Even though strong evidence was present regarding the asso-ciation between ASD and maternal teratogenic infections such as Rubella or cytomegalovirus， a large-scale nationwide study conducted with all children born between 1980 and 2005 in Den-mark has shown an increase in ASD incidence only in case of hospitalized first-trimester non-congenital viral infections and second-trimester bacterial infections . However， another nationwide study including all children born between 1984 and2007 in Sweden (n=2.371.493) claims that timing of maternal infections has no influence over ASD risk while infections at any time during pregnancy increase ASD risk in similar fashion. Timing of infection， infectious agent， maternal vaccination status and severity of the infection are possible determinants of future ASD risk in infants. Additionally， Childhood Autism Risks from Genetics and Environment (CHARGE) study con-ducted with 1122 participants has demonstrated that use of antipyretic medications including paracetamol during episodes of viral and bacterial infections attenuates the risk of ASD in infants . Nevertheless， underlying mechanisms of mater-nal infection-induced fetal consequences are poorly understood while cytokines， small immunomodulatory molecules， may have significant influence over the process.

【7】Elevated levels of interleukin (IL)-1B，IL-1 receptor antagonist， IL-4， IL-5， IL-6，IL-8，IL-12，IL-13， IL-17 and tumor necrosis factor(TNF)-a have been recorded at peripheral blood samples and cerebrospinal fluid samples of ASD patients compared to non-ASD individuals . Elevated levels of IL-1B， IL-8 and IL-17cause activation of the innate immune system while elevated levels of IL-3 and IL-5 lead to the activation of the humoral immune system. In addition to its' role in immune regulation， IL-6 is believed to be the cytokine which acts as a signal for the brain about the state of sickness . As a consequence of peripheral immune system activation， central production of two cytokines， namely macrophage chemoattractant protein (MCP)-1， and TGF-B1， from astrocytes and microglia cells，increase . Levels of peripheral cytokines and associated phenotypes in patients with ASD have been reviewed by Masi et al. in 2017

【8】Single-injection of IL-6 to mice embryo at gestational day12.5 causes autism-like phenotype， specifically latent inhibition and prepulse inhibition， while those outcomes are not observed if co-administered with anti-IL-6 antibody . Additionally， the injection of other pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1a， TNF-&， or IFN-y) do not lead to similar phenotype， demonstrating the central role of IL-6 . Transplacental transmission of IL-6has been well-established while penetration into cerebrum is less regulated in fetus and infants due to an immature blood-brain barrier. Role of IL-6 in ASD pathogenesis has not been definite in human studies. In contrast， elevated levels of IL-4/5， interferon-gamma， TNF-&，TNF-B and MCP-1 at amniotic fluid have been reported in ASD patients However， it is essential not to overlook the lack of an adequate amount of comprehensive studies.

【9】Paracetamol and ASD

【10】Paracetamol， also known as acetaminophen， is one of the most commonly prescribed medication worldwide as an analgesic and antipyretic drug and considered as category B drug during preg-nancy by Food and Drug Administration (FDA) indicating that no studies on humans have shown detrimental effects on either fetus or mother . Paracetamol is by far the most commonly used antipyretic medication in pregnant females and children under age 5 . However， caution is indicated， especially at third trimester for potential fatal risk of ductus arteriosus clo-sure in the fetus . As it implies， it has been widely used in the early infancy period in case of patent ductus arteriosus similar to other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs， mainly ibuprofen . The primary mechanism of action includes dis-ruption of prostaglandin synthesis， and it is readily penetrable to cerebrospinal fluid . Despite its’role as anti-inflammatory and antipyretic medication， use of paracetamol early in life leads to an increase in the incidence of inflammatory diseases such as asthma and eczema. Association between acetaminophen use and ASD was first implied by Schultz et al. in 2008 . After a significant shift from aspirin to paracetamol in pregnancy and early infancy period following the warning of Centers of Disease Control (CDC) in 1980 regarding the association between aspirin and Reye syndrome， a considerable rise in ASD incidence has been reported . Recently， a large scale meta-analysis，includ-ing 132.738 mother-child pairs revealed that use of paracetamol during pregnancy is associated with increased risk for ASD in infants . Similar nationwide birth control study results have been reported. However， contradictory findings are also present. Furthermore， paracetamol use at the prenatal period has been identified as a risk factor for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)， hyperkinetic disorders and impairment of psychomotor development in various birth cohort studies. The underlying pathophysiology of paracetamol-associated ASD or other neuropsychiatric conditions is not clear . We hy-pothesize that use of paracetamol at prenatal or early infancy period increases the risk of ASD in infants by impairing inflam-matory processes including inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis and impairment of cytokine release which are crucial in early neurodevelopmental processes. Additional proposed mecha-nisms of paracetamol-associated risk for ASD include elevated oxidative stress and impaired balance between lymphocyte sub-types that may lead to neurodegeneration.

【11】Paracetamol-Induced Oxidative Stress and Variations at Cytokines

【12】Paracetamol-overdose is linked to increased oxidative stress and elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as hydrogen peroxide， hydroxyl radical and superoxide via several mechanisms. Paracetamol is metabolized via either phase II re-action via the addition of glucuronide/sulphate group or phase I reaction via cytochrome p450 enzymes， mainly CYP2E1. Use of paracetamol increases ROS production via CYP2E1 and further causes oxidative stress via upregulation of CYP2E1 expression levels . Additionally， paracetamol-toxicity leads to mito-chondrial ROS formation via inhibition and downregulation of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and electron transport chain (ETC). Such a phenomenon is further shown by the improvement in oxidative stress when paracetamol is co-administered with N-acetylcysteine or glutathione， ETC inhibitors . Upregulation of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxi-dase at cells of the reticuloendothelial system is also indicated in paracetamol-related oxidative stress J. Role of oxidative stress in ASD pathophysiology is evident as shown by the higher incidence of ASD in patients with certain genetic mutations (i.e. defects at methionine or glutathione metabolism)， in cases with toxin exposure (organophosphates， organochlorines， mercury， lead， cadmium， manganese， vinyl chloride and arsenic) and dis-ruption at vitamin B metabolism or impaired vitamin B uptake N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone-imine (NAPQI)， formed by oxida-tive metabolism of paracetamol at hepatocytes via cytochrome p450 system， is the toxic metabolite of paracetamol that is re-sponsible for acute toxicity and liver failure. When glutathione stores are adequate NAPQI is metabolized into N-acetyl-p-aminophenol-mercaptopurine， though， consumption of parac-etamol either leads to depletion of glutathione stores at high doses in which NAPQI cannot be metabolized and exerts its'hepatotoxic effects or causes decline at glutathione stores which may result in oxidative stress through a defect at the metabolism of ROS produced in mitochondria . Intracellular oxida-tive stress causes activation of receptor-interacting protein (RIP)-3/RIP-1 involved in necroptosis and release of cytochrome c and Smac， which are involved in the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis. Release of DNA fragments and high mobility group box1 protein (HMGB1) from apoptotic hepatocytes causes activation of Kupffer cells and neutrophils leading to release of monocyte chemoattractant protein (MCP)-1 which is responsible from acti-vation of monocytes and their transition into macrophages . Elevation of certain cytokines including IL-1， IL-6， IL-8， and TNF-alpha which cause activation of nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-kB) signalling pathway at neighbouring hepatocytes and other cells throughout the body. Therefore， the assumption of paracetamol-induced ox-idative stress in the pathophysiology of ASD is plausible and worth investigating Additionally， use of paracetamol has been linked to varia-tions at cytokine levels， explicitly decline in IL-6 and IL-10， in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) conducted with 20 subjects during 15-months of the trial . The decline in IL-6 levels after paracetamol administration is well-established after multiple studies while elevated levels of IL-8/18/33 and TNF-alpha have also been reported along with a decline in IL-10 . Fur-thermore， protective roles of IL-15， IL-17 and IL-22BP against paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity are shown via knock-out animal models J.

【13】Paracetamol-Induced Alterations in Neurotransmission

【14】Mesocorticolimbic (MCL) circuit formed by neurons from the ventral tegmental area， prefrontal cortex and nucleus accumbens from ventral striatum is involved in the control of reward and motivation-associated behaviors in humans. In contrast， defect at MCL circuit is claimed to be associated with social deficits and communication difficulties . On the other hand， nigros-triatal (NS) circuit composed of neurons from substantia nigra and dorsal striatum is involved in motor control of goal-directed behaviour. In contrast， impairment at NS circuit is implicated in the restrictive behaviour pattern . Dopaminergic path-ways predominantly control both circuits. Thus， impairment of dopaminergic transmission might be a key component of ASD pathogenesis . Prenatal and early postnatal administration of 5-15 mg/day paracetamol alters dopaminergic， noradrenergic and glutamatergic neurotransmission in the hypothalamus of rats.

【15】In contrast， in another study involving 30 mice， a significant increase in dopamine levels in the brain following paraceta-mol administration was considered as another mechanism of its' analgesic effect . Two mechanisms are proposed for paracetamol-induced upregulation of dopaminergic pathways. First， paracetamol leads to a decline in nitric oxide (NO) synthase expression； thus， levels of NO， which is a natural inhibitor of dopamine release declines. Second， conjugation of paracetamol in the brain with arachidonic acid forms N-arachidonoyl phe-nolamine (AM404)， which leads to upregulation of anandamide levels which is a positive regulator of dopaminergic pathways. Elevated levels of dopamine following paracetamol ad-ministration have been demonstrated in a few other studies， while the use of dopamine antagonists has a beneficial effect over paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity . Thus， even the most well-established fatal adverse outcome of paracetamol intoxication has multiple determinants.

【16】Additionally， by inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2 enzyme paracetamol leads to lower levels of prostaglandin H2，D2 and E2， which have importance in early neurodevelopment . Prostaglandin E2 whose production is diminished after parac-etamol administration affects the excitability of hypothalamic neurons in addition to its' role in brainstem development and sexual differentiation of brain while prostaglandin D2 is im-plicated to have a role in dendritic and axonal growth . Similarly， impaired levels of certain cytokines are implicated in few neurodevelopmental processes. Use of prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors such as paracetamol early at postnatal life impairs cerebellar Purkinje cell development and atrophy in male rats. At the same time， similar effects are not observed in female rats with unknown sex-specific expression. No dif-ference in terms of motor development is observed in contrast to impairment at social interactions and sensory processes . Arguably， such a gender-specific effect of paracetamol may corre-spond to 4 times higher ASD incidence in males. We hypothesize that paracetamol-induced alterations in neurotransmission， es-pecially at dopaminergic pathways， at prenatal and early infancy period may be associated with future ASD risk， which is also worth investigating.

【17】Conclusion

【18】Large-scale birth cohorts strongly suggest that use of paraceta-mol at prenatal and early infancy period， the most commonly used antipyretic and analgesic at that time period， is a risk factor for ASD in infants while the underlying mechanism is unknown. We suggest that such association might be related to paracetamol-induced alterations in cytokine levels， oxidative stress and dys-regulation of neurotransmission， especially at dopaminergic pathways. Molecular studies are needed in order to confirm our hypothesis， though， it is crucial to disclose such associa-tion due to increased use of paracetamol and upwards trend in ASD incidence. However， there is no currently available better alternative to paracetamol in pregnant females. Thus， we rec-ommend wisely use of paracetamol until conduction of further comprehensive studies since maternal infections and fever are also linked to increased risk for maternal mortality， morbidity and infant ASD.

【0】Background：

【1】In early 2020， severe acute respiratory syndrome-corona virus 2 caused an outbreak of a viral pneumonia that rapidly progressed to a global pandemic. Most cases presented with mild respiratory symptoms and required only supportive care with instructions to self-quarantine at home. Others had more severe symptoms that be-came complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and required hospitalization.

【2】Case Report： In this report， we present the case of a young patient in New York City who presented to our hospital with coronavirus disease 2019-induced diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) that progressed to ARDS and subsequent death. The patient was managed for DKA on presentation with insulin protocol and acidosis management. However， it became evident that he had underlying respiratory complications， which later presented as ARDS requiring mechanical ventilation and antibiotics.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】We recommend that clinicians be aware of this potentially fatal complication in all patients with pre-exist-ing diabetes. Simultaneously， a low threshold for intubation should be advocated for patients with concurrent COVID-19 and type l diabetes mellitus since the potential for poor clinical outcomes from respiratory demise may be lessened by early respiratory intervention.

【5】MeSH Keywords： COVID-19· Diabetes Mellitus， Type 1 · Diabetic Ketoacidosis · Respiratory Distress Syndrome， Adult·SARS Virus Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)， caused by a coronavirus strain severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2)， rapidly caused a pandemic in early 2020. After being discovered in Wuhan， China， SARS-CoV-2 was found to pres-ent with a variety of symptoms，including fever， chills， and dys-pnea. As the number of cases rose， critically ill patients were developing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requir-ing mechanical ventilation at an alarming rate.

【6】Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening complication of diabetes mellitus and occurs because of the absence of in-sulin preventing glucose uptake in certain tissues， resulting in a hyperglycemic state. The demand for energy by tissue drives fatty acid metabolism， producing ketones and ultimately an anion gap metabolic acidosis. Additionally， DKA can predispose patients to infections because of a weakened immune system. Inflammatory cytokines， increased cortisol， and metabolic dys-function create a devastating picture for DKA patients who de-velop infections as their immune systems are not adequate-ly equipped to fight off such infections. Furthermore，diabetic patients experiencing infections， trauma， or other stressors have an increased susceptibility to DKA.

【7】In this case report， we present a patient with DKA precipitat-ed by SARS-CoV-2-induced COVID-19 further complicated by ARDS. This combination was fatal in our patient. We empha-size the importance of having a high clinical suspicion in such cases and intervening early to prevent rapid deterioration.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 24-year-old obese man with a known medical history of di-abetes mellitus type 1 and hyperlipidemia presented to the Emergency Department (ED) for nausea， nonbilious vomiting， and 1 episode of hematemesis. He had subjective fevers， fatigue， dry cough， and chills； however， he denied dyspnea， chest pain， diarrhea， constipation， recent ill contacts， or any recent travel. The patient was noncompliant with his medications. Vital signs on presentation were temperature 36.4℃， pulse rate 122 beats/min， blood pressure 141/84 mmHg，respiratory rate 16 breaths/min， and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air as measured by a pulse oximeter. On re-examination， the patient was hypothermic， with a temperature of 32.9℃ measured rectally. A subsequent Foley probe temperature was obtained and found to be 36.8℃

【10】On physical examination， the patient was in mild distress， le-thargic，and had delayed responses to questioning； however， he was alert and oriented to person， place， and time. His mu-cous membranes were dry. The remainder of his physical ex-amination was unremarkable.

【11】His blood glucose on arrival was 507 mg/dL， his last mea-sured hemoglobin A1c was 15.8% according to his chart， and his electrolyte panel showed a bicarbonate level of 2 mEg/L. Laboratory studies were significant for ketonuria (160 mg/dL) and elevated creatinine (1.4 mg/dL). His calculated anion gap was 30.6 mEq/L Testing for bacteremia with blood cultures， urinary tract infection with urine culture， and nasopharyngeal swab with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for SARS-CoV-2 was done in the ED using the New York State Wadsworth Center test. Initial chest X-ray  re-vealed no cardiopulmonary disease.Electrocardiogram results showed sinus tachycardia with normal axis intervals and neg-ative acute ST changes. Relevant daily laboratory results are shown in Tables 1-3.

【12】During the ED course he was assessed for DKA with metabol-ic encephalopathy and sepsis. On admission to the Medical Intensive Care Unit， he received 3 liters of fluids in addition to vancomycin， cefepime， 150 mEq of sodium bicarbonate in-fusion， potassium repletion with 100 mL， and insulin intra-venously on 6 units/h (insulin infusion protocol). On hospi-tal day 1， he remained lethargic and fell asleep multiple times while being examined. Given his clinical picture， he was di-agnosed with DKA with an anion gap metabolic acidosis sec-ondary to medication noncompliance paired with an upper-respiratory infection， and acute kidney injury secondary to DKA. His oxygen saturation at the time was 99% oxygen on room air. Laboratory results were notable for increased leu-kocyte count to 12.4 from 10.8 the previous day. Cardiac tro-ponins were negative. On hospital day 2， he began showing signs of respiratory distress and became febrile (temp 38.3℃) and tachypneic. SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngeal swab res ult was positive. Given his deteriorating respiratory status， the deci-sion was made to intubate and mechanically ventilate with a respiratory rate of 14 breaths/min， tidal volume of 500 mL， fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO，) of 80%， and positive end-ex-piratory pressure (PEEP) of 15 cm of H，O. Postintubation arteri-al blood gas testing showed respiratory improvement. A chest X-ray  at this time revealed mild perihilar patchy ar-eas of opacity on the right with increased vascular markings on the left， indicating probable COVID-19 pneumonia. On hos-pital day 3， he remained febrile with an increased temperature of 40℃， and azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine were add-ed to his regimen for COVID-19. On day 4， his blood glucose levels stabilized； however， he remained febrile and became tachycardic at a rate of 118 beats/min. An attempt to titrate FiO， to 60% was unsuccessful as his oxygen saturation again dropped to 86%， prompting an increase back to 80%. Arterial blood gas testing showed improvements with a blood pH of7.40. On day 7， he continued to desaturate， with levels as low as 75% oxygen saturation and remained febrile. His leukocyte count increased further， raising concern for a superimposed fungal or bacterial infection. A sputum sample was collected and sent to the laboratory for culture. At this time，vancomy-cin and cefepime were discontinued and replaced with me-ropenem for a broader antibiotic coverage along with vori-conazole for fungal coverage. During day 8， sputum results returned with yeast isolates， although no specific pathogen was isolated at the time. A chest X-ray  showed in-terval worsening of his infiltrates bilaterally. On day 9， he re-mained intermittently febrile. Attempts to titrate Fio， on the ventilator were unsuccessful again， and he had multiple de-saturations. Arterial blood gasses revealed worsening hyper-capnia with pCO， level of 61 mmHg. A chest X-ray  at the time revealed diffuse fluffy infiltrates throughout both lungs， consistent with ARDS. Later that day he desaturated to50% despite maximum PEEP and FiO. A computed tomogra-phy scan of the chest was not performed because of the pa-tient's body habitus. The patient subsequently became se-verely hypotensive， with a blood pressure reading of 40/20mmHg and bradycardia. He eventually became pulseless and an advanced cardiovascular life support protocol was initiat-ed.Unfortunately， he could not be resuscitated， and the cause of death was hypoxic respiratory failure secondary to SARS-CoV-2-induced COVID-19 complicated by ARDS.
