【0】Background：

【1】The last 15 years there has seen an exponential increase in the number of studies utilizing magnet-ic resonance imaging to study brain development and pathology in pediatric populations. During this period， scanners have undergone considerable technological advances and are able to pro-vide striking， high-resolution details of the gross anatomy of the developing brain. Reviewing these high resolution images eccasionally results in the detection of potentially abnormal findings， even in the brains of asymptomatic and healthy research subjects.

【2】Case Report：

【3】Incidental findings have created an ethical dilemma as to the best approach to manage these arti-facts， which may range from true pathology to develepmental differences. The case presented in-volves an incidental subcortical finding on MRI in a healthy 10 year old boy. The clinical manage-ment of the finding， the interaction with the family， and the longitudin al outcome is presented.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Few of the studies to date have presented the longitudinal course and outcome of individuals with such artifacts. The high base rate of incidental findings (13-37%) coupled with the relatively low base rate of pediatric neurological disorders will result in high false positive rates. This translates to many families being concerned that their child has brain pathology， when this is not true. Bayesian statistics can be used to determine the approximate rates of false to true positives. However， stud-ies that determine the sensitivity and specificity of specific incidental findings， coupled with longi-tudinal studies of subjects with incidental findings are required to provide more accurate rates of the true and false positives.

【6】key words： pediatric imaging·bioethics· bayesian · incidental findings· magnetic resonance imaging Structural， functional， and diffusion tensor imaging studies all tend to include the acquisition of a high-resolution struc-tural scan. The high-resolution scan is the primary image in structural imaging studies and allows for the volumetric or morphologic mapping of global and regional anatomy. In functional and diffusion tensor imaging， the high-resolution scans are used for image registration and region of interest analyses . It is not uncommon for these high-resolution structural images to have higher image resolu-tion than what is acquired in clinical practice. This higher resolution affords the opportunity to better identify brain anatomy， however it also increases the probability of find-ing incidental findings on the scans.

【7】Incidental findings on MRI scans have been defined as “ob-servations of potential clinical significance unexpectedly discovered in healthy subjects or in patients recruited to brain imaging research studies and unrelated to the pur-pose or variables of the study". Studies involving radi-ologists who blindly evaluate MRI scans have determined the rate of incidental findings to be between 13 to 37.2%. Of these， between 3 to 8% of the subjects were re-ferred for a clinical evaluation， with 0.5 to 1.2 percent of the participants required an urgent or immediate referral. These rates are very high given that they involve healthy， as-ymptomatic populations. Only one study of incidental find-ings presented outcome data . Kumra et al. found that none of the incidental findings were considered to require medical intervention.

【8】Nevertheless， incidental findings pose an ethical dilemma for the investigators. It is the creed of physicians to do no harm， and there is a genuine concern that an artifact seen on the scan could represent a serious condition (i.e.， brain tumor， arterial-venous malformation). If these conditions are caught early， they could be treated and limit the pain and suffering of an individual. As such， some institutional review boards， NIH study sections， and divisions within the intra-mural research program at the NIH have required all scans to be read by a radiologist . If the sensitivity and specific-ity of the radiologists were close to 100%， there would be no question that all scans， even in those who are asymptomatic and healthy controls，should be read by a radiologist.

【9】However， if the sensitivity of the clinical evaluation is not100%， then there is a flip side to the coin， being the possi-bility that the artifact is a false positive. In an extreme case， harm could come to an otherwise healthy subject in the re-moval of a benign brain mass. While this scenario is high-ly unlikely， it does fall within the realm of possibility. Even without the extreme case of surgery on an otherwise healthy individual， families are often very distraught by the news of the possibility of something， even something benign，in781 their child's brain .

【10】When a concerning artifact on a research MRimage is iden-tified， the subject is typically referred for a medical evalua-tion and a clinical series of scans. This usually entails scan-ning with and without gadolinium as a contrast agent. In the majority of cases， the artifact is considered develop-mental， benign or related to an artifact of the imaging pro-cess. However， a certain percentage of subjects， who now become patients， are followed by their clinicians over time to assess whether any changes are identified on the image. Since the vast majority will not have a serious brain lesion， these patients and families are in a state of anxiety that may last several months.

【11】One important question to address is how many asymp-tomatic children with incidental findings would undergo a clinical evaluation， MRI’s with and without contrast， and be followed over time in order to identify the small num-ber of individuals who have a pathological lesion that is dis-covered during the window of time when early intervention will make a difference? The field of probability and statis-tics can be informative in deriving confidence intervals for conditional probabilities for subjects with incidental find-ings on their MRI scans.

【12】CASE REPORT

【13】A 10 year old healthy male took part as a healthy con-trol for a study of brain changes associated with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The study was ap-proved by the Institutional Review Board at the University of Minnesota and informed consent and assent was obtained prior to the entry into the study. Following the scanning session， the postdoctoral research fellow running the scan， who was a trained radiologist， identified an artifact in the region of the pituitary gland. The finding was of concern and she recommended a clinical evaluation. The inciden-tal finding was explained to the mother of the subject by the physician investigator and a release of information was obtained to discuss the findings with the child's pediatri-cian. Understandably， the information was upsetting to the mother in spite of the fact that she was told that inciden-tal findings are not uncommon.The mother and child fol-lowed up immediately with the pediatrician who ordered a clinical MRI series.

【14】The clinical scan was performed with and without contrast(12.8 ml gadolinium). The radiologist noted that the pitu-itary stalk was slightly displaced with nonspecific signal low-ering along the left of the sella. The radiologist noted；“The normal posterior lobe of the pituitary gland is located to the right of midline posteriorly with some nonspecific low-er signaling tissue along the left side of the posterior sel-la， which may represent normal anterior pituitary gland. A discrete posterior pituitary gland mass is not identified and these changes may be due to some developmental asymme-try. There is slight deviation of the pituitary stalk to the right. Due to these findings， a follow up study is recommended to ensure stability. Correlation with any clinical or hormonal abnormalities would be useful as well.”

【15】The subject had an additional clinical scan 3 months after the initial clinical scan. This scan demonstrated no pra-gression and the artifact was ruled a developmental variant. While relieved by the results ofthe second scan， the mother was upset by the process， She stated that she was very wor-ried up until the time of the second scan. In addition， she mentioned the time lost due to physician appointments and the considerable co-pays for the two MRI scans. The event was reported to the local institutional review beard as an adverse event， and IRB requested additional information， which was also provided. This event also prompted a revi- sion to several of the researcher's consent forms to more specifically address this issue.

【16】DISCUSSION

【17】While it is true that the mother and the child were upset by the process， they would have likely been very relieved if the artifact proved to be a malignant tumor that was caught early and effectively treated. Included in the differential diagno-sis of a pituitary adenoma are conditions such as craniopha-ryngiomas， which are calcified and more likely to present in children， rathke cleft cysts， meningiomas aptic gliomas， dermoid tumors， metastasic lesions， nasopharyngeal carci-nomas， chordomas， aneurysms， and mucoceles . While this is a long list that includes some very serious conditions， all of these conditions are extremely rare.

【18】The true incidence of pituitary adenomas in pediatric pop-ulations is not known， although it is uncommon in children.A postmortem study found that the lifetime prev-alence of subclinical pituitary adenoma to be 22.4% in an elderly population . Thus， at some point after child-hood， approximately one in five individuals will develop a subclinical， or asymptomatic pituitary adenoma. Given the high lifetime prevalence of pituitary adenomas， it is unlike-ly that an intervention would be performed in an asymp-tomatic adolescent with an artifact in the region of the pi-tuitary. Thus， it could be argued that rather than referring the child for a clinical scan， it may have been better to forego the clinical scan and perform a careful neurelogi-cal exam and an assessment of the endocrine system cou-pled with educating the family of potential pituitary symp-toms. Yet even this may cause considerable anxiety， and most parents would likely want to pursue a clinical scan. The ra-diologist reading the clinical scans was covertly applying Bayesian statistics when he noted in his dictation “correlation with any clinical or hormonal abnormalities would be useful as well."The probability of brain pathology is much greater when a patient has both an abnormality on the MRI and related clinical signs or symptoms. However， the probabil-ity that an asymptomatic child who has an incidental find-ing on MRI actually has a severe neurologic condition will depend upon the location of the artifact， the base rate of the condition， and the sensitivity and specificity of the in-terpretation of the scan.

【19】The distribution of brain tumors differ greatly between chil-dren and adults  and thus the management of inciden-tal findings in children are different than in adult popula-tions. There are also differences in tumor types and location of tumors between infants， older children and adolescents. While rare， brain tumors are the most common solid tumors in children and adolescents and 50% of these tu-mors are malignant . In contrast to adults， who have90% of their tumors in the cerebral hemispheres， half of pediatric brain tumors are in the infratentorial regions， and thus are more likely to show clinical symptoms earlier . The overall incidence of malignant CNS tumors in children and adolescents has been shown to be between 20 to 30 per million . Understanding that CNS tumors are just one of numerous conditions that can be identified by MRI， the combination of low incidence of CNS tumors， with a high incidence of MRI artifacts creates a scenario yielding high rates of false positives.

【20】Bayesian statistics is a form of conditional probability that can be used to determine the probability of an event occur-ring given that another event has already occurred . For example， it could be used to determine the probability of an individual having a pituitary tumor knowing that there is an artifact present on the MRI scan in the region of the pituitary. As would be expected， the presence of an artifact in the region of the pituitary increases the probability of true pituitary pathology， however， the actual increased risk is dependent upen the incidence of the event and the sen-sitivity and specificity of the measure. In this case the sensi-tivity and specificity involves the reading of the MRI.

【21】One of the difficulties of applying Bayesian statistics is th at the incidence， specificity， and sensitivities are often not readily available. The case of a pituitary adenoma serves as an example， for while the prevalence is known for older adults， the actual incidence of pituitary adenomas in pedi-atric populations that are clinically significant is unknown. It is known that they account for less than 3 percent of all pediatric brain tumors ， and thus an estimate of the in-cidence of a pituitary adenoma in the pediatric population is 0.9 per million.

【22】Application of bayesian statistics to incidental MRI findings

【23】Example： In the case presentation above， an MRI scan in an asymptomatic study subiect revealed an alteration in the area surrounding the pituitary. An assumption of this example is that 99 out of 100 radiologists are able to readily identify this size oflesion accurately as a pituitary adenoma. In addi-tion， the false positive rate， or the rate that such an artifact is present in the absence of a tumor will be considered to be 0.1%， or l in 1，000 radiologists. The sensitivity and speci-ficity used in this example is overly conservative considering the 60 to 80% interrater reliability of radiologists for other body systems . Nevertheless， given these high mea-sures of the sensitivity and specificity of clinical MRI read-ings， the probability that the individual has a pituitary ade-noma can be calculated using Bayesian statistics.

【24】Bayes’ Theorem is shown below. The incidence of a pituitary adenoma (B in the equation) is 0.9 per 1，000，000. Using Bayes' Theorem the probability that the lesion is a pituitary adenoma is 0.000896， or approximately l per 1，100. Thus， the probability of a false positive for healthy， asymptomatic individuals is very high in spite of the high sensitivity and specificity of the reading of the MRI. This is due to the inci-dence of a pituitary adenoma being so low. It becomes even less probable when more realistic measures of the sensitiv-ity and specificity is used. When the sensitivity is 75%and the specificity is 95%， then the probability that the individ-ual has a pituitary adenoma is l in 75，000.

【25】Bayes Theorem for Conditional Probability . Pr(B.A) is the probability of event Bi occurring given that A has oc-curred (i.e.， probability of a pituitary adenoma given that the scan is positive). Pr(B.) is the incidence of event B. i.e.， the incidence of a pituitary adenoma in the general papu- lation. Pr(A B) is the probability of an abnormal scan giv-en that the patient has a pituitary adenoma (true positive). In the simple case， the denominator includes the numer-ator plus the product of Pr(B)， the probability of not hav-ing a pituitary adenoma， which is (1-B)， and Pr(AB )， the probability of an abnormal scan， given the patient does not have condition B.， or does not have an a pituitary adenoma(false positive rate).

【26】Bayesian statistics are frequently applied to tools used for diagnostic screening . These often is a two stage pracess in which the first stage involves a test with higher sensitivity in order to limit the number of false negatives. The second stage is a test with much greater specificity， in order to limit the number of false positives. If the current data of artifacts in MRI of healthy typically developing chil-dren being on the order of l in 100 requiring an urgent re-ferral， the question should be raised as to whether MRI scans should be utilized as a normal screening tool for healthy populations. As with sports physicals， should a truck with an MRI scanner pull up once a year in to the parking lot of our schools so that children can undergo a brain MRI to rule out potential pathology?

【27】Fortunately， the incidence of serious pathology in the brains of asymptomatic children is very low， and thus even with very conservative estimates of the sensitivity and specifici-ty of clinical readings， most artifacts will be false positives. Nevertheless， the field of pediatric neuroimaging is still fair-ly young and few studies have provided follow up data to help formulate approaches dealing with incidental artifacts. This paper provides an argument to caution against overly aggressive work ups in asymptomatic children and adoles-cents who present with incidental MRI findings until the time that longer follow up studies are performed.

【28】Ethical considerations in incidental findings

【29】In 1979 the National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects in Biomedical and Behavioral Research published the Belmont Report， which defined the princi-ples of beneficence， respect for persons， and justice in hu-man subjects research . Respect for persons implies that in dividuals， or in this case the family， are provided with all the information needed to make an autonomous decision. However， respect for persons may also imply the need for protection， “even to the point of excluding them from activ-ities which may harm them”. Families confronted with most incidental findings in the brain of their asymptomatic child will likely not understand the low probability of their child having a true pediatric CNS disorder. This knowledge is important in helping them making an informed decision regarding their child. The challenge， however， is that our current knowledge only allows very rough estimates of the sensitivity， specificity， and incidence of a number of CNS dis-orders. In addition， those of us who scan enough children will eventually come across a child whose artifact is serious， which may cause us to be more aggressive in how we treat future artifacts 35.

【30】CONCLUSION

【31】The high base rate of incidental findings in MRI scans in healthy children and adolescents， coupled with the low base rate of neurological disorders， provides a situation where numerous false positives will be identified. Cases when the scan is without any abnormalities and the case where a le-sion is present and clearly identifiable are more straightfor-ward. Abnormalities in clinical populations， who are being studied for specific disorders that affect the CNS are also more clear， as many of these subjects may have already un-dergone a clinical MRI scan of the brain. It is when inci-dental findings appear on MRI scans in the control popu-lations， who are healthy and showing no CNS symptoms， which are less clear. Missing something severe and poten-tially treatable， such as a malignant tumor， arterial-venous malformation， or CNS infection would be devastating. Alternatively， having a child undergo a surgery for a false positive is more devastating. Such a situation could possibly accur， as it is conceivable that a parent will want to be can-vinced that their child does not have serious CNS patholo-gy. Finally， there is current disagreement about whether to perform serial MRI scans on children at high risk for the reaccurrence of brain tumors . The rationale is based on evidence that serial scans may not provide any benefit to outcome in asymptomatic individuals when the reaccur-rences are caught early.

【32】None of the prior studies of incidental findings to date have attempted to quantify the probability of serious pa-thology related to the MRI findings. In addition， only one prior study presented longitudinal findings related to inci-dental MRI artifacts， of which all children were considered without severe pathology . If the family in the case study described above were presented with information that the probability that their child had pituitary adenoma was l in1，100 (or l in 75，000)， would this have altered either their fears or their decision to follow-up? Should clinicians pro-vide families be provided with estimates?

【33】If families should be provided with such estimates， then it will require investigators to work together to perform a num-ber of studies to assess the sensitivity and specificity of MRI readings， coupled with the longitudinal follow-up of chil-dren and adolescents with and without incidental findings on their MRI scans. The latter has been recommended in one of the initial reports of incidental findings in MRI re-search subjects . In order to accomplish this， one passi-bility is that research centers involved in pediatric neuroim-aging have scans read not just by one radiologist， but by a network of radiologists. This would help determine the sen-sitivity and specificity of the readings. In addition， individ-uals who do have incidental findings on their MRI should be followed to assess outcome.

【34】Studies to date do not address the emotional response of the family or child to the presence of an incidental brain MR finding. In the case presented， the mother was very up-set by the process and was fearful that her child had a seri-ous brain abnormality. Families do not typically think along Bayesian lines and thus would likely consider an incidental finding as having a high probability for being a true find-ing. Thus， an incidental finding likely places a significant stress to families.

【35】The effect on the child is likely related to their developmen-tal age. Younger school age children may not understand the potential ramifications and feel that they are somehow defective. In addition， fears of the parents may be transmit-ted to the child and augment fears in the child. Finally， old-er children and adolescents will have a better grasp on the potential impact of a brain lesion on their life and func-tion. Like their parents， they will also not know that the probability of such an event is very low. Thus， future stud-ies of incidental findings in pediatric populations should not only include the follow up of true and false positives， but should also include an evaluation of the psychosocial effects on children and their families in the presence of in-cidental MR findings.

【0】Background：

【1】DRESS is a rare， life threatening syndrome that occurs following exposure to certain medications， most com-monly antibiotics and antiepileptics. While sulfonamide antibiotics are frequently implicated as causative agents for DRESS syndrome， furosemide， a nonantibiotic sulfonamide， has not been routinely reported as the caus-ative agent despite its widespread use.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 63 year old male who started furosemide for lower extremity edema 10 weeks prior presented with diarrhea， fever of 39.4℃， dry cough and maculopapular rash involving>50% of his body. He self-discontinued furose-mide due to concern for dehydration. The diarrhea spontaneously resolved， but he developed hypoxia requir-ing hospitalization. CT scan demonstrated mediastinal lymphadenopathy and interstitial infiltrates. Laboratory evaluation revealed leukocytosis， eosinophilia and thrombocytopenia. He was treated empirically for atypical pneumonia， and after resuming furosemide for fluid excess， he developed AKl， worsening rash， fever and eo-sinophilia of 2，394 cell/uL. Extensive infectious and inflammatory work up was negative. Skin biopsy was con-sistent with a severe drug reaction. Latency from introduction and clinical worsening following re-exposure indicated furosemide was the likely inciter of DRESS. The RegiSCAR scoring system categorized this case as“definite”with a score of 8.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】We report a case of severe DRESS syndrome secondary to furosemide， only the second case report in medical literature implicating furosemide. Given its widespread use， the potentially life-threatening nature of DRESS syndrome and the commonly delayed time course in establishing the diagnosis， it is important to remember that， albeit rare， furosemide can be a cause of DRESS syndrome.

【6】MeSH Keywords：

【7】Acute Kidney Injury·Colitis·Drug Hypersensitivity Syndrome· Exanthema·Furosemide·Lung Diseases， Interstitial Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome is a rare， idiosyncratic， potentially life-threatening adverse drug reaction characterized by varying combinations of the following： fever higher than 38.5℃， skin eruptions (usu-ally pruritic maculopapular rash or diffuse erythematous erup-tion)， hematologic abnormalities (eosinophilia or/and mono-nucleosis-like atypical lymphocytes or/and thrombocytopenia)， lymphadenopathy， and multiple internal organ involvement(hepatitis being the most common， followed by nephritis， pneumonitis， colitis， encephalitis， pancreatitis， thyroiditis， or myocarditis) . Nomenclature of this syndrome has signif-icantly evolved over the last 80 years since its first descrip-tion. Initially it was named drug induced pseudolymphoma， then subsequently anticonvulsant hypersensitivity syndrome， drug induced hypersensitivity syndrome， and drug induced de-layed multiorgan hypersensitivity syndrome. The cur-rent name， DRESS， was defined in 1996 by Bocquet et al. The “R" in DRESS since then has been changed from Rash to Reaction due to the diversity of cutaneous manifestations .

【8】DRESS syndrome presents as a spectrum from mild rash with eosinophilia that favorably responds to withdrawal of the of-fending drug to multiple-organ involvement with high mortali-ty and the need for immunosuppressive medications. The syn-drome's estimated prevalence ranges from 1 in 1，000 to 1 in10，000 drug exposures， and mortality has been estimated to be up to 10% . Mortality typically results from myocarditis and severe hepatitis leading to liver failure . No specific diagnostic test currently exists for this syndrome. It requires a high index of suspicion by clinicians and exclusion of other infectious， inflammatory， autoimmune， and neoplastic condi-tions as well as other similar cutaneous drug reactions.Due to the variability of its presentation， DRESS is known as a“great mimicker" which contributes to the delay in diagnosis .

【9】RegiSCAR (European Registry of Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions) is a scoring system developed to more accurately define different entities including Steven-Johnson syndrome， toxic epidermal necrolysis， acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis， and DRESS . Depending on the score， cases of DRESS are categorized into four groups： no case， possible case， probable case， and definite case . Another score de-veloped by a Japanese consensus group for DRESS incorporat-ed reactivation of human herpes virus (HHV)-6 as a criterion in addition to those included in RegiSCAR. The Japanese con-sensus group score classifies cases as either typical DRESS or atypical DRESS .

【10】DRESS has later onset and longer duration than other drug re-actions . Latency between exposure to medication and onset of symptoms is a well-defined characteristic of this syndrome.

【11】It usually ranges from two to six weeks； however， latency pe-riods up to 105 days have been described . More than 40medications have been described to cause DRESS， among which aromatic anticonvulsants (phenytoin and carbamazepine) and antibiotic sulfonamides (dapsone， sulfasalazine， and sulfa-methoxazole) are the most common . Furosemide， a nonantibiotic sulfonamide， has rarely been cited as a cause of DRESS syndrome and， to the best of our knowledge， this is the second case published in the literature . Here， we present a severe case of DRESS syndrome caused by furosemide that was manifested by typical rash， fever， hematologic abnormal-ities， and unusually extensive visceral organ involvement in-cluding nephritis， pneumonitis and colitis. Using RegiSCAR， it scored 8 points (maximum possible score 9) classifying it in the definite DRESS case category . The Japanese consen-sus group score classified it as atypical DRESS due to the ab-sence of documented HHV-6 reactivation 11

【12】Case Report

【13】A 63-year-old male with a history of hypertension， chronic back pain secondary to spinal stenosis， and lower extremity edema was transferred to our hospital for further management of fe-ver， diffuse maculopapular rash， and cough. His medications included oxycodone for back pain， losartan for hypertension， and furosemide which had been started for lower extremity swelling approximately 10 weeks prior to hospitalization. He was fully employed and in good overall health. He was a mar-ried resident of the USA Midwest who rarely drank alcohol， did not smoke， and did not use illicit drugs. He had not recently traveled outside the USA and had no pets.

【14】His symptoms started two weeks prior to admission with pro-fuse watery diarrhea without vomiting， hematochezia， or ab-dominal pain. One week prior to admission， he developed a dif fuse， itchy maculopapular rash. At the same time， he noticed a dry， nonproductive cough， as well as fevers up to 38.6℃，and he stopped taking furosemide on his own because of concern for dehydration. His symptoms persisted， so he was admitted for further investigation and management.

【15】On admission， his physical examination revealed a man in moderate distress. Vitals signs were notable for temperature of 38.6C， blood pressure 126/59 mm Hg， heart rate 103 beats per minute， respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute， and oxygen saturation was 95% on 2 L oxygen via nasal cannula. Diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash was present on his face， up-per torso， back， and both upper and lower extremities sparing palms and soles. There was no conjunctival injection or muco-sal involvement. Apart from tachycardia， his cardiovascular ex-amination was normal without murmur. His lungs were clear bilaterally without crackles or rhonchi. His abdomen was soft and nontender， without hepatosplenomegaly. There were no focal neurological deficits.

【16】The laboratory workup was significant for leukocytosis of11.8×10°/L and elevated eosinophil count of 1.29×10°/L. Hemoglobin and platelets were normal. Creatinine， electrolyte， and liver enzymes tests were all normal. Inflammatory markers were elevated with C-reactive protein (CRP) of 229 and eryth-rocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 31. Blood gas showed hy-poxemia， and partial oxygen was 66 mm Hg. Computed to-mography (CT) scan of the chest showed significant hilar lymphadenopathy and interstitial changes consistent with pneumonitis .

【17】Empiric treatment initiated included levofloxacin for commu-nity-acquired pneumonia and intravenous (I) fluids for pre-sumed sepsis while awaiting blood and sputum culture re-sults. The following day his rash worsened， cough and fevers persisted， and he developed thrombocytopenia. Doxycycline for empiric coverage of tick-borne pathogens was added and a diagnostic panel for tick-borne illnesses sent. Skin biopsy was performed. The next day the patient was feeling slight-ly better； he was afebrile though cough and eosinophilic leu-kocytosis persisted. The patient’s home dose of furosemide20 mg by mouth was resumed for chronic lower extremity swelling， which resulted in significant clinical deterioration 12hours following re-exposure. His rash worsened， hypoxia and dyspnea progressed， fevers returned up to 39.4℃， and both leukocytosis and eosinophilia worsened. Additionally， he de-veloped acute kidney injury and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. DRESS syndrome secondary to furose-mide was suspected.

【18】Extensive infectious and autoimmune workup was negative including the following： no growth on blood and sputum cul-tures， negative respiratory panel (influenza A and B， respirato-ry syncytial virus (RSV)， parainfluenza， adenovirus， and human metapneumovirus)， negative streptolysin O antibodies， nega-tive gamma interferon release assay for tuberculosis， negative urine Legionella and streptococcal antigens， negative myco-plasma and chlamydia serologies， negative tick-borne illness panel (Lyme disease， rickettsia， human monocytic ehrlichio-sis， human granulocytic anaplasmosis， and Babesia)， negative HlV test， negative syphilis by lgG， negative stool cultures， neg-ative stool for ova and parasites including Strongyloides，neg-ative viral and parasite serologies (Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)， cy-tomegalovirus (CMV)， parvovirus B19， toxoplasma， hepatitis A， B， and C)， negative HHV-6 PCR， and negative testing for en-demic mycoses (histoplasmosis， blastomycosis， coccidioido-mycosis， and cryptococcosis).

【19】Inflammatory workup was also negative including negative or normal antinuclear antibody (ANA) and antiphospholipid anti-bodies， complement levels， C-ANCA， P-ANCA， tryptase levels， and angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) levels. Urine analysis showed no casts or eosinophils but was significant for hema-turia and proteinuria (100 mg/dL). Finally， protein electropho-resis was negative for monoclonal spike， and flow cytometry for leukemia/lymphoma was negative. Skin biopsy was con-sistent with severe drug reaction .

【20】Workup for atrial fibrillation included echocardiogram that showed normal left ventricle (LV) ejection fraction without peri-cardial effusion or wall motion abnormalities. Troponin T， cre-atine kinase (CK)-MB， and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) were negative. He did not respond to diltiazem and metopro-lol， so amiodarone was used for rate control. Use of amioda-rone coincided with initiation of steroids.

【21】On hospital day 5， following clinical worsening with resum-ing furosemide and after extensive workup ruled out infec-tious， inflammatory， and neoplastic etiologies， the diagnosis of DRESS syndrome secondary to furosemide was made and the patient was started on 1 mg/kg of oral prednisone daily.

【22】Levofloxacin and doxycycline were discontinued. The patient dramatically improved in the next few days. The trajectory of selected tests is shown in Figure 3. He was discharged on a slow taper decreasing dose of prednisone by 10 mg every two weeks. Atovaquone was given for pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis during his course of steroid treatment. Bactrim (for the same indication) was avoided due to concern for cross-reaction to the sulfa component. He was discharged on spironolactone as a diuretic for treatment of his lower ex-tremity edema. At his primary care follow-up visit six weeks after onset of symptoms， he had improved symptomatically， and his laboratory testing normalized . At that time of last follow-up， he continued to have fatigue， mild shortness of breath， and insomnia from steroids.

【23】Discussion

【24】The pathogenesis of DRESS syndrome is not completely under-stood. Multiple authors agree， however， that a complex inter-play between a patient’s genetic predispositions， abnormalities in metabolic pathways leading to accumulation of drug metab-olites， as well as drug-virus interactions leading to reactivation of HHV-6 and HHV-7， EBV， and CMV are likely responsible for the syndrome . The association between specif-ic human leukocyte antigen allele (HLA) groups in some eth nic populations and the development of DRESS with exposure to certain medications has been described . For exam-ple， minocycline induced DRESS syndrome seems to be more prevalent in Caribbean blacks . Similarly， HLA-B\*5701 is as-sociated with abacavir-induced DRESS syndrome and HLA-B\*5801 is associated with allopurinol-induced DRESS syndrome in certain Chinese groups .

【25】Diagnosis of DRESS syndrome is difficult to establish， and it requires a high level of suspicion as well as ruling out oth-er etiologies. Multi-system involvement and febrile skin erup-tion makes the list of differential diagnoses quite extensive. It includes infectious disease (e.g.， viral exanthemas， staphy-lococcal and streptococcal shock syndromes， meningococce-mia)， noninfectious drug eruptions (e.g.， Stevens-Johnson syn-drome， toxic epidermal necrolysis)， autoimmune disease (e.g.， Kawasaki disease， Stills’ disease， hypereosinophilic syndrome) and neoplastic diseases (e.g.， leukemia cutis， mycosis fungoi-des). Depending on the specific organs involved， the differen-tial diagnosis also includes viral hepatitis (liver)， glomerulone-phritis， vasculitidies， pre-and post-renal causes of acute kidney injury (kidney)， Kawasaki disease and eosinophilic myocarditis(heart)， parasitic infection (gastrointestinal (Gl) tract)， and bac-terial， viral and fungal pathogens (lung). There is no pathog-nomonic sign or diagnostic test for DRESS. The diagnosis is clinical and established by taking into account drug exposure in the appropriate clinical setting and latency between drug exposure and symptom onset. While re-challenging with the causative drug has been the gold standard to diagnose drug eruptions， it should not be used in suspected DRESS cases due to the life-threatening nature of this syndrome .

【26】Our patient was unintentionally re-challenged with furose-mide， and shortly following re-exposure his clinical symptoms and laboratory findings worsened. Following re-exposure to fu-rosemide， he developed worsening rash and hypoxia as well as increased fever， eosinophil count， and creatinine. This was when we suspected DRESS while simultaneously confirming that furosemide was the causative agent. Shorter latency pe-riod after re-challenging has been described in DRESS . Antibiotic sulfonamides have been previously described as causative agents for DRESS， and are one of the most common classes of antibiotics to cause the syndrome. The nonantibi-otic sulfonamide furosemide has not commonly been report-ed to cause DRESS syndrome. In our review of the literature， we found only one case linking furosemide to DRESS . In that case， as in our case， the patient developed visceral in-volvement including hepatitis and nephritis. That case scored 7 on RegiSCAR and the patient responded favorably to oral steroids with prednisone 1 mg/kg daily as initial therapy . Our case further substantiates furosemide as an inciting agent of DRESS considering the acute worsening of symptoms with re-exposure to furosemide. The sulfonamide group of furose-mide is likely responsible for the reaction， yet it remains an enigma why furosemide has been remarkably less frequently associated with DRESS in comparison to sulfonamide antibiot-ics despite it containing a sulfa component. One possibility is that different metabolic pathways of various sulfa-containing compounds lead to different reactive metabolites which differ in immunogenic reactivity. For example， metabolite formation is stereospecific to the N4 amino nitrogen of the sulfonamide antibiotics， a structure not found on any nonantibiotic sulfon-amide drugs . The leucocyte transformation/activation test(LAT) has been used sporadically to confirm the causative drug and confirm cases of DRESS. The test measures the prolifera-tion of T cells to a drug in vitro. Unfortunately， it is not stan-dardized for many medications， is difficult to perform， usual-ly yields a negative result early in the course of the syndrome， and lacks sensitivity . A positive LAT is useful to confirm the diagnosis due to very low false positive results (only 2%)， however， a negative test cannot exclude diagnosis . All of these factors prevent widespread use of this test.

【27】In their review of the literature， Cacoub et al. showed that proba-ble/definite cases consistently demonstrated more delayed onset of symptoms when compared to possible cases . Additionally， time to resolution of symptoms was longer in probable/definite cases when compared to possible cases. This is consistent with our case that exhibited a quite long latency period of 10 weeks and resolved over the course of three weeks. This case scored8 points on RegiSCAR which indicates a“definite” DRESS case. The Japanese consensus group criteria， however， characterized it as “atypical" DRESS due to the lack of demonstrated HHV-6 reactivation. Reactivation of HHV-6 has not been routinely tested. In the era of increasing healthcare cost and increasing pressure to cut down on spending it is important to evaluate utility of testing for HHV-6 reactivation in routine cases outside of research purposes since it does not affect management. In fact， Cacoub et al. found that reactivation of HHV-6 was tested in only 41% of cases， however， when HHV-6 reactivation was tested， 80% of cases tested positive . The severity of DRESS syndrome and mortality appears to be tightly related to the extent of involvement of visceral organs . Multiple organs and systems of organs have been described to be affected in DRESS syndrome， which can make DRESS a difficult diagnosis to make because of both the extent and diversity of presenta-tion. Previously identified affected visceral organs include liv-er， kidney， lung， intestines， and heart. Hence， we describe the manifestations of these involved organs. The liver is the organ most commonly affected in DRESS syndrome . Liver involve-ment is considered if the patient has exhibited hepatomegaly and/or increase in liver enzymes. In a study of 25 patients by Lee et al. ， the liver was affected in 80% of cases. Among these， 24% of patients had hyperbilirubinemia， while the rest had elevation in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). A study by Chen et al. of 60 consecutive patients from Taiwan between 1998-2008 re-demonstrated liv-er involvement in 80% of cases . Interestingly， our patient did not have significant liver involvement despite extensive in-volvement of other visceral organs.

【28】Renal involvement in DRESS is common with 11%-28% of patients being affected . Renal involvement is usually manifested as elevation in creatinine， decrease in glomerular filtration rate (GFR)， proteinuria， and hematuria. Our patient exhibited all of these indicators. Allopurinol is the medication most commonly associated with renal involvement . Several case reports documented favorable outcomes in renal recovery following treatment， even in the patients who tem-porarily required renal replacement therapy . Our pa-tient recovered completely three weeks following discharge， with resolution of hematuria and proteinuria and return of GFR and creatinine to pre-morbid levels.

【29】Unlike liver and kidney， lungs are rarely affected in DRESS syndrome. The most commonly described findings are inter-stitial pneumonitis， pneumonia， pleural effusion， and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) . Exact incidence of lung involvement in DRESS is unknown but it ranges from2.6% in a study by Chen et al.  to 5% as documented by Cacoub et al. Minocycline and abacavir are the medica-tions most often associated with lung involvement . Interestingly， in a study of 15 patients with severe DRESS syn-drome (with mortality rate of 20%) admitted to a critical care unit， 10 patients (67%) had lung involvement. In this group of critically ill patients， allopurinol and minocycline - known to be associated with high mortality and lung involvement -were the most common offending agents， respectively . Our patient had interstitial pneumonitis with significant medi-astinal lymphadenopathy on admission， which led to empiric treatment for community-acquired pneumonia. Due to persis-tent fevers， worsening leukocytosis and eosinophilia despite appropriate broad-spectrum antibiotics， we confidently con-cluded that lung involvement was part of DRESS syndrome in this case after infectious workup was negative for viral， bacte-rial， and fungal pathogens and serology was negative for vas-culitidies that commonly involve lungs and renal parenchyma concomitantly (systemic lupus erythematosus， Goodpasture's syndrome， antiphospholipid antibody syndrome and ANCA as-sociated vasculitis). Following administration of steroids， his lymphadenopathy and hypoxia completely resolved.

【30】Nonspecific Gl symptoms including diarrhea have been de-scribed as part of DRESS， however， they are rarely investigated which might contribute to underestimation of the prevalence of Gl involvement . Out of 25 patients described by Lee et al.， only two patients (8%) had colitis. Several case reports have described colon involvement in DRESS . Colon in-volvement in DRESS ranges from mild self-resolving diarrhea to profuse diarrhea leading to severe electrolyte abnormali-ties. One case was also complicated with hemophagocytic syn-drome resulting in death from massive Gl hemorrhage . Chung et al. described a case where the patient had signifi-cant diarrhea as part of DRESS syndrome， who failed to im-prove on oral prednisone and required IV hydrocortisone to improve. Hence， they argued that hyper motility of the diges-tive tract lead to poor absorption of steroids and suggested that in cases with significant Gl involvement initial treatment should be with I steroids . It is important to rule out infec-tious causes of diarrhea， especially parasitic， inflammatory， and ischemic causes. In our patient， infectious diarrhea had been ruled out and we believe that diarrhea was his first symptom of DRESS syndrome. It is prudent to keep in mind DRESS in the differential diagnosis for patients with fever， eosinophilia， diarrhea， and negative infectious workup since diarrhea might be the presenting symptom of DRESS colitis.

【31】Cardiovascular involvement in DRESS is usually manifested as myocarditis and， although rare， is associated with high mor-tality (55%). One of the distinct features of DRESS myocardi-tis is that it can occur late after resolution of all other symp-toms and after normalization of laboratory values. It has been documented to occur up to four months following successful treatment of DRESS . The most common medication asso-ciated with DRESS myocarditis is ampicillin.Manifestations in-clude chest pain， non-specific electrocardiogram (ECG) chang-es or gross ST segment elevation or depression， tachycardia and arrhythmias， and decrease in LV ejection fraction . Definite diagnosis is made by endomyocardial biopsy， howev-er， due to the invasive nature of the biopsy， diagnosis is most often made clinically based on ECG findings， echocardiogra-phy (ECHO) and laboratory results. Troponin and CK-MB are elevated in the majority of myocarditis cases， though neither was elevated in our case. Our patient developed atrial fibril-lation with rapid ventricular response shortly after being re-exposed to furosemide， which we considered possible cardio-vascular involvement as part of DRESS syndrome， even though the ECHO did not show evidence of reduced LV ejection frac-tion or wall motion abnormalities.

【32】There have been no prospective clinical trials done to guide treatment for DRESS syndrome. Current recommendations are based on case reports and expert opinion. The first and most important step in treatment is withdrawal of the incit-ing medication. Without this step， other treatment will be fu-tile. Earlier withdrawal of the drug is associated with better prognosis . In mild to moderate cases without visceral involvement， withdrawal of the causative agent together with topical steroids for rash and topical or systemic antihistaminic agents for itchiness is usually adequate. However， in cases of visceral involvement， systemic steroids are indicated . Optimal dose， route of administration， duration of treatment， and rapidity of dose tapering of steroid treatment have not been verified in controlled trials. The majority of case reports have suggested initiating prednisone 1 mg/kg orally with sub-sequent slow taper over three to six months. Rapid taper can be associated with relapse . Proposed mechanism by which corticosteroids benefit the patient is inhibition of IL-5， which is essential for accumulation of eosinophils and which， in turn， is responsible for visceral organ damage in DRESS syndrome. Some authors， however， suggest that corticosteroids should not be used in cases of documented viral reactivation due to the potential to exacerbate the reactivation disease . The benefit of antiviral medications is unclear in cases of doc-umented viral reactivation， yet some authors have used it suc-cessfully . Dramatic improvement in symptoms and frequent relapses associated with quick prednisone taper strongly ar-gues in favor of systemic steroid therapy in cases of moder-ate to severe disease. In severe and corticosteroid-resistant cases， more potent immunosuppressant medications includ-ing cyclosporine， azathioprine， and mycophenolate have been used， sometimes alongside adjunctive treatment with intrave-nous immunoglobulin (IG) and plasmapheresis . Our pa-tient responded favorably to oral prednisone 1 mg/kg daily for Long-term sequelae of DRESS syndrome include development of autoimmune disease including thyroiditis， diabetes melli-tus type l， systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)， systemic scle-rosis， or adrenal insufficiency. These manifestations can occur months to years following the initial episode and careful fol-low-up and awareness of this association is crucial for timely recognition and treatment should they occur .

【33】Conclusions

【34】We present a case of severe DRESS syndrome with multiple visceral organ involvement caused by furosemide that favor-ably responded to systemic steroids. Apart from classically de-scribed involvement of the skin and hematologic system， our patient exhibited colitis， pneumonitis， and nephritis- a com-bination that hasn't been reported thus far. DRESS can be life-threatening and delay in diagnosis is associated with worse outcome. Hence， it is important to recognize that furosemide， albeit rare， can cause DRESS syndrome. Increased awareness regarding the association between DRESS and furosemide will help with diagnosing future cases in timely manner and avoid-ing the morbidity of delayed diagnosis.

【0】Background： Situs inversus is a rare complication of cystic kidney diseases. Only three genes， INVS (NPHP2)， NPHP3 and PKD2 have been proved to be responsible for some cases， while the responsible genes in many others are still unknown.

【1】Case Reports： Here we report two male patients with situs inversus combined with cystic kidney disease without any family history of polycystic kidney disease. Their renal function was normal in childhood but culminated in end stage renal disease in middle age. No pathogenic mutations were found in mutation analysis of INVS， IFT88， PKD2， UMOD or NPHP3 in them.

【2】Conclusions： Past reported cases of situs inversus and cystic kidney diseases were divided into three groups， i.e.， gesta-tional lethal renal dysplasia group， infantile or juvenile nephronophthisis group and polycystic kidney disease group. The present patients are different from each of these groups. Moreover， the renal lesions of the pres-ent two cases are quite different from each other， with one showing mildly atrophic kidneys with small num-bers of cysts and the other an enlarged polycystic kidney disease， suggesting very heterogeneous entities.

【3】Key words： ADPKD ·cystic kidney disease · situs inversus

【4】Since Alfzelius reported that infertile males whose sperm cilia were immortal had the triad of Kartagener syndrome， prima-ry cilia were discovered to be the key player underlying organ laterality . Here， we describe two situs inversus totalis males with cystic kidney disease who reached end stage renal dis-ease (ESRD) in middle age in the absence of any family history of polycystic kidney disease (PKD). Situs inversus is an uncom-mon complication of cystic kidney diseases， with 28 such cases reported since 1981. Only three genes， INVS (NPHP2)，NPHP3and PKD2 have been proved to be responsible for some cases， while the responsible genes in many others are still unknown. In mutation screening analysis of INVS， IFT88，PKD2， UMOD， NPHP3， no pathogenic mutations were detected. Some muta-tions of other genes that encode protein expression in prima-ry cilia in both node and kidney are expected to be present in these patients， and will require further investigation in future.

【5】Case Reports

【6】Patient 1

【7】A 54-year-old Japanese man developed severe azotemia and anemia and required emergent hemodialysis and transfusion.

【8】On a regular chest X-ray obtained at the age of 20 years， si-tus inversus had been pointed out. At 47 years. bilateral kid-ney cysts and renal insufficiency were detected on a regular medical check-up. He had no history of sinusitis or bronchi-ectasis. A chest X-ray revealed dextracardia and cardiomeg aly . Abdominal CT scan showed situs inversus to-talis of all the abdominal organs and bilateral kidney cysts， but the number and sizes of the cysts were small . There were no extrarenal cysts. He has no family member with PKD or situs inversus. His parents were not consanguineous. He has two biological children. His karyotype was normal.

【9】Patient 2

【10】This Japanese man started regular hemodialysis at the age of45 years. He was the third child of non-consanguineous par-ents. From the age of two years he developed frequent bron-chitis， sinusitis and otitis media， and by his teens had devel-oped hearing impairment that required a hearing aid. Because he refused to consult any physicians despite his long-standing ill health， situs inversus and polycystic kidneys were not detect-ed until one year before he needed hemodialysis. At the same time bronchiectasis was detected by chest CT and he was diag nosed with Kartagener syndrome. His grandfather had situs in-versus but there was no family history of PKD. He has two bi-ological children. A chest X-ray  and an abdominal CT scan  revealed situs inversus totalis and bilater-al multiple renal and hepatic cysts. After 10 years of regular he-modialysis， he died of acute myocardial infarction at the age of55 years. Autopsy was performed then. Figures 2 and 3 shows the macroscopic and microscopic findings of the postmortem autopsy of patient 2. The kidneys were enlarged to 28×11 cm(left) and 28x13cm (right) and contained numerous and various-ly sized cysts separated by very thin parenchyma. Variously sized cysts were present in the left-right reversed liver too. The pan-creatic tail was atrophic， but the pancreas contained no cysts.

【11】In kidney specimens cysts of various sizes were prominent， with few glomeruli with no particular features. In the interstitium， atrophic and dilated tubules and calcified veins were present. All of these findings were compatible with those of end-stage kidneys due to Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease(ADPKD). The liver showed variously sized cysts， which consist-ed of a layer of biliary epithelium. The pancreas showed mild fi-brotic change that was attributed to the chronic pancreatitis as-sociated with the renal failure. There was no dysplastic change in the pancreas. In the lungs there were many bronchiectatic regions， the result of repeated inflammation characteristic of Kartagener syndrome. Figure 4 shows cilia staining of patient2 kidney  along with that of an ESRD patient due to non-cystic kidney disease  and ESRD patients receiving hemodialysis due to ADPKD . In patient 2， decreased and shortened primary cilia were observed in dilated renal tu-bular epithelial cells， although this finding is similar to that in ADPKD patients receiving hemodialysis.

【12】No pathogenic mutation was discovered in the sequencing anal- ysis of INVS， PKD2， IFT88， UMOD or NPHP3 in both patients.

【13】Prior to the genetic analysis， informed consent was obtained from both patients. Detailed methods of genetic and patho-logical testing are available upon request.

【19】It would be natural to conclude a diagnosis of ADPKD in the present two patients who started hemodialysis therapy at the age of 54 and 45 years respectively. However some features in the present patients differ from those usually seen in ADPKD including absence of family history of ADPKD in both patients. Sizes of kidneys and numbers of kidney cysts in patient 1 were small for age as compared to usual ADPKD. Patient 2 had fea-tures of typical Kartagener syndrome. Extra renal cysts are com-mon in ADPKD， but none were noted in patient 1. So the pres-ent two patients do not meet the criteria of ADPKD and differ from the two ADPKD patients reported by Bataille . Besides， the phenotypes of the two present patients are quite different.

【20】The phenotype of Medullary cystic kidney disease (MCD) is sim-ilar to that of nephronophthisis. Affected patients reach ESRD in their forties to fifties. It is caused by at least two genes， one of which is Uromodulin (UMOD). UMOD has been found to be located in cilia， although no mutations in UMOD gene were found in the present cases.

【21】A striking point is that even the same gene mutation in the same family may cause different phenotypes.Among 12 related individ-uals with renal dysplasia carrying the same homozygous NPHP3mutation， only one had situs inversus. Both of the two pairs of independent PKD2 family siblings sharing the same mutation had discordance of situs inversus in the report of Bataille. The same homozygous INVS mutation (Arg899X) in two siblings caused si-tus inversus discordantly and another independent patient with the same mutation did not show situs inversus either .On the other hand， all of three siblings manifested situs inversus in the report of Balci  with unknown genetic abnormalities. So it is dif-ficult to assume the mutated gene from the phenotype of a pa-tient because syndromes of cystic kidney diseases combined with situs inversus comprise a very heterogeneous disease spectrum.

【22】In some animals with cilia-related gene mutations there have been descriptions of the presence of no cilia or extremely short primary cilia。and this prompted us to check the cilia of patient 2. An extremely decreased number of and shortened primary cilia were detected in the kidneys of patient 2. However， this finding cannot be considered specific for this patient， since a similar picture is ob-served in the kidneys of ADPKD patients receiving hemodialysis.

【23】The occurrence of situs inversus is decided by the direction of nod-al ciliary movement during embryogenesis . Although the si-tus abnormality can be caused by mutation of a ciliary gene， other modifier genes or environmental factors also likely contribute.The existence of another mutation in another gene may be one expla-nation for the phenomenon. Numerous genes that express pro-teins in cilium and centrosome have been discovered and the num-bers of such genes are still increasing. 13 genes have been proven to be responsible for NPHP， but account for only about 30% of cas-es， which implicates other as yet undiscovered genes in NPHP. Howeverthe mechanisms of such gene complexes are still equivocal.

【24】Conclusions

【25】We describe two patients with situs inversus comorbid with cystic kidney disease that are different from any other previ-ously reported cases. Although no genetic evidence was ob-tained， this syndrome may fall into a kind of cilia dysfunction syndrome. To prove this， analysis of a greater range of cilia re-lated genes will be required in future， Such studies may also provide hints to the formation of left-right asymmetry.

【0】Background：

【1】Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor used for the treatment of depression. This case report presents a patient with sertraline overdose and serotonin syndrome complicated by rhabdomyolysis.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 3l-year-old male patient was brought to the hospital by relatives 48 hours after taking42 tablets of sertaline HCl (Lustral， 50 mg/tablet， Pfizer) during a suicide attempt. He was generally lethargic but did have brief episodes of agitation without apparent precipitating factors.

【4】The patient was admitted to intensive care unit after laboratory evaluation indicated acute renal failure and rhabdomyolysis. Physical exam was notable for hyperreflexia and inducible clonus. Therapy included administration of cyproheptadine for serotonin syndrome and forced diuresis for renal failure by administration of crystalloids and furosemide. The patient’s neurological and biochemical profile improved and the patient was discharged on the 10" day of admission without residual organ impairment.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】This case is consistent with an unusual presentation of serotonin syndrome 48 hours following an overdose of sertraline.

【7】Key words： Sertraline·serotonin syndrome·rhabdomyolysis

【8】Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor(SSRI) that is used widely in the treatment of depres-sion， eating disorders， and obsessive-compulsive disor-ders. It has a large therapeutic index and is considered relatively safe， even in situations of overdose . Serotonin syndrome is a potentially life-threatening adverse drug reaction thought to result from excess serotonergic activity at central nervous system and peripheral serotonin receptors. It is often described as a clinical triad of mental-status changes， autonomic hyperactivity， and neuromuscular abnormalities . However， not all of these findings are consistently present in all patients with the disorder. A striking number of drugs and drug combinations have been associated with serotonin syndrome . These include monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs)， tricyclic antidepressants， opioid analgesics， over-the-counter coughing medicines， antibiotics，weight-reduction agents， antiemetics， antimigraine agents， drugs of abuse， and herbal products； the withdrawal of medications has also been associated with the syndrome. The syndrome has been reported to oc-cur in up to 16 percent of persons who overdose on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. This report presents a patient with diagnostic criteria consistent with serotonin syndrome along with rhabdomyolysis48 hours after a moderate overdose of sertraline.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】A 78 kg， 31-year-old male patient was admitted to the emergency department of Baskent University Adana Teaching and Research Center after a ser- traline overdose. The patient had a history of taking42 tablets of sertraline HCl (2100 mg) for suicidal purpose two days before admission. He had been generally lethargic but with brief episodes of agita-tion. No treatment was sought nor provided between ingestion and hospital presentation.

【11】His past medical history was notable for a diagnosis of minor depression for which he had been taking sertraline (100 mg/day) for the past 3 months. There was no history of suicidal ideation or attempts. He denied illicit drug use and had never been treated with an MAOI or other antidepressant. The remain-der of his past medical history and review of systems was unremarkable.

【12】On admission， his blood pressure was 150/80 mmHg， heart rate was 123 beats/min， respiratory rate was22 breaths/min and temperature was 36.5℃. He had marked hyper-reflexia with dilated pupils and sustained inducible ankle clonus bilaterally but no muscle rigidity. Itchy skin eruptions on his upper and lower extremities were determined by dermatology consultation to be most consistent with an allergic reaction. Initial laboratory evaluations are presented in Table 1 and are notable for markedly elevated serum creatinine kinase (CK)， blood urea nitrogen and creatinine concentrations. His ECG showed sinus tachycardia with normal intervals . Urine was brown colored and was positive by dipstick for myoglobin without red blood cells on microscopic analysis consistent with myoglobinuria.

【13】Management included midazolam infusion (0.05mg/kg/h) for relief of agitation and beta blockers plus calcium channel blockers for hemodynamic stabiliza-tion. Fluid resuscitation with a goal central venous pressure of 7-9 mmHg was combined with forced diuresis by using a furosemide infusion at a rate of20 mg/h for adequate urine output (> 200 cc/h)and hyperkalemia therapy.

【17】Cyproheptadine (Sipraktin sirop 2mg/5ml， I.E.Ulugay， Istanbul， Turkey) 12 mg iv bolus administration was followed by repeated oral doses of 8 mg at 6-hr in-tervals. A 10 day tapered course of methyl predniso-lone (Prednol-L， Mustafa Nevzat， Istanbul， Turkey) was administered for allergic skin reactions (starting dose 1 mg/kg， iv). Clinical situation improved with associated normalization of blood chemistry values . After a psychiatric consultation， the patient was discharged to home on hospital day10 with his baseline mental status and no evidence of organ dysfunction.

【18】DISCUSSION

【19】Sertraline is a commonly prescribed SSRI with a high therapeutic index . However， toxic inges-tions resulting from high dose intake (6-8 gr) or concomitant ingestion with other antidepressants and/or alcohol have been reported . Most of these ingestions with adverse clinical presentations develop subacutely， within hours of drug intake. Our case presented 48 hours after an isolated ingesting of 2.1 gr of sertraline alone.

【20】serotonin syndrome can be diagnosed in individuals with exposure to a triggering drug associated with any 3 of the following findings： changes in mental status， agitation， myoclonus， hyperflexia， diaphoresis， trembling， tremor， and cooperation disorder . None of these symptoms were present in our patient until shortly before presentation 48 hours after drug ingestion. On presentation， he did display coopera-tion disorder， agitation， myoclonus and hyperflexia. It is not clear， however， to what extent the present-ing neurologic observations were related to possible serotonin syndrome or his underlying metabolic dis-orders. Serotonin toxicity can also be diagnosed with“Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria” .Presence of serotonergic agent， inducible clonus， agitation and hyperreflexia were present in our case.

【21】Although various criteria may aid in the diagnosis of serotonin syndrome， they do not indicate the severity of the clinical picture . The syndrome may present with mild， moderate or severe systemic manifestations and progression. Tachycardia，tremor， diaphoresis， and mydriasis are considered as mild symptoms， while the addition of hypertension and hyperthermia are considered to be moderate pro-gression. At that stage， neurologic changes such as agitation and hypervigilence， may develop. In clinical presentations with severe progression， life-threaten-ing alterations such as severe delirium， confusion， muscle rigidity， hyperthermia， rhabdomyolysis， renal failure， and disseminated intravascular coagulation may be seen 11-14.

【22】It is interesting that the major abnormality on pre-sentation in our case was renal failure associated with rhabdomyolysis without a precipitating event save for sertraline ingestion. The patient went on to develop hypertension and tachycardia along with agitation and cooperation disorder consistent with serotonin syndrome. It appears in the present case that rhabdomyolysis was either the presenting fea-ture of serotonin syndrome or a direct adverse side effect of sertraline ingestion. In either case， to our knowledge， such a presentation following sertraline overdose has not been reported.

【23】The treatment protocol for serotonin syndrome in-cludes elimination of the causative agent， manage-ment of agitation， hyperthermia， autonomic insta-bility through supportive treatment protocols， and treatment of organ failure . Benzodiazepines have been recommended for treatment of serotonin syndrome regardless of the severity of the clinical picture. Indeed， benzodiazepines have been reported to facilitate the management of neurological findings with their sedative quality and， in animal models， increase survival rate presumably by attenuating the hyperadrenergic response . In our patient， agitation was managed by midazolam infusion and hemodynamic stability achieved with beta blockers and calcium channel blockers.

【24】Additional treatment recommendations for serotonin syndrome includes administration of cyproheptadine， a 5-HT2A antagonist， although the mechanism has not been clearly defined . This drug which is considered as an atypical antipsychotic agent， has been reported to be efficient in the treatment of au-tonomic instability and regulation of hyperthermia. The drug was also effective in the treatment of aller-gic eruptions of our patient due to its antihistaminic characteristics. On the 10h day of hospitalization， the patient was discharged with completely normal clinical and laboratory results.

【25】CONCLUSIONS

【26】Although sertraline is considered as a safe and effec-tive antidepressant therapy， our case of moderate ser-traline overdose was associated with rhabdomyolisis， renal failure and delayed development of serotonin syndrome. Clinicians need to be aware of the various presentations of serotonin syndrome and the possible association between moderate sertraline overdose and development of rhabdomyolysis.

【0】ABSTRACT The article presents a clinical case of aspiration pneumonia (Mendelson’s syndrome) complicated by the acute respiratory syndrome. Clinical symptomatology of patient S.， 39 years old， hospitalized at the University Clinic of Ivano-Frankivsk on November 5th， 2012， included shortness of breath and cough predominantly， and hemoptysis was observed. Extensive (almost total) radiological changes in both pulmonary fields dissonated with relatively poor auscultatory data， namely， only weakened vesicular respiration was heard throughout the clinical observation period. The data of X-ray examination somewhat resembled the disseminated process， and therefore in some cases were interpreted as a case of the firstly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis (FDPTB)， and later as viral and bacterial pneumonia due to the epidemiological situation regarding the outbreak of California influenza in 2009-2011. However， with the scrupulous survey， we managed to find out that a prerequisite for breathlessness and coughing was repeated vomiting in a patient in the evening and night because of frequent epileptic attacks. This fact contributed to the formation of a proper clinical diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome. The peculiarity of this clinical observation was the fact that it occurred on the comorbidities background (epilepsy； chronic internal haemorrhoids， complicated with rectal bleeding on October 3rd， 2012 and posthemorrhagic anaemia； acute deep vein thrombosis and acute ascending thrombophlebitis of the varicose dilated saphenous veins of both lower limbs). However， with adequate mask mechanical ventilation， antibiotic therapy， mucolytics， clexane， cardiomagnyl， normoven， elastic compression of the lower extremities， dosed exercises， a rapid clinical and particularly radiological dynamic on November 9th， 2012 was noted. Due to this， on December 13th， 2012， the patient was discharged in satisfactory condition for outpatient treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS Mendelson's syndrome， aspiration pneumonia， acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)， epilepsy， X-ray examination， treatment

【2】Introduction

【3】Acid-aspiration pneumonia (Mendelson's syndrome)， or acute exudative pneumonitis， was described in 1946 as the most severe complication of anaesthesia in obstetric practice during child-birth.  Issues of diagnosis， treatment and prevention remain relevant today due to high mortality (40-50% and above). 

【4】Its development is based on the aspiration of acidic gastric juice with a pH of 2-2.5 in a volume of fewer than 25 ml. With increasing volume and its acidity， the severity of the clinical manifestation and the probability of lethal outcome increase. It is established that damage to the epithelial and endothelial layers of cells and edema can occur at low pH-5.0， such as dur-ing bile aspiration.  There is a chemical burn of the mucous membrane of the respiratory tract with damage to the epithe-lium of the trachea， bronchi， bronchioles， burns of the alveoli and capillary endothelium， which can cause pulmonary edema and the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome. At the same time， edema of the mucosal and submucosal lay-ers of the bronchial tree causes obstruction， total bronchospasm and hypoxic respiratory failure.  This usually occurs dur-ing anaesthesia， intoxication， use of sedatives， coma， convul- sions， during emergency child delivery surgical interventions， trauma of face and neck， tumors of the esophagus and trachea， gastro-oesophagal reflux， conditions after gastrectomy， diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system， mechanical and iatrogenic interventions (endotracheal tube， nasogastric tube， tracheostomy)， airway obstruction by a foreign body， vomiting of various genesis and in elderly and old age people， etc.  The respiratory tract is contaminated in 50% of cases by anaer-obic flora， in 40% by combined， and only in 10% by aerobic flora. ， The clinical presentation is characterized by acute onset， obvious signs of respiratory failure or bronchospasm，pos-sible expiratory dyspnea， grey cyanosis， even when 100% oxy-gen is given. The typical triad includes tachycardia， tachypnea， cyanosis.  Often a drop in blood pressure， cardiovascular dis-orders， wheezing over the lungs， crepitation in the lower lungs， the radiograph resembles a "shock lung”- diffuse darkening of the lung tissue are present. When infectious factor combines， the considerable increase in temperature， cold and even， devel-opment of abscessing might possibly occur. ， The effective treatment consists of ventilation with high pressure at the end of exhalation， and in severe cases， hyperbaric oxygenation； large doses of corticosteroids， as well as antibacterial drugs. 

【5】Case report

【6】Patient S.， 39 years old， unemployed， due to California flu epi-demic in 2009-2011 was admitted to the clinic of the Medical University of Ivano-Frankivsk on November 5th， 2012 with a preliminary diagnosis of viral and bacterial pneumonia of group IV， severe form. ARDS. Respiratory failure， third degree. On admission， he complained of a cough with pink and purulent sputum， severe shortness of breath， general weakness，loss of appetite， weight loss， the appearance of painful longitudinalcon-densed cord on the inner surface of the left thigh and lower leg， periodic rectal bleeding， and epileptic seizures. Upon obtaining anamnesis carefully， it was determined that on November 1st，2012， on the background of an increase in epileptic seizures， he had repeated vomiting， after which there was severe shortness of breath， cough，temperature 39 ° C， cold. Vomiting in epilep-tic seizures had been observed repeatedly before. From the of ambulance referral， from November 1st， 2012 was treated in the intensive care unit of the central district hospital， in serious condition， with shortness of breath， RR 35/min，blood oxygen saturation 51%， and on November 3rd， 2012 was transferred to the internal medicine department. The anamnesis revealed that the patient had been suffering from epilepsy for 17 years(received finlepsin medication)， had internal haemorrhoids for a long time， and had periodic rectal bleeding after defecation. A1-lergic anamnesis was not burdened； the patient denied a history of infectious hepatitis，tuberculosis and hereditary diseases in himself or his family members.

【7】The full blood count (FBC) performed on November 1， 2012in the Central District Hospital showed： Hb-74g/l， erythro-cytes - 2.5 x 1012 per liter ， colour index (CI) -0.9， leukocytes-11， 9 x10° per liter， rod-nuclear neutrophils - 20%， segmental neutrophils-72%，lymphocytes-6%， monocytes-2%，ESR-20ml/h， hematocrit-0.19.

【8】Biochemical blood analysis done on November 1， 2012： total bilirubin -11.3 mcmol/l， direct -2.2 mcmol/1， AST-0.48 and ALT -0.42 mlmol/l， urea-7 mlmol/1， creatinine -121 mcmol/1， total protein -69.8 g/l， Ca-2.4 mlmol /1，chlorides - 99 mlmol/1. 【9】Chest X-ray (CXR) performed on November 1 and 2， 2012revealed： on both sides diffused foci of infiltration and consol-idation with blurred contours， sinuses are free. The heart is spread to the left. Conclusion： disseminated pulmonary tuber-culosis? Radiographs were consulted on November 2nd， 2012by a radiologist of the tuberculosis dispensary.
